# Research question

Standard growth regressions (Dell, Jones and Olken 2012; Burke, Hsiang and
Miguel 2015) find robust effects of temperature but little or no effect of
precipitation. This notebook asks whether that changes when each variable's
deviation from its long-run climate is measured in standard deviations and
positive and negative deviations get separate arms: if dry and wet years both
lower growth, a single slope cancels them out.

1. The standard BHM specification on PWT x ERA5, with and without the conflict
   and collapse controls and the growth outliers.
2. The preferred deviation model on PWT x ERA5: deviation definitions and
   linear or quadratic arms.
3. Its robustness across national panels (PWT, World Bank) and climate datasets
   (ERA5, CRU TS, UDelaware): (a) can the precipitation terms jointly be
   rejected; (b) which arms are significant where; (c) the effect of a +/-3 SD
   deviation in cold (dry), medium and hot (wet) climates.
4. The same model on subnational data (DOSE).
5. The same model with a drought index (SPEI) added to the temperature and
   precipitation deviations (PWT x CRU TS, the climate data SPEI is built on).
6. How far the climate interactions carry: with long-run income in the
   interaction; the spread of the country responses around the climate
   gradient (prediction intervals); and the gradient within countries against
   the one across them.

Sample: `r params$start_year` to the last year of each panel. Climate:
population-density weights at base year 2000. Every model has year and unit
fixed effects and unit linear and quadratic trends (as in BHM), with errors
clustered by country. The deviations are demeaned before their arms are cut:
each unit's mean and quadratic trend are removed, so that warm and cold years
are spread over the whole period rather than split by date by the warming
(section "Deviations demeaned before the arms").

**How to read this document.** The code is folded (the "Code" buttons show
it); the text before each table or figure says what is estimated and on which
rows. Throughout:

- effects are in percentage points (pp) of the annual growth of GDP per capita,
  for one year with a deviation of +3 or -3 SD against a year at the unit's
  trend, in a unit with a given long-run climate (5, 15 or 25 °C; 0.5, 1.5 or
  3 m of precipitation a year);
- `T` is temperature and `P` precipitation; `dT+`, `dT-` (and `dP+`, `dP-`) are
  the positive and negative arms of a deviation, both measured as positive
  numbers, so a negative coefficient on `dP-` means that a drier year lowers
  growth;
- stars are two-sided significance levels, \*\*\* p < 0.01, \*\* p < 0.05,
  \* p < 0.1, with errors clustered by country; "joint tests (p)" are Wald
  tests that all the terms of a variable are zero;
- where models are compared, a verdict says whether the difference can be told
  apart from noise ("indifferent" when it cannot; see "Model terms and
  effects").

"Data and methods" describes what every section shares; each later section
describes only what it changes.

# Data and methods

## Data

**GDP per capita.** Four series, all at constant prices, so their growth rates
are real growth and comparable across sources (their levels are not):

| Label | Source and series | Unit | Prices |
|---|---|---|---|
| PWT | Penn World Table 11.0, `rgdpna / pop` | country | constant national prices, at the 2021 PPP level |
| WB | World Development Indicators, `NY.GDP.PCAP.KD` (July 2025) | country | constant 2015 local prices at the 2015 exchange rate |
| WB PPP | World Development Indicators, `NY.GDP.PCAP.PP.KD` (October 2026; from 1990) | country | constant 2021 international dollars |
| DOSE | DOSE v2.14, `grp_pc_lcu2015_usd` | region (GADM level 1) | constant 2015 local prices at the 2015 exchange rate |

The outcome of every model is the growth of GDP per capita, the difference of
its logarithm between two consecutive calendar years,

```text
g(i,t) = log y(i,t) - log y(i,t-1)
```

A gap in a series gives a missing growth rate, never a change over several
years. No series is interpolated, extrapolated or converted to another price
basis. In DOSE, growth into a year that DOSE flags as a break in the region's
series is set to missing.

**Weather.** Annual temperature and precipitation from the Weighted Climate
Dataset (Gortan, Testa, Fagiolo and Lamperti 2024), which aggregates gridded
climate data to countries (GADM level 0) and regions (GADM level 1). Three
gridded datasets are used: ERA5 (reanalysis, from 1940), CRU TS (station-based,
from 1901) and University of Delaware (station-based, to 2017). The grid cells
are weighted by population density at base year 2000, so a unit's weather is
that of the places where its people live. `TM` is the annual mean temperature
(°C, the mean of the twelve monthly means) and `RR` the annual precipitation
(metres, the sum of the monthly totals).

**Panels.** A panel pairs one GDP series with one climate dataset, e.g.
"PWT x ERA5", the main panel. The national panels are PWT and WB with each of
the three climate datasets; the subnational one is DOSE x ERA5.

**Conflict.** From the UCDP/PRIO Armed Conflict Dataset v26.1: a country-year
is in conflict when the country is a location of at least one state-based
armed conflict that year. Two indicators by the highest intensity of the
year: minor conflict (25 to 999 battle-related deaths) and war (1,000 or
more). Conflicts that UCDP locates in the Soviet Union or Yugoslavia go to the
successor state on whose territory they were fought, and a few conflicts
fought on another state's territory or by a neighbouring party are added by
hand.

**Post-communist collapses.** Dummies for each year of the collapse of the
former Soviet republics (1991 to 1995, the years in which their average growth
was negative; Albania 1990 to 1992 shares the dummies of the same stage) and
of the former Yugoslav republics (1991 to 1993). Each collapse year has its own
shift, common to the countries of the group, on top of the year effects.

Other data are described where they are used: the SPEI drought index, and the
World Bank's sector value added.

**Reproducibility.** The parameters of the notebook are the first year of the
sample (`r params$start_year`), the deviation definition and the form of the
preferred model (`r params$preferred_definition` and `r params$preferred_form`;
"auto": chosen by AIC, see "Preferred deviation model") and the DOSE GDP
series. The panels are built from the raw files in `data/` by the functions in
`functions/`. The results of each chunk are cached and rebuilt when the
functions, the data or the parameters change.



## Shared specification

**The regression.** Every model regresses growth on weather terms, controls
and fixed effects:

```text
g(i,t) = weather terms(i,t)
         + c1 minor conflict(i,t) + c2 war(i,t) + collapse-year dummies(i,t)
         + unit effect(i) + unit trend(i) x t + unit quadratic trend(i) x t^2
         + year effect(t) + error(i,t)
```

The sections differ only in the weather terms (levels of `TM` and `RR` in the
BHM specification; deviations with arms in the others) and, where stated, in
the outcome or the rows.

**Fixed effects.** Year effects, unit effects and unit-specific linear and
quadratic trends in the year (t = year - 1990), as in Burke, Hsiang and Miguel
(2015). The weather effects are therefore identified from the year-to-year
variation of each unit around its own smooth trend, net of what is common to
all units in a year. In the national panels the unit is the country; in DOSE
it is the region.

**Controls.** The two conflict indicators and the collapse-year dummies of
"Data". They are national, so in DOSE they are the same for every region of a
country.

**Estimation and inference.** Ordinary least squares with the fixed effects
and trends absorbed (`fixest::feols`). Standard errors are clustered by
country, which allows any correlation between the years of a country and, in
DOSE, between its regions. Joint tests are Wald tests with that covariance.
Effects that combine several coefficients (see "Model terms and effects") have
delta-method standard errors from the same covariance and normal confidence
intervals.

**Fit.** AIC and BIC use the Gaussian likelihood and count the fixed effects
and trends as parameters. The within R2 is the share of the variance of
growth left after the fixed effects and trends that the regressors explain;
the within adjusted R2 penalizes their number. Both are small in every model:
weather and conflict explain a few percent of the variation of growth around
the units' trends.

**Growth outliers.** Abrupt swings of growth are mostly wars, oil shocks,
crises and data breaks, which add noise, but some are droughts and storms, the
response studied. The rule (`params$outlier_rule`, "reversal"):

1. the outliers are the years of a growth reversal: the change of growth from
   the year before, g(t) - g(t-1) (both years in the panel), in its 5% lowest
   or 5% highest tail in the main panel (PWT x ERA5) from the start year,
   before any exclusion. A year of low growth after one of high growth, or the
   reverse, not a year of extreme growth as such; the year flagged is t, the
   second of the pair;
2. each is annotated by hand with the likely cause of the reversal (an event of
   year t, or the end of or the rebound from that of year t-1), a category, a
   confidence level, and whether weather (drought, storm, flood, harvest) is
   part of the cause; a country-year with no strong candidate is
   "Unidentified". A country-year already annotated keeps its cause;
3. the outliers whose cause does not involve weather, the unidentified ones
   included, are dropped; the weather-related ones stay (a harvest recovery
   after a drought among them).

The alternative rule ("level", the one used until 2026-11-04) takes the 5%
lowest and the 5% highest growth rates instead. The annotations of both are in
`data/growth_outlier_causes.csv` (the growth tails of the sample from 1960),
`data/growth_outlier_causes_1970_additions.csv` (those that enter them with a
start in 1970), `data/growth_outlier_causes_wb_additions.csv` (the growth tails
of WB x ERA5, for the app) and `data/growth_outlier_causes_reversal_additions.csv`
(the reversal tails of PWT x ERA5 and WB x ERA5 not annotated before).

They are events of a country and year, so the same country-years are dropped
from every panel (in DOSE, from every region of the country). The table after
"Panels" counts them by cause; "The preferred model with and without the
growth outliers" and "Growth outliers: none, non-weather or all dropped" show
what the rule changes, and what the other rule would drop.

```{r shared-specification}
START_YEAR <- as.integer(params$start_year)
CLIMATE_WEIGHT <- "population density"
CLIMATE_WEIGHT_YEAR <- 2000L

OUTCOME <- "dlgrp_pc_usd"
# Year effects, unit effects and unit linear and quadratic trends (t = year -
# 1990, t2 = t^2), as in BHM (2015), in every model.
FIXED_EFFECTS <- "year + GID_1[t, t2]"
BHM_FIXED_EFFECTS <- FIXED_EFFECTS

# Lags of the deviations (sections on lags); the panels keep MAX_LAGS earlier
# climate years and the demeaning covers them.
N_LAGS <- 5L
N_LAGS_LONG <- 10L
MAX_LAGS <- N_LAGS_LONG

# The UCDP/PRIO conflict indicators by the highest intensity of the country's
# conflicts that year (functions/conflict.R): conflict_low, minor (25-999
# battle deaths), and conflict_high, war (1,000 or more); and the post-Soviet
# (with Albania) and post-Yugoslav collapse-year dummies
# (functions/transition_collapse.R). National, so the same for every region of
# a country in the subnational panel.
CONFLICT_TERMS <- c("conflict_low", "conflict_high")
CONTROLS <- c(
  CONFLICT_TERMS,
  "i(fsu_collapse_year, ref = 'none')",
  "i(yug_collapse_year, ref = 'none')"
)

# Growth outliers: the tails (5% each) of PWT x ERA5 from the start year (found
# in the panel-builder chunk) under OUTLIER_RULE, each with its likely cause,
# annotated by hand; every country-year of the tails must have one. Dropped:
# those whose cause does not involve weather (including those with no
# identified cause); the droughts, storms, floods and harvests among them are
# the response studied and stay. They are events of a country and year, so
# they are dropped from every panel (in DOSE, from every region of the
# country).
#   reversal  the change of growth from the year before, g(t) - g(t-1), with
#             both years in the panel; the year flagged is t (the default)
#   level     growth itself (the rule until 2026-11-04)
OUTLIER_RULES <- c(reversal = "change of growth from the year before", level = "growth")
OUTLIER_RULE <- match.arg(params$outlier_rule %||% "reversal", names(OUTLIER_RULES))
OUTLIER_SHARE <- 0.10
# The causes: the growth tails of the sample from 1960 (growth_outliers.R),
# those that enter them with a start in 1970, the growth tails of WB x ERA5
# (for the app) and the reversal tails of PWT x ERA5 and WB x ERA5 not
# annotated in the others. A cause is that of the country-year, whatever the
# rule or the source.
OUTLIER_CAUSES <- bind_rows(lapply(
  c("growth_outlier_causes.csv", "growth_outlier_causes_1970_additions.csv",
    "growth_outlier_causes_wb_additions.csv", "growth_outlier_causes_reversal_additions.csv"),
  function(f) utils::read.csv(data_file(f), stringsAsFactors = FALSE, encoding = "UTF-8")
))
stopifnot(!anyDuplicated(OUTLIER_CAUSES[, c("GID_0", "year")]))

# The rows of `d` (one panel's) in the lowest and the highest `share / 2` of
# the measure of `rule`, with their tail ("low", "high") and the cutoffs.
outlier_tails <- function(d, rule = OUTLIER_RULE, share = OUTLIER_SHARE) {
  x <- d[[OUTCOME]]
  if (rule == "reversal") {
    x <- x - d[[OUTCOME]][match(paste(d$GID_1, d$year - 1L), paste(d$GID_1, d$year))]
  }
  cutoffs <- stats::quantile(x, c(share / 2, 1 - share / 2), names = FALSE, na.rm = TRUE)
  hit <- which(x < cutoffs[[1]] | x > cutoffs[[2]])
  rows <- d[hit, ]
  rows$tail <- ifelse(x[hit] < cutoffs[[1]], "low", "high")
  list(rows = rows, cutoffs = cutoffs)
}

# Moments of the two deviation definitions: over the horizon of the panel
# (*_all, replaced below) and over the 20 years before the current one.
MOMENTS <- c(
  "mean_TM_all", "sd_TM_all", "mean_RR_all", "sd_RR_all",
  "mean_TM_lag_20", "sd_TM_lag_20", "mean_RR_lag_20", "sd_RR_lag_20"
)
# The demeaned deviations of each variable and baseline (built by prepare_panel()).
BASELINES <- c("all", "lag_20")
DEMEANED <- as.vector(outer(c("TM", "RR"), BASELINES, function(v, b) paste0("dm_", v, "_", b)))

fit_model <- function(terms, model_data, fixed_effects = FIXED_EFFECTS, outcome = OUTCOME) {
  m <- fit_panel_model(
    paste(terms, collapse = " + "),
    model_data,
    outcome = outcome,
    fixed_effects = fixed_effects,
    cluster = ~GID_0
  )
  # The country of each estimation row, for the noise tests of differences in
  # fit (see "Model terms and effects").
  m$country <- model_data$GID_0[fixest::obs(m)]
  m
}

# Labels for the coefficient tables; the collapse dummies are left out of them.
DICT <- c(
  TM = "T", TM2 = "T^2", RR = "P", RR2 = "P^2",
  conflict_low = "Conflict, minor", conflict_high = "Conflict, war",
  mean_TM_all = "mean T", mean_RR_all = "mean P", clim_TM = "mean T", clim_RR = "mean P",
  devTM = "dT", devTM_pos = "dT+", devTM_neg = "dT-",
  devTM_pos2 = "(dT+)^2", devTM_neg2 = "(dT-)^2",
  devRR = "dP", devRR_pos = "dP+", devRR_neg = "dP-",
  devRR_pos2 = "(dP+)^2", devRR_neg2 = "(dP-)^2"
)
DROP <- "collapse_year"
# Temperature terms, then precipitation terms, then the controls (original names).
ORDER <- c("%^devTM", "%^devRR", "%^conflict")
FITSTAT <- ~n + wr2 + aic + bic
```

## Panels

**Long-run climate: two baselines.** A deviation measures a year against what
is normal for the unit, and "normal" has two definitions:

- the horizon baseline: the mean and SD of the variable over the years of the
  panel, one constant pair per unit;
- the 20-year baseline: the mean and SD of the 20 years before the year, which
  move with the climate, so a year is compared with the recent past.

Both use the unit's climate series in every year, whether or not it has GDP
then; the SDs are sample SDs of the annual values, trend included (the trend
is removed afterwards, from the deviation; see below).

Each panel runs from `r params$start_year` to its last year with both growth
and climate. `build_dat()` gives each unit's climate moments over its entire
climate series; `mean_*_all` and `sd_*_all` are replaced here by the moments
over the horizon of the panel,

```text
mean_TM_all, sd_TM_all = mean and SD of TM over start year .. last year of the panel
mean_RR_all, sd_RR_all = the same for RR
```

from the climate series of every year in that horizon. The sample is the
unit-years with growth, both weather variables, the conflict indicators and the
moments of both deviation definitions (positive SDs), without the growth
outliers whose cause does not involve weather (see the shared specification).

Each deviation, from either baseline (the horizon or the trailing 20 years), is
also demeaned here: each unit's mean and its linear and quadratic trend in the
year are removed, fitted on the years from `r params$start_year` minus ten (to
cover the lags) to the last year of the panel, with no year effects:

```text
dT     = (TM - mean_TM_<baseline>) / sd_TM_<baseline>
dm_TM  = dT - (unit mean + unit linear and quadratic trend)         (the same for RR)
```

The arms of every model are cut from the demeaned deviations (see the next
section for why), in the units of the original deviation. Because the SD is
that of the raw series, a demeaned deviation of 1 is one raw SD away from the
unit's trend: with a warming trend the raw SD of temperature exceeds the SD
around the trend, so a "+3 SD" temperature year is rarer than three SDs of
detrended variability would be (for precipitation the two SDs nearly
coincide).

The first table below describes the main panel; the second counts its growth
outliers by cause and by whether they are dropped.

```{r panel-builder}
# Panel `econ` x `source` from `start_year`, with the horizon moments, the
# controls, the sample with and without the country-years `drop`, the rows
# dropped, and every unit-year of the panel (`data`, for lags of the weather).
prepare_panel <- function(econ, source, econ_variable = NULL, drop = OUTLIERS_DROPPED,
                          start_year = START_YEAR) {
  cfg <- panel_config(
    econ_year_min = start_year,
    climate_source = source,
    climate_weight = CLIMATE_WEIGHT,
    climate_weight_year = CLIMATE_WEIGHT_YEAR,
    # Eleven earlier climate years: up to ten carry the lags of the deviations
    # into the first years, one the lagged trailing moments. The sample starts
    # at start_year regardless.
    clim_history_years = 11L
  )
  data <- suppressMessages(build_dat(econ_data = econ, config = cfg,
                                     econ_variable = econ_variable))
  level <- unique(data$gadm_level)
  end_year <- max(data$year[est_row(data) & !is.na(data$TM) & !is.na(data$RR)])

  horizon <- load_climate_panel(level, cfg) %>%
    filter(gadm_level == level, year >= start_year, year <= end_year) %>%
    group_by(GID_1) %>%
    summarise(
      mean_TM_all = mean(TM, na.rm = TRUE), sd_TM_all = sd(TM, na.rm = TRUE),
      mean_RR_all = mean(RR, na.rm = TRUE), sd_RR_all = sd(RR, na.rm = TRUE),
      .groups = "drop"
    )
  data <- data %>%
    select(-c(mean_TM_all, sd_TM_all, mean_RR_all, sd_RR_all)) %>%
    left_join(horizon, by = "GID_1")
  data <- add_yugoslav_collapse(add_soviet_collapse(add_conflict(data)))
  data$TM2 <- data$TM^2
  data$RR2 <- data$RR^2
  data$t <- data$year - 1990L
  data$t2 <- data$t^2

  # Demeaned deviations: each unit's mean and quadratic trend removed.
  window <- data$year >= start_year - MAX_LAGS & data$year <= end_year
  for (v in c("TM", "RR")) for (b in BASELINES) {
    raw <- (data[[v]] - data[[paste0("mean_", v, "_", b)]]) / data[[paste0("sd_", v, "_", b)]]
    ok <- which(window & is.finite(raw))
    sub <- data.frame(GID_1 = data$GID_1[ok], t = data$t[ok], t2 = data$t2[ok], x = raw[ok])
    m <- fixest::feols(x ~ 1 | GID_1[t, t2], sub, notes = FALSE)
    demeaned <- rep(NA_real_, nrow(data))
    demeaned[ok[fixest::obs(m)]] <- stats::resid(m)
    data[[paste0("dm_", v, "_", b)]] <- demeaned
  }

  complete <- stats::complete.cases(
    as.data.frame(data)[, c(OUTCOME, "TM", "RR", CONFLICT_TERMS, MOMENTS, DEMEANED)]
  )
  positive_sd <- Reduce(`&`, lapply(grep("^sd_", MOMENTS, value = TRUE), function(x) {
    !is.na(data[[x]]) & data[[x]] > 0
  }))
  sample_all <- data[est_row(data) & data$year >= start_year & complete & positive_sd, ]
  apply_exclusions(list(
    label = paste(econ, "x", source), econ = econ, source = source, level = level,
    start_year = start_year, end_year = end_year, all = sample_all, data = data
  ), drop)
}

# The sample of panel `p` without the country-years `drop` (clean), and the
# rows dropped (outliers).
apply_exclusions <- function(p, drop) {
  dropped <- paste(p$all$GID_0, p$all$year) %in% paste(drop$GID_0, drop$year)
  p$clean <- p$all[!dropped, ]
  p$outliers <- p$all[dropped, c("GID_0", "GID_1", "year", OUTCOME)]
  p
}

# (The argument is not called `panel`: tibble() would mask it with the column.)
panel_summary <- function(p) {
  tibble::tibble(
    panel = p$label,
    first_year = min(p$clean$year), last_year = max(p$clean$year),
    countries = n_distinct(p$clean$GID_0), units = n_distinct(p$clean$GID_1),
    observations = nrow(p$all), outliers_dropped = nrow(p$outliers),
    minor_conflict = sum(p$clean$conflict_low), war = sum(p$clean$conflict_high)
  )
}

# Every panel: the national ones (PWT and World Bank with ERA5, CRU TS and
# UDelaware; PWT x ERA5 is the main one) and DOSE x ERA5.
NATIONAL <- expand.grid(source = c("ERA5", "CRU TS", "UDelaware"), econ = c("PWT", "WB"),
                        stringsAsFactors = FALSE)

# The outliers are the tails of the main panel (PWT x ERA5) from the start
# year, so it is built first, without exclusions. Every country-year of the
# tails must have an annotated cause.
main <- prepare_panel("PWT", "ERA5", drop = OUTLIER_CAUSES[0, c("GID_0", "year")])
country_year <- function(d) paste(d$GID_0, d$year)
# The annotated outliers of rule `rule` and the non-weather ones among them.
rule_outliers <- function(rule) {
  t <- outlier_tails(main$all, rule)
  missing <- setdiff(country_year(t$rows), country_year(OUTLIER_CAUSES))
  if (length(missing)) stop(rule, " outliers without an annotated cause: ", paste(missing, collapse = ", "))
  o <- OUTLIER_CAUSES[country_year(OUTLIER_CAUSES) %in% country_year(t$rows), ]
  o$tail <- t$rows$tail[match(country_year(o), country_year(t$rows))]
  list(outliers = o, dropped = o[o$weather == "no", c("GID_0", "year")], cutoffs = t$cutoffs)
}
rule_sets <- lapply(setNames(names(OUTLIER_RULES), names(OUTLIER_RULES)), rule_outliers)
OUTLIERS <- rule_sets[[OUTLIER_RULE]]$outliers
cutoffs <- rule_sets[[OUTLIER_RULE]]$cutoffs
OUTLIERS_ALL <- OUTLIERS[, c("GID_0", "year")]
OUTLIERS_DROPPED <- rule_sets[[OUTLIER_RULE]]$dropped
# The non-weather outliers of the other rule (for the comparisons of the
# outlier sections).
OTHER_OUTLIER_RULE <- setdiff(names(OUTLIER_RULES), OUTLIER_RULE)
OTHER_OUTLIERS_DROPPED <- rule_sets[[OTHER_OUTLIER_RULE]]$dropped
# The non-weather outliers annotated in the years before the start year (the
# growth tails of the sample from 1960; the reversals of the 1960s are not
# annotated): dropped from the samples that start earlier (the start-year
# comparison) and from the growth history.
EARLY_OUTLIERS_DROPPED <- OUTLIER_CAUSES[OUTLIER_CAUSES$year < START_YEAR &
                                           OUTLIER_CAUSES$weather == "no", c("GID_0", "year")]
main <- apply_exclusions(main, OUTLIERS_DROPPED)

national_panels <- lapply(seq_len(nrow(NATIONAL)), function(i) {
  if (NATIONAL$econ[i] == "PWT" && NATIONAL$source[i] == "ERA5") return(main)
  prepare_panel(NATIONAL$econ[i], NATIONAL$source[i])
})
stopifnot(national_panels[[1]]$label == "PWT x ERA5")
dose <- prepare_panel("DOSE", "ERA5", econ_variable = params$dose_variable)
all_panels <- c(national_panels, list(dose))

panel_summary(main) %>% knitr::kable(caption = "PWT x ERA5 (unit-years; conflict after outliers)")
OUTLIERS %>%
  mutate(status = ifelse(weather == "yes", "kept (weather)", "dropped")) %>%
  count(category, status, tail) %>%
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = tail, values_from = n, values_fill = 0) %>%
  arrange(status, desc(low + high)) %>%
  knitr::kable(caption = sprintf(paste(
    "Growth outliers of PWT x ERA5 from %d (%s rule: %s below %.1f or above %.1f pp) by likely",
    "cause; see data/growth_outlier_causes*.csv"),
    START_YEAR, OUTLIER_RULE, OUTLIER_RULES[[OUTLIER_RULE]], 100 * cutoffs[[1]], 100 * cutoffs[[2]]))
tibble::tibble(
  rule = names(rule_sets),
  outliers = vapply(rule_sets, function(s) nrow(s$outliers), 0L),
  dropped = vapply(rule_sets, function(s) nrow(s$dropped), 0L),
  dropped_by_both = sum(country_year(rule_sets$reversal$dropped) %in% country_year(rule_sets$level$dropped))
) %>%
  knitr::kable(caption = paste("Growth outliers of PWT x ERA5 by rule (the", OUTLIER_RULE,
                               "rule is the notebook's): all, non-weather (dropped), and dropped by both"))
```

## Model terms and effects

The deviation forms, the effects of a deviation at given long-run climates and
the lags, used by every section below.

**From weather to regressors.** For temperature (the same for precipitation):

```text
deviation   dT(i,t) = (TM(i,t) - mean) / SD          mean, SD: the horizon or the 20-year baseline
demeaned    dm(i,t) = dT(i,t) - [unit mean + unit linear and quadratic trend of dT]
arms        dT+ = max(dm, 0)     dT- = max(-dm, 0)    both non-negative
```

**Forms.** A deviation enters the regression in one of three forms, always
with an interaction with the unit's long-run climate `clim_TM` (its mean
temperature; `clim_RR` for precipitation), so that the same anomaly can matter
differently in a cold and in a hot place:

```text
signed          a dm  + b dm x clim_TM                                    one slope: a warm year is the opposite of a cold one
linear arms     a+ dT+ + a- dT- + (b+ dT+ + b- dT-) x clim_TM             separate slopes for warm and cold years
quadratic arms  a+ (dT+)^2 + a- (dT-)^2 + [b+ (dT+)^2 + b- (dT-)^2] x clim_TM   separate, and growing with the size of the anomaly
```

With arms, warm and cold (wet and dry) years can both lower growth; a single
signed slope would average the two out. Temperature and precipitation can
take different forms (e.g. quadratic arms for temperature, linear for
precipitation), which gives five forms in all with the signed one.

**Effects.** The effect on growth of a year with deviation d, in a unit with
long-run climate m, against a year at the unit's trend (d = 0):

```text
effect(d, m) = (a+ + b+ m) h(max(d, 0)) + (a- + b- m) h(max(-d, 0))      h(x) = x (linear arms) or x^2 (quadratic arms)
```

It is reported for d = +3 and -3 SD at m = 5, 15 and 25 °C for temperature
and m = 0.5, 1.5 and 3 m a year for precipitation, in pp of growth. A +3 SD
effect uses only the positive arm and a -3 SD effect only the negative one. It
is a linear combination of the coefficients, so its standard error follows
exactly from their clustered covariance (delta method), and its confidence
interval and stars use the normal distribution. An effect at a long-run
climate outside the range of a panel's units is an extrapolation of the linear
interaction; the tables of "Robustness across national and climate datasets"
give that range.

**Lags.** Where lags are used, the deviations of the k-th year before enter
with the same forms; the cumulative effect through year K is the sum of the
effects on growth in years 0 to K, i.e. the effect on the level of GDP per
capita K years later (see "Lags of the deviations").

**Comparing models: differences against noise.** Wherever models are compared
by AIC, BIC or the within adjusted R2, the tables also give a verdict for each
criterion: better, worse, or **indifferent** when the difference cannot be
told apart from sampling noise. A difference of a few AIC points between
models with thousands of rows is a tiny share of the variance, and with
countries' years correlated it is often within the noise. The test, at the 5%
level:

```text
non-nested models   z = [criterion(A) - criterion(B)] / SE[ sum over observations of logL_A(i,t) - logL_B(i,t) ]
                    criterion in log-likelihood units: -AIC/2, -BIC/2, or -(n/2) log(1 - within adjusted R2)
                    SE from the countries' sums of the observation-level differences (Vuong test, clustered)
                    |z| < 1.96: indifferent; otherwise A is better (z > 0) or worse (z < 0)
nested models       the clustered Wald test of the terms the larger model adds, or of the restrictions
                    p >= 0.05: indifferent; otherwise the criterion's own sign says better or worse
```

The verdicts are written "AIC / BIC / R2". With the same number of parameters
the three criteria give the same verdict. For nested models "better" or
"worse" means that the difference is real; its direction is the criterion's,
so AIC or BIC can prefer the smaller model even when the terms it leaves out
are significant (their penalty for the extra parameters outweighs the gain in
fit). Against the best of a set of models the Vuong test is used throughout.

```{r model-helpers}
# Deviation terms of the demeaned deviations dm_<v>_<suffix>, with one suffix
# per variable (a definition, see DEFINITIONS), and the long-run climate they
# are interacted with, clim_<v> = mean_<v>_<suffix[["clim_<v>"]]>. The same
# column names under any definition, so the tables line up.
add_deviation_terms <- function(model_data, suffix) {
  for (v in c("TM", "RR")) {
    dev <- model_data[[paste0("dm_", v, "_", suffix[[v]])]]
    model_data[[paste0("dev", v)]] <- dev
    model_data[[paste0("dev", v, "_pos")]] <- pmax(dev, 0)
    model_data[[paste0("dev", v, "_neg")]] <- pmax(-dev, 0)
    model_data[[paste0("dev", v, "_pos2")]] <- pmax(dev, 0)^2
    model_data[[paste0("dev", v, "_neg2")]] <- pmax(-dev, 0)^2
    clim <- paste0("clim_", v)
    model_data[[clim]] <- model_data[[paste0("mean_", v, "_", suffix[[clim]])]]
  }
  model_data
}
# The same terms from the raw deviations (not demeaned), for the comparison.
raw_deviation_terms <- function(model_data, suffix) {
  for (v in c("TM", "RR")) {
    model_data[[paste0("dm_", v, "_", suffix[[v]])]] <-
      (model_data[[v]] - model_data[[paste0("mean_", v, "_", suffix[[v]])]]) /
      model_data[[paste0("sd_", v, "_", suffix[[v]])]]
  }
  add_deviation_terms(model_data, suffix)
}

# Each definition: the baseline of each variable's deviation (TM, RR: "all",
# the horizon, or "lag_20", the 20 years before) and the long-run climate it is
# interacted with (clim_TM, clim_RR): the horizon mean, or with a matched
# interaction the mean of the deviation's own baseline (for a 20-year deviation,
# the mean of the 20 years before; for a horizon deviation, the horizon mean).
definition <- function(TM, RR, matched = FALSE) {
  c(TM = TM, RR = RR, clim_TM = if (matched) TM else "all", clim_RR = if (matched) RR else "all")
}
DEFINITIONS <- list(
  "Horizon" = definition("all", "all"),
  "20-year" = definition("lag_20", "lag_20"),
  "T horizon, P 20-year" = definition("all", "lag_20"),
  "T 20-year, P horizon" = definition("lag_20", "all"),
  # With horizon deviations only, the matched interaction is the horizon one.
  "20-year, matched interaction" = definition("lag_20", "lag_20", matched = TRUE),
  "T horizon, P 20-year, matched interaction" = definition("all", "lag_20", matched = TRUE),
  "T 20-year, P horizon, matched interaction" = definition("lag_20", "all", matched = TRUE)
)
# Each form: the deviation terms of each variable, by column suffix.
SIGNED <- ""
LINEAR <- c("_pos", "_neg")
QUADRATIC <- c("_pos2", "_neg2")
FORMS <- list(
  "Signed" = list(TM = SIGNED, RR = SIGNED),
  "Linear arms" = list(TM = LINEAR, RR = LINEAR),
  "Quadratic arms" = list(TM = QUADRATIC, RR = QUADRATIC),
  "T linear, P quadratic arms" = list(TM = LINEAR, RR = QUADRATIC),
  "T quadratic, P linear arms" = list(TM = QUADRATIC, RR = LINEAR)
)
ARMS <- setdiff(names(FORMS), "Signed")

form_terms <- function(form) {
  terms <- unlist(lapply(c("TM", "RR"), function(v) {
    x <- paste0("dev", v, form[[v]])
    c(x, paste0(x, ":clim_", v))
  }))
  c(terms, CONTROLS)
}

# Value of a deviation term (by column suffix) at deviations x.
term_value <- function(suffix, x) {
  if (suffix == "") return(x)
  switch(suffix, "_pos" = pmax(x, 0), "_neg" = pmax(-x, 0),
         "_pos2" = pmax(x, 0)^2, "_neg2" = pmax(-x, 0)^2)
}
interaction_name <- function(a, b, terms) {
  intersect(c(paste0(a, ":", b), paste0(b, ":", a)), terms)[[1]]
}
wald_p <- function(m, pattern) fixest::wald(m, keep = pattern, print = FALSE)$p
stars <- function(p) ifelse(p < 0.01, "***", ifelse(p < 0.05, "**", ifelse(p < 0.1, "*", "")))

# Differences in fit against noise --------------------------------------------------
# Every comparison of models by AIC, BIC or the within adjusted R2 also says
# whether the difference can be told apart from sampling noise; when it cannot,
# the verdict is "indifferent" rather than a winner. At the 5% level:
# - non-nested models on the same rows: a Vuong test clustered by country,
#   z = (the criterion's difference in log-likelihood units: half the AIC or
#   BIC difference, or n/2 times the log-ratio of 1 - within adjusted R2) / the
#   standard error of the difference in log-likelihood, from the countries'
#   sums of its observation-level terms (Gaussian, the variance at its estimate);
# - nested models: the clustered Wald test of the terms the larger model adds
#   (or of the restrictions); when it rejects, the criterion says which is
#   better.
# Against the best of a set the Vuong test is used throughout (where the best
# nests another model it is conservative: it says "indifferent" more often).
# With the same number of parameters the three criteria give the same verdict.
NOISE_LEVEL <- 0.05
CRITERIA <- c(aic = "AIC", bic = "BIC", r2 = "within adj. R2")

# What a model contributes to the noise tests: its criteria, the Gaussian
# log-likelihood of each observation (they sum to its log-likelihood), and the
# country of each observation (recorded by fit_model()).
fit_record <- function(m) {
  e <- stats::resid(m)
  s2 <- mean(e^2)
  list(aic = stats::AIC(m), bic = stats::BIC(m), war2 = fixest::fitstat(m, "war2")[[1]],
       n = stats::nobs(m), ll = -0.5 * log(2 * pi * s2) - e^2 / (2 * s2), country = m$country)
}
as_record <- function(x) if (inherits(x, "fixest")) fit_record(x) else x
# The criterion in log-likelihood units (higher: better).
criterion_value <- function(rec, criterion) {
  switch(criterion, aic = -rec$aic / 2, bic = -rec$bic / 2, r2 = -(rec$n / 2) * log(1 - rec$war2))
}
# Model a against model b (records or models on the same rows) by `criterion`:
# "better", "worse", or "indifferent" when the difference cannot be told apart
# from noise; `nested_p`: for nested models, the Wald test (p) of the terms the
# larger one adds.
fit_verdict <- function(a, b, criterion, nested_p = NULL) {
  a <- as_record(a)
  b <- as_record(b)
  stopifnot(a$n == b$n, identical(a$country, b$country))
  difference <- criterion_value(a, criterion) - criterion_value(b, criterion)
  beyond_noise <- if (!is.null(nested_p)) {
    !is.na(nested_p) && nested_p < NOISE_LEVEL
  } else {
    D <- tapply(a$ll - b$ll, a$country, sum)
    G <- length(D)
    se <- sqrt(G / (G - 1) * sum((D - mean(D))^2))
    is.finite(se) && se > 0 && abs(difference / se) >= stats::qnorm(1 - NOISE_LEVEL / 2)
  }
  if (!beyond_noise) "indifferent" else if (difference > 0) "better" else "worse"
}
# The verdicts of a against b by the three criteria, "AIC / BIC / R2".
fit_verdicts <- function(a, b, nested_p = NULL) {
  a <- as_record(a)
  b <- as_record(b)
  paste(vapply(names(CRITERIA), function(cr) fit_verdict(a, b, cr, nested_p), ""),
        collapse = " / ")
}
# Each model of a set (records or models on the same rows) against the best of
# the set by `criterion`: "best", "indifferent" or "worse".
verdicts_vs_best <- function(records, criterion) {
  records <- lapply(records, as_record)
  value <- vapply(records, criterion_value, 0, criterion)
  best <- which.max(value)
  vapply(seq_along(records), function(i) {
    if (i == best) "best" else fit_verdict(records[[i]], records[[best]], criterion)
  }, "")
}
# For nested models: the clustered Wald test (p) of the coefficients that the
# larger model adds to the smaller one.
added_terms_p <- function(larger, smaller) {
  added <- setdiff(names(stats::coef(larger)), names(stats::coef(smaller)))
  stopifnot(length(added) > 0, all(names(stats::coef(smaller)) %in% names(stats::coef(larger))))
  b <- stats::coef(larger)[added]
  V <- stats::vcov(larger)[added, added, drop = FALSE]
  stats::pchisq(as.numeric(t(b) %*% solve(V, b)), df = length(added), lower.tail = FALSE)
}
# The three verdicts of each model of a set against the best, "AIC / BIC / R2".
set_verdicts <- function(records) {
  verdicts <- lapply(names(CRITERIA), function(cr) verdicts_vs_best(records, cr))
  do.call(paste, c(verdicts, sep = " / "))
}
VERDICT_NOTE <- paste(
  "verdict by AIC / BIC / within adjusted R2: indifferent when the difference cannot be told",
  "apart from noise (clustered Vuong test, or the Wald test of the added terms for nested",
  "models, 5%)")

# Fit of each model (all on the same rows) and the joint Wald tests of each
# variable's terms; `record`: for the noise tests.
fit_summary <- function(models) {
  tibble::tibble(
    form = names(models),
    observations = vapply(models, stats::nobs, 0),
    within_r2 = vapply(models, function(m) fixest::fitstat(m, "wr2")[[1]], 0),
    within_adj_r2 = vapply(models, function(m) fixest::fitstat(m, "war2")[[1]], 0),
    aic = vapply(models, stats::AIC, 0),
    bic = vapply(models, stats::BIC, 0),
    temperature_p = vapply(models, function(m) wald_p(m, "^devTM"), 0),
    precipitation_p = vapply(models, function(m) wald_p(m, "^devRR"), 0),
    record = lapply(models, fit_record)
  )
}

# Deviations (SD) and long-run climates (C, m a year) at which the effects are
# evaluated.
EFFECT_AT <- c(-3, 3)
EVAL_CLIMATE <- list(TM = c(5, 15, 25), RR = c(0.5, 1.5, 3))
EVAL_LABELS <- list(TM = c("5 °C", "15 °C", "25 °C"), RR = c("0.5 m", "1.5 m", "3 m"))

# Effect of a deviation of EFFECT_AT SD of each variable at each long-run
# climate of EVAL_CLIMATE in the model fit$preferred of `form`, with
# delta-method CIs (clustered by country).
climate_effects <- function(fit, form = PREFERRED_FORM) {
  model <- fit$preferred
  terms <- names(stats::coef(model))
  bind_rows(lapply(c("TM", "RR"), function(v) {
    m <- EVAL_CLIMATE[[v]]
    grid <- expand.grid(level = seq_along(m), deviation = EFFECT_AT)
    G <- t(mapply(function(g, x) {
      w <- stats::setNames(numeric(length(terms)), terms)
      for (s in FORMS[[form]][[v]]) {
        term <- paste0("dev", v, s)
        w[[term]] <- term_value(s, x)
        w[[interaction_name(term, paste0("clim_", v), terms)]] <- term_value(s, x) * m[[g]]
      }
      w
    }, grid$level, grid$deviation))
    colnames(G) <- terms
    linear_combination(model, G) %>%
      mutate(panel = fit$panel$label, variable = v, level_index = grid$level,
             level = factor(EVAL_LABELS[[v]][grid$level], levels = EVAL_LABELS[[v]]),
             climate = m[grid$level], deviation = grid$deviation,
             p_value = 2 * stats::pnorm(-abs(estimate / std_error)), .before = 1)
  }))
}

# One row per panel: each effect with its significance.
significance_map <- function(effects) {
  effects %>%
    mutate(cell = sprintf("%+.2f%s", 100 * estimate, stars(p_value)),
           column = sprintf("%s %+d SD, %s", ifelse(variable == "TM", "T", "P"),
                            deviation, level)) %>%
    select(panel, column, cell) %>%
    tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = column, values_from = cell)
}

# Lags ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
lag_suffix <- function(k) if (k == 0) "" else paste0("_l", k)

# Columns of the deviation terms of variable v in `form`.
form_columns <- function(v, form = PREFERRED_FORM) paste0("dev", v, FORMS[[form]][[v]])

# Unrestricted: the deviation terms of variable v at lag k, with their
# interactions.
lag_terms <- function(v, k, form = PREFERRED_FORM) {
  x <- paste0(form_columns(v, form), lag_suffix(k))
  c(x, paste0(x, ":clim_", v))
}
# Common interaction: the terms of variable v at lags 0..n_lags (without their
# interactions), and each arm's sum over lags 0..n_lags interacted with the
# long-run climate.
restricted_terms <- function(v, n_lags = N_LAGS, form = PREFERRED_FORM) {
  cols <- form_columns(v, form)
  c(cols, unlist(lapply(seq_len(n_lags), function(k) paste0(cols, lag_suffix(k)))),
    paste0(cols, "_sum:clim_", v))
}

# The rows of fit$data with the deviation terms of the previous n_lags calendar
# years (from every unit-year of the panel, by `deviations`), on the unit-years
# with all of them, and each arm's sum over lags 0..n_lags.
add_deviation_lags <- function(fit, n_lags = N_LAGS, suffix = PREFERRED_SUFFIX,
                               form = PREFERRED_FORM, deviations = add_deviation_terms) {
  full <- deviations(fit$panel$data, suffix)
  cols <- c(form_columns("TM", form), form_columns("RR", form))
  out <- fit$data
  for (k in seq_len(n_lags)) {
    lagged <- as.data.frame(full)[, c("GID_1", "year", cols)]
    lagged$year <- lagged$year + k
    names(lagged)[-(1:2)] <- paste0(cols, lag_suffix(k))
    out <- left_join(out, lagged, by = c("GID_1", "year"))
  }
  lag_cols <- unlist(lapply(seq_len(n_lags), function(k) paste0(cols, lag_suffix(k))))
  # Finite, not only present: a zero trailing SD gives an infinite deviation.
  out <- out[Reduce(`&`, lapply(lag_cols, function(x) is.finite(out[[x]]))), ]
  for (col in cols) {
    out[[paste0(col, "_sum")]] <- Reduce(`+`, lapply(0:n_lags, function(k) {
      out[[paste0(col, lag_suffix(k))]]
    }))
  }
  out
}

# Cumulative effect through year `through` of a deviation of EFFECT_AT SD in
# year 0, at each long-run climate of EVAL_CLIMATE. With the common interaction
# (`restricted`), the deviation enters the summed interaction in each of the
# years 0..through.
cumulative_effects <- function(model, label, restricted = FALSE, n_lags = N_LAGS,
                               form = PREFERRED_FORM) {
  terms <- names(stats::coef(model))
  bind_rows(lapply(c("TM", "RR"), function(v) {
    m <- EVAL_CLIMATE[[v]]
    climate <- paste0("clim_", v)
    grid <- expand.grid(level = seq_along(m), deviation = EFFECT_AT, through = 0:n_lags)
    G <- t(mapply(function(g, x, through) {
      w <- stats::setNames(numeric(length(terms)), terms)
      for (s in FORMS[[form]][[v]]) {
        value <- term_value(s, x)
        col <- paste0("dev", v, s)
        for (k in 0:through) w[[paste0(col, lag_suffix(k))]] <- value
        if (restricted) {
          w[[interaction_name(paste0(col, "_sum"), climate, terms)]] <- (through + 1) * value * m[[g]]
        } else {
          for (k in 0:through) {
            w[[interaction_name(paste0(col, lag_suffix(k)), climate, terms)]] <- value * m[[g]]
          }
        }
      }
      w
    }, grid$level, grid$deviation, grid$through))
    colnames(G) <- terms
    linear_combination(model, G) %>%
      mutate(panel = label, variable = v, level_index = grid$level,
             level = factor(EVAL_LABELS[[v]][grid$level], levels = EVAL_LABELS[[v]]),
             climate = m[grid$level], deviation = grid$deviation, through = grid$through,
             p_value = 2 * stats::pnorm(-abs(estimate / std_error)), .before = 1)
  }))
}
```

# Deviations demeaned before the arms

With warming, a deviation from a fixed mean is mostly negative early in the
sample and positive late (from the trailing 20-year mean too, more mildly).
The arms are cut at zero before the fixed effects act, so which arm a year
enters would be decided largely by its date: the warm arm estimated on the late
years and the cold arm on the early ones. The fixed effects of the regression
remove additive terms, not the kink. The demeaned deviations (see "Panels")
cut the arms at each unit's own mean and trend, so a year is warm or cold for
its time; a globally hot year stays hot (no year effects in the demeaning).

The comparison below, raw against demeaned, uses the arms model with the lowest
AIC among those of the demeaned deviations (the preferred model of the later
sections, unless the `preferred_definition` and `preferred_form` parameters
set it). Every later section uses the demeaned deviations.

The tables, in order:

1. the share of positive deviations by decade, raw and demeaned: the raw
   share follows the warming, and the demeaning is meant to keep it near one
   half in every decade;
2. the SD of the demeaned deviations, in units of the original SD (below one
   where the trend was a large part of the raw variation);
3. every definition and form, on the same rows, with raw and with demeaned
   deviations: AIC relative to the best of all, the verdict against that best,
   and the joint tests of each variable;
4. the reference model on every panel, raw against demeaned: the joint tests,
   the AIC difference and its verdict;
5. the effects of a +/-3 SD year under both.

```{r demeaning-comparison}
DEVIATION_VERSIONS <- list(raw = raw_deviation_terms, demeaned = add_deviation_terms)

# Every definition and form on PWT x ERA5, raw and demeaned (same rows).
comparison <- bind_rows(lapply(names(DEVIATION_VERSIONS), function(version) {
  bind_rows(lapply(names(DEFINITIONS), function(def) {
    d <- DEVIATION_VERSIONS[[version]](main$clean, DEFINITIONS[[def]])
    fit_summary(lapply(FORMS, function(f) fit_model(form_terms(f), d))) %>%
      mutate(definition = def, version = version, .before = 1)
  }))
}))
stopifnot(length(unique(comparison$observations)) == 1)

# The reference: the lowest-AIC arms model of the demeaned deviations.
best_demeaned <- comparison %>%
  filter(version == "demeaned", form %in% ARMS) %>%
  slice_min(aic, n = 1)
REFERENCE_DEFINITION <- if (params$preferred_definition == "auto") {
  best_demeaned$definition
} else {
  params$preferred_definition
}
REFERENCE_FORM <- if (params$preferred_form == "auto") best_demeaned$form else params$preferred_form
REFERENCE_SUFFIX <- DEFINITIONS[[REFERENCE_DEFINITION]]

# 1. Positive deviations by decade, raw and demeaned (PWT x ERA5).
bind_rows(lapply(c("Horizon", "20-year"), function(def) {
  bind_rows(lapply(names(DEVIATION_VERSIONS), function(version) {
    DEVIATION_VERSIONS[[version]](main$clean, DEFINITIONS[[def]]) %>%
      mutate(decade = 10 * (year %/% 10)) %>%
      group_by(decade) %>%
      summarise(T_positive = mean(devTM > 0), P_positive = mean(devRR > 0), .groups = "drop") %>%
      mutate(column = paste(def, version))
  }))
})) %>%
  mutate(across(ends_with("_positive"), ~ round(.x, 2))) %>%
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = column, values_from = c(T_positive, P_positive)) %>%
  knitr::kable(caption = "PWT x ERA5: share of positive deviations by decade, raw and demeaned")

bind_rows(lapply(c("Horizon", "20-year"), function(def) {
  d <- add_deviation_terms(main$clean, DEFINITIONS[[def]])
  tibble::tibble(definition = def, sd_T_demeaned = sd(d$devTM), sd_P_demeaned = sd(d$devRR))
})) %>%
  mutate(across(where(is.double), ~ round(.x, 2))) %>%
  knitr::kable(caption = "SD of the demeaned deviations (units of the original SD)")

# 2. Every definition and form on PWT x ERA5, raw and demeaned.
comparison %>%
  mutate(aic = aic - min(aic), verdict = set_verdicts(record)) %>%
  select(version, definition, form, aic, verdict, temperature_p, precipitation_p) %>%
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = version,
                     values_from = c(aic, verdict, temperature_p, precipitation_p)) %>%
  mutate(across(starts_with("aic_"), ~ round(.x, 1)),
         across(contains("_p_"), ~ signif(.x, 2))) %>%
  knitr::kable(caption = paste("PWT x ERA5: AIC (relative to the best of all) and joint tests of",
                               "each definition and form, raw and demeaned deviations; reference",
                               "model:", REFERENCE_FORM, "with", REFERENCE_DEFINITION,
                               "deviations;", VERDICT_NOTE, "against the best of all"))

# 3. The reference model on every panel, raw and demeaned (same rows).
reference_fit <- function(panel, version) {
  d <- DEVIATION_VERSIONS[[version]](panel$clean, REFERENCE_SUFFIX)
  list(panel = modifyList(panel, list(label = paste(panel$label, "|", version))),
       data = d, preferred = fit_model(form_terms(FORMS[[REFERENCE_FORM]]), d),
       source_panel = panel$label, version = version)
}
reference_fits <- unlist(lapply(all_panels, function(p) {
  lapply(names(DEVIATION_VERSIONS), function(version) reference_fit(p, version))
}), recursive = FALSE)

raw_fit <- function(f) {
  Filter(function(x) x$source_panel == f$source_panel && x$version == "raw", reference_fits)[[1]]
}
bind_rows(lapply(reference_fits, function(f) {
  tibble::tibble(panel = f$source_panel, version = f$version,
                 rows = stats::nobs(f$preferred), aic = stats::AIC(f$preferred),
                 temperature_p = wald_p(f$preferred, "^devTM"),
                 precipitation_p = wald_p(f$preferred, "^devRR"),
                 verdict_vs_raw = if (f$version == "raw") "" else {
                   fit_verdicts(f$preferred, raw_fit(f)$preferred)
                 })
})) %>%
  group_by(panel) %>%
  mutate(aic_vs_raw = aic - aic[version == "raw"]) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  select(-aic) %>%
  relocate(verdict_vs_raw, .after = aic_vs_raw) %>%
  mutate(aic_vs_raw = round(aic_vs_raw, 1),
         across(ends_with("_p"), ~ format.pval(signif(.x, 2), eps = 0.001))) %>%
  knitr::kable(caption = paste("Reference model, raw and demeaned deviations (same rows): joint",
                               "tests (p), AIC difference, and the demeaned model's",
                               VERDICT_NOTE, "against the raw one"))

significance_map(bind_rows(lapply(reference_fits, climate_effects, form = REFERENCE_FORM))) %>%
  knitr::kable(caption = paste("Reference model: effect of a +/-3 SD deviation in the year (pp),",
                               "raw and demeaned deviations; *** p < 0.01, ** p < 0.05, * p < 0.1"))

# Tails in the year and over five years (unrestricted lags), raw and demeaned.
COMPARISON_CELLS <- tibble::tribble(
  ~cell, ~variable, ~deviation, ~level_index,
  "T +3 SD, 25 °C", "TM", 3, 3L,
  "T -3 SD, 25 °C", "TM", -3, 3L,
  "T -3 SD, 5 °C", "TM", -3, 1L,
  "P -3 SD, 0.5 m", "RR", -3, 1L,
  "P -3 SD, 1.5 m", "RR", -3, 2L
)
reference_tails <- function(f) {
  d5 <- add_deviation_lags(f, N_LAGS, REFERENCE_SUFFIX, REFERENCE_FORM,
                           DEVIATION_VERSIONS[[f$version]])
  lags <- unlist(lapply(seq_len(N_LAGS), function(k) {
    c(lag_terms("TM", k, REFERENCE_FORM), lag_terms("RR", k, REFERENCE_FORM))
  }))
  m5 <- fit_model(c(form_terms(FORMS[[REFERENCE_FORM]]), lags), d5)
  bind_rows(
    mutate(climate_effects(f, REFERENCE_FORM), horizon = "year"),
    mutate(filter(cumulative_effects(m5, f$panel$label, FALSE, N_LAGS, REFERENCE_FORM),
                  through == N_LAGS), horizon = "5 years")
  ) %>%
    inner_join(COMPARISON_CELLS, by = c("variable", "deviation", "level_index")) %>%
    transmute(panel = f$source_panel, version = f$version, column = paste0(cell, ": ", horizon),
              value = sprintf("%+.2f%s", 100 * estimate, stars(p_value))) %>%
    tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = column, values_from = value)
}
bind_rows(lapply(reference_fits, reference_tails)) %>%
  knitr::kable(caption = paste("Reference model: hot, cold and dry tails, raw and demeaned (pp of",
                               "GDP per capita), in the year and cumulative over five years",
                               "(unrestricted lags); *** p < 0.01, ** p < 0.05, * p < 0.1"))
```

What the demeaning removes, for two countries: the raw temperature deviation,
the demeaned one, and their difference (the country's mean and quadratic trend
of the raw deviation), from either baseline.

```{r demeaning-example, fig.width=13, fig.height=7}
EXAMPLE_COUNTRIES <- c("USA", "IND")
BASELINE_LABELS <- c(all = "Horizon mean and SD", lag_20 = "Trailing 20-year mean and SD")
SERIES <- c("Raw deviation", "Demeaned deviation", "Removed: mean and quadratic trend")
example <- main$data %>%
  filter(GID_0 %in% EXAMPLE_COUNTRIES, year >= START_YEAR - MAX_LAGS, year <= main$end_year)
bind_rows(lapply(BASELINES, function(b) {
  raw <- (example$TM - example[[paste0("mean_TM_", b)]]) / example[[paste0("sd_TM_", b)]]
  demeaned <- example[[paste0("dm_TM_", b)]]
  tibble::tibble(country = example$GID_0, year = example$year, baseline = b,
                 raw = raw, demeaned = demeaned, removed = raw - demeaned)
})) %>%
  filter(!is.na(demeaned)) %>%
  tidyr::pivot_longer(c(raw, demeaned, removed), names_to = "series", values_to = "value") %>%
  mutate(
    series = factor(SERIES[match(series, c("raw", "demeaned", "removed"))], levels = SERIES),
    baseline = factor(BASELINE_LABELS[baseline], levels = BASELINE_LABELS),
    country = countrycode::countrycode(country, "iso3c", "country.name")
  ) %>%
  ggplot(aes(year, value, colour = series, linetype = series, linewidth = series)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, colour = GRID_MUTED, linewidth = 0.3) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = START_YEAR - 0.5, colour = GRID_MUTED, linewidth = 0.3,
             linetype = "dotted") +
  geom_line() +
  facet_grid(country ~ baseline) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = stats::setNames(c(GRID_PALETTE[[1]], GRID_PALETTE[[2]], GRID_INK),
                                               SERIES), name = NULL) +
  scale_linetype_manual(values = stats::setNames(c("solid", "solid", "22"), SERIES), name = NULL) +
  scale_linewidth_manual(values = stats::setNames(c(0.5, 0.7, 0.9), SERIES), name = NULL) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Temperature deviation (SDs of the baseline)",
       title = "Temperature deviations before and after demeaning: United States and India",
       subtitle = paste0(main$label, "; the trend is fitted on ", START_YEAR - MAX_LAGS, "-",
                         main$end_year, " (dotted line: start of the estimation sample, ",
                         START_YEAR, "). The 20-year deviation starts when 20 earlier ",
                         "years of climate exist.")) +
  theme_results()
```

# Standard BHM: controls and outliers

The BHM specification in levels, with country fixed effects and country
quadratic trends:

```text
growth = b1 TM + b2 TM^2 + b3 RR + b4 RR^2 [+ controls] + year + country + country quadratic trend
```

with the two conflict indicators alone, then with the collapse dummies too,
without the outliers, and with both.

This is the benchmark the deviation models are compared with. Temperature and
precipitation enter in levels (°C and metres) with their squares, so the
effect of one more degree depends on how warm the year already is:

```text
marginal effect of temperature = b1 + 2 b2 TM       zero at the turning point TM* = -b1 / (2 b2)
```

With a negative `b2`, growth is highest at the turning point and falls on
either side of it (the same for precipitation). The model is estimated on
`r main$label`, in five columns: without controls, with the conflict
indicators, with the collapse dummies too (all three on every country-year,
outliers included), then on the main sample (the non-weather outliers dropped)
without and with the controls. The second table gives the turning points and
the joint Wald tests of the two terms of each variable: a variable "matters"
when its two terms are jointly different from zero.

```{r bhm}
bhm_terms <- c("TM", "TM2", "RR", "RR2")
BHM_COLUMNS <- c("Baseline", "Conflict", "Conflict + collapse", "Outliers dropped",
                 "Controls, outliers dropped")
m_bhm <- list(
  fit_model(bhm_terms, main$all, BHM_FIXED_EFFECTS),
  fit_model(c(bhm_terms, CONFLICT_TERMS), main$all, BHM_FIXED_EFFECTS),
  fit_model(c(bhm_terms, CONTROLS), main$all, BHM_FIXED_EFFECTS),
  fit_model(bhm_terms, main$clean, BHM_FIXED_EFFECTS),
  fit_model(c(bhm_terms, CONTROLS), main$clean, BHM_FIXED_EFFECTS)
)

etable(
  m_bhm,
  headers = BHM_COLUMNS,
  dict = DICT,
  drop = DROP,
  extralines = list(
    "Collapse dummies" = c("No", "No", "Yes", "No", "Yes"),
    "Outliers dropped" = c("No", "No", "No", "Yes", "Yes")
  ),
  fitstat = FITSTAT
)

# The temperature (precipitation) at which its marginal effect is zero,
# -b1 / (2 b2), and the joint Wald tests of each variable's two terms.
tibble::tibble(
  model = BHM_COLUMNS,
  turning_point_T = vapply(m_bhm, function(m) -coef(m)[["TM"]] / (2 * coef(m)[["TM2"]]), 0),
  temperature_p = vapply(m_bhm, function(m) {
    fixest::wald(m, keep = "^TM2?$", print = FALSE)$p
  }, 0),
  turning_point_P = vapply(m_bhm, function(m) -coef(m)[["RR"]] / (2 * coef(m)[["RR2"]]), 0),
  precipitation_p = vapply(m_bhm, function(m) {
    fixest::wald(m, keep = "^RR2?$", print = FALSE)$p
  }, 0)
) %>%
  mutate(across(starts_with("turning"), ~ round(.x, 2)),
         across(ends_with("_p"), ~ signif(.x, 2))) %>%
  knitr::kable(caption = "Turning points (C, m) and joint tests of each variable")
```

# Preferred deviation model (PWT x ERA5)

Each variable's deviation from its long-run climate, in SDs, from either of

```text
horizon:  dT = (TM - mean_TM_all) / sd_TM_all            (start year .. last year)
20-year:  dT = (TM - mean_TM_lag_20) / sd_TM_lag_20      (the 20 years before)
```

each demeaned (the unit's mean and quadratic trend removed, see "Panels"), in
four combinations (the same for precipitation, dP), and three forms of each
variable's deviation, each interacted with its long-run climate `clim_TM`:

```text
dT+ = max(dT, 0)    dT- = max(-dT, 0)

signed          a dT  + b dT x clim_TM
linear arms     a+ dT+ + a- dT- + (b+ dT+ + b- dT-) x clim_TM
quadratic arms  a+ (dT+)^2 + a- (dT-)^2 + (b+ (dT+)^2 + b- (dT-)^2) x clim_TM
```

The long-run climate is the horizon mean (`clim_TM = mean_TM_all`) or, with a
matched interaction, the mean of the deviation's own baseline: for a 20-year
deviation the mean of the 20 years before (`clim_TM = mean_TM_lag_20`, which
moves with the year), for a horizon deviation the horizon mean. With horizon
deviations of both variables the two coincide, so there are seven definitions:
the four combinations with the horizon mean, and the three that contain a
20-year deviation with the matched interaction.

(and the same in dP), with the same form for both variables, or linear arms for
one and quadratic arms for the other:

```text
growth = temperature terms + precipitation terms + controls + FE
```

All on the same rows (controls included, outliers dropped). The preferred
model is the arms model (linear, quadratic or mixed arms) with the lowest AIC,
unless the `preferred_definition` and `preferred_form` parameters set it. The
verdicts say which other models cannot be told apart from the best by each
criterion.

That is seven definitions times five forms, 35 models on the same
country-years of `r main$label`. The selection table gives, for each: the
within R2 and within adjusted R2; AIC and BIC, and their distance from the
best of the 35; the verdict against that best by each criterion; and the joint
Wald tests of all the temperature terms and of all the precipitation terms
(deviations and interactions together). The four arms forms have the same
number of weather coefficients (eight), so among them AIC, BIC and the within
adjusted R2 rank alike; the signed form has four, so the criteria can
disagree about it. The selection only picks the model the later sections
work with: when other models are "indifferent", the data do not separate them
from it. After the table, the coefficients of the five forms under the
preferred definition.

```{r model-selection}
selection_models <- lapply(DEFINITIONS, function(def) {
  d <- add_deviation_terms(main$clean, def)
  lapply(FORMS, function(s) fit_model(form_terms(s), d))
})
selection <- bind_rows(lapply(names(selection_models), function(def) {
  fit_summary(selection_models[[def]]) %>% mutate(definition = def, .before = 1)
}))
stopifnot(length(unique(selection$observations)) == 1)

best_arms <- selection %>% filter(form %in% ARMS) %>% slice_min(aic, n = 1)
PREFERRED_DEFINITION <- if (params$preferred_definition == "auto") {
  best_arms$definition
} else {
  params$preferred_definition
}
PREFERRED_FORM <- if (params$preferred_form == "auto") best_arms$form else params$preferred_form
stopifnot(PREFERRED_DEFINITION %in% names(DEFINITIONS), PREFERRED_FORM %in% ARMS)
PREFERRED_SUFFIX <- DEFINITIONS[[PREFERRED_DEFINITION]]
preferred_terms <- form_terms(FORMS[[PREFERRED_FORM]])

selection %>%
  mutate(
    aic_vs_best = aic - min(aic), bic_vs_best = bic - min(bic),
    verdict = set_verdicts(record),
    preferred = definition == PREFERRED_DEFINITION & form == PREFERRED_FORM,
    within_r2 = round(within_r2, 4), within_adj_r2 = round(within_adj_r2, 4),
    across(c(aic, bic, aic_vs_best, bic_vs_best), ~ round(.x, 1)),
    across(ends_with("_p"), ~ signif(.x, 2))
  ) %>%
  select(-observations, -record) %>%
  knitr::kable(caption = paste0("PWT x ERA5, ", nrow(main$clean), " country-years: fit and ",
                                "joint tests of each variable; AIC and BIC relative to the best ",
                                "of all the models; ", VERDICT_NOTE, " against the best"))

# The arms models that cannot be told apart from the preferred one, by criterion.
preferred_record <- selection$record[[which(selection$definition == PREFERRED_DEFINITION &
                                              selection$form == PREFERRED_FORM)]]
arms_others <- filter(selection, form %in% ARMS,
                      !(definition == PREFERRED_DEFINITION & form == PREFERRED_FORM))
indifferent_to_preferred <- vapply(names(CRITERIA), function(cr) {
  sum(vapply(arms_others$record, fit_verdict, "", b = preferred_record, criterion = cr) ==
        "indifferent")
}, 0)
```

Preferred model: **`r PREFERRED_FORM`**, with the **`r PREFERRED_DEFINITION`**
deviations (temperature against mean_TM_`r PREFERRED_SUFFIX[["TM"]]`, precipitation
against mean_RR_`r PREFERRED_SUFFIX[["RR"]]`; interacted with
mean_TM_`r PREFERRED_SUFFIX[["clim_TM"]]` and mean_RR_`r PREFERRED_SUFFIX[["clim_RR"]]`).
Of the other `r nrow(arms_others)` arms models, `r indifferent_to_preferred[["aic"]]`
(AIC), `r indifferent_to_preferred[["bic"]]` (BIC) and
`r indifferent_to_preferred[["r2"]]` (within adjusted R2) cannot be told apart
from it (see the verdicts above).

```{r preferred-table}
# Short headers: etable cuts long ones.
SHORT_FORM_NAMES <- c("Signed" = "Signed", "Linear arms" = "Linear", "Quadratic arms" = "Quadratic",
                      "T linear, P quadratic arms" = "T lin, P quad",
                      "T quadratic, P linear arms" = "T quad, P lin")
etable(unname(selection_models[[PREFERRED_DEFINITION]]),
       headers = unname(SHORT_FORM_NAMES[names(FORMS)]), dict = DICT, drop = DROP,
       order = ORDER, fitstat = FITSTAT, title = paste("Deviations:", PREFERRED_DEFINITION))
```

## The preferred model with and without the growth outliers

The model is chosen on the main sample, without the growth outliers whose
cause does not involve weather. With every outlier kept (`r nrow(main$all)`
country-years of `r main$label` against `r nrow(main$clean)`), is the same
model chosen, and how do its estimates change? First the selection again on
both samples: each definition and arms form, AIC relative to the best of its
sample; then the preferred model on both: coefficients, joint tests, within
adjusted R2 and the effect of a +/-3 SD deviation. A third sample drops the
non-weather outliers of the other rule (growth reversals or growth levels, see
"Shared specification") instead. (The other panels, and the weather-driven
outliers dropped too, are in "Growth outliers: none, non-weather or all
dropped".)

```{r preferred-outliers}
PREFERRED_SAMPLES <- list("outliers dropped (main)" = main$clean, "outliers kept" = main$all)
PREFERRED_SAMPLES[[paste0("outliers dropped (", OTHER_OUTLIER_RULE, " rule)")]] <-
  apply_exclusions(main, OTHER_OUTLIERS_DROPPED)$clean

# 1. The selection on both samples.
outlier_selection <- bind_rows(lapply(names(PREFERRED_SAMPLES), function(s) {
  bind_rows(lapply(names(DEFINITIONS), function(def) {
    d <- add_deviation_terms(PREFERRED_SAMPLES[[s]], DEFINITIONS[[def]])
    fit_summary(lapply(FORMS[ARMS], function(f) fit_model(form_terms(f), d))) %>%
      mutate(sample = s, definition = def, .before = 1)
  }))
}))
outlier_selection %>%
  group_by(sample) %>%
  mutate(aic_vs_best = round(aic - min(aic), 1), verdict = set_verdicts(record)) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  select(definition, form, sample, aic_vs_best, verdict) %>%
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = sample, values_from = c(aic_vs_best, verdict)) %>%
  arrange(.data[[paste0("aic_vs_best_", names(PREFERRED_SAMPLES)[[1]])]]) %>%
  knitr::kable(caption = paste0(
    main$label, ": AIC of each definition and arms form relative to the best of its sample ",
    "(0: the model chosen), with the non-weather growth outliers dropped (", nrow(main$clean),
    " rows), with every outlier kept (", nrow(main$all), " rows) and with the non-weather ",
    "outliers of the ", OTHER_OUTLIER_RULE, " rule dropped (", nrow(PREFERRED_SAMPLES[[3]]),
    " rows); ", VERDICT_NOTE, " against the best of the sample"))

# 2. The preferred model on both samples.
preferred_by_sample <- lapply(PREFERRED_SAMPLES, function(rows) {
  fit_model(preferred_terms, add_deviation_terms(rows, PREFERRED_SUFFIX))
})
etable(unname(preferred_by_sample), headers = names(PREFERRED_SAMPLES), dict = DICT, drop = DROP,
       order = ORDER, fitstat = ~n + wr2 + war2,
       title = paste0(PREFERRED_FORM, ", ", PREFERRED_DEFINITION, " deviations"))

bind_rows(lapply(names(preferred_by_sample), function(s) {
  m <- preferred_by_sample[[s]]
  tibble::tibble(sample = s, rows = stats::nobs(m),
                 within_adj_r2_pct = round(100 * fixest::fitstat(m, "war2")[[1]], 3),
                 temperature_p = signif(wald_p(m, "^devTM"), 2),
                 precipitation_p = signif(wald_p(m, "^devRR"), 2))
})) %>%
  knitr::kable(caption = paste(main$label, "preferred model: within adjusted R2 (%) and joint",
                               "tests (p) of each variable's terms"))

significance_map(bind_rows(lapply(names(preferred_by_sample), function(s) {
  climate_effects(list(preferred = preferred_by_sample[[s]], panel = list(label = s)))
}))) %>%
  knitr::kable(caption = paste(main$label, "preferred model: effect of a +/-3 SD deviation in",
                               "the year (pp) by outlier sample; *** p < 0.01,",
                               "** p < 0.05, * p < 0.1"))
```

## The preferred model without standardization

Every deviation above is divided by the unit's SD, so a year is measured
against the unit's own variability: the same anomaly in °C is a larger
deviation where the weather varies little (in the tropics, for temperature).
Is that scaling supported by the data, or does the anomaly in physical units
do as well? Here the deviations are not divided by the SD,

```text
standardized     dT = (TM - mean) / SD        in SDs
unstandardized   dT =  TM - mean              in °C (dP in metres)
```

and are otherwise treated the same: demeaned (each unit's mean and quadratic
trend removed), cut into arms and interacted with the long-run climate, from
the horizon mean and from the trailing 20-year mean; for both variables, and
for one at a time with the other standardized. The rows are those of the
selection, and the models have the same number of coefficients, so AIC, BIC
and the within adjusted R2 rank them alike. (With the horizon baseline the
unstandardized deviation of a unit is its standardized deviation times its
SD, a constant: the two models differ only in how the units are weighted
against each other and in the scale on which the arms' curvature and the
climate interaction act.)

1. The preferred form with and without standardization: fit against the
   standardized model, its verdict, and the joint tests.
2. The arms forms under each: does the choice of form change?
3. The preferred form on every panel.
4. Effects on two common scales, averaged over the units of each third by
   long-run climate, each unit at its own long-run climate and SD: an anomaly
   of 3 of the unit's own SDs (the scale of the standardized model: in the
   unstandardized one it is 3 SD in °C or metres), and the same physical
   anomaly everywhere, 1 °C or 100 mm (the scale of the unstandardized model:
   in the standardized one it is 1 °C over the unit's SD). The SD is that of
   the model's baseline (the horizon SD, or the unit's median trailing 20-year
   SD over its sample years).

The unstandardized arms models are saved with the others for the scenario
projections; `sai_scenarios.Rmd` compares the losses they imply.

```{r unstandardized}
UNSTD <- "unstd"
# dm_<v>_<baseline>_unstd: the deviation from each baseline mean in physical
# units (not divided by the SD), demeaned as the deviations of
# prepare_panel(), on the panel's clean rows.
add_unstandardized_deviations <- function(panel) {
  data <- panel$data
  window <- data$year >= panel$start_year - MAX_LAGS & data$year <= panel$end_year
  cols <- character(0)
  for (v in c("TM", "RR")) for (b in BASELINES) {
    raw <- data[[v]] - data[[paste0("mean_", v, "_", b)]]
    ok <- which(window & is.finite(raw))
    sub <- data.frame(GID_1 = data$GID_1[ok], t = data$t[ok], t2 = data$t2[ok], x = raw[ok])
    m <- fixest::feols(x ~ 1 | GID_1[t, t2], sub, notes = FALSE)
    demeaned <- rep(NA_real_, nrow(data))
    demeaned[ok[fixest::obs(m)]] <- stats::resid(m)
    cols <- c(cols, paste0("dm_", v, "_", b, "_", UNSTD))
    data[[cols[[length(cols)]]]] <- demeaned
  }
  out <- panel$clean %>%
    left_join(select(data, GID_1, year, all_of(cols)), by = c("GID_1", "year"))
  stopifnot(nrow(out) == nrow(panel$clean),
            all(vapply(cols, function(x) all(is.finite(out[[x]])), TRUE)))
  out
}
unstd <- function(b) paste0(b, "_", UNSTD)
UNSTD_DEFINITIONS <- list(
  "Horizon, unstandardized" = definition(unstd("all"), unstd("all")),
  "Horizon, T unstandardized" = definition(unstd("all"), "all"),
  "Horizon, P unstandardized" = definition("all", unstd("all")),
  "20-year, unstandardized" = definition(unstd("lag_20"), unstd("lag_20")),
  "20-year, T unstandardized" = definition(unstd("lag_20"), "lag_20"),
  "20-year, P unstandardized" = definition("lag_20", unstd("lag_20"))
)

unstd_data <- add_unstandardized_deviations(main)
unstd_models <- lapply(UNSTD_DEFINITIONS, function(def) {
  d <- add_deviation_terms(unstd_data, def)
  lapply(FORMS, function(s) fit_model(form_terms(s), d))
})
unstd_fit <- function(def, form = PREFERRED_FORM) {
  if (def %in% names(unstd_models)) unstd_models[[def]][[form]] else selection_models[[def]][[form]]
}

# 1. The preferred form with and without standardization.
bind_rows(lapply(c("Horizon", "20-year"), function(base) {
  defs <- c(base, grep(paste0("^", base, ","), names(UNSTD_DEFINITIONS), value = TRUE))
  bind_rows(lapply(defs, function(def) {
    m <- unstd_fit(def)
    reference <- unstd_fit(base)
    tibble::tibble(baseline = base, deviations = if (def == base) "standardized" else sub(".*, ", "", def),
                   aic_vs_standardized = round(stats::AIC(m) - stats::AIC(reference), 1),
                   within_adj_r2_pct = round(100 * fixest::fitstat(m, "war2")[[1]], 3),
                   verdict_vs_standardized = if (def == base) "" else fit_verdicts(m, reference),
                   temperature_p = signif(wald_p(m, "^devTM"), 2),
                   precipitation_p = signif(wald_p(m, "^devRR"), 2))
  }))
})) %>%
  knitr::kable(caption = paste0(
    main$label, ", ", nrow(main$clean), " country-years, ", PREFERRED_FORM, ": deviations ",
    "standardized (in SDs) or not (in °C and metres), for both variables or one; AIC against ",
    "the standardized model of the same baseline (the BIC difference is the same: same ",
    "parameters), within adjusted R2 (%), the ", VERDICT_NOTE, " against the standardized ",
    "model, and the joint tests (p) of each variable's terms"))

# 2. The arms forms under each.
UNSTD_PURE <- c("Horizon", "Horizon, unstandardized", "20-year", "20-year, unstandardized")
bind_rows(lapply(UNSTD_PURE, function(def) {
  fit_summary(lapply(stats::setNames(nm = ARMS), function(f) unstd_fit(def, f))) %>%
    mutate(definition = def, .before = 1)
})) %>%
  mutate(aic_vs_best = round(aic - min(aic), 1), verdict = set_verdicts(record)) %>%
  group_by(definition) %>%
  mutate(aic_vs_best_of_definition = round(aic - min(aic), 1)) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  select(definition, form, aic_vs_best_of_definition, aic_vs_best, verdict) %>%
  knitr::kable(caption = paste0(
    main$label, ": the arms forms with standardized and unstandardized deviations; AIC ",
    "relative to the best form of the definition and to the best of all sixteen, and the ",
    VERDICT_NOTE, " against the best of all"))

# 3. The preferred form on every panel.
bind_rows(lapply(c(national_panels, list(dose)), function(p) {
  d <- add_unstandardized_deviations(p)
  bind_rows(lapply(c("Horizon", "20-year"), function(base) {
    standardized <- fit_model(preferred_terms, add_deviation_terms(d, DEFINITIONS[[base]]))
    m <- fit_model(preferred_terms,
                   add_deviation_terms(d, UNSTD_DEFINITIONS[[paste0(base, ", unstandardized")]]))
    tibble::tibble(panel = p$label, baseline = base,
                   aic_unstandardized_vs_standardized = round(stats::AIC(m) - stats::AIC(standardized), 1),
                   verdict = fit_verdicts(m, standardized),
                   T_p_standardized = signif(wald_p(standardized, "^devTM"), 2),
                   T_p_unstandardized = signif(wald_p(m, "^devTM"), 2),
                   P_p_standardized = signif(wald_p(standardized, "^devRR"), 2),
                   P_p_unstandardized = signif(wald_p(m, "^devRR"), 2))
  }))
})) %>%
  knitr::kable(caption = paste0(
    "Every panel, ", PREFERRED_FORM, ": unstandardized against standardized deviations (both ",
    "variables), AIC difference (negative: unstandardized fits better), the unstandardized ",
    "model's ", VERDICT_NOTE, ", and the joint tests (p) of each variable's terms under each"))

# 4. Effects on common scales. Each unit's long-run climate and SDs, and its
# third by long-run climate.
unstd_units <- unstd_data %>%
  group_by(GID_1) %>%
  summarise(clim_TM = first(mean_TM_all), clim_RR = first(mean_RR_all),
            sd_TM_all = first(sd_TM_all), sd_RR_all = first(sd_RR_all),
            sd_TM_lag_20 = stats::median(sd_TM_lag_20), sd_RR_lag_20 = stats::median(sd_RR_lag_20),
            .groups = "drop") %>%
  mutate(third_TM = cut(clim_TM, stats::quantile(clim_TM, 0:3 / 3), include.lowest = TRUE,
                        labels = c("cold", "mid", "hot")),
         third_RR = cut(clim_RR, stats::quantile(clim_RR, 0:3 / 3), include.lowest = TRUE,
                        labels = c("dry", "mid", "wet")))
# Mean effect over `units` of an anomaly of variable v, `size` in the units'
# own SDs (scale "sd") or in physical units ("physical"), in a model of the
# preferred form whose deviation of v is `standardized` or not; `sd`: the
# units' SD of the model's baseline.
anomaly_effect <- function(fit, v, size, scale, standardized, sd, units) {
  terms <- names(stats::coef(fit))
  x <- if (standardized == (scale == "sd")) rep(size, nrow(units)) else if (standardized) {
    size / sd
  } else size * sd
  W <- t(vapply(seq_len(nrow(units)), function(j) {
    w <- stats::setNames(numeric(length(terms)), terms)
    for (s in FORMS[[PREFERRED_FORM]][[v]]) {
      arm <- paste0("dev", v, s)
      value <- term_value(s, x[[j]])
      w[[arm]] <- value
      w[[interaction_name(arm, paste0("clim_", v), terms)]] <-
        value * units[[paste0("clim_", v)]][[j]]
    }
    w
  }, numeric(length(terms))))
  out <- linear_combination(fit, colMeans(W))
  out$p_value <- 2 * stats::pnorm(-abs(out$estimate / out$std_error))
  out
}
UNSTD_EVENTS <- tibble::tribble(
  ~variable, ~size, ~scale, ~event,
  "TM", 3, "sd", "T +3 SD", "TM", -3, "sd", "T -3 SD",
  "RR", -3, "sd", "P -3 SD", "RR", 3, "sd", "P +3 SD",
  "TM", 1, "physical", "T +1 °C", "TM", -1, "physical", "T -1 °C",
  "RR", -0.1, "physical", "P -100 mm", "RR", 0.1, "physical", "P +100 mm"
)
unstd_effects <- bind_rows(lapply(UNSTD_PURE, function(def) {
  fit <- unstd_fit(def)
  baseline <- if (startsWith(def, "Horizon")) "all" else "lag_20"
  standardized <- !grepl("unstandardized", def)
  bind_rows(lapply(seq_len(nrow(UNSTD_EVENTS)), function(i) {
    e <- UNSTD_EVENTS[i, ]
    thirds <- unstd_units[[paste0("third_", e$variable)]]
    bind_rows(lapply(levels(thirds), function(th) {
      units <- unstd_units[thirds == th, ]
      anomaly_effect(fit, e$variable, e$size, e$scale, standardized,
                     units[[paste0("sd_", e$variable, "_", baseline)]], units) %>%
        mutate(model = def, event = e$event, scale = e$scale, third = th)
    }))
  }))
}))
unstd_effect_table <- function(which_scale, what) {
  unstd_effects %>%
    filter(scale == which_scale) %>%
    mutate(cell = sprintf("%+.2f%s", 100 * estimate, stars(p_value)),
           column = factor(paste0(event, ", ", third), levels = unique(paste0(event, ", ", third)))) %>%
    select(model, column, cell) %>%
    tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = column, values_from = cell) %>%
    knitr::kable(caption = paste0(
      main$label, ", ", PREFERRED_FORM, ": effect on growth that year (pp) of ", what,
      ", averaged over the units of each third by long-run climate (each unit at its own ",
      "long-run climate and SD), with standardized and unstandardized deviations; ",
      "*** p < 0.01, ** p < 0.05, * p < 0.1"))
}
unstd_effect_table("sd", "an anomaly of 3 of the unit's own SDs")
unstd_effect_table("physical", "the same physical anomaly in every unit (1 °C; 100 mm)")

bind_rows(lapply(c("TM", "RR"), function(v) {
  unstd_units %>%
    group_by(third = .data[[paste0("third_", v)]]) %>%
    summarise(units = n(),
              long_run_climate = round(stats::median(.data[[paste0("clim_", v)]]), 2),
              horizon_sd = round(stats::median(.data[[paste0("sd_", v, "_all")]]), 3),
              trailing_20_year_sd = round(stats::median(.data[[paste0("sd_", v, "_lag_20")]]), 3),
              .groups = "drop") %>%
    mutate(variable = if (v == "TM") "temperature (°C)" else "precipitation (m)",
           third = as.character(third), .before = 1)
})) %>%
  knitr::kable(caption = paste0(
    main$label, ": the units of each third by long-run climate, their median long-run ",
    "climate and their median SDs (the horizon SD, and the unit's median trailing 20-year SD)"))
```

## 20-year means in the horizon SD

The 20-year definition measures each year against both trailing moments, so a
period of fast change also widens the SD the deviation is measured in. A third
baseline keeps the trailing 20-year mean but measures the deviation in the
horizon SD (a constant of each unit), demeaned as the others:

```text
20-year mean, horizon SD:  dT = (TM - mean_TM_lag_20) / sd_TM_all      (the same for RR)
```

Every form, with both variables on this baseline, and with one of them on it
