and the other on the horizon or the 20-year baseline, against the models above
(same rows); the effects of the preferred form; and the preferred form on
every national panel. These models do not enter the choice of the preferred
model.

```{r mixed-moments}
MIXED <- "lag_20_sd_all"
# dm_<v>_lag_20_sd_all: the deviation from the trailing 20-year mean in the
# horizon SD, demeaned as the deviations of prepare_panel(), on the panel's
# clean rows.
add_mixed_deviations <- function(panel) {
  data <- panel$data
  window <- data$year >= START_YEAR - MAX_LAGS & data$year <= panel$end_year
  for (v in c("TM", "RR")) {
    raw <- (data[[v]] - data[[paste0("mean_", v, "_lag_20")]]) / data[[paste0("sd_", v, "_all")]]
    ok <- which(window & is.finite(raw))
    sub <- data.frame(GID_1 = data$GID_1[ok], t = data$t[ok], t2 = data$t2[ok], x = raw[ok])
    m <- fixest::feols(x ~ 1 | GID_1[t, t2], sub, notes = FALSE)
    demeaned <- rep(NA_real_, nrow(data))
    demeaned[ok[fixest::obs(m)]] <- stats::resid(m)
    data[[paste0("dm_", v, "_", MIXED)]] <- demeaned
  }
  out <- panel$clean %>%
    left_join(select(data, GID_1, year, all_of(paste0("dm_", c("TM", "RR"), "_", MIXED))),
              by = c("GID_1", "year"))
  stopifnot(nrow(out) == nrow(panel$clean),
            all(is.finite(out[[paste0("dm_TM_", MIXED)]])),
            all(is.finite(out[[paste0("dm_RR_", MIXED)]])))
  out
}
MIXED_DEFINITIONS <- list(
  "20-year mean, horizon SD" = definition(MIXED, MIXED),
  "T 20-year mean in horizon SD, P horizon" = definition(MIXED, "all"),
  "T 20-year mean in horizon SD, P 20-year" = definition(MIXED, "lag_20"),
  "T horizon, P 20-year mean in horizon SD" = definition("all", MIXED)
)

mixed_data <- add_mixed_deviations(main)
mixed_models <- lapply(MIXED_DEFINITIONS, function(def) {
  d <- add_deviation_terms(mixed_data, def)
  lapply(FORMS, function(s) fit_model(form_terms(s), d))
})
mixed_selection <- bind_rows(lapply(names(mixed_models), function(def) {
  fit_summary(mixed_models[[def]]) %>% mutate(definition = def, .before = 1)
}))
stopifnot(all(mixed_selection$observations == selection$observations[[1]]))

# 1. Fit and joint tests, against the horizon and 20-year models (same rows).
bind_rows(selection, mixed_selection) %>%
  mutate(aic_vs_best = round(aic - min(aic), 1), bic_vs_best = round(bic - min(bic), 1),
         verdict = set_verdicts(record)) %>%
  filter(definition %in% c("Horizon", "20-year", "T 20-year, P horizon", names(MIXED_DEFINITIONS))) %>%
  mutate(within_r2 = round(within_r2, 4), within_adj_r2 = round(within_adj_r2, 4),
         across(ends_with("_p"), ~ signif(.x, 2))) %>%
  select(definition, form, within_r2, within_adj_r2, aic_vs_best, bic_vs_best, verdict,
         temperature_p, precipitation_p) %>%
  knitr::kable(caption = paste0(
    main$label, ", ", nrow(main$clean), " country-years: the 20-year mean in the horizon SD ",
    "against the horizon and 20-year baselines; AIC and BIC relative to the best model of ",
    "these and the selection above; ", VERDICT_NOTE, " against that best"))

# 2. Effects of a +/-3 SD deviation in the preferred form (horizon SDs, except
# the 20-year definition: trailing SDs).
MIXED_COMPARED <- c("Horizon", "20-year", "20-year mean, horizon SD")
significance_map(bind_rows(lapply(MIXED_COMPARED, function(def) {
  model <- if (def %in% names(selection_models)) {
    selection_models[[def]][[PREFERRED_FORM]]
  } else {
    mixed_models[[def]][[PREFERRED_FORM]]
  }
  climate_effects(list(preferred = model, panel = list(label = def)), PREFERRED_FORM)
}))) %>%
  knitr::kable(caption = paste0(main$label, ", ", PREFERRED_FORM, ": effect of a +/-3 SD ",
                                "deviation (pp) by baseline; *** p < 0.01, ** p < 0.05, * p < 0.1"))

# 3. The preferred form on every national panel.
bind_rows(lapply(national_panels, function(p) {
  d <- add_mixed_deviations(p)
  defs <- c(DEFINITIONS[c("Horizon", "20-year")], MIXED_DEFINITIONS[1])
  fits <- lapply(defs, function(def) fit_model(preferred_terms, add_deviation_terms(d, def)))
  same_rows <- length(unique(lapply(fits, fixest::obs))) == 1
  versus <- function(def, ref) {
    if (def == ref || !same_rows) "" else fit_verdicts(fits[[def]], fits[[ref]])
  }
  tibble::tibble(panel = p$label, definition = names(defs), same_rows = same_rows,
                 aic = vapply(fits, stats::AIC, 0),
                 verdict_vs_horizon = vapply(names(defs), versus, "", ref = "Horizon"),
                 verdict_vs_20_year = vapply(names(defs), versus, "", ref = "20-year"),
                 temperature_p = vapply(fits, wald_p, 0, "^devTM"),
                 precipitation_p = vapply(fits, wald_p, 0, "^devRR"))
})) %>%
  group_by(panel) %>%
  mutate(aic_vs_horizon = round(aic - aic[definition == "Horizon"], 1),
         aic_vs_20_year = round(aic - aic[definition == "20-year"], 1)) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  mutate(across(ends_with("_p"), ~ signif(.x, 2))) %>%
  select(panel, definition, same_rows, aic_vs_horizon, verdict_vs_horizon, aic_vs_20_year,
         verdict_vs_20_year, temperature_p, precipitation_p) %>%
  knitr::kable(caption = paste0("Every national panel, ", PREFERRED_FORM, ": AIC by baseline ",
                                "(same rows within a panel) and joint tests; ", VERDICT_NOTE,
                                " against the horizon and the 20-year baselines"))
```

The arms models of every definition (and of the 20-year mean in the horizon
SD, and the unstandardized ones) are saved for the scenario projections
(`sai_scenarios.Rmd`, which picks one; by default the preferred): their
weather coefficients with their VCOV (clustered by country) and AIC, the range
of the demeaned deviations in the sample (the support of the arms), each
country's horizon moments, and its median trailing 20-year SDs over the
sample years.

```{r preferred-export}
PREFERRED_MODEL_FILE <- file.path("results", "preferred_model", "preferred_model.rds")
local({
  # The horizon moments, and the median over the sample years of the trailing
  # 20-year SDs (a fixed SD for the 20-year deviations of the projections).
  moments <- main$data %>%
    filter(!is.na(mean_TM_all), !is.na(mean_RR_all)) %>%
    distinct(GID_0, mean_TM_all, sd_TM_all, mean_RR_all, sd_RR_all) %>%
    left_join(main$clean %>%
                group_by(GID_0) %>%
                summarise(sd_TM_lag_20 = stats::median(sd_TM_lag_20),
                          sd_RR_lag_20 = stats::median(sd_RR_lag_20), .groups = "drop"),
              by = "GID_0")
  stopifnot(!anyDuplicated(moments$GID_0))
  all_definitions <- c(DEFINITIONS, MIXED_DEFINITIONS, UNSTD_DEFINITIONS)
  all_models <- c(selection_models, mixed_models, unstd_models)
  models <- lapply(stats::setNames(nm = names(all_definitions)), function(def) {
    rows <- if (def %in% names(MIXED_DEFINITIONS)) mixed_data else if (
      def %in% names(UNSTD_DEFINITIONS)) unstd_data else main$clean
    d <- add_deviation_terms(rows, all_definitions[[def]])
    lapply(stats::setNames(nm = ARMS), function(f) {
      model <- all_models[[def]][[f]]
      weather <- grep("^dev(TM|RR)", names(stats::coef(model)), value = TRUE)
      list(definition = def, suffix = all_definitions[[def]], form = f, form_suffixes = FORMS[[f]],
           coef = stats::coef(model)[weather], vcov = stats::vcov(model)[weather, weather],
           aic = stats::AIC(model), support = list(TM = range(d$devTM), RR = range(d$devRR)))
    })
  })
  dir.create(dirname(PREFERRED_MODEL_FILE), showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)
  saveRDS(list(
    panel = main$label, observations = nrow(main$clean), horizon = c(START_YEAR, main$end_year),
    moments = moments, preferred = c(definition = PREFERRED_DEFINITION, form = PREFERRED_FORM),
    models = models, created = Sys.time()
  ), PREFERRED_MODEL_FILE)
})
```

## Linear or quadratic arms in the robust regions

On the whole sample, AIC prefers linear arms for precipitation and quadratic
ones for temperature (the main specification uses linear arms for both, set by
the `preferred_form` parameter). Does that shape hold where the
effects are robust: dry events in the dry-to-mid units (the bottom two thirds
of the units by long-run precipitation) and hot events in the hot units (the
top third by long-run temperature)? Each region is its own sample, with every
form, under the horizon and the 20-year deviations, and three checks:

1. the AIC of the five forms (relative to the best in the region and
   definition);
2. a nested test: the region's variable with both linear and quadratic arms
   (the other variable as in the AIC-best form), and the Wald test of the
   shape that the AIC-best form leaves out (the quadratic terms of
   precipitation, the linear terms of temperature);
3. the effect of a 3 SD event under the two competing forms (precipitation
   linear against quadratic; temperature quadratic against linear), at the
   quartiles of the region's long-run climate (within its range).

```{r robust-region-forms}
region_units <- distinct(main$clean, GID_1, mean_TM_all, mean_RR_all)
FORM_REGIONS <- list(
  "dry-to-mid units, precipitation" = list(
    variable = "RR",
    units = with(region_units, GID_1[mean_RR_all < stats::quantile(mean_RR_all, 2 / 3)]),
    compared = c("T quadratic, P linear arms", "Quadratic arms"), events = c(-3, 3)),
  "hot units, temperature" = list(
    variable = "TM",
    units = with(region_units, GID_1[mean_TM_all >= stats::quantile(mean_TM_all, 2 / 3)]),
    compared = c("T quadratic, P linear arms", "Linear arms"), events = c(3, -3))
)
ARMS_BOTH <- c("_pos", "_neg", "_pos2", "_neg2")
# The shape the preferred form leaves out: quadratic terms (P), linear terms (T).
LEFT_OUT <- c(RR = "(^|:)devRR_(pos|neg)2($|:)", TM = "(^|:)devTM_(pos|neg)($|:)")

region_fits <- lapply(FORM_REGIONS, function(reg) {
  both <- FORMS[["T quadratic, P linear arms"]]
  both[[reg$variable]] <- ARMS_BOTH
  forms <- c(FORMS, stats::setNames(list(both), "linear + quadratic arms"))
  lapply(c(Horizon = "Horizon", "20-year" = "20-year"), function(def) {
    d <- add_deviation_terms(filter(main$clean, GID_1 %in% reg$units), DEFINITIONS[[def]])
    list(data = d, fits = lapply(forms, function(f) fit_model(form_terms(f), d)))
  })
})

# 1-2. AIC of the forms, and the nested test.
bind_rows(lapply(names(region_fits), function(r) {
  bind_rows(lapply(names(region_fits[[r]]), function(def) {
    fits <- region_fits[[r]][[def]]$fits
    standard <- fits[names(FORMS)]
    left_out_p <- wald_p(fits[["linear + quadratic arms"]], LEFT_OUT[[FORM_REGIONS[[r]]$variable]])
    fit_summary(standard) %>%
      mutate(region = r, definition = def, .before = 1) %>%
      mutate(aic_vs_best = round(aic - min(aic), 1), verdict = set_verdicts(record),
             left_out_shape_p = signif(left_out_p, 2),
             left_out_shape_verdict = fit_verdicts(fits[["linear + quadratic arms"]],
                                                   fits[["T quadratic, P linear arms"]],
                                                   nested_p = left_out_p),
             across(c(temperature_p, precipitation_p), ~ signif(.x, 2))) %>%
      select(region, definition, form, observations, aic_vs_best, verdict, temperature_p,
             precipitation_p, left_out_shape_p, left_out_shape_verdict)
  }))
})) %>%
  knitr::kable(caption = paste0(
    main$label, ": the five forms in each robust region (its own sample), AIC relative to the ",
    "best form in the region and definition, and the ", VERDICT_NOTE, " against that best; ",
    "joint tests (p); left_out_shape_p: with the region's variable in both linear and ",
    "quadratic arms, the Wald test of the quadratic terms of precipitation (dry-to-mid) or the ",
    "linear terms of temperature (hot), and the verdict of that model against the preferred ",
    "form (nested)"))

# 3. Effects of a 3 SD event at the quartiles of the region's long-run climate.
bind_rows(lapply(names(region_fits), function(r) {
  reg <- FORM_REGIONS[[r]]
  v <- reg$variable
  bind_rows(lapply(names(region_fits[[r]]), function(def) {
    d <- region_fits[[r]][[def]]$data
    unit_climate <- d[[paste0("clim_", v)]][!duplicated(d$GID_1)]
    climates <- stats::quantile(unit_climate, c(0.25, 0.5, 0.75), names = FALSE)
    bind_rows(lapply(reg$compared, function(f) {
      fit <- region_fits[[r]][[def]]$fits[[f]]
      terms <- names(stats::coef(fit))
      bind_rows(lapply(reg$events, function(x) {
        G <- t(vapply(climates, function(m) {
          w <- stats::setNames(numeric(length(terms)), terms)
          for (s in FORMS[[f]][[v]]) {
            term <- paste0("dev", v, s)
            w[[term]] <- term_value(s, x)
            w[[interaction_name(term, paste0("clim_", v), terms)]] <- term_value(s, x) * m
          }
          w
        }, numeric(length(terms))))
        colnames(G) <- terms
        linear_combination(fit, G) %>%
          mutate(region = r, definition = def, form = f,
                 event = sprintf("%s %+d SD", if (v == "TM") "T" else "P", x),
                 climate = sprintf("%s %.2f", c("q25", "q50", "q75"), climates),
                 cell = sprintf("%+.2f%s", 100 * estimate,
                                stars(2 * stats::pnorm(-abs(estimate / std_error)))))
      }))
    }))
  }))
})) %>%
  mutate(quartile = substr(climate, 1, 3)) %>%
  group_by(region, definition) %>%
  mutate(climates = paste(unique(climate), collapse = ", ")) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  select(region, definition, climates, event, form, quartile, cell) %>%
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = quartile, values_from = cell) %>%
  knitr::kable(caption = paste0(
    main$label, ": effect on growth that year (pp) of a 3 SD event under the two competing ",
    "forms, at the 25th, 50th and 75th percentile of the region's long-run climate (C or m a ",
    "year, listed); *** p < 0.01, ** p < 0.05, * p < 0.1"))
```

## Linear or quadratic arms when the sample starts later

Does the choice of form rest on the early years? With the 20-year deviations
(the trailing 20-year mean and SD, interacted with the sample's horizon
climate) the five forms are compared on samples that start in
`r paste(c(1960, 1970, 1980, 1990), collapse = ", ")` and 2000 and run to each
panel's last year, for three GDP series and the three climate datasets:

- PWT (`rgdpna`: constant national prices, in 2021 PPP dollars);
- World Bank, constant 2015 US$ (the World Bank panels above, from 1960);
- World Bank, constant 2021 PPP (from 1990, so only the 1990 and 2000 samples;
  its growth is that of the constant-US$ series of the same vintage, see "World
  Bank GDP at PPP").

Each sample is rebuilt from its start year (the horizon climate, the demeaning
window and the first year), with the same exclusions in all of them (the growth
outliers of the main sample whose cause does not involve weather, and in the
years before `r START_YEAR` the growth tails of the sample from 1960, which
are the only ones annotated there). Two
comparisons isolate the two shape choices of the AIC-best form of the whole
sample (T quadratic, P linear arms; the main specification uses linear arms for
both), each with the other variable as in that form:

```text
T shape:  AIC(T linear, P linear arms)  - AIC(T quadratic, P linear arms)   > 0: quadratic T fits better
P shape:  AIC(T quadratic, P quadratic arms) - AIC(T quadratic, P linear arms) > 0: linear P fits better
```

and the same with the within adjusted R2 (that form's minus the
alternative's, in percentage points).

```{r start-year-forms}
START_YEARS <- c(1960L, 1970L, 1980L, 1990L, 2000L)
START_ECON <- c("PWT" = "PWT", "WB" = "WB", "WB PPP" = "WB_PPP")
START_REFERENCE <- "T quadratic, P linear arms"
national_labels <- vapply(national_panels, `[[`, "", "label")
start_grid <- expand.grid(start = START_YEARS, climate = c("ERA5", "CRU TS", "UDelaware"),
                          econ = names(START_ECON), stringsAsFactors = FALSE) %>%
  filter(!(econ == "WB PPP" & start < 1990L))
start_results <- bind_rows(lapply(seq_len(nrow(start_grid)), function(i) {
  g <- start_grid[i, ]
  label <- paste(START_ECON[[g$econ]], "x", g$climate)
  p <- if (g$start == START_YEAR && label %in% national_labels) {
    national_panels[[match(label, national_labels)]]
  } else {
    prepare_panel(START_ECON[[g$econ]], g$climate, start_year = g$start,
                  drop = bind_rows(OUTLIERS_DROPPED, EARLY_OUTLIERS_DROPPED))
  }
  d <- add_deviation_terms(p$clean, DEFINITIONS[["20-year"]])
  fits <- lapply(FORMS, function(s) fit_model(form_terms(s), d))
  stopifnot(length(unique(vapply(fits, stats::nobs, 0))) == 1)
  records <- lapply(fits, fit_record)
  # Each arms form against the best arms form, by criterion; the two shapes:
  # the preferred form against linear T arms and against quadratic P arms.
  arms_verdict <- function(cr) {
    stats::setNames(c("", verdicts_vs_best(records[ARMS], cr)), c("Signed", ARMS))[names(FORMS)]
  }
  tibble::tibble(econ = g$econ, climate = g$climate, start = g$start,
                 years = paste(range(d$year), collapse = "-"), rows = nrow(d),
                 countries = n_distinct(d$GID_0), form = names(FORMS),
                 aic = vapply(fits, stats::AIC, 0), bic = vapply(fits, stats::BIC, 0),
                 within_adj_r2 = vapply(fits, function(m) fixest::fitstat(m, "war2")[[1]], 0),
                 temperature_p = vapply(fits, wald_p, 0, "^devTM"),
                 precipitation_p = vapply(fits, wald_p, 0, "^devRR"),
                 verdict_aic = arms_verdict("aic"), verdict_bic = arms_verdict("bic"),
                 verdict_r2 = arms_verdict("r2"),
                 t_shape_verdict = fit_verdicts(records[[START_REFERENCE]], records[["Linear arms"]]),
                 p_shape_verdict = fit_verdicts(records[[START_REFERENCE]],
                                                records[["Quadratic arms"]]))
}))
```

```{r start-year-forms-results, fig.width=12, fig.height=10}
# Rows ordered by GDP series, climate dataset (ERA5, CRU TS, UDelaware) and
# start year.
start_levels <- function(x) {
  mutate(x, econ = factor(econ, levels = names(START_ECON)),
         climate = factor(climate, levels = c("ERA5", "CRU TS", "UDelaware"))) %>%
    arrange(econ, climate, start)
}
# The arms form chosen by a criterion, or "indifferent: ..." with the forms
# that cannot be told apart from the best (the best first).
form_choice <- function(form, verdict) {
  tied <- c(form[verdict == "best"], form[verdict == "indifferent"])
  if (length(tied) == 1) tied else paste("indifferent:", paste(SHORT_FORM_NAMES[tied], collapse = ", "))
}
# The preferred form's standing: "chosen" (best, beyond noise from every other
# arms form), "indifferent" (best or not, within noise of the best), "worse".
preferred_standing <- function(form, verdict) {
  v <- verdict[form == START_REFERENCE]
  if (v == "worse") "worse" else if (sum(verdict %in% c("best", "indifferent")) == 1) "chosen" else
    "indifferent"
}
first_word <- function(x) sub(" .*", "", x)
start_shapes <- start_results %>%
  group_by(econ, climate, start) %>%
  summarise(t_shape = aic[form == "Linear arms"] - aic[form == START_REFERENCE],
            p_shape = aic[form == "Quadratic arms"] - aic[form == START_REFERENCE],
            t_shape_r2 = 100 * (within_adj_r2[form == START_REFERENCE] -
                                  within_adj_r2[form == "Linear arms"]),
            p_shape_r2 = 100 * (within_adj_r2[form == START_REFERENCE] -
                                  within_adj_r2[form == "Quadratic arms"]),
            t_shape_verdict = first(t_shape_verdict), p_shape_verdict = first(p_shape_verdict),
            aic_choice = form_choice(form[form %in% ARMS], verdict_aic[form %in% ARMS]),
            bic_choice = form_choice(form[form %in% ARMS], verdict_bic[form %in% ARMS]),
            r2_choice = form_choice(form[form %in% ARMS], verdict_r2[form %in% ARMS]),
            preferred_aic = preferred_standing(form[form %in% ARMS], verdict_aic[form %in% ARMS]),
            preferred_bic = preferred_standing(form[form %in% ARMS], verdict_bic[form %in% ARMS]),
            preferred_r2 = preferred_standing(form[form %in% ARMS], verdict_r2[form %in% ARMS]),
            .groups = "drop")

# 1. Every sample: AIC of each form relative to the preferred form, the form
# each criterion chooses (or "indifferent"), the two shape verdicts, and the
# joint tests of the preferred form.
start_results %>%
  group_by(econ, climate, start) %>%
  mutate(aic_vs_reference = aic - aic[form == START_REFERENCE],
         reference_T_p = temperature_p[form == START_REFERENCE],
         reference_P_p = precipitation_p[form == START_REFERENCE]) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  select(econ, climate, start, years, rows, countries, form, aic_vs_reference, reference_T_p,
         reference_P_p) %>%
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = form, values_from = aic_vs_reference) %>%
  left_join(select(start_shapes, econ, climate, start, aic_choice, bic_choice,
                   t_shape_verdict, p_shape_verdict),
            by = c("econ", "climate", "start")) %>%
  start_levels() %>%
  mutate(across(all_of(names(FORMS)), ~ round(.x, 1)),
         across(starts_with("reference_"), ~ signif(.x, 2))) %>%
  select(-all_of(START_REFERENCE)) %>%
  knitr::kable(caption = paste0(
    "20-year deviations, samples from each start year to the panel's last year: AIC of each ",
    "form relative to the AIC-best form (", START_REFERENCE, "; negative: better); the arms ",
    "form chosen by AIC and by BIC, or 'indifferent' with the forms that cannot be told apart ",
    "from the best; the preferred form against linear T arms (T shape) and against quadratic P ",
    "arms (P shape), ", VERDICT_NOTE, " (the same here: same parameters); and the joint tests ",
    "(p) of the temperature and the precipitation terms in the preferred form"))

# 2. Every sample: the within adjusted R2 of each form.
start_results %>%
  select(econ, climate, start, form, within_adj_r2) %>%
  mutate(within_adj_r2 = round(100 * within_adj_r2, 3)) %>%
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = form, values_from = within_adj_r2) %>%
  left_join(select(start_shapes, econ, climate, start, r2_choice),
            by = c("econ", "climate", "start")) %>%
  start_levels() %>%
  knitr::kable(caption = paste(
    "20-year deviations, samples from each start year: within adjusted R2 (%) of each form,",
    "and the arms form with the highest, or 'indifferent' with the forms that cannot be told",
    "apart from it"))

# 3. The preferred form's standing and the two shapes, over the climate
# datasets.
count_of <- function(x, levels) paste(vapply(levels, function(l) sum(x == l), 0), collapse = " / ")
start_shapes %>%
  start_levels() %>%
  group_by(econ, start) %>%
  summarise(samples = n(),
            preferred_aic = count_of(preferred_aic, c("chosen", "indifferent", "worse")),
            preferred_bic = count_of(preferred_bic, c("chosen", "indifferent", "worse")),
            preferred_r2 = count_of(preferred_r2, c("chosen", "indifferent", "worse")),
            T_shape = count_of(first_word(t_shape_verdict), c("better", "indifferent", "worse")),
            P_shape = count_of(first_word(p_shape_verdict), c("better", "indifferent", "worse")),
            t_shape_aic = paste(sprintf("%+.1f", t_shape), collapse = " / "),
            p_shape_aic = paste(sprintf("%+.1f", p_shape), collapse = " / "),
            t_shape_r2 = paste(sprintf("%+.3f", t_shape_r2), collapse = " / "),
            p_shape_r2 = paste(sprintf("%+.3f", p_shape_r2), collapse = " / "),
            .groups = "drop") %>%
  knitr::kable(caption = paste(
    "By GDP series and start year, over the climate datasets: the preferred form chosen /",
    "indifferent (within noise of the best) / worse, by AIC, BIC and within adjusted R2; the",
    "preferred shape better / indifferent / worse, for T (quadratic against linear arms) and",
    "P (linear against quadratic arms); and each shape's gain in each dataset (ERA5 / CRU TS /",
    "UDelaware; AIC of the alternative minus the preferred; within adjusted R2 of the",
    "preferred minus the alternative, pp; positive: the preferred shape fits better)"))

# 4. The two shape comparisons by start year; ringed: beyond noise.
shape_long <- start_shapes %>%
  tidyr::pivot_longer(c(t_shape, p_shape, t_shape_r2, p_shape_r2), names_to = "key",
                      values_to = "gain") %>%
  mutate(measure = ifelse(grepl("_r2$", key), "within adj. R2 gain (pp)", "AIC gain"),
         comparison = ifelse(grepl("^t_", key), "T: quadratic vs linear",
                             "P: linear vs quadratic"),
         beyond_noise = first_word(ifelse(grepl("^t_", key), t_shape_verdict, p_shape_verdict)) !=
           "indifferent",
         panel = factor(paste0(comparison, "\n", measure),
                        levels = c("T: quadratic vs linear\nAIC gain",
                                   "T: quadratic vs linear\nwithin adj. R2 gain (pp)",
                                   "P: linear vs quadratic\nAIC gain",
                                   "P: linear vs quadratic\nwithin adj. R2 gain (pp)"))) %>%
  start_levels()
ggplot(shape_long, aes(start, gain, colour = climate, shape = climate)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, colour = GRID_MUTED, linewidth = 0.3) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.6) +
  geom_point(size = 2.2) +
  geom_point(data = filter(shape_long, beyond_noise), shape = 1, size = 4.5, stroke = 0.8,
             show.legend = FALSE) +
  facet_grid(panel ~ econ, scales = "free_y") +
  scale_colour_manual(values = grid_colours(levels(shape_long$climate)), name = NULL) +
  scale_shape_manual(values = grid_shapes(levels(shape_long$climate)), name = NULL) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = START_YEARS) +
  labs(x = "First year of the sample", y = "Gain of the preferred shape",
       title = "Does the preferred form hold when the sample starts later?",
       subtitle = paste(strwrap(paste0(
         "20-year deviations; the AIC-best form (", START_REFERENCE, ") against the ",
         "alternative shape of one variable, the other as in the preferred form: AIC of the ",
         "alternative minus the preferred, and within adjusted R2 of the preferred minus the ",
         "alternative; above zero the preferred shape fits better. Ringed: the difference is ",
         "beyond noise (clustered Vuong test, 5%); the others are indifferent. Each sample runs ",
         "to the panel's last year."), 150), collapse = "\n")) +
  theme_results()
```

## What drives the precipitation results: reference mean, normalization or arms

A statement to test: after the units' quadratic trends are removed, the
precipitation results hardly depend on the reference mean, and what sets them
apart from the standard level specification is the normalization by the local
variability and the separate responses to positive and negative anomalies. On
the same rows (`r main$label`, the main sample), with the temperature terms of
the preferred model, the controls, the fixed effects and the interaction with
the long-run precipitation all held fixed, the precipitation terms change one
factor at a time, in a 2 x 2 x 2 design:

- reference mean: fixed (the horizon mean) or trailing (the mean of the 20
  years before);
- normalization: none (metres) or the unit's horizon SD (the same SD for both
  means, so that only the mean differs);
- shape: signed, or positive and negative arms.

Every deviation is demeaned as in the models above (each unit's mean and
quadratic trend removed). For reference, the standard level specification (P
and P^2), the level with the same climate interaction (with the unit trends in
the model it is the fixed-mean signed deviation in metres), and the arms
without removing the trends from the deviations (fixed and trailing mean, in
the horizon SD). The effects are on a common scale: a dry (-3 SD) and a wet
(+3 SD) year in each unit's horizon SD (in metres for the unnormalized
models), at its long-run precipitation, averaged over the units of each third
by long-run precipitation.

```{r precipitation-decomposition}
P_REFERENCES <- c(fixed = "mean_RR_all", trailing = "mean_RR_lag_20")
# Each reference mean's precipitation deviation, in metres (m) or in the
# horizon SD (sd), demeaned as the deviations of prepare_panel() (pdm_) and as
# it is (praw_), on the panel's main sample with the preferred terms.
precipitation_deviations <- function(panel) {
  data <- panel$data
  window <- data$year >= START_YEAR - MAX_LAGS & data$year <= panel$end_year
  for (r in names(P_REFERENCES)) for (scale in c("m", "sd")) {
    raw <- data$RR - data[[P_REFERENCES[[r]]]]
    if (scale == "sd") raw <- raw / data$sd_RR_all
    ok <- which(window & is.finite(raw))
    sub <- data.frame(GID_1 = data$GID_1[ok], t = data$t[ok], t2 = data$t2[ok], x = raw[ok])
    m <- fixest::feols(x ~ 1 | GID_1[t, t2], sub, notes = FALSE)
    demeaned <- rep(NA_real_, nrow(data))
    demeaned[ok[fixest::obs(m)]] <- stats::resid(m)
    data[[paste0("pdm_", r, "_", scale)]] <- demeaned
    data[[paste0("praw_", r, "_", scale)]] <- raw
  }
  cols <- grep("^p(dm|raw)_", names(data), value = TRUE)
  out <- add_deviation_terms(panel$clean, DEFINITIONS[["Horizon"]]) %>%
    left_join(select(data, GID_1, year, all_of(cols)), by = c("GID_1", "year"))
  stopifnot(nrow(out) == nrow(panel$clean),
            all(vapply(cols, function(x) all(is.finite(out[[x]])), TRUE)))
  out
}
p_data <- precipitation_deviations(main)

P_SPECS <- tibble::tribble(
  ~spec, ~column, ~shape, ~mean, ~scale,
  "standard level: P + P^2", NA, "bhm", "fixed", "m",
  "level with interaction: P + P x mean P", NA, "level", "fixed", "m",
  "fixed mean, metres, signed", "pdm_fixed_m", "signed", "fixed", "m",
  "trailing mean, metres, signed", "pdm_trailing_m", "signed", "trailing", "m",
  "fixed mean, horizon SD, signed", "pdm_fixed_sd", "signed", "fixed", "sd",
  "trailing mean, horizon SD, signed", "pdm_trailing_sd", "signed", "trailing", "sd",
  "fixed mean, metres, arms", "pdm_fixed_m", "arms", "fixed", "m",
  "trailing mean, metres, arms", "pdm_trailing_m", "arms", "trailing", "m",
  "fixed mean, horizon SD, arms", "pdm_fixed_sd", "arms", "fixed", "sd",
  "trailing mean, horizon SD, arms", "pdm_trailing_sd", "arms", "trailing", "sd",
  "fixed mean, horizon SD, arms, trends not removed", "praw_fixed_sd", "arms", "fixed", "sd",
  "trailing mean, horizon SD, arms, trends not removed", "praw_trailing_sd", "arms", "trailing", "sd"
)
P_TEMPERATURE_TERMS <- grep("^devTM", form_terms(FORMS[[PREFERRED_FORM]]), value = TRUE)
precipitation_terms <- function(shape) {
  switch(shape,
         bhm = c("RR", "RR2"),
         level = c("RR", "RR:clim_RR"),
         signed = c("pdev", "pdev:clim_RR"),
         arms = c("pdev_pos", "pdev_neg", "pdev_pos:clim_RR", "pdev_neg:clim_RR"))
}
p_fits <- lapply(seq_len(nrow(P_SPECS)), function(i) {
  s <- P_SPECS[i, ]
  d <- p_data
  if (!is.na(s$column)) {
    d$pdev <- d[[s$column]]
    d$pdev_pos <- pmax(d$pdev, 0)
    d$pdev_neg <- pmax(-d$pdev, 0)
  }
  fit_model(c(P_TEMPERATURE_TERMS, precipitation_terms(s$shape), CONTROLS), d)
})
stopifnot(length(unique(vapply(p_fits, stats::nobs, 0))) == 1)

# Effect of a year `sign` x 3 horizon SDs (in metres x sd for the unnormalized
# models) at each unit's long-run precipitation, averaged over the units of a
# third.
p_units <- distinct(p_data, GID_1, clim_RR, sd_RR_all) %>%
  mutate(third = cut(clim_RR, stats::quantile(clim_RR, c(0, 1, 2, 3) / 3),
                     labels = c("dry third", "mid third", "wet third"), include.lowest = TRUE))
p_effect <- function(fit, s, sign, units) {
  terms <- names(stats::coef(fit))
  W <- t(vapply(seq_len(nrow(units)), function(j) {
    w <- stats::setNames(numeric(length(terms)), terms)
    m <- units$clim_RR[[j]]
    x_m <- sign * 3 * units$sd_RR_all[[j]]
    x <- if (s$scale == "sd") sign * 3 else x_m
    if (s$shape == "bhm") {
      w[["RR"]] <- x_m
      w[["RR2"]] <- 2 * m * x_m + x_m^2
    } else if (s$shape == "level") {
      w[["RR"]] <- x_m
      w[[interaction_name("RR", "clim_RR", terms)]] <- x_m * m
    } else {
      arms <- if (s$shape == "signed") c(pdev = x) else c(pdev_pos = max(x, 0), pdev_neg = max(-x, 0))
      for (a in names(arms)) {
        w[[a]] <- arms[[a]]
        w[[interaction_name(a, "clim_RR", terms)]] <- arms[[a]] * m
      }
    }
    w
  }, numeric(length(terms))))
  combination_row_p <- linear_combination(fit, colMeans(W))
  combination_row_p$p_value <- 2 * stats::pnorm(-abs(combination_row_p$estimate /
                                                      combination_row_p$std_error))
  combination_row_p
}
p_results <- bind_rows(lapply(seq_len(nrow(P_SPECS)), function(i) {
  s <- P_SPECS[i, ]
  fit <- p_fits[[i]]
  bind_rows(lapply(c(dry = -1, wet = 1), function(sign) {
    bind_rows(lapply(levels(p_units$third), function(th) {
      p_effect(fit, s, sign, filter(p_units, third == th)) %>%
        mutate(event = if (sign < 0) "dry" else "wet", third = th)
    }))
  })) %>%
    mutate(spec = s$spec, aic = stats::AIC(fit), bic = stats::BIC(fit),
           wr2 = fixest::fitstat(fit, "wr2")[[1]], war2 = fixest::fitstat(fit, "war2")[[1]],
           precipitation_p = wald_p(fit, "^(pdev|RR)|:(pdev|RR)"),
           parameters = length(precipitation_terms(s$shape)))
}))

# 1. The deviations after the trends are removed: correlations.
round(stats::cor(as.data.frame(p_data)[, c("pdm_fixed_m", "pdm_trailing_m", "pdm_fixed_sd",
                                           "pdm_trailing_sd", "RR")]), 3) %>%
  knitr::kable(caption = paste0(main$label, ": correlations of the precipitation deviations ",
                                "(demeaned; fixed or trailing mean, metres or horizon SD) and of ",
                                "the level"))

# 2. Every specification: fit, joint test, and the effects on the common scale.
P_REFERENCE_SPEC <- "fixed mean, horizon SD, arms"
reference_aic <- p_results$aic[p_results$spec == P_REFERENCE_SPEC][[1]]
reference_bic <- p_results$bic[p_results$spec == P_REFERENCE_SPEC][[1]]
# Without precipitation terms: what the precipitation terms add to the within R2.
p_none <- fit_model(c(P_TEMPERATURE_TERMS, CONTROLS), p_data)
p_none_war2 <- fixest::fitstat(p_none, "war2")[[1]]
p_none_wr2 <- fixest::fitstat(p_none, "wr2")[[1]]
p_records <- stats::setNames(lapply(p_fits, fit_record), P_SPECS$spec)
p_none_record <- fit_record(p_none)
p_verdicts <- tibble::tibble(
  spec = P_SPECS$spec,
  verdict_vs_preferred_p = vapply(P_SPECS$spec, function(s) {
    if (s == P_REFERENCE_SPEC) "" else fit_verdicts(p_records[[s]], p_records[[P_REFERENCE_SPEC]])
  }, ""),
  verdict_vs_none = vapply(seq_along(p_fits), function(i) {
    fit_verdicts(p_records[[i]], p_none_record,
                 nested_p = wald_p(p_fits[[i]], "^(pdev|RR)|:(pdev|RR)"))
  }, "")
)
p_results %>%
  mutate(cell = sprintf("%+.2f%s", 100 * estimate, stars(p_value)),
         column = paste(event, sub(" third", "", third))) %>%
  select(spec, parameters, aic, bic, wr2, war2, precipitation_p, column, cell) %>%
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = column, values_from = cell) %>%
  left_join(p_verdicts, by = "spec") %>%
  mutate(aic_vs_preferred_p = round(aic - reference_aic, 1),
         bic_vs_preferred_p = round(bic - reference_bic, 1),
         within_adj_r2_pct = round(100 * war2, 3),
         added_within_r2_pct = round(100 * (wr2 - p_none_wr2), 3),
         added_within_adj_r2_pct = round(100 * (war2 - p_none_war2), 3),
         precipitation_p = signif(precipitation_p, 2)) %>%
  select(spec, parameters, aic_vs_preferred_p, bic_vs_preferred_p, verdict_vs_preferred_p,
         within_adj_r2_pct, added_within_r2_pct, added_within_adj_r2_pct, verdict_vs_none,
         precipitation_p, starts_with("dry"), starts_with("wet")) %>%
  knitr::kable(caption = paste0(
    main$label, ", ", nrow(p_data), " country-years, the temperature terms of the preferred ",
    "model in every row: the precipitation terms by specification; AIC and BIC against the ",
    "preferred precipitation terms (", P_REFERENCE_SPEC, ") and the ", VERDICT_NOTE,
    " against them; within adjusted R2 (%), and ",
    "what the precipitation terms add to the within R2 and within adjusted R2 (percentage points ",
    "over the model without them: within R2 ", sprintf("%.3f%%", 100 * p_none_wr2), ", adjusted ",
    sprintf("%.3f%%", 100 * p_none_war2), "), with the verdict against that model (nested: the ",
    "joint test of the precipitation terms); ",
    "effect on growth that year (pp) of a dry (-3 SD) and a wet (+3 SD) year in each unit's ",
    "horizon SD, averaged over the units of each third of long-run precipitation; *** p < 0.01, ",
    "** p < 0.05, * p < 0.1"))

# 3. Which modification matters: each factor switched with the other two fixed,
# averaged over the four pairs of the 2 x 2 x 2 design.
p_design <- P_SPECS %>%
  mutate(row = row_number()) %>%
  filter(shape %in% c("signed", "arms"), grepl("^pdm_", column))
# Signed against arms is nested (signed: the arms with b+ = -b-, in the
# deviation and in its interaction): the Wald test of the two restrictions.
signed_restriction_p <- function(m) {
  terms <- names(stats::coef(m))
  H <- rbind(as.numeric(terms %in% c("pdev_pos", "pdev_neg")),
             as.numeric(terms %in% c(interaction_name("pdev_pos", "clim_RR", terms),
                                     interaction_name("pdev_neg", "clim_RR", terms))))
  r <- H %*% stats::coef(m)
  stat <- as.numeric(t(r) %*% solve(H %*% stats::vcov(m) %*% t(H)) %*% r)
  stats::pchisq(stat, df = nrow(H), lower.tail = FALSE)
}
factor_change <- function(factor, from, to) {
  others <- setdiff(c("mean", "scale", "shape"), factor)
  pairs <- inner_join(filter(p_design, .data[[factor]] == from),
                      filter(p_design, .data[[factor]] == to), by = others,
                      suffix = c("_from", "_to"))
  bind_rows(lapply(seq_len(nrow(pairs)), function(k) {
    a <- filter(p_results, spec == pairs$spec_from[[k]])
    b <- filter(p_results, spec == pairs$spec_to[[k]])
    nested_p <- if (factor == "shape") signed_restriction_p(p_fits[[pairs$row_to[[k]]]])
    verdict <- function(cr) {
      fit_verdict(p_records[[pairs$spec_to[[k]]]], p_records[[pairs$spec_from[[k]]]], cr,
                  nested_p = nested_p)
    }
    tibble::tibble(aic_verdict = verdict("aic"), bic_verdict = verdict("bic"),
                   r2_verdict = verdict("r2"),
                   aic = b$aic[[1]] - a$aic[[1]], bic = b$bic[[1]] - a$bic[[1]],
                   war2 = 100 * (b$war2[[1]] - a$war2[[1]]),
                   abs_effect_change = mean(abs(100 * (b$estimate - a$estimate))),
                   dry_dry_change = 100 * (b$estimate[b$event == "dry" & b$third == "dry third"] -
                                             a$estimate[a$event == "dry" & a$third == "dry third"]),
                   wet_wet_change = 100 * (b$estimate[b$event == "wet" & b$third == "wet third"] -
                                             a$estimate[a$event == "wet" & a$third == "wet third"]))
  })) %>%
    summarise(change = paste(from, "->", to), pairs = n(), mean_aic_change = round(mean(aic), 1),
              aic_verdicts = paste(aic_verdict, collapse = ", "),
              mean_bic_change = round(mean(bic), 1),
              bic_changes = paste(sprintf("%+.1f", bic), collapse = ", "),
              bic_verdicts = paste(bic_verdict, collapse = ", "),
              mean_within_adj_r2_change_pct = round(mean(war2), 3),
              within_adj_r2_changes_pct = paste(sprintf("%+.3f", war2), collapse = ", "),
              r2_verdicts = paste(r2_verdict, collapse = ", "),
              mean_abs_effect_change_pp = round(mean(abs_effect_change), 2),
              dry_in_dry_change_pp = round(mean(dry_dry_change), 2),
              wet_in_wet_change_pp = round(mean(wet_wet_change), 2))
}
bind_rows(
  factor_change("mean", "fixed", "trailing"),
  factor_change("scale", "m", "sd"),
  factor_change("shape", "signed", "arms")
) %>%
  knitr::kable(caption = paste0(
    main$label, ": each modification of the precipitation terms with the other two held fixed ",
    "(the average over its four pairs in the 2 x 2 x 2 design): change in AIC and BIC (and the ",
    "BIC change of each pair), in the within adjusted R2 (percentage points, and each pair's), ",
    "each pair's verdict by each criterion (the modified model against the original: better, ",
    "worse, or indifferent when the difference cannot be told apart from noise; clustered Vuong ",
    "test, and for signed -> arms the Wald test of the restriction), mean absolute ",
    "change of the six effects (pp), and the change of the dry year in the dry third and of the ",
    "wet year in the wet third (pp)"))
```

## A spline in the climate interaction

Each arm's effect depends on the long-run climate through a linear
interaction. Does a non-linear dependence fit better? The interaction is
replaced by a restricted (natural) cubic spline of the long-run climate (Harrell
2015): the climate itself and two non-linear terms, with knots at the 5th,
35th, 65th and 95th percentiles of the units' long-run climate, linear beyond
the outer knots. The linear interaction is the spline with the non-linear
terms at zero, so the comparison is nested: the Wald test of the non-linear
terms, and AIC, BIC and the within adjusted R2. The form, the rows, the fixed
effects and the controls are those of the preferred model; the spline is
applied to temperature, to precipitation or to both, under the horizon and the
20-year deviations, on `r main$label`, and with both on every panel. The
curves show the effect of a +/-3 SD year across the long-run climate, with the
spline and with the linear interaction (95% CI), and the units' long-run
climates on the axis.

```{r climate-splines, fig.width=13, fig.height=11}
SPLINE_KNOT_PROBS <- c(0.05, 0.35, 0.65, 0.95)
# Restricted cubic spline basis of x with `knots` (Harrell): the K - 2
# non-linear terms (the linear one is x itself), scaled by the squared range
# of the knots; linear beyond the outer knots.
rcs_nonlinear <- function(x, knots) {
  K <- length(knots)
  cube <- function(z) pmax(z, 0)^3
  out <- vapply(seq_len(K - 2), function(j) {
    (cube(x - knots[[j]]) -
       cube(x - knots[[K - 1]]) * (knots[[K]] - knots[[j]]) / (knots[[K]] - knots[[K - 1]]) +
       cube(x - knots[[K]]) * (knots[[K - 1]] - knots[[j]]) / (knots[[K]] - knots[[K - 1]])) /
      (knots[[K]] - knots[[1]])^2
  }, numeric(length(x)))
  matrix(out, nrow = length(x))
}
# The knots of each variable (quantiles of the units' long-run climate), and
# the non-linear terms clim_<v>_nl<j> on the rows `d`.
spline_knots <- function(d) {
  units <- distinct(d, GID_1, clim_TM, clim_RR)
  list(TM = stats::quantile(units$clim_TM, SPLINE_KNOT_PROBS, names = FALSE),
       RR = stats::quantile(units$clim_RR, SPLINE_KNOT_PROBS, names = FALSE))
}
add_spline_terms <- function(d, knots) {
  for (v in c("TM", "RR")) {
    nl <- rcs_nonlinear(d[[paste0("clim_", v)]], knots[[v]])
    for (j in seq_len(ncol(nl))) d[[paste0("clim_", v, "_nl", j)]] <- nl[, j]
  }
  d
}
SPLINE_NONLINEAR <- length(SPLINE_KNOT_PROBS) - 2
# The preferred form's terms with the spline interaction for the variables
# `spline_vars`.
spline_terms <- function(spline_vars) {
  terms <- unlist(lapply(c("TM", "RR"), function(v) {
    arms <- paste0("dev", v, FORMS[[PREFERRED_FORM]][[v]])
    extra <- if (v %in% spline_vars) {
      as.vector(outer(arms, paste0(":clim_", v, "_nl", seq_len(SPLINE_NONLINEAR)), paste0))
    }
    c(arms, paste0(arms, ":clim_", v), extra)
  }))
  c(terms, CONTROLS)
}
SPLINE_MODELS <- list("linear" = character(0), "spline T" = "TM", "spline P" = "RR",
                      "spline T and P" = c("TM", "RR"))
spline_tests <- function(d, label) {
  fits <- lapply(SPLINE_MODELS, function(vars) fit_model(spline_terms(vars), d))
  stopifnot(length(unique(vapply(fits, stats::nobs, 0))) == 1)
  list(fits = fits, table = bind_rows(lapply(names(fits), function(k) {
    m <- fits[[k]]
    nonlinear_p <- function(v) {
      if (v %in% SPLINE_MODELS[[k]]) wald_p(m, paste0("clim_", v, "_nl")) else NA_real_
    }
    added_p <- if (length(SPLINE_MODELS[[k]])) {
      wald_p(m, paste0("clim_(", paste(SPLINE_MODELS[[k]], collapse = "|"), ")_nl"))
    }
    tibble::tibble(panel = label, model = k,
                   aic_vs_linear = stats::AIC(m) - stats::AIC(fits$linear),
                   bic_vs_linear = stats::BIC(m) - stats::BIC(fits$linear),
                   within_adj_r2_pct = 100 * fixest::fitstat(m, "war2")[[1]],
                   verdict_vs_linear = if (is.null(added_p)) "" else {
                     fit_verdicts(m, fits$linear, nested_p = added_p)
                   },
                   T_nonlinear_p = nonlinear_p("TM"), P_nonlinear_p = nonlinear_p("RR"))
  })))
}

# 1. PWT x ERA5, horizon and 20-year deviations.
spline_main <- lapply(c(Horizon = "Horizon", "20-year" = "20-year"), function(def) {
  d <- add_deviation_terms(main$clean, DEFINITIONS[[def]])
  knots <- spline_knots(d)
  d <- add_spline_terms(d, knots)
  c(spline_tests(d, paste0(main$label, ", ", def)), list(knots = knots, data = d))
})
bind_rows(lapply(spline_main, `[[`, "table")) %>%
  mutate(across(c(aic_vs_linear, bic_vs_linear), ~ round(.x, 1)),
         within_adj_r2_pct = round(within_adj_r2_pct, 3),
         across(ends_with("_p"), ~ signif(.x, 2))) %>%
  knitr::kable(caption = paste0(
    main$label, ", ", PREFERRED_FORM, ": the climate interaction linear or a restricted cubic ",
    "spline (knots at the ", paste(100 * SPLINE_KNOT_PROBS, collapse = ", "), "th percentiles ",
    "of the units' long-run climate; T: ", paste(sprintf("%.1f", spline_main$Horizon$knots$TM),
                                                collapse = ", "), " C; P: ",
    paste(sprintf("%.2f", spline_main$Horizon$knots$RR), collapse = ", "), " m), AIC and BIC ",
    "against the linear interaction, within adjusted R2 (%), the spline's ", VERDICT_NOTE,
    " against the linear interaction (nested: the joint test of its non-linear terms), and ",
    "the Wald test (p) of the non-linear terms of each variable"))

# 2. Every panel, the preferred definition, spline for both.
bind_rows(lapply(c(national_panels, list(dose)), function(p) {
  d <- add_deviation_terms(p$clean, PREFERRED_SUFFIX)
  d <- add_spline_terms(d, spline_knots(d))
  spline_tests(d, p$label)$table %>% filter(model == "spline T and P")
})) %>%
  transmute(panel, aic_vs_linear = round(aic_vs_linear, 1), bic_vs_linear = round(bic_vs_linear, 1),
            verdict_vs_linear,
            T_nonlinear_p = signif(T_nonlinear_p, 2), P_nonlinear_p = signif(P_nonlinear_p, 2)) %>%
  knitr::kable(caption = paste0(
    "Every panel, ", PREFERRED_FORM, ", ", PREFERRED_DEFINITION, " deviations: the spline ",
    "interaction for both variables against the linear one (AIC, BIC, and the ", VERDICT_NOTE,
    ") and the Wald tests (p) of the non-linear terms"))

# 3. Effect curves, spline (both) against linear, PWT x ERA5.
SPLINE_EVENTS <- tibble::tribble(
  ~variable, ~deviation, ~event,
  "TM", 3, "T +3 SD", "TM", -3, "T -3 SD", "RR", -3, "P -3 SD", "RR", 3, "P +3 SD"
)
spline_curve <- function(fit, v, x, climates, knots, spline) {
  terms <- names(stats::coef(fit))
  nl <- rcs_nonlinear(climates, knots)
  G <- t(vapply(seq_along(climates), function(i) {
    w <- stats::setNames(numeric(length(terms)), terms)
    for (s in FORMS[[PREFERRED_FORM]][[v]]) {
      arm <- paste0("dev", v, s)
      value <- term_value(s, x)
      w[[arm]] <- value
      w[[interaction_name(arm, paste0("clim_", v), terms)]] <- value * climates[[i]]
      if (spline) for (j in seq_len(ncol(nl))) {
        w[[interaction_name(arm, paste0("clim_", v, "_nl", j), terms)]] <- value * nl[i, j]
      }
    }
    w
  }, numeric(length(terms))))
  colnames(G) <- terms
  linear_combination(fit, G) %>% mutate(climate = climates)
}
spline_curves <- bind_rows(lapply(names(spline_main), function(def) {
  run <- spline_main[[def]]
  units <- distinct(run$data, GID_1, clim_TM, clim_RR)
  bind_rows(lapply(seq_len(nrow(SPLINE_EVENTS)), function(i) {
    e <- SPLINE_EVENTS[i, ]
    unit_climate <- units[[paste0("clim_", e$variable)]]
    climates <- seq(min(unit_climate), max(unit_climate), length.out = 80)
    bind_rows(
      spline_curve(run$fits$linear, e$variable, e$deviation, climates, run$knots[[e$variable]],
                   FALSE) %>% mutate(interaction = "linear"),
      spline_curve(run$fits[["spline T and P"]], e$variable, e$deviation, climates,
                   run$knots[[e$variable]], TRUE) %>% mutate(interaction = "spline")
    ) %>%
      mutate(panel = paste0(e$event, ", ", def), event = e$event, definition = def)
  }))
}))
rug_data <- bind_rows(lapply(names(spline_main), function(def) {
  units <- distinct(spline_main[[def]]$data, GID_1, clim_TM, clim_RR)
  bind_rows(lapply(seq_len(nrow(SPLINE_EVENTS)), function(i) {
    e <- SPLINE_EVENTS[i, ]
    tibble::tibble(panel = paste0(e$event, ", ", def),
                   climate = units[[paste0("clim_", e$variable)]])
  }))
}))
panel_levels <- unique(spline_curves$panel)
ggplot(mutate(spline_curves, panel = factor(panel, levels = panel_levels)),
       aes(climate, 100 * estimate, colour = interaction, fill = interaction)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, colour = GRID_MUTED, linewidth = 0.3) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = 100 * conf_low, ymax = 100 * conf_high), alpha = 0.12, colour = NA) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.8) +
  geom_rug(data = mutate(rug_data, panel = factor(panel, levels = panel_levels)),
           aes(x = climate), inherit.aes = FALSE, sides = "b", alpha = 0.4, colour = GRID_MUTED) +
  facet_wrap(~panel, ncol = 2, scales = "free") +
  scale_colour_manual(values = grid_colours(c("linear", "spline")), name = "Climate interaction") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = grid_colours(c("linear", "spline")), guide = "none") +
  labs(x = "Long-run climate (C, or m a year)", y = "Effect on growth that year (pp)",
       title = "Effect of a +/-3 SD year across the long-run climate: linear or spline interaction",
       subtitle = paste(strwrap(paste0(
         main$label, ", ", PREFERRED_FORM, "; spline for both variables (knots at the ",
         paste(100 * SPLINE_KNOT_PROBS, collapse = ", "), "th percentiles of the units' long-run ",
         "climate); bands: 95% CI; ticks: the units' long-run climates."), 150),
         collapse = "\n")) +
  theme_results()
```

## A spline in the interaction of the level model

The same question without deviations or arms: temperature and precipitation
in levels (°C and metres), each interacted with the unit's long-run climate
(the horizon mean), signed:

```text
growth = a T + T x s_T(mean T) + c P + P x s_P(mean P) + controls + FE

linear interaction   s(m) = b m
spline               s(m) = b m + two non-linear terms (restricted cubic spline, the knots of the section above)
```

With the unit effects and trends, the variation of `T` is that of each unit
around its own trend, so `a + s(m)` is the effect on growth of a year 1 °C
warmer than usual in a unit with long-run temperature m (the same for
precipitation, per metre), equal and opposite for a colder year: no SD
scaling and no separate arms. The standard BHM terms, `T` and `T^2`, imply an
effect that is linear in the temperature, `b1 + 2 b2 T`, so the linear
interaction is close to what BHM imposes, and the spline tests it. The linear
interaction is the spline with the non-linear terms at zero: the test is the
clustered Wald test of those terms, with AIC, BIC and the within adjusted R2
and their verdicts. On `r main$label`, with the spline for temperature, for
precipitation and for both; with both, on every panel; and the curves of the
effect across the long-run climate under the linear interaction and the
spline (95% CI). The rows, controls and fixed effects are those of the
preferred model.

```{r level-splines, fig.width=12, fig.height=5}
# The level terms of each variable, with its interaction with the long-run
# climate linear, or a spline for the variables `spline_vars`.
level_spline_terms <- function(spline_vars) {
  terms <- unlist(lapply(c("TM", "RR"), function(v) {
    extra <- if (v %in% spline_vars) paste0(v, ":clim_", v, "_nl", seq_len(SPLINE_NONLINEAR))
    c(v, paste0(v, ":clim_", v), extra)
  }))
  c(terms, CONTROLS)
}
level_spline_tests <- function(d, label) {
  fits <- lapply(SPLINE_MODELS, function(vars) fit_model(level_spline_terms(vars), d))
  stopifnot(length(unique(vapply(fits, stats::nobs, 0))) == 1)
  list(fits = fits, table = bind_rows(lapply(names(fits), function(k) {
    m <- fits[[k]]
    nonlinear_p <- function(v) {
      if (v %in% SPLINE_MODELS[[k]]) wald_p(m, paste0("clim_", v, "_nl")) else NA_real_
    }
    added_p <- if (length(SPLINE_MODELS[[k]])) {
      wald_p(m, paste0("clim_(", paste(SPLINE_MODELS[[k]], collapse = "|"), ")_nl"))
    }
    tibble::tibble(panel = label, model = k,
                   aic_vs_linear = stats::AIC(m) - stats::AIC(fits$linear),
                   bic_vs_linear = stats::BIC(m) - stats::BIC(fits$linear),
                   within_adj_r2_pct = 100 * fixest::fitstat(m, "war2")[[1]],
                   verdict_vs_linear = if (is.null(added_p)) "" else {
                     fit_verdicts(m, fits$linear, nested_p = added_p)
                   },
                   T_nonlinear_p = nonlinear_p("TM"), P_nonlinear_p = nonlinear_p("RR"),
                   T_terms_p = wald_p(m, "^TM(:|$)|:TM$"), P_terms_p = wald_p(m, "^RR(:|$)|:RR$"))
  })))
}
level_data <- function(p) {
  d <- add_deviation_terms(p$clean, DEFINITIONS[["Horizon"]])
  knots <- spline_knots(d)
  list(data = add_spline_terms(d, knots), knots = knots)
}

# 1. PWT x ERA5: the spline for temperature, for precipitation and for both.
level_main_data <- level_data(main)
level_main <- level_spline_tests(level_main_data$data, main$label)
level_main$table %>%
  mutate(across(c(aic_vs_linear, bic_vs_linear), ~ round(.x, 1)),
         within_adj_r2_pct = round(within_adj_r2_pct, 3),
         across(ends_with("_p"), ~ signif(.x, 2))) %>%
  knitr::kable(caption = paste0(
    main$label, ", levels of T and P interacted with the long-run climate: the interaction ",
    "linear or a restricted cubic spline (knots at the ",
    paste(100 * SPLINE_KNOT_PROBS, collapse = ", "), "th percentiles of the units' long-run ",
    "climate); AIC and BIC against the linear interaction, within adjusted R2 (%), the ",
    "spline's ", VERDICT_NOTE, " against the linear interaction (nested: the joint test of ",
    "its non-linear terms), the Wald tests (p) of the non-linear terms of each variable, and ",
    "of all the terms of each variable"))

# 2. Every panel: the spline for both variables against the linear interaction.
bind_rows(lapply(c(national_panels, list(dose)), function(p) {
  level_spline_tests(level_data(p)$data, p$label)$table %>%
    filter(model %in% c("linear", "spline T and P"))
})) %>%
  group_by(panel) %>%
  summarise(linear_T_terms_p = signif(T_terms_p[model == "linear"], 2),
            linear_P_terms_p = signif(P_terms_p[model == "linear"], 2),
            aic_vs_linear = round(aic_vs_linear[model == "spline T and P"], 1),
            bic_vs_linear = round(bic_vs_linear[model == "spline T and P"], 1),
            verdict_vs_linear = verdict_vs_linear[model == "spline T and P"],
            T_nonlinear_p = signif(T_nonlinear_p[model == "spline T and P"], 2),
            P_nonlinear_p = signif(P_nonlinear_p[model == "spline T and P"], 2), .groups = "drop") %>%
  arrange(match(panel, vapply(c(national_panels, list(dose)), `[[`, "", "label"))) %>%
  knitr::kable(caption = paste0(
    "Every panel, levels of T and P interacted with the long-run climate: joint tests (p) of ",
    "each variable's terms with the linear interaction; the spline for both variables against ",
    "the linear interaction (AIC, BIC, and the ", VERDICT_NOTE, "); and the Wald tests (p) of ",
    "the non-linear terms"))

# 3. The effect of a warmer (wetter) year across the long-run climate, PWT x ERA5.
level_curve <- function(fit, v, climates, knots, spline) {
  terms <- names(stats::coef(fit))
  nl <- rcs_nonlinear(climates, knots)
  G <- t(vapply(seq_along(climates), function(i) {
    w <- stats::setNames(numeric(length(terms)), terms)
    w[[v]] <- 1
    w[[interaction_name(v, paste0("clim_", v), terms)]] <- climates[[i]]
    if (spline) for (j in seq_len(ncol(nl))) {
      w[[interaction_name(v, paste0("clim_", v, "_nl", j), terms)]] <- nl[i, j]
    }
    w
  }, numeric(length(terms))))
  colnames(G) <- terms
  linear_combination(fit, G) %>% mutate(climate = climates)
}
# pp of growth per 1 C, and per 0.1 m of precipitation.
LEVEL_EVENTS <- tibble::tribble(
  ~variable, ~scale, ~event,
  "TM", 100, "A year 1 °C warmer, by long-run temperature (°C)",
  "RR", 10, "A year 100 mm wetter, by long-run precipitation (m a year)"
)
level_units <- distinct(level_main_data$data, GID_1, clim_TM, clim_RR)
level_curves <- bind_rows(lapply(seq_len(nrow(LEVEL_EVENTS)), function(i) {
  e <- LEVEL_EVENTS[i, ]
  unit_climate <- level_units[[paste0("clim_", e$variable)]]
  climates <- seq(min(unit_climate), max(unit_climate), length.out = 80)
  bind_rows(
    level_curve(level_main$fits$linear, e$variable, climates, level_main_data$knots[[e$variable]],
                FALSE) %>% mutate(interaction = "linear"),
    level_curve(level_main$fits[["spline T and P"]], e$variable, climates,
                level_main_data$knots[[e$variable]], TRUE) %>% mutate(interaction = "spline")
  ) %>%
    mutate(across(c(estimate, conf_low, conf_high), ~ e$scale * .x), event = e$event)
}))
level_rug <- bind_rows(lapply(seq_len(nrow(LEVEL_EVENTS)), function(i) {
  tibble::tibble(event = LEVEL_EVENTS$event[[i]],
                 climate = level_units[[paste0("clim_", LEVEL_EVENTS$variable[[i]])]])
}))
ggplot(mutate(level_curves, event = factor(event, levels = LEVEL_EVENTS$event)),
       aes(climate, estimate, colour = interaction, fill = interaction)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, colour = GRID_MUTED, linewidth = 0.3) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = conf_low, ymax = conf_high), alpha = 0.12, colour = NA) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.8) +
  geom_rug(data = mutate(level_rug, event = factor(event, levels = LEVEL_EVENTS$event)),
           aes(x = climate), inherit.aes = FALSE, sides = "b", alpha = 0.4, colour = GRID_MUTED) +
  facet_wrap(~event, ncol = 2, scales = "free") +
  scale_colour_manual(values = grid_colours(c("linear", "spline")), name = "Climate interaction") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = grid_colours(c("linear", "spline")), guide = "none") +
  labs(x = "Long-run climate", y = "Effect on growth that year (pp)",
       title = "Level model: the effect of a warmer or wetter year across the long-run climate",
       subtitle = paste(strwrap(paste0(
         main$label, ", T and P in levels interacted with the long-run climate, linear or a ",
         "spline for both variables (knots at the ",
         paste(100 * SPLINE_KNOT_PROBS, collapse = ", "), "th percentiles of the units' ",
         "long-run climate); bands: 95% CI; ticks: the units' long-run climates."), 150),
         collapse = "\n")) +
  theme_results()
```

## Binned response of the preferred model

The preferred deviations by quarter of the long-run climate of the
interactions (the quartiles of `clim_TM` and `clim_RR` over the sample):

- bins: 0.5 SD bins of the deviation within each quarter, centred on zero, with
  the tails pooled until they hold 10 countries; the bin containing zero is the
  quarter's reference. One model per variable: its bins, the other variable in
  signed + quadratic arms (interacted with its long-run mean), and the controls;
- curves: the signed and preferred forms, estimated once on the whole sample
  (no quarter terms) and evaluated at the quarter's mean long-run climate,
  relative to their mean over the quarter's reference-bin observations.

```{r binned-helpers}
BIN_WIDTH <- 0.5
MIN_COUNTRIES <- 10L
VARIABLE_LABELS <- c(TM = "Temperature", RR = "Precipitation")
QUARTER_NAMES <- list(TM = c("coldest", "cool", "warm", "hottest"),
                      RR = c("driest", "dry", "wet", "wettest"))
CLIMATE_UNITS <- c(TM = "°C", RR = "m")
CLIMATE_DIGITS <- c(TM = 1L, RR = 2L)
# The other variable's terms in the bin models: signed + quadratic arms.
ENCOMPASSING <- c("", "_pos2", "_neg2")
wrap_text <- function(x, width) paste(strwrap(x, width = width), collapse = "\n")

# Quarter of each variable's long-run climate and bins of its deviation within
# each quarter (ids "<quarter>_<index>"), with each bin's size and mean deviation.
add_quarter_bins <- function(model_data) {
  quarters <- list()
  bins <- list()
  for (v in names(VARIABLE_LABELS)) {
    climate <- model_data[[paste0("clim_", v)]]
    breaks <- stats::quantile(climate, seq(0, 1, 0.25), names = FALSE)
    quarter <- as.integer(cut(climate, breaks, include.lowest = TRUE))
    dev <- model_data[[paste0("dev", v)]]
    k_max <- ceiling((max(abs(dev)) + BIN_WIDTH / 2) / BIN_WIDTH)
    edges <- seq(-BIN_WIDTH / 2 - k_max * BIN_WIDTH, BIN_WIDTH / 2 + k_max * BIN_WIDTH,
                 by = BIN_WIDTH)
    bin <- character(nrow(model_data))
    for (q in 1:4) {
      rows <- quarter == q
      q_breaks <- pool_tails(dev[rows], edges, model_data$GID_0[rows], MIN_COUNTRIES)
      bin[rows] <- sprintf("%d_%02d", q, as.integer(cut(dev[rows], q_breaks,
                                                        include.lowest = TRUE)))
      reference <- sprintf("%d_%02d", q, as.integer(cut(0, q_breaks)))
      bins[[length(bins) + 1]] <- tibble::tibble(
        variable = v, quarter = q, bin = bin[rows], deviation = dev[rows],
        GID_0 = model_data$GID_0[rows]
      ) %>%
        group_by(variable, quarter, bin) %>%
        summarise(observations = n(), countries = n_distinct(GID_0),
                  mean_deviation = mean(deviation), .groups = "drop") %>%
        mutate(reference = bin == !!reference)
    }
    model_data[[paste0(v, "_quarter")]] <- quarter
    model_data[[paste0(v, "_bin")]] <- bin
    fmt <- function(x) formatC(x, format = "f", digits = CLIMATE_DIGITS[[v]])
    # Outside tibble(), whose `quarter` column would mask the vector.
    mean_climate <- as.numeric(tapply(climate, quarter, mean))
    quarters[[v]] <- tibble::tibble(
      variable = v, quarter = 1:4, mean_climate = mean_climate,
      label = sprintf("%s, %s quarter\n%s to %s %s; curves at the mean, %s %s",
                      VARIABLE_LABELS[[v]], QUARTER_NAMES[[v]], fmt(breaks[-5]),
                      fmt(breaks[-1]), CLIMATE_UNITS[[v]], fmt(mean_climate),
                      CLIMATE_UNITS[[v]])
    )
  }
  list(data = model_data, quarters = bind_rows(quarters), bins = bind_rows(bins))
}

# Effect of the interacted form with `suffixes` of variable v at long-run
# climate m and deviations `devs`, relative to its mean over `ref_devs`.
form_curve <- function(model, v, suffixes, m, devs, ref_devs) {
  terms <- names(stats::coef(model))
  G <- t(vapply(devs, function(x) {
    w <- stats::setNames(numeric(length(terms)), terms)
    for (s in suffixes) {
      term <- paste0("dev", v, s)
      value <- term_value(s, x) - mean(term_value(s, ref_devs))
      w[[term]] <- value
      w[[interaction_name(term, paste0("clim_", v), terms)]] <- value * m
    }
    w
  }, numeric(length(terms))))
  colnames(G) <- terms
  linear_combination(model, G) %>% mutate(deviation = devs)
}

# Bins by quarter of long-run climate against the interacted `forms`, both
# variables, on common axes.
plot_binned_response <- function(model_data, forms, title, note, caption) {
  qb <- add_quarter_bins(model_data)
  d <- qb$data
  models <- lapply(FORMS[forms], function(s) fit_model(form_terms(s), d))
  bins <- list()
  curves <- list()
  for (v in names(VARIABLE_LABELS)) {
    other <- setdiff(names(VARIABLE_LABELS), v)
    other_terms <- paste0("dev", other, ENCOMPASSING)
    references <- qb$bins %>% filter(variable == v, reference) %>% pull(bin)
    bin_term <- sprintf("i(%s_bin, ref = c(%s))", v,
                        paste0("'", references, "'", collapse = ", "))
    m_bins <- fit_model(c(bin_term, other_terms,
                          paste0(other_terms, ":clim_", other), CONTROLS), d)
    prefix <- paste0(v, "_bin::")
    estimates <- tidy_fixest(m_bins) %>%
      filter(startsWith(term, prefix)) %>%
      mutate(bin = sub(prefix, "", term, fixed = TRUE))
    bins[[v]] <- qb$bins %>%
      filter(variable == v) %>%
      left_join(select(estimates, bin, estimate, conf_low, conf_high), by = "bin") %>%
      mutate(across(c(estimate, conf_low, conf_high), ~ ifelse(reference, 0, .x)))

    dev <- d[[paste0("dev", v)]]
    for (q in 1:4) {
      rows <- d[[paste0(v, "_quarter")]] == q
      ref_devs <- dev[rows & d[[paste0(v, "_bin")]] %in% references]
      grid <- seq(min(dev[rows]), max(dev[rows]), length.out = 100)
      m <- qb$quarters$mean_climate[qb$quarters$variable == v & qb$quarters$quarter == q]
      for (f in names(models)) {
        curves[[length(curves) + 1]] <-
          form_curve(models[[f]], v, FORMS[[f]][[v]], m, grid, ref_devs) %>%
          mutate(variable = v, quarter = q, form = f)
      }
    }
  }

  facet_of <- function(variable, quarter) {
    factor(qb$quarters$label[match(paste(variable, quarter),
                                   paste(qb$quarters$variable, qb$quarters$quarter))],
           levels = qb$quarters$label)
  }
  bins <- bind_rows(bins) %>%
    mutate(facet = facet_of(variable, quarter),
           across(c(estimate, conf_low, conf_high), ~ 100 * .x))
  curves <- bind_rows(curves) %>%
    mutate(facet = facet_of(variable, quarter), form = factor(form, levels = names(models)),
           across(c(estimate, conf_low, conf_high), ~ 100 * .x))

  ggplot() +
    geom_hline(yintercept = 0, colour = GRID_MUTED, linewidth = 0.3) +
    geom_vline(xintercept = 0, colour = GRID_MUTED, linewidth = 0.3) +
    geom_line(data = curves, aes(deviation, estimate, colour = form), linewidth = 0.9) +
    geom_linerange(data = filter(bins, !reference),
                   aes(mean_deviation, ymin = conf_low, ymax = conf_high),
                   colour = GRID_INK, linewidth = 0.5) +
    geom_point(data = bins, aes(mean_deviation, estimate, shape = reference),
               colour = GRID_INK, fill = "white", size = 2.2) +
    # Common axes across all panels.
    facet_wrap(~facet, nrow = 2) +
    scale_colour_manual(values = grid_colours(names(FORMS))[names(models)], name = NULL) +
    scale_shape_manual(values = c(`FALSE` = 16, `TRUE` = 21),
                       labels = c(`FALSE` = "Deviation bin (95% CI)", `TRUE` = "Reference bin"),
                       name = NULL) +
    guides(colour = guide_legend(nrow = 1, order = 1), shape = guide_legend(order = 2)) +
    labs(
      x = "Deviation (SD)",
      y = "Effect on growth that year (pp), relative to the reference bin",
      title = title,
      subtitle = wrap_text(paste0(
        note, " Top: temperature, by quarter of long-run temperature; bottom: ",
        "precipitation, by quarter of long-run precipitation. Bins of ", BIN_WIDTH,
        " SD centred on zero (points at the bin's mean deviation; tails pooled to ",
        MIN_COUNTRIES, " countries). Curves: the forms interacted with the long-run ",
        "climate, estimated on the whole sample and evaluated at the quarter's mean ",
        "long-run climate, relative to the reference bin. Common axes."), 175),
      caption = wrap_text(caption, 175)
    ) +
    theme_results()
}

panel_caption <- function(panel) {
  paste0(panel$label, ", ", CLIMATE_WEIGHT, " ", CLIMATE_WEIGHT_YEAR, " weights, ",
         min(panel$clean$year), "-", max(panel$clean$year), "; controls: conflict ",
         "(minor, war), post-Soviet and post-Yugoslav collapse dummies; ",
         nrow(panel$outliers), " growth outliers not involving weather dropped. ",
         "Demeaned deviations; fixed effects year + unit + unit linear and quadratic trends; ",
         "errors clustered by country.")
}
```

```{r binned-preferred, fig.width=15, fig.height=8.5}
plot_binned_response(
  add_deviation_terms(main$clean, PREFERRED_SUFFIX),
  forms = c("Signed", PREFERRED_FORM),
  title = paste0("PWT x ERA5, ", PREFERRED_DEFINITION, " deviations: bins against signed and ",
                 tolower(PREFERRED_FORM)),
  note = paste0("dT from mean_TM_", PREFERRED_SUFFIX[["TM"]], ", dP from mean_RR_",
                PREFERRED_SUFFIX[["RR"]], " (in the matching SDs); interactions with mean_TM_",
                PREFERRED_SUFFIX[["clim_TM"]], " and mean_RR_", PREFERRED_SUFFIX[["clim_RR"]],
                "."),
  caption = panel_caption(main)
)
```

# Robustness across national and climate datasets

The preferred model (and the signed form, for comparison) on every national
panel: PWT and World Bank GDP per capita (both at constant prices) with ERA5,
CRU TS and UDelaware climate. Each panel has its own horizon, long-run
climate, sample and outliers.

- (a) Joint Wald tests of all temperature terms and of all precipitation terms
  of the preferred model, and of the precipitation terms of the signed form.
- (b) and (c) The effect of a deviation of +3 SD and of -3 SD, against a normal
  year, for a unit with a long-run temperature of 5, 15 or 25 °C and a
  long-run precipitation of 0.5, 1.5 or 3 m a year. With arms, the +3 SD effect
  depends only on the positive arm and the -3 SD effect only on the negative
  one, so (b) is which of these effects are significant. The range of the
  long-run climate across the units of each panel shows how far inside the
  data each of these climates is.

Each panel is estimated separately, on its own rows: its years, its long-run
climate and demeaning, and the common exclusions. Table (a) also compares the
preferred model with the signed form on the same rows (AIC difference and
verdict): the signed form is the same deviation without separate arms, so
the comparison is what the arms add. The figure shows every effect of (c) with
its 95% confidence interval, one row per panel: rows are the variable and the
sign of the deviation, columns the long-run climate. An effect is robust when
its sign and size agree across the six panels, not only when it is significant
in one.

```{r robustness-helpers}
# The preferred and signed models on a panel, with its deviation data.
fit_robustness <- function(panel) {
  d <- add_deviation_terms(panel$clean, PREFERRED_SUFFIX)
  list(
    panel = panel, data = d,
    preferred = fit_model(form_terms(FORMS[[PREFERRED_FORM]]), d),
    signed = fit_model(form_terms(FORMS[["Signed"]]), d)
  )
}

# (a) joint tests.
joint_tests <- function(fit) {
  wald_p <- function(m, pattern) fixest::wald(m, keep = pattern, print = FALSE)$p
  panel_summary(fit$panel) %>%
    select(panel, first_year, last_year, countries, units, outliers_dropped) %>%
    mutate(
      observations = stats::nobs(fit$preferred),
      temperature_p = wald_p(fit$preferred, "^devTM"),
      precipitation_p = wald_p(fit$preferred, "^devRR"),
      precipitation_p_signed = wald_p(fit$signed, "^devRR"),
      aic_vs_signed = stats::AIC(fit$preferred) - stats::AIC(fit$signed),
      verdict_vs_signed = fit_verdicts(fit$preferred, fit$signed)
    )
}

# (c) one table per variable: rows panel x deviation, columns long-run
# climates, effect [95% CI] in pp.
effects_table <- function(effects, v) {
  effects %>%
    filter(variable == v) %>%
    mutate(cell = sprintf("%+.2f [%+.2f, %+.2f]%s", 100 * estimate, 100 * conf_low,
                          100 * conf_high, stars(p_value)),
           deviation = sprintf("%+d SD", deviation)) %>%
    select(panel, deviation, level, cell) %>%
    tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = level, values_from = cell) %>%
    mutate(panel = factor(panel, levels = unique(panel))) %>%
    arrange(panel, deviation)
}

# Range of the long-run climate of the interactions across the units (countries
# or regions) of each panel; a trailing mean is averaged over the unit's years.
climate_support <- function(fits) {
  bind_rows(lapply(fits, function(fit) {
    units <- fit$data %>%
      group_by(GID_1) %>%
      summarise(clim_TM = mean(clim_TM), clim_RR = mean(clim_RR), .groups = "drop")
    bind_rows(lapply(c("TM", "RR"), function(v) {
      q <- stats::quantile(units[[paste0("clim_", v)]], c(0, 0.1, 0.5, 0.9, 1),
                           names = FALSE)
      tibble::tibble(panel = fit$panel$label,
                     variable = paste0(VARIABLE_LABELS[[v]], " (", CLIMATE_UNITS[[v]], ")"),
                     units = nrow(units), min = q[1], p10 = q[2], median = q[3], p90 = q[4],
                     max = q[5])
    }))
  })) %>%
    mutate(across(c(min, p10, median, p90, max), ~ round(.x, 2))) %>%
    arrange(variable)
}

PLOT_COLUMNS <- paste(EVAL_LABELS$TM, "/", EVAL_LABELS$RR)
plot_effects <- function(effects, title) {
  effects %>%
    mutate(
      row = factor(sprintf("%s, %+d SD", VARIABLE_LABELS[variable], deviation),
                   levels = c("Temperature, +3 SD", "Temperature, -3 SD",
                              "Precipitation, +3 SD", "Precipitation, -3 SD")),
      column = factor(PLOT_COLUMNS[level_index], levels = PLOT_COLUMNS),
      panel = factor(panel, levels = rev(unique(panel))),
      across(c(estimate, conf_low, conf_high), ~ 100 * .x)
    ) %>%
    ggplot(aes(estimate, panel)) +
    geom_vline(xintercept = 0, colour = GRID_MUTED, linewidth = 0.3) +
    geom_linerange(aes(xmin = conf_low, xmax = conf_high), colour = GRID_PALETTE[[1]],
                   linewidth = 0.6) +
    geom_point(colour = GRID_PALETTE[[1]], size = 2) +
    facet_grid(row ~ column) +
    labs(x = "Effect on growth that year (pp), against a normal year; 95% CI", y = NULL,
         title = title,
         subtitle = paste0(PREFERRED_FORM, ", ", PREFERRED_DEFINITION, " deviations; at ",
                           "long-run climates of 5, 15 and 25 °C (temperature) and 0.5, 1.5 ",
                           "and 3 m a year (precipitation).")) +
    theme_results() +
    theme(panel.grid.major.x = element_line(colour = "#e6e5df", linewidth = 0.3))
}
```

```{r robustness-national}
national_fits <- lapply(national_panels, fit_robustness)
national_effects <- bind_rows(lapply(national_fits, climate_effects))

bind_rows(lapply(national_fits, joint_tests)) %>%
  mutate(across(c(temperature_p, precipitation_p, precipitation_p_signed), ~ signif(.x, 2)),
         aic_vs_signed = round(aic_vs_signed, 1)) %>%
  knitr::kable(caption = paste("(a) Joint Wald tests of the preferred model (temperature,",
                               "precipitation) and of the signed form (precipitation); AIC of the",
                               "preferred model minus the signed form, and the preferred model's",
                               VERDICT_NOTE, "against the signed form"))

significance_map(national_effects) %>%
  knitr::kable(caption = paste("(b) Effect of a +/-3 SD deviation at long-run climates of 5, 15,",
                               "25 °C and 0.5, 1.5, 3 m (pp); *** p < 0.01, ** p < 0.05, * p < 0.1"))

climate_support(national_fits) %>%
  knitr::kable(caption = "Long-run climate across the countries of each panel")

effects_table(national_effects, "TM") %>%
  knitr::kable(caption = paste("(c) Temperature: effect of a +/-3 SD deviation (pp, 95% CI) at",
                               "long-run temperatures of 5, 15 and 25 °C"))
effects_table(national_effects, "RR") %>%
  knitr::kable(caption = paste("(c) Precipitation: effect of a +/-3 SD deviation (pp, 95% CI) at",
                               "long-run precipitation of 0.5, 1.5 and 3 m a year"))
```

# Subnational data (DOSE)

The same model on DOSE v2.14 regional GDP per capita (GADM1) with ERA5 climate
(population-density weights at base year 2000, aggregated to the regions):
GDP per capita at constant 2015 local prices converted at the fixed 2015
exchange rate (`lcu2015_usd`; its growth is constant-local-price growth, free
of exchange-rate movements). Region fixed effects and region linear and
quadratic trends (and the deviations demeaned by region);
the conflict and collapse controls are national; the dropped outliers are the
national country-years of the shared specification, dropped in every region of
the country; errors are clustered by country.

```{r subnational}
dose_fit <- fit_robustness(dose)
dose_effects <- climate_effects(dose_fit)

joint_tests(dose_fit) %>%
  mutate(across(c(temperature_p, precipitation_p, precipitation_p_signed), ~ signif(.x, 2)),
         aic_vs_signed = round(aic_vs_signed, 1)) %>%
  knitr::kable(caption = paste("(a) DOSE x ERA5: joint Wald tests, and the preferred model's",
                               VERDICT_NOTE, "against the signed form"))

etable(list("Signed" = dose_fit$signed, "Preferred" = dose_fit$preferred), dict = DICT,
       drop = DROP, order = ORDER, fitstat = FITSTAT, title = "DOSE x ERA5")

significance_map(dose_effects) %>%
  knitr::kable(caption = paste("(b) DOSE x ERA5: effect of a +/-3 SD deviation at long-run",
                               "climates of 5, 15, 25 °C and 0.5, 1.5, 3 m (pp); *** p < 0.01,",
                               "** p < 0.05, * p < 0.1"))
climate_support(list(dose_fit)) %>%
  knitr::kable(caption = "Long-run climate across the DOSE regions")
effects_table(dose_effects, "TM") %>%
  knitr::kable(caption = "(c) DOSE x ERA5, temperature: effect of a +/-3 SD deviation (pp, 95% CI)")
effects_table(dose_effects, "RR") %>%
  knitr::kable(caption = "(c) DOSE x ERA5, precipitation: effect of a +/-3 SD deviation (pp, 95% CI)")
```

```{r subnational-plot, fig.width=12, fig.height=9}
             "Effect of a +/-3 SD deviation: national panels and DOSE regions")
```
