# PWT and World Bank on identical samples

The PWT and World Bank panels differ in their GDP series, but also in their
country-years (each has years and countries the other lacks), and their
climate terms differ slightly too: the horizon moments and the demeaning of
the deviations are computed over each panel's own years. To tell measurement
from coverage, the preferred model (`r PREFERRED_FORM`, `r PREFERRED_DEFINITION`
deviations) goes from PWT to the World Bank one change at a time, with every
climate dataset:

```text
A  PWT, its sample
B  PWT growth, the country-years of both samples                    A -> B: PWT-only rows out
C  World Bank growth, the same rows and the PWT climate terms        B -> C: the GDP series only
D  World Bank growth, the same rows and the World Bank climate terms C -> D: normalization periods
E  World Bank, its sample                                            D -> E: World Bank-only rows in
```

In B, C and D the country-years, the exclusions (the growth outliers of
both samples) and the controls are the same; B to C changes the GDP series
alone, so it is the measurement difference; A to B and D to E are the sample
composition; C to D the normalization periods of the climate terms.

Three tables, for each climate dataset: the overlap of the two samples
(country-years in both, only in PWT and only in the World Bank, with the
countries that account for most of them) and, on the common rows, how closely
the two growth series agree (correlation, mean absolute difference, share of
country-years differing by more than 2 pp, and their SDs); the five fits of
the chain, with the joint tests and the effects of a +/-3 SD year; and the
change of each effect at each step, which adds up to the total difference
between the two panels. The steps are not a unique decomposition (their sizes
depend on the order), but B to C isolates the GDP series exactly: the same
country-years, the same regressors, two measures of the same growth.

```{r identical-samples}
SAMPLE_CELLS <- c("T +3 SD, 25 °C", "T -3 SD, 5 °C", "P -3 SD, 0.5 m", "P -3 SD, 1.5 m",
                  "P +3 SD, 0.5 m")
panel_labels <- vapply(national_panels, `[[`, "", "label")
sample_keys <- c("GID_0", "GID_1", "year")
# The preferred model on the rows `d`: fit, joint tests, and the effects of the
# cells (pp, with stars, and the estimates).
sample_fit <- function(d, label) {
  m <- fit_model(preferred_terms, d)
  effects <- climate_effects(list(preferred = m, panel = list(label = label)), PREFERRED_FORM)
  cells <- significance_map(effects)
  estimates <- effects %>%
    transmute(cell = sprintf("%s %+d SD, %s", ifelse(variable == "TM", "T", "P"), deviation, level),
              estimate = 100 * estimate) %>%
    filter(cell %in% SAMPLE_CELLS)
  list(row = tibble::tibble(sample = label, observations = stats::nobs(m),
                            countries = n_distinct(d$GID_0),
                            temperature_p = wald_p(m, "^devTM"),
                            precipitation_p = wald_p(m, "^devRR")) %>%
         bind_cols(select(cells, all_of(SAMPLE_CELLS))),
       estimates = mutate(estimates, sample = label))
}

# 1-2. Overlap, and the chain from PWT to the World Bank, by climate dataset.
pair_chains <- lapply(c("ERA5", "CRU TS", "UDelaware"), function(source) {
  pwt <- national_panels[[match(paste("PWT x", source), panel_labels)]]
  wb <- national_panels[[match(paste("WB x", source), panel_labels)]]
  pwt_d <- add_deviation_terms(pwt$clean, PREFERRED_SUFFIX)
  wb_d <- add_deviation_terms(wb$clean, PREFERRED_SUFFIX)
  common <- inner_join(distinct(pwt_d, GID_0, GID_1, year), distinct(wb_d, GID_0, GID_1, year),
                       by = sample_keys)
  wb_growth <- select(wb_d, GID_1, year, g_wb = all_of(OUTCOME))
  B <- semi_join(pwt_d, common, by = sample_keys)
  C <- B %>%
    left_join(wb_growth, by = c("GID_1", "year")) %>%
    mutate(g_pwt = .data[[OUTCOME]])
  C[[OUTCOME]] <- C$g_wb
  D <- semi_join(wb_d, common, by = sample_keys)
  steps <- list("A. PWT, its sample" = pwt_d, "B. PWT growth, common rows" = B,
                "C. WB growth, common rows, PWT climate terms" = C,
                "D. WB growth, common rows, WB climate terms" = D, "E. WB, its sample" = wb_d)
  fits <- lapply(names(steps), function(k) sample_fit(steps[[k]], k))
  only <- function(a, b) anti_join(distinct(a, GID_0, year), distinct(b, GID_0, year),
                                   by = c("GID_0", "year"))
  pwt_only <- only(pwt_d, wb_d)
  wb_only <- only(wb_d, pwt_d)
  overlap <- tibble::tibble(
    climate = source, common_rows = nrow(common), pwt_only_rows = nrow(pwt_only),
    wb_only_rows = nrow(wb_only),
    pwt_only = paste(utils::head(names(sort(table(pwt_only$GID_0), decreasing = TRUE)), 6),
                     collapse = " "),
    wb_only = paste(utils::head(names(sort(table(wb_only$GID_0), decreasing = TRUE)), 6),
                    collapse = " "),
    growth_correlation = stats::cor(C$g_pwt, C$g_wb),
    mean_abs_difference_pp = 100 * mean(abs(C$g_pwt - C$g_wb)),
    share_above_2pp = mean(abs(C$g_pwt - C$g_wb) > 0.02),
    sd_pwt_pp = 100 * stats::sd(C$g_pwt), sd_wb_pp = 100 * stats::sd(C$g_wb))
  list(source = source, overlap = overlap,
       rows = bind_rows(lapply(fits, `[[`, "row")) %>% mutate(climate = source, .before = 1),
       estimates = bind_rows(lapply(fits, `[[`, "estimates")) %>% mutate(climate = source))
})

bind_rows(lapply(pair_chains, `[[`, "overlap")) %>%
  mutate(across(c(growth_correlation, share_above_2pp), ~ round(.x, 3)),
         across(c(mean_abs_difference_pp, sd_pwt_pp, sd_wb_pp), ~ round(.x, 2))) %>%
  knitr::kable(caption = paste(
    "PWT and World Bank samples (after the exclusions): country-years in both, only in PWT and",
    "only in the World Bank (with the countries with most such years), and on the common rows",
    "the agreement of the two growth series (correlation, mean absolute difference, share",
    "differing by more than 2 pp, SDs)"))

bind_rows(lapply(pair_chains, `[[`, "rows")) %>%
  mutate(across(ends_with("_p"), ~ signif(.x, 2))) %>%
  knitr::kable(caption = paste0(
    "From PWT to the World Bank one change at a time (", PREFERRED_FORM, ", ",
    PREFERRED_DEFINITION, " deviations): joint tests (p) and the effect of a +/-3 SD deviation ",
    "(pp); *** p < 0.01, ** p < 0.05, * p < 0.1"))

# 3. What each change contributes: the change of each effect (pp) at each step.
bind_rows(lapply(pair_chains, function(ch) {
  e <- ch$estimates %>% tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = sample, values_from = estimate)
  step <- function(to, from, what) {
    tibble::tibble(climate = ch$source, change = what, cell = e$cell,
                   pp = e[[to]] - e[[from]])
  }
  bind_rows(
    step("B. PWT growth, common rows", "A. PWT, its sample", "1 sample: PWT-only rows out"),
    step("C. WB growth, common rows, PWT climate terms", "B. PWT growth, common rows",
         "2 GDP series (measurement)"),
    step("D. WB growth, common rows, WB climate terms",
         "C. WB growth, common rows, PWT climate terms", "3 normalization periods"),
    step("E. WB, its sample", "D. WB growth, common rows, WB climate terms",
         "4 sample: WB-only rows in"),
    step("E. WB, its sample", "A. PWT, its sample", "total, PWT to WB")
  )
})) %>%
  mutate(pp = sprintf("%+.2f", pp), cell = factor(cell, levels = SAMPLE_CELLS)) %>%
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = cell, values_from = pp) %>%
  knitr::kable(caption = paste(
    "What each change contributes to the PWT-World Bank difference: the change of the effect",
    "of each +/-3 SD deviation (pp) at each step of the chain, and the total"))
```

## World Bank GDP at PPP

The World Bank series above is GDP per capita at constant 2015 US$ (constant
local prices at the 2015 exchange rate). The World Bank also publishes GDP per
capita at constant 2021 PPP (NY.GDP.PCAP.PP.KD, from 1990), downloaded here
with the constant-US$ series of the same vintage (WDI, October 2026;
`functions/wdi_download.R`). PWT's `rgdpna` is in 2021 PPP dollars too, but
its growth is the growth of GDP at constant national prices; the World Bank's
constant-PPP series is its 2021 PPP level carried over the years with the
growth at constant local prices, so its growth should be that of the
constant-US$ series. On the rows that every series has (from 1991), with the
exclusions of both panels and the PWT climate terms, only the GDP series
changes:

```text
B   PWT growth
C1  World Bank, constant 2015 US$, July 2025 (the World Bank panels above)
C2  World Bank, constant 2015 US$, October 2026         C1 -> C2: data revisions
C3  World Bank, constant 2021 PPP, October 2026         C2 -> C3: PPP
```

```{r wb-ppp}
wdi_growth <- load_wdi_growth()
PPP_STEPS <- c("B. PWT" = "g_pwt", "C1. WB, 2015 USD, July 2025" = "g_wb",
               "C2. WB, 2015 USD, October 2026" = "g_gdp_pc",
               "C3. WB, 2021 PPP, October 2026" = "g_gdp_pc_ppp")
ppp_chains <- lapply(c("ERA5", "CRU TS", "UDelaware"), function(source) {
  pwt <- national_panels[[match(paste("PWT x", source), panel_labels)]]
  wb <- national_panels[[match(paste("WB x", source), panel_labels)]]
  d <- add_deviation_terms(pwt$clean, PREFERRED_SUFFIX) %>%
    mutate(g_pwt = .data[[OUTCOME]]) %>%
    inner_join(select(wb$clean, GID_1, year, g_wb = all_of(OUTCOME)), by = c("GID_1", "year")) %>%
    inner_join(select(wdi_growth, GID_0, year, g_gdp_pc, g_gdp_pc_ppp), by = c("GID_0", "year")) %>%
    filter(if_all(all_of(unname(PPP_STEPS)), is.finite))
  fits <- lapply(names(PPP_STEPS), function(k) {
    d_k <- d
    d_k[[OUTCOME]] <- d[[PPP_STEPS[[k]]]]
    sample_fit(d_k, k)
  })
  agreement <- bind_rows(lapply(names(PPP_STEPS)[-1], function(k) {
    x <- d[[PPP_STEPS[[k]]]]
    tibble::tibble(climate = source, series = k, rows = nrow(d), countries = n_distinct(d$GID_0),
                   years = paste(range(d$year), collapse = "-"),
                   correlation_pwt = stats::cor(x, d$g_pwt),
                   mean_abs_difference_pwt_pp = 100 * mean(abs(x - d$g_pwt)),
                   mean_abs_difference_c2_pp = 100 * mean(abs(x - d$g_gdp_pc)),
                   share_off_c2_by_0.1pp = mean(abs(x - d$g_gdp_pc) > 0.001))
  }))
  list(source = source, agreement = agreement,
       rows = bind_rows(lapply(fits, `[[`, "row")) %>% mutate(climate = source, .before = 1),
       estimates = bind_rows(lapply(fits, `[[`, "estimates")) %>% mutate(climate = source))
})

# 1. Agreement of the World Bank series with PWT and with each other.
bind_rows(lapply(ppp_chains, `[[`, "agreement")) %>%
  mutate(across(c(correlation_pwt, share_off_c2_by_0.1pp), ~ round(.x, 3)),
         across(ends_with("_pp"), ~ round(.x, 2))) %>%
  knitr::kable(caption = paste(
    "Rows with PWT growth and the three World Bank series (after the exclusions of both panels):",
    "each World Bank series against PWT (correlation, mean absolute difference) and against the",
    "constant-USD series of October 2026 (C2: mean absolute difference, share differing by more",
    "than 0.1 pp)"))

# 2. The fits.
bind_rows(lapply(ppp_chains, `[[`, "rows")) %>%
  mutate(across(ends_with("_p"), ~ signif(.x, 2))) %>%
  knitr::kable(caption = paste0(
    "PWT and the World Bank series on identical rows with the PWT climate terms (",
    PREFERRED_FORM, ", ", PREFERRED_DEFINITION, " deviations): joint tests (p) and the effect ",
    "of a +/-3 SD deviation (pp); *** p < 0.01, ** p < 0.05, * p < 0.1"))

# 3. What each change contributes.
bind_rows(lapply(ppp_chains, function(ch) {
  e <- ch$estimates %>% tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = sample, values_from = estimate)
  k <- names(PPP_STEPS)
  step <- function(to, from, what) {
    tibble::tibble(climate = ch$source, change = what, cell = e$cell, pp = e[[to]] - e[[from]])
  }
  bind_rows(step(k[[2]], k[[1]], "1 PWT to WB, July 2025"),
            step(k[[3]], k[[2]], "2 revisions, July 2025 to October 2026"),
            step(k[[4]], k[[3]], "3 constant USD to PPP"),
            step(k[[4]], k[[1]], "total, PWT to WB at PPP"))
})) %>%
  mutate(pp = sprintf("%+.2f", pp), cell = factor(cell, levels = SAMPLE_CELLS)) %>%
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = cell, values_from = pp) %>%
  knitr::kable(caption = paste(
    "What each change of GDP series contributes: the change of the effect of each +/-3 SD",
    "deviation (pp), and the total from PWT to the World Bank at PPP"))
```


# Sector growth (World Bank)

Which sector's growth responds to the weather? The World Bank's value added
at constant 2015 US$ of agriculture (with forestry and fishing; ISIC A),
industry (mining, manufacturing, utilities and construction; ISIC B-F) and
services (ISIC G-U), from the same download (WDI, October 2026), each per head
like the GDP outcome, log growth matched on calendar year. The preferred
model (`r PREFERRED_FORM`, `r PREFERRED_DEFINITION` deviations) runs on each
World Bank panel's rows, with their climate terms, exclusions, controls and
fixed effects, restricted to the country-years with the growth of all three
sectors and of GDP per capita of the same vintage, so that every regression
has the same rows. The growth outliers dropped are those of GDP per capita, as
in every panel; nothing is dropped by sector. Three outcomes:

```text
growth        g_j = log growth of sector j's value added per head: how sensitive the sector is
difference    g_j - g_k: the coefficients are the differences of the two sectors'
              coefficients (same rows), so its tests are tests of equal responses
contribution  c_j = change of sector j's value added per head / the three sectors'
              value added per head the year before (= the sector's simple growth x its
              lagged share); c_agr + c_ind + c_srv is the simple growth of the three
              sectors' value added per head, and so are the effects (OLS is linear):
              what each sector contributes to the effect on value added
```

```{r sector-growth, fig.width=13, fig.height=8}
SECTOR_SETS <- list(
  growth = c("GDP per capita" = "g_gdp_pc", agriculture = "g_agr", industry = "g_ind",
             services = "g_srv"),
  difference = c("agriculture - industry" = "d_agr_ind", "agriculture - services" = "d_agr_srv",
                 "industry - services" = "d_ind_srv"),
  contribution = c("value added" = "c_total", agriculture = "c_agr", industry = "c_ind",
                   services = "c_srv")
)
SECTOR_COLUMNS <- c("g_gdp_pc", "g_agr", "g_ind", "g_srv", "c_total", "c_agr", "c_ind", "c_srv",
                    "s_agr", "s_ind", "s_srv")
# The preferred model with `outcome` on the rows `d`: joint tests, and the
# effects of the cells SAMPLE_CELLS with their CIs.
sector_fit <- function(d, outcome, label) {
  m <- fit_model(preferred_terms, d, outcome = outcome)
  effects <- climate_effects(list(preferred = m, panel = list(label = label)), PREFERRED_FORM) %>%
    mutate(cell = sprintf("%s %+d SD, %s", ifelse(variable == "TM", "T", "P"), deviation, level)) %>%
    filter(cell %in% SAMPLE_CELLS)
  list(effects = effects, observations = stats::nobs(m),
       temperature_p = wald_p(m, "^devTM"), precipitation_p = wald_p(m, "^devRR"))
}
sector_runs <- lapply(c("ERA5", "CRU TS", "UDelaware"), function(source) {
  wb <- national_panels[[match(paste("WB x", source), panel_labels)]]
  d <- add_deviation_terms(wb$clean, PREFERRED_SUFFIX) %>%
    inner_join(select(wdi_growth, GID_0, year, all_of(SECTOR_COLUMNS)), by = c("GID_0", "year")) %>%
    filter(if_all(all_of(SECTOR_COLUMNS), is.finite)) %>%
    mutate(d_agr_ind = g_agr - g_ind, d_agr_srv = g_agr - g_srv, d_ind_srv = g_ind - g_srv)
  fits <- lapply(SECTOR_SETS, function(set) lapply(set, function(y) sector_fit(d, y, source)))
  stopifnot(length(unique(unlist(lapply(fits, function(f) lapply(f, `[[`, "observations"))))) == 1)
  # The sectors' contributions add up to the value added's.
  total <- fits$contribution[["value added"]]$effects$estimate
  parts <- Reduce(`+`, lapply(fits$contribution[-1], function(f) f$effects$estimate))
  stopifnot(isTRUE(all.equal(total, parts, tolerance = 1e-6)))
  list(source = source, panel_rows = nrow(wb$clean), data = d, fits = fits)
})

# 1. Rows, the dispersion of each growth rate, and the sectors' shares.
bind_rows(lapply(sector_runs, function(r) {
  d <- r$data
  tibble::tibble(climate = r$source, panel_rows = r$panel_rows, rows = nrow(d),
                 countries = n_distinct(d$GID_0), years = paste(range(d$year), collapse = "-"),
                 sd_gdp_pc_pp = 100 * stats::sd(d$g_gdp_pc), sd_agr_pp = 100 * stats::sd(d$g_agr),
                 sd_ind_pp = 100 * stats::sd(d$g_ind), sd_srv_pp = 100 * stats::sd(d$g_srv),
                 share_agr = mean(d$s_agr), share_ind = mean(d$s_ind), share_srv = mean(d$s_srv),
                 correlation_value_added_gdp = stats::cor(d$c_total, d$g_gdp_pc))
})) %>%
  mutate(across(ends_with("_pp"), ~ round(.x, 2)),
         across(c(starts_with("share_"), correlation_value_added_gdp), ~ round(.x, 3))) %>%
  knitr::kable(caption = paste(
    "World Bank panels: rows of the panel (after the exclusions) and with the growth of every",
    "sector, SD of each growth rate (pp), the sectors' mean lagged shares of value added, and",
    "the correlation of value-added growth (sum of the contributions) with GDP-per-capita",
    "growth"))

# 2-4. Growth, differences and contributions.
sector_table <- function(set) {
  bind_rows(lapply(sector_runs, function(r) {
    bind_rows(lapply(names(r$fits[[set]]), function(k) {
      f <- r$fits[[set]][[k]]
      f$effects %>%
        transmute(cell, value = sprintf("%+.2f%s", 100 * estimate, stars(p_value))) %>%
        tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = cell, values_from = value) %>%
        mutate(climate = r$source, outcome = k, observations = f$observations,
               temperature_p = signif(f$temperature_p, 2),
               precipitation_p = signif(f$precipitation_p, 2))
    }))
  })) %>%
    select(climate, outcome, observations, temperature_p, precipitation_p, all_of(SAMPLE_CELLS))
}
sector_table("growth") %>%
  knitr::kable(caption = paste0(
    "World Bank panels, ", PREFERRED_FORM, ", ", PREFERRED_DEFINITION, " deviations: growth of ",
    "GDP per capita and of each sector's value added per head on identical rows; joint tests ",
    "(p) and the effect of a +/-3 SD deviation (pp of the sector's growth); *** p < 0.01, ",
    "** p < 0.05, * p < 0.1"))
sector_table("difference") %>%
  knitr::kable(caption = paste(
    "Differences between the sectors' responses (pp of growth): the same model on the",
    "difference of the two sectors' growth; joint tests (p) of equal temperature and equal",
    "precipitation responses, and the difference of each effect"))
sector_table("contribution") %>%
  knitr::kable(caption = paste(
    "Contributions (pp of the growth of the three sectors' value added per head): the effect",
    "on value added and each sector's part of it (the parts add up to the total)"))

# 5. The effects with their 95% CIs.
sector_effects <- bind_rows(lapply(sector_runs, function(r) {
  bind_rows(lapply(c("growth", "contribution"), function(set) {
    bind_rows(lapply(names(r$fits[[set]]), function(k) {
      mutate(r$fits[[set]][[k]]$effects, climate = r$source, set = set, outcome = k)
    }))
  }))
})) %>%
  mutate(series = ifelse(outcome %in% c("GDP per capita", "value added"), "total", outcome),
         series = factor(series, levels = c("total", unname(WDI_SECTORS))),
         cell = factor(cell, levels = SAMPLE_CELLS),
         climate = factor(climate, levels = c("ERA5", "CRU TS", "UDelaware")),
         set = factor(set, levels = c("growth", "contribution"),
                      labels = c("Growth of the sector (pp)",
                                 "Contribution to value-added growth (pp)")))
ggplot(sector_effects, aes(cell, 100 * estimate, colour = series)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, colour = GRID_MUTED, linewidth = 0.3) +
  geom_pointrange(aes(ymin = 100 * conf_low, ymax = 100 * conf_high),
                  position = position_dodge(width = 0.7), size = 0.3) +
  facet_grid(set ~ climate, scales = "free_y") +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c(total = GRID_INK, stats::setNames(GRID_PALETTE[1:3], WDI_SECTORS)),
                      name = NULL) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Effect (pp)",
       title = "Which sector responds: effect of a +/-3 SD year on each sector",
       subtitle = wrap_text(paste0(
         "World Bank panels, ", PREFERRED_FORM, ", ", PREFERRED_DEFINITION, " deviations, ",
         "identical rows; top: growth of GDP per capita (total) and of each sector's value added ",
         "per head; bottom: each sector's contribution to the growth of value added per head ",
         "(total: their sum); 95% CIs clustered by country."), 150)) +
  theme_results() +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 20, hjust = 1))
```


# Preferred model and SPEI (PWT x CRU TS)

SPEI, the Standardized Precipitation-Evapotranspiration Index (CSIC SPEIbase,
from the Weighted Climate Dataset with population-density weights at base year
2000), is the standardized climatic water balance, precipitation minus
potential evapotranspiration, accumulated over 1, 12 or 36 months. SPEIbase is
computed from CRU TS, so this section uses PWT x CRU TS, whose temperature and
precipitation deviations come from the same data. SPEI is monthly; the annual
indicators are

- SPEI1, annual mean: the mean of the twelve monthly 1-month values;
- SPEI12, December: the water balance of the calendar year;
- SPEI36, December: the water balance of the three calendar years to December.

Like the deviations, each is demeaned (each country's mean and linear and
quadratic trend removed, on the years from `r params$start_year` minus ten to
the last year of the panel) before its arms are cut, S- = max(-S, 0) (dry) and
S+ = max(S, 0) (wet). Each enters the preferred model in two forms, interacted
with the long-run precipitation as the precipitation deviations are:

```text
signed SPEI:  c S + d S x clim_RR
SPEI arms:    c+ S+ + c- S- + (d+ S+ + d- S-) x clim_RR
```

All models on the same rows: the PWT x CRU TS sample (outliers dropped) with
every SPEI indicator.

```{r spei}
SPEI_INDICATORS <- c(spei1 = "SPEI1, annual mean", spei12 = "SPEI12, December",
                     spei36 = "SPEI36, December")
SPEI_FORMS <- c("signed", "arms")

# Monthly SPEI by country (cached on disk by wcd_get()).
spei_monthly <- function(variable) {
  x <- wcd_get(variable = variable, source = "CSIC", geo_resolution = "gadm0",
               weight = CLIMATE_WEIGHT, weight_year = CLIMATE_WEIGHT_YEAR,
               time_frequency = "monthly", verbose = FALSE)
  tibble::tibble(GID_0 = x$GID_0, year = as.integer(format(x$date, "%Y")),
                 month = as.integer(format(x$date, "%m")), value = x[[3]])
}
spei_december <- function(variable, name) {
  spei_monthly(variable) %>% filter(month == 12) %>% transmute(GID_0, year, !!name := value)
}
spei_raw <- spei_monthly("SPEI1") %>%
  group_by(GID_0, year) %>%
  summarise(spei1 = if (sum(!is.na(value)) == 12) mean(value) else NA_real_, .groups = "drop") %>%
  full_join(spei_december("SPEI12", "spei12"), by = c("GID_0", "year")) %>%
  full_join(spei_december("SPEI36", "spei36"), by = c("GID_0", "year"))

cru <- national_panels[[match("PWT x CRU TS", vapply(national_panels, `[[`, "", "label"))]]

# Availability: the SPEI series, and the PWT x CRU TS country-years they cover.
bind_rows(lapply(names(SPEI_INDICATORS), function(k) {
  have <- spei_raw[!is.na(spei_raw[[k]]), ]
  covered <- paste(cru$clean$GID_0, cru$clean$year) %in% paste(have$GID_0, have$year)
  tibble::tibble(indicator = SPEI_INDICATORS[[k]], first_year = min(have$year),
                 last_year = max(have$year), countries = n_distinct(have$GID_0),
                 sample_rows = nrow(cru$clean), rows_with_spei = sum(covered),
                 countries_without = paste(sort(unique(cru$clean$GID_0[!covered])),
                                           collapse = ", "))
})) %>%
  knitr::kable(caption = paste("SPEI (CSIC SPEIbase, WCD, population density 2000): availability",
                               "and coverage of the PWT x CRU TS sample"))

# Demeaned SPEI (each country's mean and quadratic trend removed, as the
# deviations) and its arms.
spei <- spei_raw %>% filter(year >= START_YEAR - MAX_LAGS, year <= cru$end_year)
for (k in names(SPEI_INDICATORS)) {
  ok <- which(is.finite(spei[[k]]))
  sub <- data.frame(GID_1 = spei$GID_0[ok], t = spei$year[ok] - 1990L, x = spei[[k]][ok])
  sub$t2 <- sub$t^2
  m <- fixest::feols(x ~ 1 | GID_1[t, t2], sub, notes = FALSE)
  demeaned <- rep(NA_real_, nrow(spei))
  demeaned[ok[fixest::obs(m)]] <- stats::resid(m)
  spei[[k]] <- demeaned
  spei[[paste0(k, "_dry")]] <- pmax(-demeaned, 0)
  spei[[paste0(k, "_wet")]] <- pmax(demeaned, 0)
}

spei_data <- add_deviation_terms(cru$clean, PREFERRED_SUFFIX) %>%
  inner_join(spei, by = c("GID_0", "year")) %>%
  filter(if_all(all_of(names(SPEI_INDICATORS)), ~ !is.na(.x)))

# Correlations of the demeaned indicators with the deviations (same rows).
stats::cor(as.data.frame(spei_data)[, c(names(SPEI_INDICATORS), "devRR", "devTM")]) %>%
  round(2) %>%
  knitr::kable(caption = paste("PWT x CRU TS: correlations of the demeaned SPEI indicators and",
                               "deviations (dP = devRR, dT = devTM)"))

spei_terms <- function(k, form) {
  x <- if (form == "signed") k else paste0(k, c("_dry", "_wet"))
  c(x, paste0(x, ":clim_RR"))
}
spei_models <- c(
  list("Preferred" = fit_model(preferred_terms, spei_data)),
  unlist(lapply(names(SPEI_INDICATORS), function(k) {
    stats::setNames(lapply(SPEI_FORMS, function(f) {
      fit_model(c(preferred_terms, spei_terms(k, f)), spei_data)
    }), paste0(SPEI_INDICATORS[[k]], ", ", SPEI_FORMS))
  }), recursive = FALSE)
)
stopifnot(length(unique(vapply(spei_models, stats::nobs, 0))) == 1)

spei_p <- vapply(spei_models, function(m) {
  if (any(startsWith(names(stats::coef(m)), "spei"))) wald_p(m, "^spei") else NA_real_
}, 0)
tibble::tibble(
  model = names(spei_models),
  within_r2 = vapply(spei_models, function(m) fixest::fitstat(m, "wr2")[[1]], 0),
  aic_vs_preferred = vapply(spei_models, stats::AIC, 0) - stats::AIC(spei_models[[1]]),
  verdict_vs_preferred = c("", vapply(names(spei_models)[-1], function(k) {
    fit_verdicts(spei_models[[k]], spei_models[[1]], nested_p = spei_p[[k]])
  }, "")),
  spei_p = spei_p,
  temperature_p = vapply(spei_models, function(m) wald_p(m, "^devTM"), 0),
  precipitation_p = vapply(spei_models, function(m) wald_p(m, "^devRR"), 0)
) %>%
  mutate(within_r2 = round(within_r2, 4), aic_vs_preferred = round(aic_vs_preferred, 1),
         across(ends_with("_p"), ~ signif(.x, 2))) %>%
  knitr::kable(caption = paste0("PWT x CRU TS, ", stats::nobs(spei_models[[1]]),
                                " country-years: the preferred model with each SPEI indicator; ",
                                "AIC relative to the preferred model and the ", VERDICT_NOTE,
                                " against it (nested: the joint test of the SPEI terms); joint ",
                                "tests (p) of the SPEI, temperature and precipitation terms"))

SPEI_DICT <- c(DICT, stats::setNames(
  paste0(rep(c("SPEI1", "SPEI12", "SPEI36"), each = 3), c("", " dry", " wet")),
  paste0(rep(names(SPEI_INDICATORS), each = 3), c("", "_dry", "_wet"))
))
etable(spei_models[c("Preferred", paste0(SPEI_INDICATORS, ", arms"))],
       headers = c("Preferred", "SPEI1", "SPEI12", "SPEI36"), dict = SPEI_DICT, drop = DROP,
       order = c("%^devTM", "%^devRR", "%^spei", "%^conflict"), fitstat = FITSTAT,
       title = "PWT x CRU TS: the preferred model and SPEI arms")

# Effect of SPEI = x at the long-run precipitation of EVAL_CLIMATE$RR.
SPEI_AT <- c(-2, 2)
spei_effects <- function(model, k, form, label) {
  terms <- names(stats::coef(model))
  m <- EVAL_CLIMATE$RR
  grid <- expand.grid(level = seq_along(m), x = SPEI_AT)
  G <- t(mapply(function(g, x) {
    w <- stats::setNames(numeric(length(terms)), terms)
    values <- if (form == "signed") {
      stats::setNames(x, k)
    } else {
      stats::setNames(c(max(-x, 0), max(x, 0)), paste0(k, c("_dry", "_wet")))
    }
    for (term in names(values)) {
      w[[term]] <- values[[term]]
      w[[interaction_name(term, "clim_RR", terms)]] <- values[[term]] * m[[g]]
    }
    w
  }, grid$level, grid$x))
  colnames(G) <- terms
  linear_combination(model, G) %>%
    mutate(model = label, column = sprintf("SPEI %+d, %s", grid$x, EVAL_LABELS$RR[grid$level]),
           p_value = 2 * stats::pnorm(-abs(estimate / std_error)))
}
bind_rows(lapply(names(SPEI_INDICATORS), function(k) {
  bind_rows(lapply(SPEI_FORMS, function(f) {
    label <- paste0(SPEI_INDICATORS[[k]], ", ", f)
    spei_effects(spei_models[[label]], k, f, label)
  }))
})) %>%
  mutate(cell = sprintf("%+.2f%s", 100 * estimate, stars(p_value))) %>%
  select(model, column, cell) %>%
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = column, values_from = cell) %>%
  knitr::kable(caption = paste("Effect of SPEI of -2 (extremely dry) and +2 (extremely wet) on",
                               "growth (pp) at long-run precipitation of 0.5, 1.5 and 3 m;",
                               "*** p < 0.01, ** p < 0.05, * p < 0.1"))

# The temperature and precipitation deviations with and without SPEI.
significance_map(bind_rows(lapply(names(spei_models), function(k) {
  climate_effects(list(preferred = spei_models[[k]], panel = list(label = k)))
}))) %>%
  knitr::kable(caption = paste("Effect of a +/-3 SD deviation (pp) without and with SPEI;",
                               "*** p < 0.01, ** p < 0.05, * p < 0.1"))
```

# 20-year deviations with the baseline fixed during runs

With a trailing baseline, a sequence of warm years raises the baseline as it
goes, so each later warm year looks less anomalous than the first. The
run-fixed deviation (as `add_climate_runs()` in functions/climate_runs.R, there
for temperature) holds the trailing mean and SD at their value at the start of
the run:

- a warming run is a maximal sequence of at least two consecutive years with
  strictly rising temperature; position 1 is the year before the first rise.
  Cooling runs are the same with falling temperature, so a peak or trough ends
  one run and starts the other;
- within a run, the deviation uses the trailing 20-year mean and SD of its
  position-1 year; outside runs (and at position 1), the moving ones;
- the warm arm is cut from the warming-run deviation, the cold arm from the
  cooling-run deviation.

Precipitation is treated the same way, with wetting (rising) and drying
(falling) runs. The run-fixed deviations are demeaned as the others (each
unit's mean and quadratic trend removed) before their arms are cut. The model:
20-year deviations with the arms of the preferred form (`r PREFERRED_FORM`),
interacted with the horizon mean, as in the selection table; the moving and
run-fixed versions on the same rows.

```{r run-fixed-baseline}
RUN_FORM <- PREFERRED_FORM
# The arms of RUN_FORM by role: warm and cold (T), wet and dry (P).
RUN_HOT_ARM <- paste0("devTM", FORMS[[RUN_FORM]]$TM[[1]])
RUN_COLD_ARM <- paste0("devTM", FORMS[[RUN_FORM]]$TM[[2]])
RUN_WET_ARM <- paste0("devRR", FORMS[[RUN_FORM]]$RR[[1]])
RUN_DRY_ARM <- paste0("devRR", FORMS[[RUN_FORM]]$RR[[2]])
# Value of arm term `arm` at a deviation of `sd` SD on its side.
arm_event_value <- function(arm, sd) term_value(sub("^dev(TM|RR)", "", arm), if (grepl("_neg", arm)) -sd else sd)
RUN_DEFINITION <- "20-year"
RUN_DIRECTIONS <- c(up = 1, down = -1)

# Each unit's mean and linear and quadratic trend removed from x (as the
# deviations of prepare_panel()), on the finite values.
demean_unit_trend <- function(unit, year, x) {
  ok <- which(is.finite(x))
  sub <- data.frame(GID_1 = unit[ok], t = year[ok] - 1990L, x = x[ok])
  sub$t2 <- sub$t^2
  m <- fixest::feols(x ~ 1 | GID_1[t, t2], sub, notes = FALSE)
  out <- rep(NA_real_, length(x))
  out[ok[fixest::obs(m)]] <- stats::resid(m)
  out
}

# Deviation of variable v from its trailing moments (`baseline`), with the
# moments held at their position-1 values through each rising (direction 1)
# or falling (-1) run of v; outside runs, the moving deviation. The run
# identifiers are those of add_climate_runs() (.run_ids()).
run_fixed_deviation <- function(data, v, direction, baseline = "lag_20") {
  mean_col <- paste0("mean_", v, "_", baseline)
  sd_col <- paste0("sd_", v, "_", baseline)
  data %>%
    group_by(GID_1) %>%
    arrange(year, .by_group = TRUE) %>%
    mutate(change = if_else(year == dplyr::lag(year) + 1L,
                            .data[[v]] - dplyr::lag(.data[[v]]), NA_real_),
           run_id = .run_ids(change, direction)) %>%
    group_by(GID_1, run_id) %>%
    mutate(in_run = !is.na(run_id) & n() >= 2L,
           position = if_else(in_run, row_number(), 1L),
           mean_fixed = if_else(in_run, first(.data[[mean_col]]), .data[[mean_col]]),
           sd_fixed = if_else(in_run, first(.data[[sd_col]]), .data[[sd_col]]),
           deviation = (.data[[v]] - mean_fixed) / sd_fixed) %>%
    ungroup() %>%
    select(GID_1, year, position, deviation)
}

# The panel's clean rows with the demeaned fixed-baseline deviations of each
# variable and direction from `fixed_deviation` (dm_<v>_<tag><direction>) and
# the positions in the runs or spells (position_<v>_<tag>_<direction>).
add_run_fixed <- function(panel, fixed_deviation = run_fixed_deviation, tag = "run") {
  data <- panel$data %>%
    filter(year >= START_YEAR - MAX_LAGS, year <= panel$end_year, !is.na(TM), !is.na(RR))
  out <- data %>% select(GID_1, year)
  for (v in c("TM", "RR")) for (dir in names(RUN_DIRECTIONS)) {
    x <- fixed_deviation(data, v, RUN_DIRECTIONS[[dir]])
    x[[paste0("dm_", v, "_", tag, dir)]] <- demean_unit_trend(x$GID_1, x$year, x$deviation)
    names(x)[names(x) == "position"] <- paste0("position_", v, "_", tag, "_", dir)
    out <- left_join(out, select(x, -deviation), by = c("GID_1", "year"))
  }
  # A run that starts before the trailing moments exist has no fixed baseline;
  # those rows are left out, for the moving baseline too.
  fixed_columns <- paste0("dm_", rep(c("TM", "RR"), each = 2), "_", tag, names(RUN_DIRECTIONS))
  panel$clean %>%
    inner_join(out, by = c("GID_1", "year")) %>%
    filter(if_all(all_of(fixed_columns), is.finite))
}

# The deviation terms of the 20-year definition, with the arms of `fixed`
# variables cut from the fixed-baseline deviations (warm or wet arm from the
# rising runs or warm spells, cold or dry arm from the falling runs or cold
# spells).
run_fixed_terms <- function(model_data, fixed = c("TM", "RR"), tag = "run") {
  d <- add_deviation_terms(model_data, DEFINITIONS[[RUN_DEFINITION]])
  for (v in fixed) {
    up <- model_data[[paste0("dm_", v, "_", tag, "up")]]
    down <- model_data[[paste0("dm_", v, "_", tag, "down")]]
    d[[paste0("dev", v, "_pos")]] <- pmax(up, 0)
    d[[paste0("dev", v, "_neg")]] <- pmax(-down, 0)
    d[[paste0("dev", v, "_pos2")]] <- pmax(up, 0)^2
    d[[paste0("dev", v, "_neg2")]] <- pmax(-down, 0)^2
  }
  d
}
# The variants: which variables have the fixed baseline ("<label>-fixed T and
# P", "... T", "... P"), against the moving baseline.
run_variants <- function(label) {
  stats::setNames(list(character(0), c("TM", "RR"), "TM", "RR"),
                  c("Moving baseline", paste0(label, "-fixed ", c("T and P", "T", "P"))))
}

# 1. How often and how much the fixed baseline changes the deviation, on the
# rows `d` (names: the rising and falling sequences of each variable).
fixed_change_table <- function(d, tag, names_TM, names_RR, what) {
  moving <- add_deviation_terms(d, DEFINITIONS[[RUN_DEFINITION]])
  bind_rows(lapply(c("TM", "RR"), function(v) {
    sequence_names <- if (v == "TM") names_TM else names_RR
    bind_rows(lapply(names(RUN_DIRECTIONS), function(dir) {
      fixed <- d[[paste0("dm_", v, "_", tag, dir)]]
      position <- d[[paste0("position_", v, "_", tag, "_", dir)]]
      later <- position >= 2
      arm <- if (dir == "up") pmax(fixed, 0) else pmax(-fixed, 0)
      arm_moving <- moving[[paste0("dev", v, if (dir == "up") "_pos" else "_neg")]]
      tibble::tibble(variable = v, sequence = sequence_names[[dir]],
                     share_at_position_2_plus = mean(later),
                     share_at_position_5_plus = mean(position >= 5),
                     mean_change_at_2_plus = mean((fixed - moving[[paste0("dev", v)]])[later]),
                     arm_above_2sd_moving = sum(arm_moving > 2), arm_above_2sd_fixed = sum(arm > 2),
                     correlation = stats::cor(fixed, moving[[paste0("dev", v)]]))
    }))
  })) %>%
    mutate(across(where(is.double), ~ round(.x, 3))) %>%
    knitr::kable(caption = paste0(
      main$label, ": country-years at ", what, " position 2 or later and 5 or later, mean ",
      "change of the demeaned deviation from position 2 (fixed minus moving, SD), arm values ",
      "above 2 SD, and the correlation of the two deviations"))
}

# 2. The model with moving and fixed baselines on the main panel (same rows):
# fit and joint tests, effects, and coefficients (printed by the caller, so
# that knitr renders the tables).
fixed_model_tables <- function(d, tag, label) {
  models <- lapply(run_variants(label), function(fixed) {
    fit_model(form_terms(FORMS[[RUN_FORM]]), run_fixed_terms(d, fixed, tag))
  })
  stopifnot(length(unique(vapply(models, stats::nobs, 0))) == 1)
  list(
    fit = fit_summary(models) %>%
      mutate(aic_vs_moving = round(aic - aic[1], 1),
             verdict_vs_moving = c("", vapply(record[-1], fit_verdicts, "", b = record[[1]])),
             within_r2 = round(within_r2, 4), within_adj_r2 = round(within_adj_r2, 4),
             across(ends_with("_p"), ~ signif(.x, 2))) %>%
      select(-aic, -bic, -record) %>%
      knitr::kable(caption = paste0(main$label, ": ", RUN_FORM, ", ", RUN_DEFINITION,
                                    " deviations, moving and ", tolower(label), "-fixed ",
                                    "baselines; joint tests (p), AIC relative to the moving ",
                                    "baseline, and the ", VERDICT_NOTE, " against it")),
    effects = significance_map(bind_rows(lapply(names(models), function(k) {
      climate_effects(list(preferred = models[[k]], panel = list(label = k)), RUN_FORM)
    }))) %>%
      knitr::kable(caption = paste0(main$label, ": effect of a +/-3 SD deviation (pp), moving ",
                                    "and ", tolower(label), "-fixed baselines; *** p < 0.01, ",
                                    "** p < 0.05, * p < 0.1")),
    coefficients = etable(models, dict = DICT, drop = DROP, order = ORDER, fitstat = FITSTAT,
                          title = paste0(main$label, ": ", RUN_FORM, " with moving and ",
                                         tolower(label), "-fixed baselines"))
  )
}

# 3. Moving against fixed (T and P) on every national panel.
RUN_CELLS <- c("T +3 SD, 25 °C", "T -3 SD, 5 °C", "P -3 SD, 0.5 m", "P -3 SD, 1.5 m")
fixed_panel_table <- function(panel_data, tag, label) {
  variants <- run_variants(label)[1:2]
  bind_rows(lapply(names(panel_data), function(p) {
    models <- lapply(variants, function(v) {
      fit_model(form_terms(FORMS[[RUN_FORM]]), run_fixed_terms(panel_data[[p]], v, tag))
    })
    bind_rows(lapply(names(variants), function(k) {
      m <- models[[k]]
      effects <- significance_map(climate_effects(list(preferred = m, panel = list(label = p)),
                                                  RUN_FORM))
      tibble::tibble(panel = p, baseline = k, aic = stats::AIC(m),
                     verdict_vs_moving = if (k == names(variants)[[1]]) "" else {
                       fit_verdicts(m, models[[1]])
                     },
                     temperature_p = wald_p(m, "^devTM"),
                     precipitation_p = wald_p(m, "^devRR")) %>%
        bind_cols(select(effects, all_of(RUN_CELLS)))
    }))
  })) %>%
    group_by(panel) %>%
    mutate(aic_vs_moving = round(aic - aic[1], 1)) %>%
    ungroup() %>%
    select(panel, baseline, aic_vs_moving, verdict_vs_moving, temperature_p, precipitation_p,
           all_of(RUN_CELLS)) %>%
    mutate(across(ends_with("_p"), ~ signif(.x, 2))) %>%
    knitr::kable(caption = paste0(
      "Every national panel: ", RUN_FORM, ", ", RUN_DEFINITION, " deviations, moving against ",
      tolower(label), "-fixed (T and P) baselines; joint tests (p), AIC relative to the moving ",
      "baseline and the ", VERDICT_NOTE, " against it, and effects of a +/-3 SD deviation ",
      "(pp); *** p < 0.01, ** p < 0.05, * p < 0.1"))
}

run_data <- lapply(national_panels, add_run_fixed)
names(run_data) <- vapply(national_panels, `[[`, "", "label")
fixed_change_table(run_data[[main$label]], "run", c(up = "warming run", down = "cooling run"),
                   c(up = "wetting run", down = "drying run"), "run")
run_tables <- fixed_model_tables(run_data[[main$label]], "run", "Run")
run_tables$fit
run_tables$effects
run_tables$coefficients
fixed_panel_table(run_data, "run", "Run")
```

## Fixed during spells above or below the baseline

A spell is a sequence of years on the same side of the baseline, rather than of
rising (falling) years: a warm spell starts in a year above its trailing
20-year mean, and the baseline (mean and SD) is held at that year's value for
as long as the following years stay above it; it ends with the first year at or
below the held mean (or a gap), and the next year starts afresh from its own
trailing moments. Membership is judged against the held baseline, so the rising
trailing mean cannot end a spell by itself. Cold, wet and dry spells are the
same, below or above. The first year of a spell has its moving deviation; the
warm (wet) arm is cut from the warm-spell deviation and the cold (dry) arm from
the cold-spell one, demeaned as before. Everything else as above.

```{r spell-fixed-baseline}
# Deviation of x from its trailing moments (mu, s), held at the first year of
# each spell on the `direction` side (1 above, -1 below), and the position in
# the spell (0 outside spells).
fix_spells <- function(x, mu, s, year, direction) {
  n <- length(x)
  deviation <- rep(NA_real_, n)
  position <- integer(n)
  held_mean <- NA_real_
  held_sd <- NA_real_
  p <- 0L
  for (i in seq_len(n)) {
    continuing <- p > 0L && year[i] == year[i - 1L] + 1L && is.finite(x[i]) &&
      direction * (x[i] - held_mean) > 0
    if (continuing) {
      p <- p + 1L
    } else {
      held_mean <- mu[i]
      held_sd <- s[i]
      p <- if (is.finite(x[i]) && is.finite(held_mean) && direction * (x[i] - held_mean) > 0) 1L else 0L
    }
    deviation[i] <- (x[i] - held_mean) / held_sd
    position[i] <- p
  }
  list(deviation = deviation, position = position)
}
spell_fixed_deviation <- function(data, v, direction, baseline = "lag_20") {
  data <- data[order(data$GID_1, data$year), ]
  deviation <- rep(NA_real_, nrow(data))
  position <- integer(nrow(data))
  for (idx in split(seq_len(nrow(data)), data$GID_1)) {
    r <- fix_spells(data[[v]][idx], data[[paste0("mean_", v, "_", baseline)]][idx],
                    data[[paste0("sd_", v, "_", baseline)]][idx], data$year[idx], direction)
    deviation[idx] <- r$deviation
    position[idx] <- r$position
  }
  tibble::tibble(GID_1 = data$GID_1, year = data$year, position = position,
                 deviation = deviation)
}

spell_data <- lapply(national_panels, add_run_fixed, fixed_deviation = spell_fixed_deviation,
                     tag = "spell")
names(spell_data) <- vapply(national_panels, `[[`, "", "label")
fixed_change_table(spell_data[[main$label]], "spell", c(up = "warm spell", down = "cold spell"),
                   c(up = "wet spell", down = "dry spell"), "spell")
spell_tables <- fixed_model_tables(spell_data[[main$label]], "spell", "Spell")
spell_tables$fit
spell_tables$effects
spell_tables$coefficients
fixed_panel_table(spell_data, "spell", "Spell")
```

## Fixed during spells with a one-SD rule

A warm spell starts, as a run, at the year before a rise, and its baseline
(mean and SD) is held at that year's trailing 20-year moments, but it does not
end at the first cooler year. It ends with a year cooler than the one before
by more than one SD (the held SD), or with the third consecutive cooler year
(each by less than one SD; a warmer year resets the count). Cold, wet and dry
spells are the same with the signs reversed (`fix_sigma_spells()` in
`functions/climate_runs.R`, also used by the scenario projections). Outside
spells, the moving deviation; the warm (wet) arm is cut from the warm-spell
deviation and the cold (dry) arm from the cold-spell one, demeaned as before.

The spells are found on the year-to-year changes of the variable itself. The
deviations are then demeaned (each unit's mean and quadratic trend removed),
so a year can sit in a warm spell of the raw series and below its unit's
trend. As a check, the spells are also found on the demeaned variable (the
same window and trend removal as the deviations; the held SD and the deviation
unchanged), which removes the trend's slope from every change. The two are
compared by the share of unit-years on which they agree (in a spell from
position 2 or not), the correlation of the demeaned deviations and the fit.

```{r sigma-spell-baseline}
# `detect`: find the spells on the variable ("raw") or on the variable without
# each unit's mean and quadratic trend ("demeaned").
sigma_spell_deviation <- function(data, v, direction, baseline = "lag_20",
                                  detect = c("raw", "demeaned")) {
  detect <- match.arg(detect)
  data <- data[order(data$GID_1, data$year), ]
  series <- if (detect == "raw") data[[v]] else demean_unit_trend(data$GID_1, data$year, data[[v]])
  deviation <- rep(NA_real_, nrow(data))
  position <- integer(nrow(data))
  for (idx in split(seq_len(nrow(data)), data$GID_1)) {
    r <- fix_sigma_spells(data[[v]][idx], data[[paste0("mean_", v, "_", baseline)]][idx],
                          data[[paste0("sd_", v, "_", baseline)]][idx], data$year[idx], direction,
                          detect = series[idx])
    deviation[idx] <- r$deviation
    position[idx] <- r$position
  }
  tibble::tibble(GID_1 = data$GID_1, year = data$year, position = position,
                 deviation = deviation)
}

# Length of the runs, spells and one-SD spells of the main panel's units over
# the years of the demeaning (START_YEAR - MAX_LAGS to the last year).
sequence_lengths <- function(fixed_deviation, label) {
  data <- main$data %>%
    filter(year >= START_YEAR - MAX_LAGS, year <= main$end_year, !is.na(TM), !is.na(RR))
  bind_rows(lapply(c("TM", "RR"), function(v) bind_rows(lapply(names(RUN_DIRECTIONS), function(dir) {
    p <- fixed_deviation(data, v, RUN_DIRECTIONS[[dir]])$position
    last <- p >= 2L & c(p[-1], 0L) != p + 1L
    tibble::tibble(definition = label, variable = v, direction = dir,
                   sequences = sum(last), mean_length = mean(p[last]),
                   p90_length = stats::quantile(p[last], 0.9, names = FALSE),
                   longest = max(p[last]), share_position_2_plus = mean(p >= 2L))
  }))))
}
sigma_spell_demeaned <- function(data, v, direction) {
  sigma_spell_deviation(data, v, direction, detect = "demeaned")
}
bind_rows(sequence_lengths(run_fixed_deviation, "Runs"),
          sequence_lengths(spell_fixed_deviation, "Spells above or below the baseline"),
          sequence_lengths(sigma_spell_deviation, "One-SD spells"),
          sequence_lengths(sigma_spell_demeaned, "One-SD spells, found on the demeaned variable")) %>%
  mutate(across(c(mean_length, share_position_2_plus), ~ round(.x, 2))) %>%
  knitr::kable(caption = paste0(main$label, ": number and length (years, from the year before ",
                                "the first rise or fall) of the runs and spells, and the share of ",
                                "unit-years at position 2 or later"))

sigma_data <- lapply(national_panels, add_run_fixed, fixed_deviation = sigma_spell_deviation,
                     tag = "sigma")
names(sigma_data) <- vapply(national_panels, `[[`, "", "label")
fixed_change_table(sigma_data[[main$label]], "sigma", c(up = "warm spell", down = "cold spell"),
                   c(up = "wet spell", down = "dry spell"), "one-SD spell")
sigma_tables <- fixed_model_tables(sigma_data[[main$label]], "sigma", "One-SD spell")
sigma_tables$fit
sigma_tables$effects
sigma_tables$coefficients
fixed_panel_table(sigma_data, "sigma", "One-SD spell")

# Spells found on the demeaned variable against the raw one: agreement,
# correlation of the demeaned deviations (main panel), and fit on every panel
# (same rows).
sigma_dm_data <- lapply(national_panels, add_run_fixed, fixed_deviation = sigma_spell_demeaned,
                        tag = "sigmadm")
names(sigma_dm_data) <- names(sigma_data)
detection_rows <- function(p) {
  sigma_data[[p]] %>%
    inner_join(select(sigma_dm_data[[p]], GID_1, year, matches("_sigmadm")),
               by = c("GID_1", "year"))
}
detection <- detection_rows(main$label)
bind_rows(lapply(c("TM", "RR"), function(v) bind_rows(lapply(names(RUN_DIRECTIONS), function(dir) {
  raw <- detection[[paste0("position_", v, "_sigma_", dir)]]
  dm <- detection[[paste0("position_", v, "_sigmadm_", dir)]]
  tibble::tibble(variable = v, direction = dir,
                 in_spell_raw = mean(raw >= 2), in_spell_demeaned = mean(dm >= 2),
                 agreement = mean((raw >= 2) == (dm >= 2)),
                 position_correlation = stats::cor(raw, dm),
                 deviation_correlation = stats::cor(detection[[paste0("dm_", v, "_sigma", dir)]],
                                                    detection[[paste0("dm_", v, "_sigmadm", dir)]]))
})))) %>%
  mutate(across(where(is.double), ~ round(.x, 3))) %>%
  knitr::kable(caption = paste0(main$label, ": one-SD spells found on the raw and on the ",
                                "demeaned variable: share of country-years in a spell (position ",
                                "2 or later), agreement, correlation of the positions and of the ",
                                "demeaned deviations"))
bind_rows(lapply(names(sigma_data), function(p) {
  d <- detection_rows(p)
  fits <- list(moving = run_fixed_terms(d, character(0), "sigma"),
               raw = run_fixed_terms(d, c("TM", "RR"), "sigma"),
               demeaned = run_fixed_terms(d, c("TM", "RR"), "sigmadm"))
  models <- lapply(fits, function(x) fit_model(form_terms(FORMS[[RUN_FORM]]), x))
  aic <- vapply(models, stats::AIC, 0)
  tibble::tibble(panel = p, observations = nrow(d), raw_vs_moving = aic[["raw"]] - aic[["moving"]],
                 raw_vs_moving_verdict = fit_verdicts(models$raw, models$moving),
                 demeaned_vs_moving = aic[["demeaned"]] - aic[["moving"]],
                 demeaned_vs_moving_verdict = fit_verdicts(models$demeaned, models$moving),
                 demeaned_vs_raw = aic[["demeaned"]] - aic[["raw"]],
                 demeaned_vs_raw_verdict = fit_verdicts(models$demeaned, models$raw))
})) %>%
  mutate(across(ends_with(c("moving", "raw")), ~ round(.x, 1))) %>%
  knitr::kable(caption = paste0("Every national panel: ", RUN_FORM, ", AIC of the one-SD ",
                                "spell-fixed baselines (T and P) found on the raw and on the ",
                                "demeaned variable, against the moving baseline and each other ",
                                "(same rows), each with the ", VERDICT_NOTE))
```

# The same event later in a spell

Does a hot (dry) year hurt more, or less, when it comes late in a warm (dry)
spell than at its start? The question is asked where the effects are robust:
hot events (the warm arm of temperature) in hot countries, the top third of
the units by long-run temperature, and dry events (the dry arm of
precipitation) in dry-to-mid countries, the bottom two thirds by long-run
precipitation. The model is the 20-year one (`r RUN_FORM`), and the spells
are the one-SD spells of the previous section: the stage of an event year is
its position in the warm spell (for temperature) or the dry spell (for
precipitation), in three bins,

```text
1-2   the first two years of a spell, or no spell (the reference)
3-4   the third and fourth year
5+    the fifth year or later
```

The arm of the robust region gets one extra coefficient per later bin (its
change from the reference), and, as an alternative, one for the spell's length
(years since its first year, capped at nine). The long-run climate enters
either as before (linear interactions) or through dummies of the climate
terciles (each arm with a coefficient per tercile), which can follow a
non-linear pattern across climates. All the models are on the same rows; the
deviations are the moving 20-year ones (the projections) or those held through
the one-SD spells.

```{r spell-stage}
EVENT_SD <- 2  # size of the event whose effect is reported (SD)
STAGES <- c("1-2", "3-4", "5+")

# The 20-year deviation terms (moving or held through the one-SD spells), the
# climate terciles of the panel's units, the stage of each year in its warm and
# dry spell, and the spell lengths.
add_stage_terms <- function(d, deviation = c("moving", "held")) {
  deviation <- match.arg(deviation)
  d <- run_fixed_terms(d, if (deviation == "moving") character(0) else c("TM", "RR"), "sigma")
  units <- distinct(d, GID_1, clim_TM, clim_RR)
  qT <- stats::quantile(units$clim_TM, c(1, 2) / 3, names = FALSE)
  qP <- stats::quantile(units$clim_RR, c(1, 2) / 3, names = FALSE)
  d$Tclim_cold <- as.numeric(d$clim_TM < qT[[1]])
  d$Tclim_mid <- as.numeric(d$clim_TM >= qT[[1]] & d$clim_TM < qT[[2]])
  d$Tclim_hot <- as.numeric(d$clim_TM >= qT[[2]])
  d$Pclim_dry <- as.numeric(d$clim_RR < qP[[1]])
  d$Pclim_mid <- as.numeric(d$clim_RR >= qP[[1]] & d$clim_RR < qP[[2]])
  d$Pclim_wet <- as.numeric(d$clim_RR >= qP[[2]])
  d$Pclim_drymid <- 1 - d$Pclim_wet
  warm <- d$position_TM_sigma_up
  dry <- d$position_RR_sigma_down
  d$warm_3_4 <- as.numeric(warm %in% 3:4)
  d$warm_5plus <- as.numeric(warm >= 5)
  d$dry_3_4 <- as.numeric(dry %in% 3:4)
  d$dry_5plus <- as.numeric(dry >= 5)
  d$warm_length <- pmin(pmax(warm - 1, 0), 9)
  d$dry_length <- pmin(pmax(dry - 1, 0), 9)
  d$warm_stage <- factor(ifelse(warm >= 5, "5+", ifelse(warm >= 3, "3-4", "1-2")), levels = STAGES)
  d$dry_stage <- factor(ifelse(dry >= 5, "5+", ifelse(dry >= 3, "3-4", "1-2")), levels = STAGES)
  attr(d, "thresholds") <- c(hot = qT[[2]], drymid = qP[[2]])
  d
}

TERCILE_TERMS <- c(
  paste0(rep(c(RUN_HOT_ARM, RUN_COLD_ARM), 3), ":",
         rep(c("Tclim_cold", "Tclim_mid", "Tclim_hot"), each = 2)),
  paste0(rep(c(RUN_WET_ARM, RUN_DRY_ARM), 3), ":",
         rep(c("Pclim_dry", "Pclim_mid", "Pclim_wet"), each = 2)),
  CONTROLS
)
HOT_STAGE <- paste0(RUN_HOT_ARM, c(":Tclim_hot:warm_3_4", ":Tclim_hot:warm_5plus"))
DRY_STAGE <- paste0(RUN_DRY_ARM, c(":Pclim_drymid:dry_3_4", ":Pclim_drymid:dry_5plus"))
LENGTH_TERMS <- c(paste0(RUN_HOT_ARM, ":Tclim_hot:warm_length"), paste0(RUN_DRY_ARM, ":Pclim_drymid:dry_length"))
STAGE_MODELS <- list(
  "Linear climate" = form_terms(FORMS[[RUN_FORM]]),
  "Linear climate + stages" = c(form_terms(FORMS[[RUN_FORM]]), HOT_STAGE, DRY_STAGE),
  "Climate terciles" = TERCILE_TERMS,
  "Climate terciles + stages" = c(TERCILE_TERMS, HOT_STAGE, DRY_STAGE),
  "Climate terciles + spell length" = c(TERCILE_TERMS, LENGTH_TERMS)
)
stage_fits <- function(d) lapply(STAGE_MODELS, fit_model, model_data = d)
# Each model with stage or length terms and the same model without them.
STAGE_BASES <- list("Linear climate + stages" = "Linear climate",
                    "Climate terciles + stages" = "Climate terciles",
                    "Climate terciles + spell length" = "Climate terciles")

# The model's name of an interaction, whatever the order of its parts
# (fixest may reorder them); NA if the model has none.
term_named <- function(name, terms) {
  key <- function(x) vapply(strsplit(x, ":", fixed = TRUE), function(p) paste(sort(p), collapse = ":"), "")
  hit <- terms[key(terms) == key(name)]
  if (length(hit)) hit[[1]] else NA_character_
}

# Effect of an event of EVENT_SD SD at each stage: hot in hot countries, dry in
# dry (and mid) countries, from a model with stages (terciles: the tercile's
# coefficient; linear climate: at the median climate of the region's units).
stage_effects <- function(model, d) {
  terms <- names(stats::coef(model))
  units <- distinct(d, GID_1, clim_TM, clim_RR, Tclim_hot, Pclim_dry, Pclim_mid)
  rows <- list(
    list(event = "hot, hot countries", arm = RUN_HOT_ARM, value = arm_event_value(RUN_HOT_ARM, EVENT_SD),
         base = c(Tclim_hot = 1), clim = "clim_TM", region = units$clim_TM[units$Tclim_hot == 1],
         stage = c(NA, HOT_STAGE)),
    list(event = "dry, dry countries", arm = RUN_DRY_ARM, value = arm_event_value(RUN_DRY_ARM, EVENT_SD),
         base = c(Pclim_dry = 1), clim = "clim_RR", region = units$clim_RR[units$Pclim_dry == 1],
         stage = c(NA, DRY_STAGE)),
    list(event = "dry, mid countries", arm = RUN_DRY_ARM, value = arm_event_value(RUN_DRY_ARM, EVENT_SD),
         base = c(Pclim_mid = 1), clim = "clim_RR", region = units$clim_RR[units$Pclim_mid == 1],
         stage = c(NA, DRY_STAGE))
  )
  bind_rows(lapply(rows, function(r) {
    G <- t(vapply(seq_along(STAGES), function(k) {
      w <- stats::setNames(numeric(length(terms)), terms)
      tercile <- term_named(paste0(r$arm, ":", names(r$base)), terms)
      if (!is.na(tercile)) {
        w[[tercile]] <- r$value
      } else {
        w[[r$arm]] <- r$value
        w[[term_named(paste0(r$arm, ":", r$clim), terms)]] <- r$value * stats::median(r$region)
      }
      if (k > 1) w[[term_named(r$stage[[k]], terms)]] <- r$value
      w
    }, numeric(length(terms))))
    colnames(G) <- terms
    linear_combination(model, G) %>%
      mutate(event = r$event, stage = factor(STAGES, levels = STAGES),
             p_value = 2 * stats::pnorm(-abs(estimate / std_error)), .before = 1)
  }))
}

stage_data <- lapply(c(moving = "moving", held = "held"), function(k) {
  add_stage_terms(sigma_data[[main$label]], k)
})
stage_models <- lapply(stage_data, stage_fits)
stopifnot(length(unique(unlist(lapply(stage_models, function(x) vapply(x, stats::nobs, 0))))) == 1)

thresholds <- attr(stage_data$moving, "thresholds")
stage_moving <- stage_data$moving
bind_rows(
  tibble::tibble(event = sprintf("hot (dT > 1 SD), hot countries (mean T >= %.1f C)", thresholds[["hot"]]),
                 stage = with(stage_moving, warm_stage[Tclim_hot == 1 & devTM > 1])),
  tibble::tibble(event = sprintf("dry (dP < -1 SD), dry-to-mid countries (mean P < %.2f m)",
                                 thresholds[["drymid"]]),
                 stage = with(stage_moving, dry_stage[Pclim_drymid == 1 & devRR < -1]))
) %>%
  count(event, stage) %>%
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = stage, values_from = n) %>%
  knitr::kable(caption = paste0(main$label, ": events of more than 1 SD (moving deviations) by ",
                                "stage of their spell (position in the one-SD spell)"))

# 1. Fit and joint tests of the stage (or length) terms of each arm.
bind_rows(lapply(names(stage_models), function(k) {
  bind_rows(lapply(names(stage_models[[k]]), function(m) {
    fit <- stage_models[[k]][[m]]
    test <- function(pattern) {
      if (any(grepl(pattern, names(stats::coef(fit))))) wald_p(fit, pattern) else NA_real_
    }
    # Against the linear-climate model (nested only for "Linear climate +
    # stages"), and against the same model without the stage or length terms.
    linear <- stage_models[[k]][["Linear climate"]]
    base <- STAGE_BASES[[m]]
    tibble::tibble(deviation = k, model = m, parameters = length(stats::coef(fit)),
                   aic = stats::AIC(fit),
                   verdict_vs_linear_climate = if (m == "Linear climate") "" else if (
                     m == "Linear climate + stages") {
                     fit_verdicts(fit, linear, nested_p = added_terms_p(fit, linear))
                   } else fit_verdicts(fit, linear),
                   verdict_vs_without_stages = if (is.null(base)) "" else {
                     without <- stage_models[[k]][[base]]
                     fit_verdicts(fit, without, nested_p = added_terms_p(fit, without))
                   },
                   hot_stage_p = test("Tclim_hot:warm"), dry_stage_p = test("Pclim_drymid:dry"))
  }))
})) %>%
  group_by(deviation) %>%
  mutate(aic_vs_linear_climate = round(aic - aic[model == "Linear climate"], 1)) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  mutate(across(ends_with("_p"), ~ signif(.x, 2))) %>%
  select(deviation, model, parameters, aic_vs_linear_climate, verdict_vs_linear_climate,
         verdict_vs_without_stages, hot_stage_p, dry_stage_p) %>%
  knitr::kable(caption = paste0(main$label, ", ", RUN_FORM, ", 20-year deviations: AIC against ",
                                "the linear-climate model (same deviations) and the ", VERDICT_NOTE,
                                " against it and against the same model without the stage or ",
                                "length terms (nested: their joint test); joint tests (p) of ",
                                "the stage or length terms of the hot arm in hot countries and of ",
                                "the dry arm in dry-to-mid countries"))

# 2. Effect of a 2 SD event at each stage.
bind_rows(lapply(names(stage_models), function(k) {
  bind_rows(lapply(c("Linear climate + stages", "Climate terciles + stages"), function(m) {
    stage_effects(stage_models[[k]][[m]], stage_data[[k]]) %>%
      mutate(column = paste0(m, " (", k, ")"))
  }))
})) %>%
  mutate(cell = sprintf("%+.2f [%+.2f, %+.2f]%s", 100 * estimate, 100 * conf_low, 100 * conf_high,
                        stars(p_value))) %>%
  select(event, stage, column, cell) %>%
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = column, values_from = cell) %>%
  knitr::kable(caption = paste0(main$label, ": effect on growth that year (pp, 95% CI) of a ",
                                EVENT_SD, " SD event by stage of its spell; linear climate at the ",
                                "median climate of the region's units; *** p < 0.01, ** p < 0.05, ",
                                "* p < 0.1"))

# 3. Every national panel (moving deviations, climate terciles + stages): the
# change of the arm's coefficient at each later stage, relative to its start.
bind_rows(lapply(names(sigma_data), function(p) {
  dd <- add_stage_terms(sigma_data[[p]], "moving")
  fit <- fit_model(STAGE_MODELS[["Climate terciles + stages"]], dd)
  ct <- fixest::coeftable(fit)
  cell <- function(term) {
    term <- term_named(term, rownames(ct))
    sprintf("%+.4f%s", ct[term, "Estimate"],
            stars(2 * stats::pnorm(-abs(ct[term, "Estimate"] / ct[term, "Std. Error"]))))
  }
  tibble::tibble(panel = p, hot_3_4 = cell(HOT_STAGE[[1]]), hot_5plus = cell(HOT_STAGE[[2]]),
                 hot_p = signif(wald_p(fit, "Tclim_hot:warm"), 2),
                 dry_3_4 = cell(DRY_STAGE[[1]]), dry_5plus = cell(DRY_STAGE[[2]]),
                 dry_p = signif(wald_p(fit, "Pclim_drymid:dry"), 2),
                 hot_base = cell(paste0(RUN_HOT_ARM, ":Tclim_hot")), dry_base_dry = cell(paste0(RUN_DRY_ARM, ":Pclim_dry")))
})) %>%
  knitr::kable(caption = paste0("Every national panel, climate terciles + stages, moving ",
                                "deviations: change of the coefficient of the hot arm (hot ",
                                "countries) and of the dry arm (dry-to-mid countries) at stages 3-4 ",
                                "and 5+ relative to 1-2, joint tests (p), and the coefficients at ",
                                "1-2 (hot countries; dry countries); *** p < 0.01, ** p < 0.05, * p < 0.1"))
```

# Preferred model and the BHM level terms

The preferred model with the BHM level terms added, on every panel (the same
fixed effects as the preferred model: unit linear and quadratic trends):

```text
growth = deviation terms (preferred model) + b1 TM + b2 TM^2 + b3 RR + b4 RR^2 + controls + FE
```

Does each block still matter given the other? Joint Wald tests of the deviation
terms of each variable and of its BHM terms, alone and together, and the AIC of
the combined model against each alone. In the combined model a deviation of
the year also moves `TM` and `TM^2` (or `RR`, `RR^2`), so its effect is not
the deviation terms alone; the joint tests and the AIC are the comparison.

```{r bhm-preferred}
BHM_TERMS <- c("TM", "TM2", "RR", "RR2")

bhm_comparison <- function(fit) {
  d <- fit$data
  m_bhm <- fit_model(c(BHM_TERMS, CONTROLS), d)
  m_both <- fit_model(c(preferred_terms, BHM_TERMS), d)
  stopifnot(stats::nobs(m_bhm) == stats::nobs(fit$preferred),
            stats::nobs(m_both) == stats::nobs(fit$preferred))
  list(
    models = list("BHM" = m_bhm, "Preferred" = fit$preferred, "Preferred + BHM" = m_both),
    tests = tibble::tibble(
      panel = fit$panel$label,
      dev_T_alone = wald_p(fit$preferred, "^devTM"),
      dev_T_with_bhm = wald_p(m_both, "^devTM"),
      bhm_T_alone = wald_p(m_bhm, "^TM2?$"),
      bhm_T_with_dev = wald_p(m_both, "^TM2?$"),
      dev_P_alone = wald_p(fit$preferred, "^devRR"),
      dev_P_with_bhm = wald_p(m_both, "^devRR"),
      bhm_P_alone = wald_p(m_bhm, "^RR2?$"),
      bhm_P_with_dev = wald_p(m_both, "^RR2?$"),
      aic_vs_preferred = stats::AIC(m_both) - stats::AIC(fit$preferred),
      verdict_vs_preferred = fit_verdicts(m_both, fit$preferred,
                                          nested_p = added_terms_p(m_both, fit$preferred)),
      aic_vs_bhm = stats::AIC(m_both) - stats::AIC(m_bhm),
      verdict_vs_bhm = fit_verdicts(m_both, m_bhm, nested_p = added_terms_p(m_both, m_bhm))
    )
  )
}

bhm_comparisons <- lapply(c(national_fits, list(dose_fit)), bhm_comparison)

etable(bhm_comparisons[[1]]$models, dict = DICT, drop = DROP,
       order = c("%^TM$", "%^TM2$", "%^RR$", "%^RR2$", ORDER), fitstat = FITSTAT,
       title = main$label)

bind_rows(lapply(bhm_comparisons, `[[`, "tests")) %>%
  mutate(across(c(starts_with("dev_"), starts_with("bhm_")), ~ signif(.x, 2)),
         across(starts_with("aic_"), ~ round(.x, 1))) %>%
  knitr::kable(caption = paste("Joint Wald tests (p) of the deviation terms (dev) and of the BHM",
                               "terms (bhm) of each variable, alone and with the other block;",
                               "AIC of the combined model minus each alone, and its",
                               VERDICT_NOTE, "against each (nested: the joint test of the block",
                               "it adds)"))
```

# Preferred model and lagged income

The preferred model with the previous year's log GDP per capita, on every
panel:

```text
growth = deviation terms (preferred model) + h log(GDP per capita)(t-1) + controls + FE
```

With unit fixed effects and trends, `h` is mostly mean reversion within units
(and has the small-T bias of a lagged level with unit effects). Do the
deviation terms survive it?

The lagged level is log GDP per capita of the year before, from the same
series as the outcome, so the rows are those of the preferred model. The
first table gives its coefficient and standard error, the within R2 without
and with it, and the joint tests of each variable's deviation terms without
and with it; the second, the effects of a +/-3 SD year in the model with it.
A lagged level also makes growth depend on past shocks through income, so
these effects are those on growth in the year, holding last year's income
fixed.

```{r lagged-income}
lagged_income <- function(fit) {
  d <- mutate(fit$data, lag_log_gdp_pc = lgrp_pc_usd - dlgrp_pc_usd)
  m <- fit_model(c(preferred_terms, "lag_log_gdp_pc"), d)
  stopifnot(stats::nobs(m) == stats::nobs(fit$preferred))
  ct <- fixest::coeftable(m)
  list(
    model = m,
    tests = tibble::tibble(
      panel = fit$panel$label,
      lag_gdp = ct["lag_log_gdp_pc", 1], lag_gdp_se = ct["lag_log_gdp_pc", 2],
      within_r2_without = fixest::fitstat(fit$preferred, "wr2")[[1]],
      within_r2_with = fixest::fitstat(m, "wr2")[[1]],
      T_p_without = wald_p(fit$preferred, "^devTM"), T_p_with = wald_p(m, "^devTM"),
      P_p_without = wald_p(fit$preferred, "^devRR"), P_p_with = wald_p(m, "^devRR")
    )
  )
}

income_fits <- lapply(c(national_fits, list(dose_fit)), lagged_income)

bind_rows(lapply(income_fits, `[[`, "tests")) %>%
  mutate(across(c(lag_gdp, lag_gdp_se, within_r2_without, within_r2_with), ~ round(.x, 4)),
         across(ends_with("_without") | ends_with("_with"), ~ signif(.x, 2))) %>%
  knitr::kable(caption = paste("Lagged log GDP per capita: its coefficient, the within R2 and the",
                               "joint tests (p) of each variable's deviation terms without and",
                               "with it"))

income_effects <- bind_rows(lapply(seq_along(income_fits), function(i) {
  climate_effects(list(preferred = income_fits[[i]]$model,
                       panel = list(label = income_fits[[i]]$tests$panel)))
}))
significance_map(income_effects) %>%
  knitr::kable(caption = paste("With lagged log GDP per capita: effect of a +/-3 SD deviation",
                               "(pp) at long-run climates of 5, 15, 25 °C and 0.5, 1.5, 3 m;",
                               "*** p < 0.01, ** p < 0.05, * p < 0.1"))
```

# Lags of the deviations

Instead of lagged income, the deviation terms of the previous five years, in
the same forms and interacted with the same long-run climate, for both
variables:

```text
growth = sum over k = 0..5 of [ temperature terms(t-k) + precipitation terms(t-k) ] + controls + FE
```

The lags are the deviations of the calendar years before (from every year of
the panel, whether or not it has growth), so a unit-year enters only with all
five lags. The cumulative effect of a deviation through year K is the sum of
its effects on growth in years 0..K, i.e. its effect on the level of GDP per
capita after K years: if a loss is recovered it returns towards zero, if it
persists it stays. The model without lags is re-estimated on the same rows.

Two versions:

- unrestricted: every lag has its own arm coefficients and its own
  interactions with the long-run climate (8 coefficients a lag);
- common interaction: every lag has its own arm coefficients, but each arm has
  one interaction with the long-run climate shared by all lags,

  ```text
  sum over k of [ a+_k dT+(t-k) + a-_k dT-(t-k) ]
    + b+ (sum over k of dT+(t-k)) x clim_TM + b- (sum over k of dT-(t-k)) x clim_TM
  ```

  (and the same for precipitation), so the effect of lag k at long-run climate
  m is `a_k + b m`: the climate shifts the response equally in every year.

  In both, the long-run climate is that of the current year t (with a matched
  20-year interaction, the mean of the 20 years before t, for every lag).
  The test of the restriction is the joint (chi-square) Wald test, in the
  unrestricted model, that each arm's interaction is the same at every lag.

```{r deviation-lags}
# Chi-square Wald test of H b = 0 (clustered VCOV of the model).
wald_linear_p <- function(model, H) {
  b <- stats::coef(model)[colnames(H)]
  V <- stats::vcov(model)[colnames(H), colnames(H)]
  r <- H %*% b
  stat <- as.numeric(t(r) %*% solve(H %*% V %*% t(H)) %*% r)
  stats::pchisq(stat, df = nrow(H), lower.tail = FALSE)
}
# In the unrestricted model: each arm of the variables `vars` has the same
# interaction at every lag (b_k = b_0 for k = 1..N_LAGS).
equal_interactions_p <- function(model, vars) {
  terms <- names(stats::coef(model))
  rows <- list()
  for (v in vars) for (col in form_columns(v)) {
    climate <- paste0("clim_", v)
    base <- interaction_name(col, climate, terms)
    for (k in seq_len(N_LAGS)) {
      h <- stats::setNames(numeric(length(terms)), terms)
      h[[interaction_name(paste0(col, lag_suffix(k)), climate, terms)]] <- 1
      h[[base]] <- -1
      rows[[length(rows) + 1]] <- h
    }
  }
  wald_linear_p(model, do.call(rbind, rows))
}

distributed_lags <- function(fit) {
  d <- add_deviation_lags(fit)
  all_lags <- unlist(lapply(seq_len(N_LAGS), function(k) c(lag_terms("TM", k), lag_terms("RR", k))))
  m0 <- fit_model(preferred_terms, d)
  m <- fit_model(c(preferred_terms, all_lags), d)
  mr <- fit_model(c(restricted_terms("TM"), restricted_terms("RR"), CONTROLS), d)
  stopifnot(stats::nobs(m0) == stats::nobs(m), stats::nobs(m0) == stats::nobs(mr))
  list(
    panel = fit$panel, no_lags = m0, lags = m, restricted = mr,
    tests = tibble::tibble(
      panel = fit$panel$label, first_year = min(d$year), observations = stats::nobs(m),
      T_p_no_lags = wald_p(m0, "^devTM"), P_p_no_lags = wald_p(m0, "^devRR"),
      T_lags_p = wald_p(m, "^devTM[^:]*_l[0-9]"), P_lags_p = wald_p(m, "^devRR[^:]*_l[0-9]"),
      T_lags_p_common = wald_p(mr, "^devTM[^:]*_l[0-9]"),
      P_lags_p_common = wald_p(mr, "^devRR[^:]*_l[0-9]"),
      equal_T_p = equal_interactions_p(m, "TM"), equal_P_p = equal_interactions_p(m, "RR"),
      aic_lags_vs_no_lags = stats::AIC(m) - stats::AIC(m0),
      aic_common_vs_no_lags = stats::AIC(mr) - stats::AIC(m0),
      verdict_lags_vs_no_lags = fit_verdicts(m, m0, nested_p = added_terms_p(m, m0)),
      verdict_common_vs_no_lags = fit_verdicts(mr, m0),
      verdict_common_vs_unrestricted = fit_verdicts(
        mr, m, nested_p = equal_interactions_p(m, c("TM", "RR")))
    )
  )
}

lag_fits <- lapply(c(national_fits, list(dose_fit)), distributed_lags)
lag_effects <- bind_rows(lapply(lag_fits, function(x) {
  cumulative_effects(x$lags, x$panel$label)
}))
common_effects <- bind_rows(lapply(lag_fits, function(x) {
  cumulative_effects(x$restricted, x$panel$label, restricted = TRUE)
}))

lag_tests <- bind_rows(lapply(lag_fits, `[[`, "tests")) %>%
  mutate(across(c(starts_with("T_"), starts_with("P_"), starts_with("equal_")),
                ~ format.pval(signif(.x, 2), eps = 0.001)),
         across(starts_with("aic_"), ~ round(.x, 1)))
lag_tests %>%
  select(panel, first_year, observations, T_p_no_lags, P_p_no_lags, T_lags_p, P_lags_p,
         aic_lags_vs_no_lags, verdict_lags_vs_no_lags) %>%
  knitr::kable(caption = paste("Unrestricted lags: joint tests (p) of the deviation terms without",
                               "lags and of all the lags of each variable; AIC with lags minus",
                               "without, and the", VERDICT_NOTE, "(nested: the joint test of all",
                               "the lags)"))
lag_tests %>%
  select(panel, T_lags_p_common, P_lags_p_common, equal_T_p, equal_P_p, aic_common_vs_no_lags,
         verdict_common_vs_no_lags, aic_lags_vs_no_lags, verdict_common_vs_unrestricted) %>%
  mutate(aic_common_vs_unrestricted = aic_common_vs_no_lags - aic_lags_vs_no_lags) %>%
  select(-aic_lags_vs_no_lags) %>%
  relocate(aic_common_vs_unrestricted, .before = verdict_common_vs_unrestricted) %>%
  knitr::kable(caption = paste("Common interaction: joint tests (p) of the lags of each variable;",
                               "test that each arm's interaction is the same at every lag (in",
                               "the unrestricted model); AIC against no lags and against the",
                               "unrestricted lags, each with the", VERDICT_NOTE, "(against the",
                               "unrestricted lags: the joint test of the equal interactions of",
                               "both variables)"))

significance_map(filter(lag_effects, through == 0)) %>%
  knitr::kable(caption = paste("Unrestricted lags: effect in the year of the deviation (pp);",
                               "*** p < 0.01, ** p < 0.05, * p < 0.1"))
significance_map(filter(lag_effects, through == N_LAGS)) %>%
  knitr::kable(caption = paste("Unrestricted lags: cumulative effect over the year of the",
                               "deviation and the five after (pp of GDP per capita); *** p < 0.01,",
                               "** p < 0.05, * p < 0.1"))
significance_map(filter(common_effects, through == 0)) %>%
  knitr::kable(caption = paste("Common interaction: effect in the year of the deviation (pp);",
                               "*** p < 0.01, ** p < 0.05, * p < 0.1"))
significance_map(filter(common_effects, through == N_LAGS)) %>%
  knitr::kable(caption = paste("Common interaction: cumulative effect over the year of the",
                               "deviation and the five after (pp of GDP per capita); *** p < 0.01,",
                               "** p < 0.05, * p < 0.1"))
```

```{r deviation-lags-plot, fig.width=13, fig.height=7}
LAG_CELLS <- tibble::tribble(
```

## Ten lags, common interaction

The common-interaction model with the deviations of the previous ten years,
against the model without lags on the same rows (the ERA5 panels then start in
1970: a 20-year precipitation deviation needs climate from 20 years before).
The confidence intervals of the cumulative effects use the full clustered
covariance of all the lag coefficients.

```{r ten-lags}
common_long_lags <- function(fit) {
  d <- add_deviation_lags(fit, N_LAGS_LONG)
  m0 <- fit_model(preferred_terms, d)
  mr <- fit_model(c(restricted_terms("TM", N_LAGS_LONG), restricted_terms("RR", N_LAGS_LONG),
                    CONTROLS), d)
  stopifnot(stats::nobs(m0) == stats::nobs(mr))
  list(
    panel = fit$panel, model = mr,
    tests = tibble::tibble(
      panel = fit$panel$label, first_year = min(d$year), observations = stats::nobs(mr),
      T_lags_p = wald_p(mr, "^devTM[^:]*_l[0-9]"), P_lags_p = wald_p(mr, "^devRR[^:]*_l[0-9]"),
      aic_vs_no_lags = stats::AIC(mr) - stats::AIC(m0),
      verdict_vs_no_lags = fit_verdicts(mr, m0)
    )
  )
}

long_fits <- lapply(c(national_fits, list(dose_fit)), common_long_lags)
long_effects <- bind_rows(lapply(long_fits, function(x) {
  cumulative_effects(x$model, x$panel$label, restricted = TRUE, n_lags = N_LAGS_LONG)
}))

bind_rows(lapply(long_fits, `[[`, "tests")) %>%
  mutate(across(c(T_lags_p, P_lags_p), ~ format.pval(signif(.x, 2), eps = 0.001)),
         aic_vs_no_lags = round(aic_vs_no_lags, 1)) %>%
  knitr::kable(caption = paste("Ten lags, common interaction: joint tests (p) of the lags of each",
                               "variable; AIC minus the model without lags on the same rows, and",
                               "the", VERDICT_NOTE))

significance_map(filter(long_effects, through == 5)) %>%
  knitr::kable(caption = paste("Ten lags, common interaction: cumulative effect through five years",
                               "(pp of GDP per capita); *** p < 0.01, ** p < 0.05, * p < 0.1"))
significance_map(filter(long_effects, through == N_LAGS_LONG)) %>%
  knitr::kable(caption = paste("Ten lags, common interaction: cumulative effect through ten years",
                               "(pp of GDP per capita); *** p < 0.01, ** p < 0.05, * p < 0.1"))
```

```{r ten-lags-plot, fig.width=13, fig.height=7}
  labs(subtitle = paste0(PREFERRED_FORM, ", ", PREFERRED_DEFINITION, " deviations, ten lags; ",
```

# Persistence: fewer restrictions on the lag response, and local projections

The common interaction above makes every lag's response depend on the
long-run climate in the same way (one slope per arm, shared by the lags), and
the test of that restriction rejects it in several panels. Here the lag
response is estimated with fewer restrictions, against local projections that
estimate the response at each horizon separately, and the recovery of the
losses and their persistence are tested explicitly.

1. Distributed lags, ten lags, each lag with its own arm coefficients, and the
   interaction with the long-run climate
   - common: one per arm, shared by all the lags (as above);
   - blocks: one per arm for each block of lags, {0}, {1-2}, {3-5}, {6-10};
   - unrestricted: one per arm and lag (88 weather coefficients).

   The restrictions are tested in the unrestricted model (each arm's
   interaction the same at every lag; the same within each block), and the
   three compared by AIC and BIC, on every panel.
2. Local projections (Jorda 2005): for each horizon h = 0..10 its own
