   regression of the cumulative change of log GDP per capita from t-1 to t+h
   (the sum of growth over t..t+h) on the deviation terms of year t with their
   interactions, controlling for the deviation terms of t-1 and t-2 and for
   growth in t-1 and t-2, with the fixed effects of every model (year, and each
   unit's level and trends) and errors clustered by country. Each horizon has
   its own coefficients and climate interaction, so nothing ties the response
   across horizons. The rows are the same at every horizon (the outcome over
   all ten years); a window with a growth outlier dropped from the sample (a
   cause not involving weather) is left out.
3. Tests, for the cells of the figures above: persistent loss, the cumulative
   effect after ten years is zero (H0: cum10 = 0); recovery, the cumulative
   effect after ten years equals the effect in the year of the deviation (H0:
   cum10 = impact; rejected towards zero when the loss is recovered, away
   from it when it grows). In the distributed lags both are linear
   combinations of the coefficients; in the local projections the second is
   the regression of the growth of years t+1..t+10 (exactly the difference of
   the two horizons, with its own standard error).

The models are the preferred one (`r PREFERRED_FORM`, `r PREFERRED_DEFINITION`
deviations), and on PWT x ERA5 also with the 20-year deviations. The
restrictions on the interaction (the first table and figure) are tested on the
main samples of every national panel and DOSE. The comparison of the
distributed lags with the local projections (the other tables and the figure
of the cumulative paths) is on the full national panels, the growth outliers
included (as rows and within the ten years ahead), and on the same rows for
both methods: those with the ten lags of the distributed lags, and with the
two lags and the ten years ahead of the local projections.

```{r persistence, fig.width=13, fig.height=7}
PERSIST_LAGS <- N_LAGS_LONG
PERSIST_HORIZON <- N_LAGS_LONG
LAG_BLOCKS <- list(b0 = 0L, b1_2 = 1:2, b3_5 = 3:5, b6_10 = 6:10)
PERSIST_CELLS <- tibble::tribble(
  ~variable, ~deviation, ~climate, ~cell,
  "TM", 3, 25, "T +3 SD at 25 C",
  "TM", -3, 25, "T -3 SD at 25 C",
  "TM", -3, 5, "T -3 SD at 5 C",
  "RR", -3, 0.5, "P -3 SD at 0.5 m",
  "RR", -3, 1.5, "P -3 SD at 1.5 m",
  "RR", 3, 0.5, "P +3 SD at 0.5 m"
)
DL_VERSIONS <- c("common", "blocks", "unrestricted")
block_of <- function(k) names(LAG_BLOCKS)[vapply(LAG_BLOCKS, function(b) k %in% b, TRUE)]

# Each arm's sum over the lags of each block.
add_lag_blocks <- function(d) {
  for (v in c("TM", "RR")) for (col in form_columns(v)) for (b in names(LAG_BLOCKS)) {
    d[[paste0(col, "_", b)]] <- Reduce(`+`, lapply(LAG_BLOCKS[[b]], function(k) {
      d[[paste0(col, lag_suffix(k))]]
    }))
  }
  d
}
# Terms of the distributed lags, 0..PERSIST_LAGS, by version of the interaction.
persistence_terms <- function(version) {
  weather <- unlist(lapply(c("TM", "RR"), function(v) {
    cols <- form_columns(v)
    arms <- unlist(lapply(0:PERSIST_LAGS, function(k) paste0(cols, lag_suffix(k))))
    climate <- paste0(":clim_", v)
    interactions <- switch(
      version,
      common = paste0(cols, "_sum", climate),
      blocks = as.vector(outer(cols, names(LAG_BLOCKS), function(c, b) paste0(c, "_", b, climate))),
      unrestricted = paste0(arms, climate)
    )
    c(arms, interactions)
  }))
  c(weather, CONTROLS)
}
# Weights on the coefficients `terms` of the cumulative effect through year K of
# a deviation x in year 0 at long-run climate m (K = 0 and "unrestricted": the
# terms of year t, as in a local projection).
cumulative_weights <- function(terms, version, v, x, m, K) {
  w <- stats::setNames(numeric(length(terms)), terms)
  climate <- paste0("clim_", v)
  for (s in FORMS[[PREFERRED_FORM]][[v]]) {
    value <- term_value(s, x)
    col <- paste0("dev", v, s)
    for (k in 0:K) {
      w[[paste0(col, lag_suffix(k))]] <- w[[paste0(col, lag_suffix(k))]] + value
      target <- switch(version, common = paste0(col, "_sum"),
                       blocks = paste0(col, "_", block_of(k)),
                       unrestricted = paste0(col, lag_suffix(k)))
      name <- interaction_name(target, climate, terms)
      w[[name]] <- w[[name]] + value * m
    }
  }
  w
}
combination_row <- function(model, w) {
  linear_combination(model, w) %>%
    mutate(p_value = 2 * stats::pnorm(-abs(estimate / std_error)))
}
# Wald test (clustered) that each arm's interaction is the same at every lag of
# each group of `groups` (in the unrestricted model).
equal_interaction_p <- function(model, groups) {
  terms <- names(stats::coef(model))
  rows <- list()
  for (v in c("TM", "RR")) for (col in form_columns(v)) for (g in groups) {
    if (length(g) < 2) next
    first <- interaction_name(paste0(col, lag_suffix(g[[1]])), paste0("clim_", v), terms)
    for (k in g[-1]) {
      h <- stats::setNames(numeric(length(terms)), terms)
      h[[interaction_name(paste0(col, lag_suffix(k)), paste0("clim_", v), terms)]] <- 1
      h[[first]] <- -1
      rows[[length(rows) + 1]] <- h
    }
  }
  wald_linear_p(model, do.call(rbind, rows))
}

# 1. Distributed lags, the three versions of the interaction, on the rows `d`
# (with the lags and their blocks), and the tests of the restrictions.
dl_models <- function(d) {
  models <- lapply(stats::setNames(nm = DL_VERSIONS), function(k) {
    fit_model(persistence_terms(k), d)
  })
  stopifnot(length(unique(vapply(models, stats::nobs, 0))) == 1)
  models
}
restriction_tests <- function(models, label) {
  common_p <- equal_interaction_p(models$unrestricted, list(0:PERSIST_LAGS))
  blocks_p <- equal_interaction_p(models$unrestricted, LAG_BLOCKS)
  tibble::tibble(
    panel = label, observations = stats::nobs(models$unrestricted),
    common_p = common_p, blocks_p = blocks_p,
    aic_common = stats::AIC(models$common) - stats::AIC(models$unrestricted),
    aic_blocks = stats::AIC(models$blocks) - stats::AIC(models$unrestricted),
    bic_common = stats::BIC(models$common) - stats::BIC(models$unrestricted),
    bic_blocks = stats::BIC(models$blocks) - stats::BIC(models$unrestricted),
    verdict_common = fit_verdicts(models$common, models$unrestricted, nested_p = common_p),
    verdict_blocks = fit_verdicts(models$blocks, models$unrestricted, nested_p = blocks_p))
}
# On the main sample of a fit (the restrictions).
distributed_persistence <- function(fit, suffix = PREFERRED_SUFFIX, label = fit$panel$label) {
  models <- dl_models(add_lag_blocks(add_deviation_lags(fit, PERSIST_LAGS, suffix = suffix)))
  list(label = label, models = models, tests = restriction_tests(models, label))
}
dl_runs <- c(lapply(c(national_fits, list(dose_fit)), distributed_persistence),
             list(distributed_persistence(
               list(panel = main, data = add_deviation_terms(main$clean, DEFINITIONS[["20-year"]])),
               suffix = DEFINITIONS[["20-year"]], label = paste(main$label, "(20-year)"))))

# 2. The comparison: the full panel (the growth outliers included), the rows
# with the ten lags of the distributed lags and with the two lags and the ten
# years ahead of the local projections, the cumulative changes of log GDP per
# capita from t-1 to t+h (cum_h), and the growth of t+1..t+10 (after_impact).
comparison_rows <- function(panel, suffix) {
  base <- add_lag_blocks(add_deviation_lags(
    list(panel = panel, data = add_deviation_terms(panel$all, suffix)),
    n_lags = PERSIST_LAGS, suffix = suffix))
  growth <- panel$data %>%
    transmute(GID_1, year, g = .data[[OUTCOME]]) %>%
    filter(year >= START_YEAR)
  at <- function(shift, name) {
    x <- growth
    x$year <- x$year - shift
    stats::setNames(x, c("GID_1", "year", name))
  }
  for (j in 1:2) base <- left_join(base, at(-j, paste0("g_lag", j)), by = c("GID_1", "year"))
  for (h in 0:PERSIST_HORIZON) {
    base <- left_join(base, at(h, "g_ahead"), by = c("GID_1", "year"))
    base[[paste0("cum_", h)]] <- (if (h == 0) 0 else base[[paste0("cum_", h - 1)]]) + base$g_ahead
    base$g_ahead <- NULL
  }
  base$after_impact <- base[[paste0("cum_", PERSIST_HORIZON)]] - base$cum_0
  base[is.finite(base[[paste0("cum_", PERSIST_HORIZON)]]) & is.finite(base$g_lag1) &
         is.finite(base$g_lag2), ]
}
LP_TERMS <- c(form_terms(FORMS[[PREFERRED_FORM]]), lag_terms("TM", 1), lag_terms("TM", 2),
              lag_terms("RR", 1), lag_terms("RR", 2), "g_lag1", "g_lag2")
comparison_run <- function(panel, suffix = PREFERRED_SUFFIX, label = panel$label) {
  d <- comparison_rows(panel, suffix)
  outcomes <- c(paste0("cum_", 0:PERSIST_HORIZON), "after_impact")
  lp <- lapply(stats::setNames(nm = outcomes), function(y) fit_model(LP_TERMS, d, outcome = y))
  dl <- dl_models(d)
  stopifnot(stats::nobs(dl$unrestricted) == stats::nobs(lp$cum_0))
  list(label = label, rows = stats::nobs(lp$cum_0), years = range(d$year), dl = dl, lp = lp)
}
comparison_runs <- c(lapply(national_panels, comparison_run),
                     list(comparison_run(main, DEFINITIONS[["20-year"]],
                                         paste(main$label, "(20-year)"))))

# Cumulative paths, and the two tests at ten years, of every comparison run.
persistence_paths <- bind_rows(lapply(comparison_runs, function(run) {
  bind_rows(
    bind_rows(lapply(DL_VERSIONS, function(k) {
      m <- run$dl[[k]]
      terms <- names(stats::coef(m))
      bind_rows(lapply(seq_len(nrow(PERSIST_CELLS)), function(i) {
        cell <- PERSIST_CELLS[i, ]
        bind_rows(lapply(0:PERSIST_LAGS, function(K) {
          combination_row(m, cumulative_weights(terms, k, cell$variable, cell$deviation,
                                                cell$climate, K)) %>%
            mutate(panel = run$label, method = paste("distributed lags,", k), cell = cell$cell,
                   through = K)
        }))
      }))
    })),
    bind_rows(lapply(seq_len(nrow(PERSIST_CELLS)), function(i) {
      cell <- PERSIST_CELLS[i, ]
      bind_rows(lapply(0:PERSIST_HORIZON, function(h) {
        m <- run$lp[[paste0("cum_", h)]]
        combination_row(m, cumulative_weights(names(stats::coef(m)), "unrestricted",
                                              cell$variable, cell$deviation, cell$climate, 0)) %>%
          mutate(panel = run$label, method = "local projections", cell = cell$cell, through = h)
      }))
    }))
  )
}))
persistence_tests <- bind_rows(lapply(comparison_runs, function(run) {
  bind_rows(
    bind_rows(lapply(DL_VERSIONS, function(k) {
      m <- run$dl[[k]]
      terms <- names(stats::coef(m))
      bind_rows(lapply(seq_len(nrow(PERSIST_CELLS)), function(i) {
        cell <- PERSIST_CELLS[i, ]
        w <- function(K) cumulative_weights(terms, k, cell$variable, cell$deviation, cell$climate, K)
        tibble::tibble(panel = run$label, method = paste("distributed lags,", k), cell = cell$cell,
                       zero_p = combination_row(m, w(PERSIST_LAGS))$p_value,
                       recovery = combination_row(m, w(PERSIST_LAGS) - w(0)))
      }))
    })),
    bind_rows(lapply(seq_len(nrow(PERSIST_CELLS)), function(i) {
      cell <- PERSIST_CELLS[i, ]
      impact <- function(m) {
        cumulative_weights(names(stats::coef(m)), "unrestricted", cell$variable, cell$deviation,
                           cell$climate, 0)
      }
      m10 <- run$lp[[paste0("cum_", PERSIST_HORIZON)]]
      after <- run$lp$after_impact
      tibble::tibble(panel = run$label, method = "local projections", cell = cell$cell,
                     zero_p = combination_row(m10, impact(m10))$p_value,
                     recovery = combination_row(after, impact(after)))
    }))
  )
})) %>%
  tidyr::unpack(recovery, names_sep = "_")

# Table 1: the restrictions on the interaction, every panel.
bind_rows(lapply(dl_runs, `[[`, "tests")) %>%
  mutate(across(ends_with("_p"), ~ format.pval(signif(.x, 2), eps = 0.001)),
         across(starts_with(c("aic_", "bic_")), ~ round(.x, 1))) %>%
  knitr::kable(caption = paste0(
    "Ten lags, main samples: tests (p, clustered Wald, in the unrestricted model) that each ",
    "arm's climate interaction is the same at every lag (common) and within each block of lags ",
    "(blocks), and the AIC and BIC of the common and block models minus the unrestricted one ",
    "(same rows), with their ", VERDICT_NOTE, " against it (nested: the test of the ",
    "restriction)"))

cat("Comparison rows (full panels, growth outliers included; the same for both methods):",
    paste(vapply(comparison_runs, function(r) {
      sprintf("%s %d (%d-%d)", r$label, r$rows, r$years[[1]], r$years[[2]])
    }, ""), collapse = "; "))

# Table 2: impact, cumulative effects and the two tests, PWT x ERA5.
summary_cells <- function(panels) {
  persistence_paths %>%
    filter(panel %in% panels, through %in% c(0, 5, PERSIST_HORIZON)) %>%
    mutate(value = sprintf("%+.2f%s", 100 * estimate, stars(p_value)),
           through = paste0("cum", through)) %>%
    select(panel, method, cell, through, value) %>%
    tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = through, values_from = value) %>%
    left_join(persistence_tests %>%
                transmute(panel, method, cell, cum10_zero_p = signif(zero_p, 2),
                          cum10_minus_impact = sprintf("%+.2f%s", 100 * recovery_estimate,
                                                       stars(recovery_p_value)),
                          recovery_p = signif(recovery_p_value, 2)),
              by = c("panel", "method", "cell")) %>%
    arrange(panel, factor(cell, levels = PERSIST_CELLS$cell), method)
}
summary_cells(c(main$label, paste(main$label, "(20-year)"))) %>%
  knitr::kable(caption = paste0(
    main$label, ", full panel (growth outliers included), the same rows for every method: ",
    "effect in the year of the deviation (cum0) and cumulative effect through ",
    "five and ten years (pp of GDP per capita); cum10_zero_p: test of no persistent loss ",
    "(cum10 = 0); cum10_minus_impact and recovery_p: what is recovered (or added) after the ",
    "first year, and the test that it is zero (cum10 = impact); *** p < 0.01, ** p < 0.05, ",
    "* p < 0.1"))

# Table 3: local projections and unrestricted distributed lags on every
# national panel.
persistence_tests %>%
  filter(method %in% c("local projections", "distributed lags, unrestricted"),
         !grepl("(", panel, fixed = TRUE)) %>%
  left_join(persistence_paths %>%
              filter(through %in% c(0, PERSIST_HORIZON)) %>%
              transmute(panel, method, cell, through = paste0("cum", through),
                        value = sprintf("%+.2f%s", 100 * estimate, stars(p_value))) %>%
              tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = through, values_from = value),
            by = c("panel", "method", "cell")) %>%
  transmute(cell = factor(cell, levels = PERSIST_CELLS$cell), panel,
            method = sub("distributed lags, ", "DL ", method), cum0, cum10,
            zero_p = signif(zero_p, 2), recovery_p = signif(recovery_p_value, 2)) %>%
  arrange(cell, panel, method) %>%
  knitr::kable(caption = paste0(
    "Every national panel, full panels (growth outliers included), the same rows for both ",
    "methods: effect in the year of the deviation and through ten years (pp), the test of no ",
    "persistent loss (zero_p) and of no recovery (recovery_p), local projections and unrestricted ",
    "distributed lags; *** p < 0.01, ** p < 0.05, * p < 0.1"))

# Figure 1: each lag's climate interaction in the unrestricted model, PWT x ERA5,
# against the common one and the block ones.
main_run <- dl_runs[[which(vapply(dl_runs, `[[`, "", "label") == main$label)]]
interaction_rows <- bind_rows(lapply(c("TM", "RR"), function(v) {
  bind_rows(lapply(form_columns(v), function(col) {
    climate <- paste0("clim_", v)
    unrestricted <- fixest::coeftable(main_run$models$unrestricted)
    common <- fixest::coeftable(main_run$models$common)
    blocks <- fixest::coeftable(main_run$models$blocks)
    get <- function(ct, target) {
      name <- interaction_name(target, climate, rownames(ct))
      ct[name, c("Estimate", "Std. Error")]
    }
    bind_rows(lapply(0:PERSIST_LAGS, function(k) {
      u <- get(unrestricted, paste0(col, lag_suffix(k)))
      tibble::tibble(arm = paste0(col, " x ", climate), lag = k,
                     estimate = u[[1]], low = u[[1]] - 1.96 * u[[2]], high = u[[1]] + 1.96 * u[[2]],
                     common = get(common, paste0(col, "_sum"))[[1]],
                     block = get(blocks, paste0(col, "_", block_of(k)))[[1]])
    }))
  }))
}))
ggplot(interaction_rows, aes(lag, estimate)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, colour = GRID_MUTED, linewidth = 0.3) +
  geom_hline(aes(yintercept = common), colour = GRID_PALETTE[[2]], linetype = "dashed") +
  geom_step(aes(y = block), colour = GRID_PALETTE[[3]], direction = "mid", linewidth = 0.7) +
  geom_pointrange(aes(ymin = low, ymax = high), colour = GRID_PALETTE[[1]], size = 0.3) +
  facet_wrap(~arm, scales = "free_y") +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = 0:PERSIST_LAGS) +
  labs(x = "Lag (years after the deviation)", y = "Interaction with the long-run climate",
       title = "Each lag's climate interaction, ten lags",
       subtitle = paste0(main$label, ", ", PREFERRED_FORM, ", ", PREFERRED_DEFINITION,
                         " deviations. Blue: unrestricted, with 95% CI; green: blocks {0}, ",
                         "{1-2}, {3-5}, {6-10}; orange dashed: common to all the lags.")) +
  theme_results()

# Figure 2: cumulative paths, PWT x ERA5, by method.
persistence_paths %>%
  filter(panel == main$label) %>%
  mutate(cell = factor(cell, levels = PERSIST_CELLS$cell),
         method = factor(method, levels = c(paste("distributed lags,", DL_VERSIONS),
                                            "local projections")),
         across(c(estimate, conf_low, conf_high), ~ 100 * .x)) %>%
  ggplot(aes(through, estimate, colour = method, fill = method)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, colour = GRID_MUTED, linewidth = 0.3) +
  geom_ribbon(data = function(x) filter(x, method %in% c("local projections",
                                                          "distributed lags, unrestricted")),
              aes(ymin = conf_low, ymax = conf_high), alpha = 0.10, colour = NA) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.8) +
  geom_point(size = 1.2) +
  facet_wrap(~cell, nrow = 2, scales = "free_y") +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = 0:PERSIST_HORIZON) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = grid_colours(c(paste("distributed lags,", DL_VERSIONS),
                                              "local projections")), name = NULL) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = grid_colours(c(paste("distributed lags,", DL_VERSIONS),
                                            "local projections")), name = NULL, guide = "none") +
  labs(x = "Years after the deviation", y = "Cumulative effect on GDP per capita (pp)",
       title = "Cumulative effect of a +/-3 SD year: distributed lags and local projections",
       subtitle = wrap_text(paste0(
         main$label, ", full panel (growth outliers included), the same rows for every method; ",
         PREFERRED_FORM, ", ", PREFERRED_DEFINITION, " deviations; bands: 95% CI of the local ",
         "projections and of the unrestricted distributed lags."), 150)) +
  theme_results()

# The fitted models are too large for the knitr cache (over 2 GB); only the
# results above are kept.
rm(dl_runs, comparison_runs, main_run)
```

# Growth outliers: none, non-weather or all dropped

The preferred model on every panel with no growth outlier dropped, with the
outliers whose cause does not involve weather dropped (the main sample), and
with all of them dropped (the weather-driven ones too). The same country-years
in every panel. For each: the joint tests, the effect of a +/-3 SD deviation in
the year, and the cumulative effects of the dry and hot tails (five
unrestricted lags; ten lags with the common interaction).

The samples differ only in the country-years left out: none; the
outliers annotated with a cause that does not involve weather (the rule of
"Shared specification"); every outlier, the droughts, storms, floods and
harvests among them too; or the non-weather outliers of the other rule
(growth reversals or growth levels). The rows, the long-run climate and the
demeaning of each panel are otherwise the same. If the weather-related outliers carry the
response, the effects should weaken when they are dropped as well; if the
non-weather outliers only add noise, keeping them should widen the
confidence intervals without moving the estimates. The last table follows
three effects, a dry year (-3 SD) at 0.5 and at 1.5 m of long-run
precipitation and a hot year (+3 SD) at 25 °C: in the year, and cumulated
over five and ten years with the lag models of "Lags of the deviations".

```{r outlier-samples}
OUTLIER_SAMPLES <- list(
  "none dropped" = OUTLIERS_ALL[0, ],
  "non-weather dropped" = OUTLIERS_DROPPED,
  "all dropped" = OUTLIERS_ALL
)
OUTLIER_SAMPLES[[paste0("non-weather dropped (", OTHER_OUTLIER_RULE, " rule)")]] <- OTHER_OUTLIERS_DROPPED
outlier_fit <- function(panel, sample) {
  drop <- OUTLIER_SAMPLES[[sample]]
  keep <- !paste(panel$all$GID_0, panel$all$year) %in% paste(drop$GID_0, drop$year)
  d <- add_deviation_terms(panel$all[keep, ], PREFERRED_SUFFIX)
  list(panel = modifyList(panel, list(label = paste0(panel$label, " | ", sample))),
       data = d, preferred = fit_model(preferred_terms, d),
       source_panel = panel$label, sample = sample)
}
outlier_fits <- unlist(lapply(all_panels, function(p) {
  lapply(names(OUTLIER_SAMPLES), function(s) outlier_fit(p, s))
}), recursive = FALSE)

bind_rows(lapply(outlier_fits, function(f) {
  tibble::tibble(panel = f$source_panel, sample = f$sample, rows = stats::nobs(f$preferred),
                 temperature_p = wald_p(f$preferred, "^devTM"),
                 precipitation_p = wald_p(f$preferred, "^devRR"))
})) %>%
  mutate(across(ends_with("_p"), ~ format.pval(signif(.x, 2), eps = 0.001))) %>%
  knitr::kable(caption = "Joint tests (p) of each variable's deviation terms by outlier sample")

significance_map(bind_rows(lapply(outlier_fits, climate_effects))) %>%
  knitr::kable(caption = paste("Effect of a +/-3 SD deviation in the year (pp) by outlier sample;",
                               "*** p < 0.01, ** p < 0.05, * p < 0.1"))

# Dry and hot tails: in the year, and cumulative with lags.
TAIL_CELLS <- tibble::tribble(
  ~cell, ~variable, ~deviation, ~level_index,
  "P -3 SD, 0.5 m", "RR", -3, 1L,
  "P -3 SD, 1.5 m", "RR", -3, 2L,
  "T +3 SD, 25 °C", "TM", 3, 3L
)
tail_summary <- function(f) {
  d5 <- add_deviation_lags(f, 5L)
  lags5 <- unlist(lapply(1:5, function(k) c(lag_terms("TM", k), lag_terms("RR", k))))
  m5 <- fit_model(c(preferred_terms, lags5), d5)
  d10 <- add_deviation_lags(f, 10L)
  m10 <- fit_model(c(restricted_terms("TM", 10L), restricted_terms("RR", 10L), CONTROLS), d10)
  effects <- bind_rows(
    mutate(climate_effects(f), horizon = "year"),
    mutate(filter(cumulative_effects(m5, f$panel$label, FALSE, 5L), through == 5), horizon = "5 years"),
    mutate(filter(cumulative_effects(m10, f$panel$label, TRUE, 10L), through == 10),
           horizon = "10 years")
  )
  effects %>%
    inner_join(TAIL_CELLS, by = c("variable", "deviation", "level_index")) %>%
    transmute(panel = f$source_panel, sample = f$sample,
              column = paste0(cell, ": ", horizon),
              value = sprintf("%+.2f%s", 100 * estimate, stars(p_value))) %>%
    tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = column, values_from = value)
}
bind_rows(lapply(outlier_fits, tail_summary)) %>%
  knitr::kable(caption = paste("Dry and hot tails by outlier sample (pp of GDP per capita): in the",
                               "year, cumulative over five years (unrestricted lags) and ten years",
                               "(common interaction); *** p < 0.01, ** p < 0.05, * p < 0.1"))
```

# Warming scenario: one set of coefficients, three deviation definitions

Three warming paths, with no natural variability and each country's SD
unchanged:

- gradual: a linear warming of 0.2 °C a decade until +1 °C (50 years), then
  constant for 30 years;
- step: +1 °C at once, then constant for 30 years;
- pulse: +1 °C for one year, then back to the pre-warming climate (30 years
  after).

Precipitation is unchanged (dP = 0). The temperature coefficients are those of
the preferred model (PWT x ERA5) in every case, so the three definitions differ
only in how the warming becomes a deviation and in the long-run climate of the
interaction:

```text
(a) horizon:                          dT_t = W_t / sd_all,          climate T0
(b) 20-year, horizon interaction:     dT_t = (W_t - W20_t) / sd_20, climate T0
(c) 20-year, matched interaction:     dT_t = (W_t - W20_t) / sd_20, climate T0 + W20_t
```

where W_t is the warming in year t, W20_t its mean over the 20 years before t
(zero before the warming starts; after the pulse, the years back at T0 are
below W20_t, so they enter the cold arm), T0 the pre-warming climate (the horizon
mean), and sd_all and sd_20 the horizon and trailing 20-year SDs. The growth
effect in year t is the preferred form's temperature terms at dT_t and the
climate; the cumulative effect through year K is their sum over years 1..K (the
effect on the level of GDP per capita, in log points x 100), with 95% CIs by the
delta method (errors clustered by country).

Typical cold, average and hot country: the terciles of the countries of
PWT x ERA5 by long-run temperature; within each, the median long-run
temperature, horizon SD, and trailing 20-year SD (each country's median over
its years).

The model was estimated on deviations with each unit's mean and quadratic trend
removed, i.e. on year-to-year deviations around the unit's trend; applying it
to a sustained shift extrapolates those responses.

```{r warming-scenario, fig.width=13, fig.height=7}
WARMING_TOTAL <- 1       # °C
YEARS_AFTER <- 30L       # years after +1 °C is reached
TRAILING <- 20L          # years of the trailing mean of the 20-year definition

# Each path: the warming above the pre-warming climate in years 1, 2, ... and
# the year +1 °C is reached.
gradual_path <- function(rate_per_decade) {
  reach <- as.integer(round(10 * WARMING_TOTAL / rate_per_decade))
  list(warming = pmin(rate_per_decade / 10 * seq_len(reach + YEARS_AFTER), WARMING_TOTAL),
       reach = reach)
}
WARMING_PATHS <- list(
  "Gradual: 0.2 C a decade to +1 C, then constant" = gradual_path(0.2),
  "Step: +1 C at once, then constant" = list(warming = rep(WARMING_TOTAL, 1L + YEARS_AFTER),
                                             reach = 1L),
  "Pulse: +1 C for one year" = list(warming = c(WARMING_TOTAL, rep(0, YEARS_AFTER)), reach = 1L)
)
# Mean of the warming over the TRAILING years before each year (zero before year 1).
trailing_mean <- function(warming) {
  padded <- c(rep(0, TRAILING), warming)
  vapply(seq_along(warming), function(t) mean(padded[t:(t + TRAILING - 1)]), 0)
}

countries <- main$clean %>%
  group_by(GID_1) %>%
  summarise(T0 = first(mean_TM_all), sd_all = first(sd_TM_all),
            sd_20 = stats::median(sd_TM_lag_20), .groups = "drop")
countries$type <- cut(countries$T0, stats::quantile(countries$T0, c(0, 1 / 3, 2 / 3, 1)),
                      labels = c("Cold", "Average", "Hot"), include.lowest = TRUE)
typical <- countries %>%
  group_by(type) %>%
  summarise(countries = n(), T_range = sprintf("%.1f to %.1f", min(T0), max(T0)),
            T0 = stats::median(T0), sd_all = stats::median(sd_all),
            sd_20 = stats::median(sd_20), .groups = "drop") %>%
  mutate(warming_sd_all = WARMING_TOTAL / sd_all, warming_sd_20 = WARMING_TOTAL / sd_20)

typical %>%
  mutate(across(where(is.double), ~ round(.x, 2))) %>%
  knitr::kable(caption = paste("Typical countries (terciles of PWT x ERA5 by long-run temperature,",
                               "medians): long-run temperature (C), SDs (C) and +1 C in SDs"))

SCENARIOS <- c("(a) Horizon", "(b) 20-year, horizon interaction",
               "(c) 20-year, matched interaction")
# Deviation (SD) and long-run climate (C) of each year of `warming` under
# definition `s`.
scenario_path <- function(s, warming, T0, sd_all, sd_20) {
  trailing <- trailing_mean(warming)
  fixed <- rep(T0, length(warming))
  switch(s,
         "(a) Horizon" = list(deviation = warming / sd_all, climate = fixed),
         "(b) 20-year, horizon interaction" = list(deviation = (warming - trailing) / sd_20,
                                                   climate = fixed),
         "(c) 20-year, matched interaction" = list(deviation = (warming - trailing) / sd_20,
                                                   climate = T0 + trailing))
}

scenario_model <- selection_models[[PREFERRED_DEFINITION]][[PREFERRED_FORM]]
scenario_terms <- names(stats::coef(scenario_model))
# Growth effect of each year (rows) as weights on the coefficients.
year_weights <- function(path) {
  t(mapply(function(x, m) {
    w <- stats::setNames(numeric(length(scenario_terms)), scenario_terms)
    for (s in FORMS[[PREFERRED_FORM]][["TM"]]) {
      term <- paste0("devTM", s)
      w[[term]] <- term_value(s, x)
      w[[interaction_name(term, "clim_TM", scenario_terms)]] <- term_value(s, x) * m
    }
    w
  }, path$deviation, path$climate))
}

scenario_effects <- bind_rows(lapply(names(WARMING_PATHS), function(p) {
  warming <- WARMING_PATHS[[p]]$warming
  bind_rows(lapply(SCENARIOS, function(s) {
    bind_rows(lapply(seq_len(nrow(typical)), function(i) {
      # (Not called `path`: mutate() below creates a column of that name.)
      dev_path <- scenario_path(s, warming, typical$T0[i], typical$sd_all[i], typical$sd_20[i])
      W <- year_weights(dev_path)
      colnames(W) <- scenario_terms
      cumulative <- apply(W, 2, cumsum)
      bind_rows(
        mutate(linear_combination(scenario_model, W), quantity = "year"),
        mutate(linear_combination(scenario_model, cumulative), quantity = "cumulative")
      ) %>%
        mutate(path = p, scenario = s, type = as.character(typical$type[i]),
               year = rep(seq_along(warming), 2), deviation = rep(dev_path$deviation, 2),
               climate = rep(dev_path$climate, 2),
               p_value = 2 * stats::pnorm(-abs(estimate / std_error)))
    }))
  }))
}))

# Cumulative effect when +1 °C is reached and 10, 20 and 30 years after.
REPORT_AFTER <- c(0L, 10L, 20L, YEARS_AFTER)
scenario_effects %>%
  filter(quantity == "cumulative") %>%
  mutate(after = year - vapply(WARMING_PATHS[path], `[[`, 0L, "reach")) %>%
  filter(after %in% REPORT_AFTER) %>%
  mutate(cell = sprintf("%+.1f [%+.1f, %+.1f]%s", 100 * estimate, 100 * conf_low,
                        100 * conf_high, stars(p_value)),
         column = factor(ifelse(after == 0, "+1 C reached", sprintf("%d years after", after)),
                         levels = c("+1 C reached", sprintf("%d years after", REPORT_AFTER[-1])))) %>%
  select(path, scenario, type, column, cell) %>%
  arrange(column) %>%
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = column, values_from = cell) %>%
  knitr::kable(caption = paste0(
    "Cumulative effect of the warming on GDP per capita (log points x 100, 95% CI), with the ",
    "coefficients of the preferred model (", PREFERRED_FORM, ", ", PREFERRED_DEFINITION,
    "); +1 C is reached in year ", WARMING_PATHS[[1]]$reach, " (gradual) or year 1 (step, ",
    "pulse); *** p < 0.01, ** p < 0.05, * p < 0.1"))

QUANTITY_LABELS <- c(deviation = "Deviation (SD)",
                     cumulative = "Cumulative effect (log points x 100)")
plot_scenario <- function(p) {
  plot_data <- bind_rows(
    scenario_effects %>%
      filter(path == p, quantity == "year") %>%
      transmute(scenario, type, year, quantity = "deviation", estimate = deviation,
                conf_low = NA_real_, conf_high = NA_real_),
    scenario_effects %>%
      filter(path == p, quantity == "cumulative") %>%
      transmute(scenario, type, year, quantity = "cumulative", estimate = 100 * estimate,
                conf_low = 100 * conf_low, conf_high = 100 * conf_high)
  ) %>%
    mutate(quantity = factor(QUANTITY_LABELS[quantity], levels = QUANTITY_LABELS),
           scenario = factor(scenario, levels = SCENARIOS),
           type = sprintf("%s country (%.1f C; SD %.2f horizon, %.2f 20-year)", type,
                          typical$T0[match(type, as.character(typical$type))],
                          typical$sd_all[match(type, as.character(typical$type))],
                          typical$sd_20[match(type, as.character(typical$type))])) %>%
    mutate(type = factor(type, levels = unique(type)))

  ggplot(plot_data, aes(year, estimate, colour = scenario, fill = scenario)) +
    geom_hline(yintercept = 0, colour = GRID_MUTED, linewidth = 0.3) +
    geom_vline(xintercept = WARMING_PATHS[[p]]$reach, colour = GRID_MUTED, linewidth = 0.3,
               linetype = "dotted") +
    geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = conf_low, ymax = conf_high), alpha = 0.15, colour = NA,
                data = filter(plot_data, !is.na(conf_low))) +
    geom_line(linewidth = 0.8) +
    facet_grid(quantity ~ type, scales = "free_y", switch = "y") +
    scale_colour_manual(values = grid_colours(SCENARIOS), name = NULL) +
    scale_fill_manual(values = grid_colours(SCENARIOS), name = NULL) +
    labs(x = "Year from the start of the warming", y = NULL,
         title = paste0(p, ": one set of coefficients, three deviation definitions"),
         subtitle = wrap_text(paste0(
           "Coefficients of the preferred model (", PREFERRED_FORM, ", ", PREFERRED_DEFINITION,
           " deviations, PWT x ERA5). No natural variability; SDs unchanged; precipitation ",
           "unchanged. Top: the temperature deviation ((b) and (c) share it); bottom: the ",
           "cumulative effect on GDP per capita. Dotted line: +1 C reached. Shaded: 95% CI ",
           "(clustered by country)."), 175)) +
    theme_results() +
    theme(strip.placement = "outside")
}
for (p in names(WARMING_PATHS)) print(plot_scenario(p))
```

# Where shocks matter: robustness by country

For every national panel (PWT and World Bank with ERA5, CRU TS and UDelaware),
every deviation definition interacted with the horizon mean (horizon, 20-year
and the two mixes) and every arms form (linear, quadratic and the two mixes),
6 x 4 x 4 = 96 fits, each on its own rows: the effect on growth that year of a
cold (dry) and a hot (wet) shock in each country, at its recent climate.

- The shock is three times the SD of the country's last 10 years of the panel
  (°C or m), converted to the deviation units of the fit: divided by the
  country's horizon SD, or by its trailing 20-year SD of the last year. The
  same physical shock in every fit.
- The long-run climate of the interaction is the country's mean of the same 10
  years.
- Each panel uses its own climate data for both.

The maps show the effect of the shock in the preferred model (PWT x ERA5), and
its robustness across the 96 fits by pattern, against the sign of the
preferred estimate:

- plain fill: the estimate has that sign (significant or not) in more than 80%
  of the fits; with a thick border if it is also significant at 5% with that
  sign in more than 80% of them;
- dots: otherwise, the estimate has that sign in more than 50% of the fits;
- stripes: neither.

Countries outside the PWT x ERA5 sample are grey. The table lists the countries
with a thick border, ranked by recent mean climate.

```{r robust-shocks, fig.width=14, fig.height=8.5}
RECENT_YEARS <- 10L
SHOCK_SD <- 3
PLAIN_SIGN <- 0.8        # plain fill: share of fits with the preferred sign
DOTS_SIGN <- 0.5         # dots: share of fits with the preferred sign
BORDER_SIGNIFICANT <- 0.8 # thick border: share of fits significant with the preferred sign
PATTERN_SPACING <- 250e3 # metres between dots and between stripes (Robinson projection)
ROBINSON <- "+proj=robin"
SHOCK_DEFINITIONS <- names(DEFINITIONS)[!grepl("matched", names(DEFINITIONS))]

# Each country's climate over the last RECENT_YEARS years of the panel (mean
# and SD of each variable), and the SDs of the two deviation baselines (horizon,
# and the trailing 20 years of the last year).
recent_climate <- function(panel) {
  panel$data %>%
    filter(GID_0 %in% panel$clean$GID_0, year > panel$end_year - RECENT_YEARS,
           year <= panel$end_year, !is.na(TM), !is.na(RR)) %>%
    group_by(GID_0) %>%
    filter(n() == RECENT_YEARS) %>%
    summarise(mean_TM = mean(TM), sd_TM = sd(TM), mean_RR = mean(RR), sd_RR = sd(RR),
              sd_TM_all = first(sd_TM_all), sd_RR_all = first(sd_RR_all),
              sd_TM_lag_20 = sd_TM_lag_20[which.max(year)],
              sd_RR_lag_20 = sd_RR_lag_20[which.max(year)], .groups = "drop") %>%
    filter(sd_TM_lag_20 > 0, sd_RR_lag_20 > 0)
}

# Effect of a shock of -/+ SHOCK_SD recent SDs in each country of `rc`, in a
# model of `form` with deviations of definition `def`.
shock_effects <- function(model, form, def, rc) {
  terms <- names(stats::coef(model))
  bind_rows(lapply(c("TM", "RR"), function(v) {
    grid <- expand.grid(i = seq_len(nrow(rc)), sign = c(-1, 1))
    sd_fit <- rc[[paste0("sd_", v, "_", DEFINITIONS[[def]][[v]])]][grid$i]
    x <- grid$sign * SHOCK_SD * rc[[paste0("sd_", v)]][grid$i] / sd_fit
    m <- rc[[paste0("mean_", v)]][grid$i]
    G <- matrix(0, nrow(grid), length(terms), dimnames = list(NULL, terms))
    for (s in FORMS[[form]][[v]]) {
      term <- paste0("dev", v, s)
      G[, term] <- term_value(s, x)
      G[, interaction_name(term, paste0("clim_", v), terms)] <- term_value(s, x) * m
    }
    linear_combination(model, G) %>%
      mutate(GID_0 = rc$GID_0[grid$i], variable = v,
             shock = ifelse(grid$sign < 0, "negative", "positive"),
             p_value = 2 * stats::pnorm(-abs(estimate / std_error)))
  }))
}

recent <- lapply(national_panels, recent_climate)
shock_fits <- bind_rows(lapply(seq_along(national_panels), function(j) {
  p <- national_panels[[j]]
  bind_rows(lapply(SHOCK_DEFINITIONS, function(def) {
    d <- add_deviation_terms(p$clean, DEFINITIONS[[def]])
    bind_rows(lapply(ARMS, function(f) {
      shock_effects(fit_model(form_terms(FORMS[[f]]), d), f, def, recent[[j]]) %>%
        mutate(panel = p$label, definition = def, form = f)
    }))
  }))
}))

SHOCK_FACETS <- tibble::tibble(
  variable = c("TM", "TM", "RR", "RR"), shock = c("negative", "positive", "negative", "positive"),
  facet = c("Temperature: cold shock (-3 recent SD)", "Temperature: hot shock (+3 recent SD)",
            "Precipitation: dry shock (-3 recent SD)", "Precipitation: wet shock (+3 recent SD)")
)
# Recent climate of each country, averaged over the panels that have it.
recent_mean <- bind_rows(recent) %>%
  group_by(GID_0) %>%
  summarise(across(c(mean_TM, sd_TM, mean_RR, sd_RR), mean), .groups = "drop")
# The shock in the preferred model (PWT x ERA5, at its recent climate), and the
# agreement of the 96 fits with the sign of that estimate.
preferred_shock <- shock_effects(selection_models[[PREFERRED_DEFINITION]][[PREFERRED_FORM]],
                                 PREFERRED_FORM, PREFERRED_DEFINITION, recent[[1]]) %>%
  select(GID_0, variable, shock, preferred = estimate, preferred_p = p_value)
shock_summary <- shock_fits %>%
  inner_join(preferred_shock, by = c("GID_0", "variable", "shock")) %>%
  group_by(GID_0, variable, shock, preferred, preferred_p) %>%
  summarise(fits = n(),
            robust = mean(p_value < 0.05 & sign(estimate) == sign(preferred)),
            same_sign = mean(sign(estimate) == sign(preferred)), .groups = "drop") %>%
  mutate(pattern = case_when(same_sign > PLAIN_SIGN ~ "fill", same_sign > DOTS_SIGN ~ "dots",
                             TRUE ~ "stripes"),
         border = pattern == "fill" & robust > BORDER_SIGNIFICANT) %>%
  inner_join(SHOCK_FACETS, by = c("variable", "shock")) %>%
  left_join(recent_mean, by = "GID_0")

world <- rnaturalearth::ne_countries(scale = "small", returnclass = "sf") %>%
  mutate(GID_0 = ifelse(iso_a3 == "-99", adm0_a3, iso_a3)) %>%
  filter(GID_0 != "ATA") %>%
  select(GID_0, geometry) %>%
  sf::st_transform(ROBINSON) %>%
  sf::st_make_valid()
# (rbind, not bind_rows(): it keeps the sf class.)
shock_map <- do.call(rbind, lapply(SHOCK_FACETS$facet, function(f) {
  world %>%
    left_join(filter(shock_summary, facet == f) %>% select(GID_0, preferred, pattern, border),
              by = "GID_0") %>%
    mutate(facet = factor(f, levels = SHOCK_FACETS$facet))
}))

# Patterns as ordinary geometries, built once (fast to draw, unlike pattern
# fills): a regular grid of dots kept inside the dotted countries, and diagonal
# lines clipped to the striped ones.
box <- sf::st_bbox(world)
height <- box[["ymax"]] - box[["ymin"]]
dot_grid <- sf::st_sf(geometry = sf::st_make_grid(world, cellsize = PATTERN_SPACING,
                                                  what = "centers"))
stripe_lines <- sf::st_sfc(lapply(
  seq(box[["xmin"]] - height, box[["xmax"]], by = PATTERN_SPACING * sqrt(2)),
  function(x0) sf::st_linestring(rbind(c(x0, box[["ymin"]]), c(x0 + height, box[["ymax"]])))
), crs = sf::st_crs(world))
pattern_layer <- function(kind) {
  layers <- lapply(SHOCK_FACETS$facet, function(f) {
    polygons <- shock_map[shock_map$facet == f & shock_map$pattern %in% kind, ]
    if (!nrow(polygons)) return(NULL)
    geometry <- if (kind == "dots") {
      sf::st_geometry(dot_grid)[lengths(sf::st_intersects(dot_grid, polygons)) > 0]
    } else {
      sf::st_collection_extract(sf::st_intersection(stripe_lines, sf::st_union(polygons)),
                                "LINESTRING")
    }
    if (!length(geometry)) return(NULL)
    sf::st_sf(facet = factor(f, levels = SHOCK_FACETS$facet), geometry = geometry)
  })
  do.call(rbind, Filter(Negate(is.null), layers))
}
dots <- pattern_layer("dots")
stripes <- pattern_layer("stripes")

fill_limit <- stats::quantile(abs(100 * shock_summary$preferred), 0.98, names = FALSE)
ggplot() +
  geom_sf(data = shock_map, aes(fill = 100 * preferred), colour = "white", linewidth = 0.1) +
  (if (!is.null(stripes)) geom_sf(data = stripes, colour = "grey20", linewidth = 0.2)) +
  (if (!is.null(dots)) geom_sf(data = dots, colour = "grey15", size = 0.35, shape = 16)) +
  geom_sf(data = shock_map[shock_map$border %in% TRUE, ], fill = NA, colour = "grey10",
          linewidth = 0.5) +
  facet_wrap(~facet, nrow = 2) +
  coord_sf(crs = ROBINSON, expand = FALSE, datum = NA) +
  scale_fill_gradient2(low = "#c0392b", mid = "#f2f1ec", high = GRID_PALETTE[[1]], midpoint = 0,
                       limits = c(-fill_limit, fill_limit), oob = scales::squish,
                       na.value = "grey85",
                       name = "Effect on growth that year,\npreferred model (pp)") +
  labs(title = "Effect of a shock in the preferred model, and its robustness across specifications and datasets",
       subtitle = wrap_text(paste0(
         "Effect that year of a shock of ", SHOCK_SD, " SDs of the country's last ", RECENT_YEARS,
         " years, at the mean climate of those years: ", PREFERRED_FORM, ", ",
         PREFERRED_DEFINITION, " deviations, PWT x ERA5 (colour scale capped at the 98th ",
         "percentile). Robustness across the fits (up to ",
         length(national_panels) * length(SHOCK_DEFINITIONS) * length(ARMS), ": ",
         length(national_panels), " national panels x ", length(SHOCK_DEFINITIONS),
         " deviation definitions x ", length(ARMS), " arms forms), against the sign of the ",
         "preferred estimate: plain, that sign in more than ", 100 * PLAIN_SIGN, "% of them ",
         "(thick border: also significant at 5% in more than ", 100 * BORDER_SIGNIFICANT,
         "%); dots, that sign in more than ", 100 * DOTS_SIGN, "%; stripes, neither. Grey: ",
         "outside the PWT x ERA5 sample."), 170)) +
  theme_results() +
  theme(axis.text = element_blank(), legend.key.width = grid::unit(2.5, "cm"))

# Countries with a thick border, ranked by recent mean climate.
shock_summary %>%
  filter(border) %>%
  mutate(country = countrycode::countrycode(GID_0, "iso3c", "country.name", warn = FALSE),
         recent_mean = ifelse(variable == "TM", mean_TM, mean_RR),
         recent_sd = ifelse(variable == "TM", sd_TM, sd_RR),
         facet = factor(facet, levels = SHOCK_FACETS$facet)) %>%
  arrange(facet, recent_mean) %>%
  transmute(shock = facet, country, preferred_pp = round(100 * preferred, 2),
            preferred_p = signif(preferred_p, 2), robust_share = round(robust, 2), fits,
            recent_mean = round(recent_mean, 2), recent_sd = round(recent_sd, 2)) %>%
  knitr::kable(caption = paste0(
    "Countries where the shock is significant (5%) with the sign of the preferred estimate in ",
    "more than ", 100 * BORDER_SIGNIFICANT, "% of their fits (thick border), by shock, ranked ",
    "by the mean climate of ",
    "the last ", RECENT_YEARS, " years (°C or m a year, averaged over the panels; SD of the ",
    "same years)"))

# Countries by pattern.
shock_summary %>%
  mutate(pattern = factor(ifelse(border, "fill, thick border", pattern),
                          levels = c("fill, thick border", "fill", "dots", "stripes"))) %>%
  count(facet = factor(facet, levels = SHOCK_FACETS$facet), pattern, .drop = FALSE) %>%
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = pattern, values_from = n, values_fill = 0) %>%
  knitr::kable(caption = "Countries of the PWT x ERA5 sample by robustness pattern")
```

# Growth as a deviation

The dependent variable built as the climate deviations are: each year's growth
of GDP per capita against the mean of the 10 years before it (10 rather than
20, so that fewer years are lost to the window), in an SD of growth, signed,

```text
dG_all = (g - mean_g_lag) / sd_g_all   sd_g_all: the unit's fixed SD over the panel horizon
dG_10  = (g - mean_g_lag) / sd_g_lag   sd_g_lag: the SD of the same 10 years before
```

with g = dlog(GDP per capita), the outcome of every model above. The moments
come from each unit's full growth series in its economic source (PWT from
1951, the World Bank from 1961), not only from the sample years; the trailing
ones from the years of the window with growth, at least 8 of the 10 (gaps are
not filled). Like the climate moments, they use every year with growth, the
growth outliers included; a variant leaves out the outliers dropped from the
sample (those whose cause does not involve weather). Only statistics for now:
coverage, distribution, persistence, and the relation to the climate
deviations, on the sample rows of PWT x ERA5 and WB x ERA5.

```{r growth-deviations, fig.width=12, fig.height=5}
GROWTH_WINDOW <- 10L
GROWTH_MIN_YEARS <- 8L
GROWTH_PANELS <- c("PWT x ERA5", "WB x ERA5")

# Each unit's growth series (every year of its source, gaps as missing), the
# mean and SD of the GROWTH_WINDOW years before each year, and the SD over the panel's
# horizon; `drop`: country-years whose growth is left out of the moments.
growth_moments <- function(panel, drop = NULL) {
  econ <- load_econ_panel(resolve_econ_source(panel$econ)) %>%
    filter(gadm_level == panel$level, !is.na(dlgrp_pc_usd)) %>%
    transmute(GID_0, GID_1, year, g = dlgrp_pc_usd) %>%
    group_by(GID_0, GID_1) %>%
    tidyr::complete(year = seq(min(year), max(year))) %>%
    arrange(year, .by_group = TRUE) %>%
    ungroup()
  g_moments <- econ$g
  if (!is.null(drop)) {
    g_moments[paste(econ$GID_0, econ$year) %in% paste(drop$GID_0, drop$year)] <- NA_real_
  }
  trailing <- grouped_trailing_moments(g_moments, econ$GID_1, GROWTH_MIN_YEARS,
                                       window = GROWTH_WINDOW)
  econ$mean_g_lag <- trailing$mean
  econ$sd_g_lag <- trailing$sd
  econ$g_moments <- g_moments
  econ %>%
    group_by(GID_1) %>%
    mutate(sd_g_all = stats::sd(g_moments[year >= START_YEAR & year <= panel$end_year],
                                na.rm = TRUE)) %>%
    ungroup() %>%
    select(GID_1, year, g, mean_g_lag, sd_g_lag, sd_g_all)
}

# The sample rows of `panel` with the normalized growth.
add_growth_deviations <- function(panel, drop = NULL) {
  out <- panel$clean %>%
    left_join(growth_moments(panel, drop), by = c("GID_1", "year")) %>%
    mutate(growth_dev = g - mean_g_lag, dG_all = growth_dev / sd_g_all,
           dG_10 = growth_dev / sd_g_lag)
  stopifnot(max(abs(out$g - out[[OUTCOME]])) < 1e-12)
  out
}

growth_panels <- national_panels[match(GROWTH_PANELS, vapply(national_panels, `[[`, "", "label"))]
names(growth_panels) <- GROWTH_PANELS
growth_data <- lapply(growth_panels, add_growth_deviations)
# (Before the start year, the growth history leaves out the non-weather
# outliers of the sample from 1960.)
growth_data_no_outliers <- lapply(growth_panels, add_growth_deviations,
                                  drop = bind_rows(OUTLIERS_DROPPED, EARLY_OUTLIERS_DROPPED))
with_both <- function(d) d[is.finite(d$dG_10) & is.finite(d$dG_all), ]

# 1. Coverage: sample rows with the normalized growth, by decade.
bind_rows(lapply(GROWTH_PANELS, function(p) {
  growth_data[[p]] %>%
    mutate(decade = paste0(10 * (year %/% 10), "s")) %>%
    group_by(decade) %>%
    summarise(rows = n(), with_dG = sum(is.finite(dG_10) & is.finite(dG_all)), .groups = "drop") %>%
    mutate(panel = p, cell = sprintf("%d / %d", with_dG, rows))
})) %>%
  select(panel, decade, cell) %>%
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = decade, values_from = cell) %>%
  knitr::kable(caption = paste0("Sample rows with the normalized growth (at least ",
                                GROWTH_MIN_YEARS, " of the ", GROWTH_WINDOW, " years before observed) / all ",
                                "sample rows, by decade"))

# 2. Distribution, on the rows with both normalizations (a normal variable:
# 4.6% beyond 2 SD, 0.27% beyond 3 SD).
distribution <- function(x, label) {
  x <- x[is.finite(x)]
  z <- (x - mean(x)) / stats::sd(x)
  q <- stats::quantile(x, c(0.01, 0.05, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 0.95, 0.99), names = FALSE)
  tibble::tibble(series = label, n = length(x), mean = mean(x), sd = stats::sd(x),
                 p1 = q[1], p5 = q[2], p25 = q[3], median = q[4], p75 = q[5], p95 = q[6],
                 p99 = q[7], min = min(x), max = max(x), skewness = mean(z^3),
                 excess_kurtosis = mean(z^4) - 3, beyond_2 = mean(abs(x) > 2),
                 beyond_3 = mean(abs(x) > 3))
}
bind_rows(lapply(GROWTH_PANELS, function(p) {
  d <- with_both(growth_data[[p]])
  e <- with_both(growth_data_no_outliers[[p]])
  bind_rows(
    distribution(100 * d$g, "growth (pp)"),
    distribution(100 * d$growth_dev, "growth - mean of the 10 years before (pp)"),
    distribution(d$dG_all, "dG_all"),
    distribution(d$dG_10, "dG_10"),
    distribution(e$dG_all, "dG_all, moments without the outliers"),
    distribution(e$dG_10, "dG_10, moments without the outliers")
  ) %>%
    mutate(panel = p, .before = 1)
})) %>%
  mutate(across(c(beyond_2, beyond_3), ~ round(100 * .x, 2)),
         across(c(mean, sd, p1, p5, p25, median, p75, p95, p99, min, max, skewness,
                  excess_kurtosis), ~ round(.x, 2))) %>%
  knitr::kable(caption = paste0("Distribution of growth and of the normalized growth (sample ",
                                "rows with both normalizations); beyond_2, beyond_3: % of rows ",
                                "above 2 and 3 in absolute value (for the two pp series, 2 and 3 pp)"))

# 3. Over time: mean (SD) of the normalized growth by decade.
bind_rows(lapply(GROWTH_PANELS, function(p) {
  with_both(growth_data[[p]]) %>%
    mutate(decade = paste0(10 * (year %/% 10), "s")) %>%
    group_by(decade) %>%
    summarise(rows = n(), dG_all = sprintf("%+.2f (%.2f)", mean(dG_all), stats::sd(dG_all)),
              dG_10 = sprintf("%+.2f (%.2f)", mean(dG_10), stats::sd(dG_10)), .groups = "drop") %>%
    mutate(panel = p, .before = 1)
})) %>%
  knitr::kable(caption = "Mean (SD) of the normalized growth by decade")

# 4. Persistence, the two SDs, and the relation to growth and to the demeaned
# 20-year climate deviations of the models above.
bind_rows(lapply(GROWTH_PANELS, function(p) {
  d <- with_both(growth_data[[p]]) %>%
    arrange(GID_1, year) %>%
    group_by(GID_1) %>%
    mutate(across(c(g, dG_all, dG_10), ~ ifelse(year - lag(year) == 1L, lag(.x), NA_real_),
                  .names = "lag_{.col}")) %>%
    ungroup()
  ar1 <- function(x, lx) stats::cor(x, lx, use = "complete.obs")
  tibble::tibble(
    panel = p, units = n_distinct(d$GID_1),
    ar1_growth = ar1(d$g, d$lag_g), ar1_dG_all = ar1(d$dG_all, d$lag_dG_all),
    ar1_dG_10 = ar1(d$dG_10, d$lag_dG_10),
    cor_growth_dG_all = stats::cor(d$g, d$dG_all), cor_growth_dG_10 = stats::cor(d$g, d$dG_10),
    cor_dG_all_dG_10 = stats::cor(d$dG_all, d$dG_10),
    median_sd10_over_sdall = stats::median(d$sd_g_lag / d$sd_g_all),
    share_sd10_below_half = mean(d$sd_g_lag < 0.5 * d$sd_g_all),
    cor_dG_10_dT = stats::cor(d$dG_10, d$dm_TM_lag_20),
    cor_dG_10_dP = stats::cor(d$dG_10, d$dm_RR_lag_20)
  )
})) %>%
  mutate(across(where(is.double), ~ round(.x, 3))) %>%
  knitr::kable(caption = paste0("Persistence (first-order autocorrelation within units), ",
                                "correlations, the trailing against the horizon SD of growth, and ",
                                "the correlation with the demeaned 20-year climate deviations"))

# 5. The largest normalized values (PWT x ERA5).
with_both(growth_data[["PWT x ERA5"]]) %>%
  slice_max(abs(dG_10), n = 12) %>%
  transmute(GID_0, year, growth_pp = round(100 * g, 1), mean_10_pp = round(100 * mean_g_lag, 1),
            sd_10_pp = round(100 * sd_g_lag, 1), sd_all_pp = round(100 * sd_g_all, 1),
            dG_10 = round(dG_10, 1), dG_all = round(dG_all, 1)) %>%
  knitr::kable(caption = "PWT x ERA5: the 12 sample rows with the largest |dG_10|")

# 6. Density against the standard normal.
bind_rows(lapply(GROWTH_PANELS, function(p) {
  with_both(growth_data[[p]]) %>%
    select(dG_all, dG_10) %>%
    tidyr::pivot_longer(everything(), names_to = "series") %>%
    mutate(panel = p)
})) %>%
  ggplot(aes(value, colour = series)) +
  geom_density(linewidth = 0.8) +
  stat_function(fun = stats::dnorm, colour = GRID_MUTED, linetype = "dashed",
                inherit.aes = FALSE) +
  facet_wrap(~panel) +
  coord_cartesian(xlim = c(-6, 6)) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = grid_colours(c("dG_all", "dG_10")), name = NULL) +
  labs(x = "Normalized growth (SD)", y = "Density", title = "Normalized growth on the sample rows",
       subtitle = "Dashed: the standard normal; the axis is cut at +/-6 SD") +
  theme_results()
```

## Normalized growth as the outcome

The model of the previous sections (`r RUN_FORM`, horizon and 20-year
deviations) with dG_all as the outcome, its moments without the outlier years,
on PWT x ERA5. Dividing each unit's growth by its own SD (sigma) does two
things at once: it puts the effects in units of each unit's growth SD (a
common coefficient then means larger effects in pp where growth is more
volatile), and, like weighted least squares with weights 1 / sigma^2, it gives
the low-volatility units more weight. To separate them, on the same rows:

```text
growth (pp)                                the model as before
growth - mean of the 10 years before (pp)  the trailing mean alone
dG_all (growth SDs)                        the trailing mean and the scaling
growth (pp), weights 1 / sigma^2           the weighting alone
```

The fixed effects are the same as before (year, and unit trends). The effects
of dG_all are converted to pp at the median sigma of the units (and below at
the median sigma of the poorest and richest third of the units by income).

```{r growth-outcome-models}
growth_outcome <- growth_data_no_outliers[["PWT x ERA5"]] %>%
  filter(is.finite(dG_all)) %>%
  mutate(sigma = sd_g_all, sigma_weight = 1 / sd_g_all^2)
outcome_units <- distinct(growth_outcome, GID_1, log_gdp_av, sigma) %>%
  mutate(income = cut(log_gdp_av, stats::quantile(log_gdp_av, c(0, 1, 2, 3) / 3),
                      labels = c("poorest third", "middle third", "richest third"),
                      include.lowest = TRUE))
MEDIAN_SIGMA <- stats::median(outcome_units$sigma)

# 1. Volatility and income: sigma by income third, and each third's share of
# the rows and of the weights 1 / sigma^2.
growth_outcome %>%
  left_join(select(outcome_units, GID_1, income), by = "GID_1") %>%
  group_by(income) %>%
  summarise(units = n_distinct(GID_1), median_sigma_pp = 100 * stats::median(sigma),
            share_rows = n(), share_weight = sum(sigma_weight), .groups = "drop") %>%
  mutate(share_rows = share_rows / sum(share_rows), share_weight = share_weight / sum(share_weight),
         across(where(is.double), ~ round(.x, 3))) %>%
  knitr::kable(caption = sprintf(paste(
    "PWT x ERA5: the units' growth SD (sigma, pp, the horizon without the outliers) by third of",
    "income (log mean GDP per capita), and each third's share of the rows and of the weights",
    "1 / sigma^2; correlation of log sigma with log income across units: %.2f"),
    stats::cor(log(outcome_units$sigma), outcome_units$log_gdp_av)))

OUTCOME_MODELS <- c("Growth (pp), all sample rows", "Growth (pp)",
                    "Growth - mean of 10 years before (pp)", "dG_all (growth SDs)",
                    "Growth (pp), weights 1 / sigma^2")
outcome_fits <- lapply(c("Horizon", "20-year"), function(def) {
  terms <- form_terms(FORMS[[RUN_FORM]])
  d <- add_deviation_terms(growth_outcome, DEFINITIONS[[def]])
  stats::setNames(list(
    fit_model(terms, add_deviation_terms(main$clean, DEFINITIONS[[def]])),
    fit_model(terms, d),
    fit_model(terms, d, outcome = "growth_dev"),
    fit_model(terms, d, outcome = "dG_all"),
    fit_panel_model(paste(terms, collapse = " + "), d, outcome = OUTCOME,
                    fixed_effects = FIXED_EFFECTS, cluster = ~GID_0, weights = ~sigma_weight)
  ), OUTCOME_MODELS)
})
names(outcome_fits) <- c("Horizon", "20-year")

# 2. Joint tests (unit-free).
bind_rows(lapply(names(outcome_fits), function(def) {
  bind_rows(lapply(OUTCOME_MODELS, function(k) {
    m <- outcome_fits[[def]][[k]]
    tibble::tibble(definition = def, outcome = k, observations = stats::nobs(m),
                   temperature_p = signif(wald_p(m, "^devTM"), 2),
                   precipitation_p = signif(wald_p(m, "^devRR"), 2))
  }))
})) %>%
  knitr::kable(caption = "PWT x ERA5: joint tests (p) of each variable's deviation terms by outcome")

# 3. Effects of a +/-3 SD deviation, in pp (dG_all at the median sigma).
bind_rows(lapply(names(outcome_fits), function(def) {
  bind_rows(lapply(OUTCOME_MODELS, function(k) {
    scale <- if (grepl("^dG_all", k)) MEDIAN_SIGMA else 1
    climate_effects(list(preferred = outcome_fits[[def]][[k]],
                         panel = list(label = paste0(def, ": ", k))), RUN_FORM) %>%
      mutate(across(c(estimate, conf_low, conf_high), ~ .x * scale))
  }))
})) %>%
  significance_map() %>%
  knitr::kable(caption = sprintf(paste(
    "PWT x ERA5: effect of a +/-3 SD deviation (pp) by outcome; dG_all converted at the median",
    "sigma of the units (%.2f pp); *** p < 0.01, ** p < 0.05, * p < 0.1"), 100 * MEDIAN_SIGMA))

# 4. dG_all in pp at the sigma of the poorest and of the richest third.
sigma_by_income <- outcome_units %>%
  group_by(income) %>%
  summarise(sigma = stats::median(sigma), .groups = "drop")
bind_rows(lapply(names(outcome_fits), function(def) {
  effects <- climate_effects(list(preferred = outcome_fits[[def]][["dG_all (growth SDs)"]],
                                  panel = list(label = def)), RUN_FORM) %>%
    filter((variable == "TM" & deviation == 3 & climate == 25) |
             (variable == "RR" & deviation == -3 & climate == 0.5))
  bind_rows(lapply(seq_len(nrow(sigma_by_income)), function(i) {
    effects %>%
      transmute(definition = def, effect = ifelse(variable == "TM", "T +3 SD, 25 C", "P -3 SD, 0.5 m"),
                income = as.character(sigma_by_income$income[i]),
                cell = sprintf("%+.2f%s", 100 * estimate * sigma_by_income$sigma[i], stars(p_value)))
  }))
})) %>%
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = income, values_from = cell) %>%
  knitr::kable(caption = paste("PWT x ERA5, dG_all as the outcome: effects in pp at the median",
                               "sigma of each third of the units by income"))
```

## Bad and good years

Instead of the mean of growth, the probability of a bad year (dG_all below -1:
growth more than one of the unit's SDs below its mean of the 10 years before),
of a typical one (within +/-1), and of a good year (above +1), in linear
probability models with the terms, controls and fixed effects of the model
above, on the same rows (dG_all with its moments without the outlier years).
The three add up to one, so the effects on the typical year are minus the sum
of the other two. Splitting the sample by the sign of growth would select on
the outcome; these use every row. The effects are the change in the
probability (pp) with an event of +/-3 SD.

```{r growth-event-probabilities}
EVENTS <- c(bad = "dG_all < -1", typical = "-1 <= dG_all <= 1", good = "dG_all > 1")
event_data <- growth_outcome %>%
  mutate(bad = as.numeric(dG_all < -1), typical = as.numeric(abs(dG_all) <= 1),
         good = as.numeric(dG_all > 1))
event_fits <- lapply(c("Horizon", "20-year"), function(def) {
  d <- add_deviation_terms(event_data, DEFINITIONS[[def]])
  lapply(stats::setNames(nm = names(EVENTS)), function(k) {
    fit_model(form_terms(FORMS[[RUN_FORM]]), d, outcome = k)
  })
})
names(event_fits) <- c("Horizon", "20-year")

# 1. How often, and joint tests.
bind_rows(lapply(names(event_fits), function(def) {
  bind_rows(lapply(names(EVENTS), function(k) {
    m <- event_fits[[def]][[k]]
    tibble::tibble(definition = def, event = paste0(k, " (", EVENTS[[k]], ")"),
                   observations = stats::nobs(m), frequency = round(mean(event_data[[k]]), 3),
                   temperature_p = signif(wald_p(m, "^devTM"), 2),
                   precipitation_p = signif(wald_p(m, "^devRR"), 2))
  }))
})) %>%
  knitr::kable(caption = paste0("PWT x ERA5, ", RUN_FORM, ": frequency of each event and joint ",
                                "tests (p) of each variable's deviation terms in its linear ",
                                "probability model"))

# 2. Change in the probability of each event with a +/-3 SD deviation.
bind_rows(lapply(names(event_fits), function(def) {
  bind_rows(lapply(names(EVENTS), function(k) {
    climate_effects(list(preferred = event_fits[[def]][[k]],
                         panel = list(label = paste0(def, ": ", k, " (", EVENTS[[k]], ")"))),
                    RUN_FORM)
  }))
})) %>%
  significance_map() %>%
  knitr::kable(caption = paste0("PWT x ERA5: change in the probability (pp) of a bad, typical and ",
                                "good year with a +/-3 SD deviation; *** p < 0.01, ** p < 0.05, ",
                                "* p < 0.1"))
```

## Quantile regressions

Do the robust events shift the whole distribution of growth, or mostly one of
its tails? Quantile regressions model the distribution themselves, so the
outcome is growth as it is (g, in pp, signed), on PWT x ERA5 (no trailing
window needed), with the 20-year model of the sections above, on the main
sample (the growth outliers whose cause does not involve weather dropped) and
on the full sample with every outlier kept: the quantile methods should absorb
heavy tails themselves, so the full sample is their natural test. Besides the
mean (OLS), two methods keep the fixed effects (year, and each unit's level
and linear and quadratic trend):

- Machado and Santos Silva (2019), quantiles via moments, the main one: growth
  is a location plus a scale times an error, both linear in the terms,
  `g = FE + X b + (FE_s + X c) U`. The location b is the model above; the
  scale c, the same model of the absolute residual (with its own fixed
  effects, so each unit has its own volatility); and the effect at quantile tau
  is `b + q(tau) c`, with q(tau) the tau-quantile of the residuals over their
  fitted scale. An event moves the quantiles apart only through c, so the
  difference between the 10th and the 90th percentile tests whether it
  changes the spread.
- Canay (2011), a check without the location-scale form: the fixed effects of
  the model above are taken out of g (as pure location shifts), and the rest
  is a quantile regression on the terms, quantile by quantile. Its quantiles
  are pooled over the units, so their tails come mostly from the units with
  the most volatile growth.

The confidence intervals are the 2.5th and 97.5th percentiles of
`r 200L` country-cluster bootstrap draws (countries drawn with replacement,
both steps of each method re-estimated). The effects are in pp of growth.

```{r growth-quantiles, fig.width=16, fig.height=9}
QUANTILES <- c(0.1, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 0.9)
QUANTILE_CURVE <- seq(0.05, 0.95, by = 0.05)
BOOTSTRAP_DRAWS <- 200L
QUANTILE_EVENTS <- tibble::tribble(
  ~event, ~variable, ~deviation, ~climate,
  "hot +3 SD, 25 C", "TM", 3, 25,
  "dry -3 SD, 0.5 m", "RR", -3, 0.5,
  "dry -3 SD, 1.5 m", "RR", -3, 1.5,
  "cold -3 SD, 5 C", "TM", -3, 5
)
quantile_terms <- paste(form_terms(FORMS[[RUN_FORM]]), collapse = " + ")
# The main sample (the growth outliers whose cause does not involve weather
# dropped) and the full sample (every outlier kept).
QUANTILE_SAMPLES <- list("main sample (outliers dropped)" = main$clean,
                         "full sample (outliers included)" = main$all)
quantile_inputs <- lapply(QUANTILE_SAMPLES, function(rows) {
  d <- add_deviation_terms(rows, DEFINITIONS[["20-year"]])
  d$g_pp <- 100 * d[[OUTCOME]]
  d
})

# Weights of each event on the coefficients `terms`.
event_design <- function(terms) {
  G <- matrix(0, nrow(QUANTILE_EVENTS), length(terms),
              dimnames = list(QUANTILE_EVENTS$event, terms))
  for (i in seq_len(nrow(QUANTILE_EVENTS))) {
    v <- QUANTILE_EVENTS$variable[[i]]
    for (s in FORMS[[RUN_FORM]][[v]]) {
      term <- paste0("dev", v, s)
      x <- term_value(s, QUANTILE_EVENTS$deviation[[i]])
      G[i, term] <- x
      G[i, interaction_name(term, paste0("clim_", v), terms)] <- x * QUANTILE_EVENTS$climate[[i]]
    }
  }
  G
}
quantile_fit <- function(d, outcome) {
  fixest::feols(make_panel_formula(quantile_terms, outcome, FIXED_EFFECTS), d, vcov = "iid",
                notes = FALSE, warn = FALSE)
}

# Both methods on the rows `d`: the mean (location) effect of each event, its
# scale effect, its effects at the quantiles QUANTILE_CURVE (Machado-Santos
# Silva) and QUANTILES (Canay), and the share of fitted scales that are not
# positive (left out of q(tau)).
quantile_effects <- function(d) {
  location <- quantile_fit(d, "g_pp")
  rows <- d[fixest::obs(location), ]
  rows$abs_resid <- abs(stats::resid(location))
  scale <- quantile_fit(rows, "abs_resid")
  scale_hat <- stats::fitted(scale)
  u <- stats::resid(location)[fixest::obs(scale)] / scale_hat
  positive <- scale_hat > 0
  q <- stats::quantile(u[positive], QUANTILE_CURVE, names = FALSE)
  terms <- intersect(names(stats::coef(location)), names(stats::coef(scale)))
  G <- event_design(terms)
  b <- drop(G %*% stats::coef(location)[terms])
  c_scale <- drop(G %*% stats::coef(scale)[terms])
  mss <- outer(b, rep(1, length(q))) + outer(c_scale, q)
  colnames(mss) <- QUANTILE_CURVE

  coefs <- stats::coef(location)
  X <- stats::model.matrix(location, data = rows, type = "rhs")[, names(coefs), drop = FALSE]
  adjusted <- rows$g_pp - (stats::fitted(location) - drop(X %*% coefs))
  G_all <- event_design(names(coefs))
  canay <- vapply(QUANTILES, function(tau) {
    fit <- quantreg::rq.fit(cbind(1, X), adjusted, tau = tau, method = "br")
    drop(G_all %*% fit$coefficients[-1])
  }, numeric(nrow(G_all)))
  colnames(canay) <- QUANTILES
  list(mean = b, scale = c_scale, mss = mss, canay = canay, nonpositive = mean(!positive))
}

# Countries drawn with replacement; a country drawn k times enters as k units.
bootstrap_quantiles <- function(d, draws) {
  pieces <- split(d, d$GID_0)
  lapply(seq_len(draws), function(b) {
    draw <- sample(names(pieces), length(pieces), replace = TRUE)
    quantile_effects(bind_rows(lapply(seq_along(draw), function(k) {
      mutate(pieces[[draw[[k]]]], GID_1 = paste0(GID_1, "_", k))
    })))
  })
}

set.seed(20261009)
quantile_runs <- lapply(quantile_inputs, function(d) {
  list(point = quantile_effects(d), draws = bootstrap_quantiles(d, BOOTSTRAP_DRAWS),
       rows = nrow(d))
})
interval <- function(x) stats::quantile(x, c(0.025, 0.975), names = FALSE, na.rm = TRUE)
draws_of <- function(run, part, tau) {
  vapply(run$draws, function(x) x[[part]][, as.character(tau)], numeric(nrow(QUANTILE_EVENTS)))
}
cell <- function(estimate, draws) {
  ci <- t(apply(matrix(draws, nrow = length(estimate)), 1, interval))
  sprintf("%+.2f [%+.2f, %+.2f]", estimate, ci[, 1], ci[, 2])
}
METHOD_NAMES <- c(mss = "Machado-Santos Silva", canay = "Canay")

# 1. Mean and quantile effects, and the 10th minus the 90th percentile, on
# both samples.
quantile_table <- bind_rows(lapply(names(quantile_runs), function(s) {
  run <- quantile_runs[[s]]
  point <- run$point
  mean_draws <- vapply(run$draws, `[[`, numeric(nrow(QUANTILE_EVENTS)), "mean")
  bind_rows(
    tibble::tibble(event = QUANTILE_EVENTS$event, method = "Mean (OLS)",
                   column = "mean", cell = cell(point$mean, mean_draws)),
    bind_rows(lapply(names(METHOD_NAMES), function(part) {
      bind_rows(lapply(QUANTILES, function(tau) {
        tibble::tibble(event = QUANTILE_EVENTS$event, method = METHOD_NAMES[[part]],
                       column = paste0("q", 100 * tau),
                       cell = cell(point[[part]][, as.character(tau)], draws_of(run, part, tau)))
      })) %>%
        bind_rows(tibble::tibble(
          event = QUANTILE_EVENTS$event, method = METHOD_NAMES[[part]], column = "q10 - q90",
          cell = cell(point[[part]][, "0.1"] - point[[part]][, "0.9"],
                      draws_of(run, part, 0.1) - draws_of(run, part, 0.9))))
    }))
  ) %>%
    mutate(sample = s)
}))
quantile_table %>%
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = column, values_from = cell, values_fill = "") %>%
  arrange(factor(event, levels = QUANTILE_EVENTS$event),
          factor(method, levels = c("Mean (OLS)", unname(METHOD_NAMES))), sample) %>%
  select(event, method, sample, everything()) %>%
  knitr::kable(caption = paste0(
    "PWT x ERA5, ", RUN_FORM, ", 20-year deviations: effect of each event on the mean and on ",
    "the quantiles of growth (pp, 95% country-cluster bootstrap CI, ", BOOTSTRAP_DRAWS,
    " draws), on the main sample (", quantile_runs[[1]]$rows, " rows) and on the full sample ",
    "with the growth outliers (", quantile_runs[[2]]$rows, " rows); fitted scales not ",
    "positive: ", paste(vapply(quantile_runs, function(r) {
      sprintf("%.1f%%", 100 * r$point$nonpositive)
    }, ""), collapse = " and ")))

# 2. The quantile curves.
curve <- bind_rows(lapply(names(quantile_runs), function(s) {
  run <- quantile_runs[[s]]
  bind_rows(lapply(QUANTILE_CURVE, function(tau) {
    ci <- t(apply(draws_of(run, "mss", tau), 1, interval))
    tibble::tibble(sample = s, event = QUANTILE_EVENTS$event, tau = tau,
                   estimate = run$point$mss[, as.character(tau)], low = ci[, 1], high = ci[, 2])
  }))
}))
canay_points <- bind_rows(lapply(names(quantile_runs), function(s) {
  run <- quantile_runs[[s]]
  bind_rows(lapply(QUANTILES, function(tau) {
    ci <- t(apply(draws_of(run, "canay", tau), 1, interval))
    tibble::tibble(sample = s, event = QUANTILE_EVENTS$event, tau = tau,
                   estimate = run$point$canay[, as.character(tau)], low = ci[, 1], high = ci[, 2])
  }))
}))
mean_lines <- bind_rows(lapply(names(quantile_runs), function(s) {
  tibble::tibble(sample = s, event = QUANTILE_EVENTS$event, mean = quantile_runs[[s]]$point$mean)
}))
facet_levels <- function(x) {
  mutate(x, event = factor(event, levels = QUANTILE_EVENTS$event),
         sample = factor(sample, levels = names(QUANTILE_SAMPLES)))
}
ggplot(facet_levels(curve), aes(tau, estimate)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, colour = GRID_MUTED, linewidth = 0.3) +
  geom_hline(data = facet_levels(mean_lines), aes(yintercept = mean), linetype = "dashed",
             colour = GRID_INK, linewidth = 0.4) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = low, ymax = high), fill = GRID_PALETTE[[1]], alpha = 0.15) +
  geom_line(colour = GRID_PALETTE[[1]], linewidth = 0.9) +
  geom_pointrange(data = facet_levels(canay_points), aes(ymin = low, ymax = high),
                  colour = GRID_PALETTE[[2]], size = 0.3, position = position_nudge(x = 0.01)) +
  facet_grid(sample ~ event, scales = "free_y") +
  labs(x = "Quantile of growth", y = "Effect (pp of growth)",
       title = "Effect of the robust events across the distribution of growth",
       subtitle = wrap_text(paste0(
         "PWT x ERA5, ", RUN_FORM, ", 20-year deviations; top: the main sample, bottom: with ",
         "the growth outliers. Blue: Machado-Santos Silva, with its 95% bootstrap band; ",
         "orange: Canay, with 95% bootstrap intervals; dashed: the effect on the mean (OLS)."),
         150)) +
  theme_results()
```

# Compound hot and dry years

Is a dry year more harmful when it is also hot than when its temperature is
typical? Three steps, with growth in pp, the 20-year deviations (demeaned, as
in every model above), and the fixed effects and controls of the models above:

1. How often hot and dry years coincide. Each year has a temperature state
   (cold, typical or hot: its deviation below -1, within +/-1, or above +1 SD)
   and a precipitation state (dry, typical or wet, the same cuts); the counts
   of the nine combinations and the correlation of the two deviations (the
   arms of the models already share the effect of years that are both hot
   and dry).
2. The nine combinations as dummies, the year typical in both the reference,
   with no functional form: a hot and dry year against a dry year of typical
   temperature, and against a hot year of typical precipitation, and their
   interaction, hot-dry minus hot-typical minus typical-dry (what the
   combination adds to the two alone); on every unit and on the dry-to-mid
   ones (the bottom two thirds of the units by long-run precipitation).
3. The model of the sections above (`r RUN_FORM`, with its climate
   interactions) with the slope of the dry arm allowed to differ in hot years,
   and that of the hot arm in dry years: does a drought of a given size cost
   more when the year is also hot? The fit against the model without them, and
   the effect of a -2 SD dry year in a hot and in a typical year.

```{r compound-events}
COMPOUND_CUT <- 1  # SD beyond which a year is hot (cold) or wet (dry)
COMBINATION_REFERENCE <- "T typical, P typical"
compound_data <- add_deviation_terms(main$clean, DEFINITIONS[["20-year"]]) %>%
  mutate(T_state = cut(devTM, c(-Inf, -COMPOUND_CUT, COMPOUND_CUT, Inf),
                       labels = c("cold", "typical", "hot")),
         P_state = cut(devRR, c(-Inf, -COMPOUND_CUT, COMPOUND_CUT, Inf),
                       labels = c("dry", "typical", "wet")),
         combination = paste0("T ", T_state, ", P ", P_state),
         hot_year = as.numeric(devTM > COMPOUND_CUT),
         dry_year = as.numeric(devRR < -COMPOUND_CUT),
         g_pp = 100 * .data[[OUTCOME]])
drymid_cut <- stats::quantile(distinct(compound_data, GID_1, clim_RR)$clim_RR, 2 / 3, names = FALSE)
COMPOUND_SAMPLES <- list(
  "every unit" = compound_data,
  "dry-to-mid units" = filter(compound_data, clim_RR < drymid_cut)
)

# 1. How often: the nine combinations, and the correlation of the deviations.
for (s in names(COMPOUND_SAMPLES)) {
  d <- COMPOUND_SAMPLES[[s]]
  print(knitr::kable(
    as.data.frame.matrix(table(d$T_state, d$P_state)) %>% tibble::rownames_to_column("T state"),
    caption = sprintf(paste("%s, %s: country-years by temperature (rows) and precipitation",
                            "(columns) state; correlation of the two deviations %.2f"),
                      main$label, s, stats::cor(d$devTM, d$devRR))))
}

# 2. The nine combinations as dummies: contrasts of a hot and dry year.
combination_term <- function(x) paste0("combination::", x)
COMPOUND_CONTRASTS <- list(
  "hot and dry" = c("T hot, P dry" = 1),
  "dry, typical temperature" = c("T typical, P dry" = 1),
  "hot, typical precipitation" = c("T hot, P typical" = 1),
  "hot and dry - dry with typical temperature" = c("T hot, P dry" = 1, "T typical, P dry" = -1),
  "hot and dry - hot with typical precipitation" = c("T hot, P dry" = 1, "T hot, P typical" = -1),
  "interaction: hot-dry - hot-typical - typical-dry" =
    c("T hot, P dry" = 1, "T hot, P typical" = -1, "T typical, P dry" = -1)
)
combination_fits <- lapply(COMPOUND_SAMPLES, function(d) {
  fit_model(c(sprintf("i(combination, ref = '%s')", COMBINATION_REFERENCE), CONTROLS), d,
            outcome = "g_pp")
})
bind_rows(lapply(names(combination_fits), function(s) {
  m <- combination_fits[[s]]
  G <- t(vapply(COMPOUND_CONTRASTS, function(w) {
    x <- stats::setNames(numeric(length(stats::coef(m))), names(stats::coef(m)))
    x[combination_term(names(w))] <- w
    x
  }, numeric(length(stats::coef(m)))))
  linear_combination(m, G) %>%
    mutate(sample = s, contrast = names(COMPOUND_CONTRASTS),
           p_value = 2 * stats::pnorm(-abs(estimate / std_error)),
           cell = sprintf("%+.2f [%+.2f, %+.2f]%s", estimate, conf_low, conf_high, stars(p_value)))
})) %>%
  select(contrast, sample, cell) %>%
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = sample, values_from = cell) %>%
  knitr::kable(caption = paste0(
    main$label, ": growth (pp, 95% CI) in each combination against the year typical in both, ",
    "and the contrasts of a hot and dry year (dummies for the nine combinations, with the ",
    "fixed effects and controls of the models above); hot and dry years: ",
    paste(vapply(COMPOUND_SAMPLES, function(d) sum(d$combination == "T hot, P dry"), 0),
          collapse = " and "), "; *** p < 0.01, ** p < 0.05, * p < 0.1"))

# 3. The model with the dry arm's slope in hot years and the hot arm's in dry
# years.
COMPOUND_DRY_SLOPE <- paste0(RUN_DRY_ARM, ":hot_year")
COMPOUND_HOT_SLOPE <- paste0(RUN_HOT_ARM, ":dry_year")
compound_terms <- c(form_terms(FORMS[[RUN_FORM]]), COMPOUND_DRY_SLOPE, COMPOUND_HOT_SLOPE)
compound_models <- lapply(COMPOUND_SAMPLES, function(d) {
  list(base = fit_model(form_terms(FORMS[[RUN_FORM]]), d, outcome = "g_pp"),
       compound = fit_model(compound_terms, d, outcome = "g_pp"))
})
COMPOUND_EFFECTS <- tibble::tribble(
  ~effect, ~arm, ~value, ~clim_term, ~climate, ~state_term,
  "dry -2 SD, 0.5 m, typical temperature", RUN_DRY_ARM, arm_event_value(RUN_DRY_ARM, 2), "clim_RR", 0.5, NA,
  "dry -2 SD, 0.5 m, hot year", RUN_DRY_ARM, arm_event_value(RUN_DRY_ARM, 2), "clim_RR", 0.5, COMPOUND_DRY_SLOPE,
  "dry -2 SD, 1.5 m, typical temperature", RUN_DRY_ARM, arm_event_value(RUN_DRY_ARM, 2), "clim_RR", 1.5, NA,
  "dry -2 SD, 1.5 m, hot year", RUN_DRY_ARM, arm_event_value(RUN_DRY_ARM, 2), "clim_RR", 1.5, COMPOUND_DRY_SLOPE,
  "hot +2 SD, 25 C, typical precipitation", RUN_HOT_ARM, arm_event_value(RUN_HOT_ARM, 2), "clim_TM", 25, NA,
  "hot +2 SD, 25 C, dry year", RUN_HOT_ARM, arm_event_value(RUN_HOT_ARM, 2), "clim_TM", 25, COMPOUND_HOT_SLOPE
)
bind_rows(lapply(names(compound_models), function(s) {
  m <- compound_models[[s]]$compound
  terms <- names(stats::coef(m))
  G <- t(vapply(seq_len(nrow(COMPOUND_EFFECTS)), function(i) {
    e <- COMPOUND_EFFECTS[i, ]
    w <- stats::setNames(numeric(length(terms)), terms)
    w[[e$arm]] <- e$value
    w[[term_named(paste0(e$arm, ":", e$clim_term), terms)]] <- e$value * e$climate
    if (!is.na(e$state_term)) w[[term_named(e$state_term, terms)]] <- e$value
    w
  }, numeric(length(terms))))
  colnames(G) <- terms
  slopes <- fixest::coeftable(m)
  slope_cell <- function(term) {
    term <- term_named(term, rownames(slopes))
    sprintf("%+.3f (p %.2f)", slopes[term, "Estimate"], slopes[term, "Pr(>|t|)"])
  }
  linear_combination(m, G) %>%
```
