```{r compound-events}
    mutate(p_value = 2 * stats::pnorm(-abs(estimate / std_error)),
           cell = sprintf("%+.2f [%+.2f, %+.2f]%s", estimate, conf_low, conf_high, stars(p_value)),
           effect = COMPOUND_EFFECTS$effect) %>%
    select(effect, cell) %>%
    bind_rows(tibble::tibble(
      effect = c("dry arm x hot year (pp per arm unit)", "hot arm x dry year (pp per arm unit)",
                 "AIC, with the two terms minus without",
                 "verdict with the two terms (AIC / BIC / R2)"),
      cell = c(slope_cell(COMPOUND_DRY_SLOPE), slope_cell(COMPOUND_HOT_SLOPE),
               sprintf("%+.1f", stats::AIC(m) - stats::AIC(compound_models[[s]]$base)),
               fit_verdicts(m, compound_models[[s]]$base,
                            nested_p = added_terms_p(m, compound_models[[s]]$base))))) %>%
    mutate(sample = s)
})) %>%
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = sample, values_from = cell) %>%
  knitr::kable(caption = paste0(
    main$label, ", ", RUN_FORM, ", 20-year deviations, with the dry arm's slope in hot years ",
    "and the hot arm's in dry years: effects (pp, 95% CI), the two slopes, and the AIC against ",
    "the model without them with the ", VERDICT_NOTE, " (nested: the joint test of the two ",
    "terms); *** p < 0.01, ** p < 0.05, * p < 0.1"))
```


# Long-run income in the interaction

The climate interactions of the preferred model give a country at 25 °C the
response the data find in hot countries. Hot countries are also poor, so the
gradient across climates may be one across incomes. Here every deviation term
of the preferred form also enters interacted with the unit's long-run income,
with the horizon deviations (the standard long-run climate: the horizon mean
and SD):

```text
inc(i)  = log of the mean GDP per capita of unit i over the horizon (start year
          .. last year of the panel, every year with GDP), minus its mean over
          the sample rows
growth  = sum over arms a of  dev_a x (c_a + b_a clim + h_a inc)  + controls + FE
```

Income is centred, so `c_a + b_a clim` is the response at the sample's
average income. On the rows of `r main$label`, the same as the model without
income:

1. how closely long-run income and climate move together across the units;
2. the coefficients with and without the income terms;
3. the joint tests: the income terms (all, and of each variable), and the
   climate interactions once income is in (does the climate gradient survive?),
   with the verdict of the model with income against the one without;
4. the effects of a +/-3 SD year at each long-run climate: without income, at
   the average income, and at the mean income of the poorest and of the richest
   third of the units.

```{r income-interaction}
INCOME_DEFINITION <- "Horizon"
INCOME_FORM <- PREFERRED_FORM
# Each unit's long-run income over the horizon of panel `p`, centred at the mean
# over the rows `d`.
add_income <- function(p, d) {
  income <- p$data %>%
    filter(year >= p$start_year, year <= p$end_year, !is.na(grp_pc_usd)) %>%
    group_by(GID_1) %>%
    summarise(inc_level = log(mean(grp_pc_usd)), .groups = "drop")
  d <- left_join(d, income, by = "GID_1")
  stopifnot(!anyNA(d$inc_level))
  d$inc <- d$inc_level - mean(d$inc_level)
  d
}
# Weights on the coefficients `terms` of a deviation x (SD) of variable v in a
# model with the arms `suffixes`, at the values `modifiers` (named: the
# variables interacted with every deviation term, e.g. clim_TM, inc).
deviation_weights <- function(terms, suffixes, v, x, modifiers) {
  w <- stats::setNames(numeric(length(terms)), terms)
  for (s in suffixes) {
    term <- paste0("dev", v, s)
    w[[term]] <- term_value(s, x)
    for (z in names(modifiers)) {
      w[[interaction_name(term, z, terms)]] <- term_value(s, x) * modifiers[[z]]
    }
  }
  w
}
# Effects (pp, 95% CI) of EFFECT_AT SD of each variable at each long-run
# climate of EVAL_CLIMATE in model m (arms `form`), at the extra modifiers
# `at` (e.g. list(inc = 0)).
effects_at <- function(m, form, at = list()) {
  terms <- names(stats::coef(m))
  bind_rows(lapply(c("TM", "RR"), function(v) {
    grid <- expand.grid(level = seq_along(EVAL_CLIMATE[[v]]), deviation = EFFECT_AT)
    G <- t(mapply(function(g, x) {
      mods <- c(stats::setNames(list(EVAL_CLIMATE[[v]][[g]]), paste0("clim_", v)), at)
      deviation_weights(terms, form[[v]], v, x, mods)
    }, grid$level, grid$deviation))
    colnames(G) <- terms
    linear_combination(m, G) %>%
      mutate(variable = v, level = EVAL_LABELS[[v]][grid$level], deviation = grid$deviation,
             p_value = 2 * stats::pnorm(-abs(estimate / std_error)), .before = 1)
  }))
}
effect_cell <- function(e) {
  sprintf("%+.2f [%+.2f, %+.2f]%s", 100 * e$estimate, 100 * e$conf_low, 100 * e$conf_high,
          stars(e$p_value))
}
effect_row <- function(e) paste0(ifelse(e$variable == "TM", "T ", "P "),
                                 sprintf("%+d SD, ", e$deviation), e$level)

income_data <- add_income(main, add_deviation_terms(main$clean, DEFINITIONS[[INCOME_DEFINITION]]))
income_interactions <- unlist(lapply(c("TM", "RR"), function(v) {
  paste0("dev", v, FORMS[[INCOME_FORM]][[v]], ":inc")
}))
income_models <- list(
  "without income" = fit_model(form_terms(FORMS[[INCOME_FORM]]), income_data),
  "with income" = fit_model(c(form_terms(FORMS[[INCOME_FORM]]), income_interactions), income_data)
)

# 1. Income and climate across the units.
income_units <- distinct(income_data, GID_1, inc_level, clim_TM, clim_RR)
income_thirds <- income_units %>%
  mutate(third = factor(c("poorest third", "middle third", "richest third")[dplyr::ntile(inc_level, 3)],
                        levels = c("poorest third", "middle third", "richest third")))
income_thirds %>%
  group_by(third) %>%
  summarise(units = n(), gdp_pc = round(exp(mean(inc_level))),
            mean_T = round(mean(clim_TM), 1), mean_P = round(mean(clim_RR), 2), .groups = "drop") %>%
  knitr::kable(caption = sprintf(paste(
    "%s, units by third of long-run income: GDP per capita (geometric mean) and mean long-run",
    "climate; across the units, correlation of log income with mean T %.2f, with mean P %.2f"),
    main$label, stats::cor(income_units$inc_level, income_units$clim_TM),
    stats::cor(income_units$inc_level, income_units$clim_RR)))

# 2. Coefficients.
DICT_INCOME <- c(DICT, inc = "income")
etable(unname(income_models), headers = names(income_models), dict = DICT_INCOME, drop = DROP,
       order = ORDER, fitstat = FITSTAT,
       title = paste0(main$label, ", ", INCOME_FORM, ", ", INCOME_DEFINITION, " deviations"))

# 3. Joint tests.
with_income <- income_models[["with income"]]
income_p <- added_terms_p(with_income, income_models[["without income"]])
tibble::tibble(
  test = c("income terms, all", "income terms, T", "income terms, P",
           "climate interactions with income, T", "climate interactions with income, P",
           "climate interactions without income, T", "climate interactions without income, P",
           "with income against without (AIC / BIC / R2)"),
  result = c(signif(income_p, 2), signif(wald_p(with_income, "^devTM.*:inc$|^inc:devTM"), 2),
             signif(wald_p(with_income, "^devRR.*:inc$|^inc:devRR"), 2),
             signif(wald_p(with_income, "clim_TM"), 2), signif(wald_p(with_income, "clim_RR"), 2),
             signif(wald_p(income_models[["without income"]], "clim_TM"), 2),
             signif(wald_p(income_models[["without income"]], "clim_RR"), 2),
             fit_verdicts(with_income, income_models[["without income"]], nested_p = income_p))
) %>%
  knitr::kable(caption = paste0(main$label, ": joint Wald tests (p) and the ", VERDICT_NOTE))

# 4. Effects at each climate, with and without income.
income_at <- c(list("without income" = NULL, "average income" = 0),
               lapply(split(income_thirds$inc_level, income_thirds$third),
                      function(x) mean(x) - mean(income_data$inc_level)))
names(income_at)[3:5] <- paste("income of the", names(income_at)[3:5])
income_effects <- lapply(names(income_at), function(k) {
  if (is.null(income_at[[k]])) {
    effects_at(income_models[["without income"]], FORMS[[INCOME_FORM]])
  } else {
    effects_at(with_income, FORMS[[INCOME_FORM]], list(inc = income_at[[k]]))
  }
})
tibble::tibble(effect = effect_row(income_effects[[1]])) %>%
  bind_cols(stats::setNames(lapply(income_effects, effect_cell), names(income_at))) %>%
  knitr::kable(caption = paste(
    paste0(main$label, ":"), "effect (pp, 95% CI) of a year at +/-3 SD at each long-run climate, without",
    "the income terms and, with them, at the average income and at the mean income of each",
    "third; *** p < 0.01, ** p < 0.05, * p < 0.1"))
```

The figures below show the response of growth to a deviation from -3 to +3 SD
in the model with income, in each cell of units by third of long-run climate
(rows: cold, temperate, hot; dry, mid, wet) and third of long-run income
(columns), at the mean climate and income of the cell's units; against it, the
model without income at the same climate, which gives every income the same
response. Each panel gives the number of units in the cell and its mean
climate; the bands are 95% CIs (clustered by country).

```{r income-interaction-figure, fig.width = 10, fig.height = 8}
INCOME_CURVE_X <- seq(-3, 3, by = 0.1)
CLIMATE_THIRDS <- list(TM = c("cold", "temperate", "hot"), RR = c("dry", "mid", "wet"))
# Cells of units by third of long-run climate and of income: units, mean
# climate and mean centred income.
income_cells <- bind_rows(lapply(c("TM", "RR"), function(v) {
  clim <- paste0("clim_", v)
  income_thirds %>%
    mutate(climate_third = factor(CLIMATE_THIRDS[[v]][dplyr::ntile(.data[[clim]], 3)],
                                  levels = CLIMATE_THIRDS[[v]])) %>%
    group_by(climate_third, third) %>%
    summarise(units = n(), climate = mean(.data[[clim]]),
              inc = mean(inc_level) - mean(income_data$inc_level), .groups = "drop") %>%
    mutate(variable = v)
}))
# Effect (pp) of the deviations INCOME_CURVE_X of variable v in model m at the
# values `mods`, with its 95% CI.
curve_at <- function(m, v, mods) {
  terms <- names(stats::coef(m))
  G <- t(vapply(INCOME_CURVE_X, function(x) {
    deviation_weights(terms, FORMS[[INCOME_FORM]][[v]], v, x, mods)
  }, numeric(length(terms))))
  colnames(G) <- terms
  linear_combination(m, G) %>%
    transmute(x = INCOME_CURVE_X, estimate = 100 * estimate, conf_low = 100 * conf_low,
              conf_high = 100 * conf_high)
}
income_curves <- bind_rows(lapply(seq_len(nrow(income_cells)), function(i) {
  cell <- income_cells[i, ]
  clim <- stats::setNames(list(cell$climate), paste0("clim_", cell$variable))
  bind_rows(
    curve_at(with_income, cell$variable, c(clim, list(inc = cell$inc))) %>%
      mutate(model = "with income"),
    curve_at(income_models[["without income"]], cell$variable, clim) %>%
      mutate(model = "without income")
  ) %>%
    mutate(variable = cell$variable, climate_third = cell$climate_third, third = cell$third)
})) %>%
  mutate(model = factor(model, levels = c("with income", "without income")))
INCOME_COLOURS <- c("with income" = "#2a78d6", "without income" = "#eb6834")
for (v in c("TM", "RR")) {
  cells <- filter(income_cells, variable == v) %>%
    mutate(label = sprintf("%d units, %s", units,
                           if (v == "TM") sprintf("%.1f °C", climate) else sprintf("%.2f m", climate)))
  p <- ggplot(filter(income_curves, variable == v), aes(x, estimate, colour = model, fill = model)) +
    geom_hline(yintercept = 0, colour = "grey55", linewidth = 0.4) +
    geom_vline(xintercept = 0, colour = "grey85", linewidth = 0.3) +
    geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = conf_low, ymax = conf_high), alpha = 0.15, colour = NA) +
    geom_line(aes(linetype = model), linewidth = 0.8) +
    geom_text(data = cells, aes(x = -3, y = Inf, label = label), inherit.aes = FALSE,
              hjust = 0, vjust = 1.5, size = 3, colour = "grey30") +
    facet_grid(climate_third ~ third) +
    scale_colour_manual(values = INCOME_COLOURS, name = NULL) +
    scale_fill_manual(values = INCOME_COLOURS, name = NULL) +
    scale_linetype_manual(values = c("solid", "longdash"), name = NULL) +
    scale_x_continuous(breaks = -3:3) +
    labs(x = paste(if (v == "TM") "Temperature" else "Precipitation",
                   "deviation (horizon SD, demeaned)"),
         y = "Effect on growth of GDP per capita (pp)",
         title = paste(if (v == "TM") "Temperature" else "Precipitation",
                       "response by long-run climate and income"),
         subtitle = paste0(main$label, ", ", INCOME_FORM, ", ", INCOME_DEFINITION,
                           " deviations; rows: third of long-run climate, columns: third of ",
                           "long-run income;\neach panel at its units' mean climate and income; ",
                           "bands: 95% CI, clustered by country")) +
    theme_minimal(base_size = 11) +
    theme(legend.position = "top", panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
          panel.grid.major = element_line(colour = "grey92", linewidth = 0.3),
          strip.text = element_text(face = "bold"))
  print(p)
}
```

## Splines in climate and income

The interactions above are linear in the long-run climate and in income, so a
gradient that bends in one can be picked up by the other (hot countries are
poor). Here both are made flexible together: each interaction is replaced by a
restricted cubic spline (as in "A spline in the climate interaction": the
variable itself and two non-linear terms, knots at the
`r paste(100 * SPLINE_KNOT_PROBS, collapse = ", ")`th percentiles of the
units, linear beyond the outer knots), for the climate, for income, or for
both:

```text
growth = sum over arms a of  dev_a x (c_a + f_a(clim) + g_a(inc))  + controls + FE
f_a, g_a: restricted cubic splines (linear: the non-linear terms at zero)
```

The linear model is the one with income above, so every comparison is nested.
On the same rows:

1. the fit of each version against the linear one (the joint Wald test of the
   non-linear terms it adds), the Wald tests of the non-linear terms of each
   variable in climate and in income, and in each version the joint tests of
   all the income terms and of all the climate terms (does income survive a
   flexible climate, and climate a flexible income?);
2. the effects of a +/-3 SD year in the cells of the figures above (third of
   climate x third of income, at the cell's mean), linear and with both
   splines;
3. figure: the effect of a +/-3 SD year across the long-run climate at the
   average income, and across income at the average climate, linear and with
   both splines (95% CI; ticks: the units).

```{r income-splines, fig.width = 13, fig.height = 8}
# The knots of the climates and of income (quantiles of the units), and the
# non-linear terms clim_<v>_nl<j> and inc_nl<j>.
income_spline_units <- distinct(income_data, GID_1, inc, clim_TM, clim_RR)
income_knots <- lapply(c(TM = "clim_TM", RR = "clim_RR", inc = "inc"), function(z) {
  stats::quantile(income_spline_units[[z]], SPLINE_KNOT_PROBS, names = FALSE)
})
income_spline_data <- add_spline_terms(income_data, income_knots[c("TM", "RR")])
inc_nonlinear <- rcs_nonlinear(income_spline_data$inc, income_knots$inc)
for (j in seq_len(ncol(inc_nonlinear))) {
  income_spline_data[[paste0("inc_nl", j)]] <- inc_nonlinear[, j]
}
# The model with income, with the non-linear terms of the climate and/or of
# income for every arm.
income_spline_terms <- function(climate_spline, income_spline) {
  nl <- seq_len(SPLINE_NONLINEAR)
  extra <- unlist(lapply(c("TM", "RR"), function(v) {
    arms <- paste0("dev", v, FORMS[[INCOME_FORM]][[v]])
    c(if (climate_spline) as.vector(outer(arms, paste0(":clim_", v, "_nl", nl), paste0)),
      if (income_spline) as.vector(outer(arms, paste0(":inc_nl", nl), paste0)))
  }))
  c(form_terms(FORMS[[INCOME_FORM]]), income_interactions, extra)
}
INCOME_SPLINE_MODELS <- list("linear" = c(climate = FALSE, income = FALSE),
                             "spline climate" = c(climate = TRUE, income = FALSE),
                             "spline income" = c(climate = FALSE, income = TRUE),
                             "spline climate and income" = c(climate = TRUE, income = TRUE))
income_spline_fits <- lapply(INCOME_SPLINE_MODELS, function(s) {
  fit_model(income_spline_terms(s[["climate"]], s[["income"]]), income_spline_data)
})
stopifnot(length(unique(vapply(income_spline_fits, stats::nobs, 0))) == 1)
# Wald test (p) of the interactions of variable v's arms with the terms `z`
# (a regular expression), whatever the order of the parts; NA if none.
arm_terms_p <- function(m, v, z) {
  pattern <- sprintf("^dev%s[^:]*:%s|^%s:dev%s", v, z, z, v)
  if (!any(grepl(pattern, names(stats::coef(m))))) return(NA_real_)
  wald_p(m, pattern)
}

# 1. Fit and tests.
bind_rows(lapply(names(income_spline_fits), function(k) {
  m <- income_spline_fits[[k]]
  linear <- income_spline_fits$linear
  added_p <- if (k != "linear") added_terms_p(m, linear)
  tibble::tibble(
    model = k,
    aic_vs_linear = round(stats::AIC(m) - stats::AIC(linear), 1),
    bic_vs_linear = round(stats::BIC(m) - stats::BIC(linear), 1),
    within_adj_r2_pct = round(100 * fixest::fitstat(m, "war2")[[1]], 3),
    verdict_vs_linear = if (is.null(added_p)) "" else fit_verdicts(m, linear, nested_p = added_p),
    T_climate_nl_p = arm_terms_p(m, "TM", "clim_TM_nl[0-9]+"),
    P_climate_nl_p = arm_terms_p(m, "RR", "clim_RR_nl[0-9]+"),
    T_income_nl_p = arm_terms_p(m, "TM", "inc_nl[0-9]+"),
    P_income_nl_p = arm_terms_p(m, "RR", "inc_nl[0-9]+"),
    income_all_p = wald_p(m, "inc"),
    climate_all_p = wald_p(m, "clim_")
  )
})) %>%
  mutate(across(ends_with("_p"), ~ signif(.x, 2))) %>%
  knitr::kable(caption = paste0(
    main$label, ", ", INCOME_FORM, ", ", INCOME_DEFINITION, " deviations, with income: the ",
    "interactions linear or restricted cubic splines in the climate and/or income; AIC and BIC ",
    "against the linear model, within adjusted R2 (%), the ", VERDICT_NOTE, " against the linear ",
    "model (nested: the joint test of the non-linear terms added); Wald tests (p) of the ",
    "non-linear terms of each variable in the climate and in income, and of all the income ",
    "terms and all the climate terms of the model"))

# Weights on the coefficients of model m of a deviation x of variable v at
# long-run climate `clim` and centred income `inc`, with the non-linear terms
# of the splines the model has (knots `knots`).
income_spline_weights <- function(m, v, x, clim, inc, spline, knots = income_knots) {
  terms <- names(stats::coef(m))
  mods <- c(stats::setNames(list(clim), paste0("clim_", v)), list(inc = inc))
  if (spline[["climate"]]) {
    nl <- rcs_nonlinear(clim, knots[[v]])
    mods <- c(mods, stats::setNames(as.list(nl[1, ]), paste0("clim_", v, "_nl", seq_len(ncol(nl)))))
  }
  if (spline[["income"]]) {
    nl <- rcs_nonlinear(inc, knots$inc)
    mods <- c(mods, stats::setNames(as.list(nl[1, ]), paste0("inc_nl", seq_len(ncol(nl)))))
  }
  deviation_weights(terms, FORMS[[INCOME_FORM]][[v]], v, x, mods)
}
# Effects (linear_combination) of x at each row of `at` (columns clim, inc) in
# model k of `fits` (named as INCOME_SPLINE_MODELS) with the knots `knots`.
income_spline_effects <- function(k, v, x, at, fits = income_spline_fits, knots = income_knots) {
  m <- fits[[k]]
  G <- t(vapply(seq_len(nrow(at)), function(i) {
    income_spline_weights(m, v, x, at$clim[i], at$inc[i], INCOME_SPLINE_MODELS[[k]], knots)
  }, numeric(length(stats::coef(m)))))
  colnames(G) <- names(stats::coef(m))
  linear_combination(m, G)
}
INCOME_SPLINE_COMPARED <- c("linear", "spline climate and income")

# 2. The cells of climate and income.
bind_rows(lapply(seq_len(nrow(income_cells)), function(i) {
  cell <- income_cells[i, ]
  at <- tibble::tibble(clim = cell$climate, inc = cell$inc)
  cells <- unlist(lapply(EFFECT_AT, function(x) {
    vapply(INCOME_SPLINE_COMPARED, function(k) {
      effect_cell(income_spline_effects(k, cell$variable, x, at) %>%
                    mutate(p_value = 2 * stats::pnorm(-abs(estimate / std_error))))
    }, "")
  }))
  names(cells) <- as.vector(outer(c("linear", "splines"), sprintf("%+d SD", EFFECT_AT),
                                  function(k, x) paste(x, k)))
  tibble::tibble(variable = ifelse(cell$variable == "TM", "T", "P"),
                 climate = as.character(cell$climate_third), income = as.character(cell$third),
                 units = cell$units, !!!as.list(cells))
})) %>%
  knitr::kable(caption = paste(
    main$label, ": effect (pp, 95% CI) of a year at +/-3 SD in each cell of units (third of",
    "long-run climate x third of long-run income, at the cell's mean), with linear interactions",
    "and with splines in both the climate and income; *** p < 0.01, ** p < 0.05, * p < 0.1"))

# 3. Curves across the climate (at the average income) and across income (at
# the average climate of the rows).
INCOME_SPLINE_EVENTS <- tibble::tribble(
  ~variable, ~deviation, ~event,
  "TM", 3, "T +3 SD", "TM", -3, "T -3 SD", "RR", -3, "P -3 SD", "RR", 3, "P +3 SD"
)
mean_inc_level <- mean(income_data$inc_level)
income_spline_curves <- bind_rows(lapply(seq_len(nrow(INCOME_SPLINE_EVENTS)), function(i) {
  e <- INCOME_SPLINE_EVENTS[i, ]
  unit_climate <- income_spline_units[[paste0("clim_", e$variable)]]
  along <- list(
    climate = tibble::tibble(clim = seq(min(unit_climate), max(unit_climate), length.out = 80),
                             inc = 0),
    income = tibble::tibble(clim = mean(income_data[[paste0("clim_", e$variable)]]),
                            inc = seq(min(income_spline_units$inc), max(income_spline_units$inc),
                                      length.out = 80))
  )
  bind_rows(lapply(names(along), function(a) {
    bind_rows(lapply(INCOME_SPLINE_COMPARED, function(k) {
      income_spline_effects(k, e$variable, e$deviation, along[[a]]) %>%
        mutate(interaction = ifelse(k == "linear", "linear", "splines"),
               position = if (a == "climate") along[[a]]$clim else along[[a]]$inc + mean_inc_level)
    })) %>%
      mutate(panel = paste0(e$event, ", across ", a))
  }))
}))
income_spline_rug <- bind_rows(lapply(seq_len(nrow(INCOME_SPLINE_EVENTS)), function(i) {
  e <- INCOME_SPLINE_EVENTS[i, ]
  bind_rows(
    tibble::tibble(panel = paste0(e$event, ", across climate"),
                   position = income_spline_units[[paste0("clim_", e$variable)]]),
    tibble::tibble(panel = paste0(e$event, ", across income"),
                   position = income_spline_units$inc + mean_inc_level)
  )
}))
spline_panel_levels <- as.vector(t(outer(INCOME_SPLINE_EVENTS$event, c("climate", "income"),
                                         function(e, a) paste0(e, ", across ", a))))
ggplot(mutate(income_spline_curves, panel = factor(panel, levels = spline_panel_levels)),
       aes(position, 100 * estimate, colour = interaction, fill = interaction)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, colour = GRID_MUTED, linewidth = 0.3) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = 100 * conf_low, ymax = 100 * conf_high), alpha = 0.12, colour = NA) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.8) +
  geom_rug(data = mutate(income_spline_rug, panel = factor(panel, levels = spline_panel_levels)),
           aes(x = position), inherit.aes = FALSE, sides = "b", alpha = 0.4, colour = GRID_MUTED) +
  facet_wrap(~panel, ncol = 4, scales = "free") +
  scale_colour_manual(values = grid_colours(c("linear", "splines")), name = "Interactions") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = grid_colours(c("linear", "splines")), guide = "none") +
  labs(x = "Long-run climate (C, or m a year), or log long-run GDP per capita (horizon mean)",
       y = "Effect on growth that year (pp)",
       title = "Effect of a +/-3 SD year across climate and income: linear or spline interactions",
       subtitle = paste(strwrap(paste0(
         main$label, ", ", INCOME_FORM, ", ", INCOME_DEFINITION, " deviations, with income; ",
         "across the climate at the average income, across income at the average climate of ",
         "the rows; splines in both the climate and income; bands: 95% CI; ticks: the units."),
         150), collapse = "\n")) +
  theme_results()
```

The response of growth to a deviation from -3 to +3 SD in the model with
splines in both the climate and income, in the cells of units by third of
long-run climate (rows) and of long-run income (columns), at the cell's mean
climate and income, as in the figures of the linear model above; against it,
the linear model with income. Bands: 95% CIs (clustered by country).

```{r income-splines-cells, fig.width = 10, fig.height = 8}
# Effect (pp, 95% CI) of the deviations INCOME_CURVE_X of variable v in model
# k of INCOME_SPLINE_MODELS at long-run climate `clim` and centred income `inc`.
income_spline_curve <- function(k, v, clim, inc) {
  m <- income_spline_fits[[k]]
  G <- t(vapply(INCOME_CURVE_X, function(x) {
    income_spline_weights(m, v, x, clim, inc, INCOME_SPLINE_MODELS[[k]])
  }, numeric(length(stats::coef(m)))))
  colnames(G) <- names(stats::coef(m))
  linear_combination(m, G) %>%
    transmute(x = INCOME_CURVE_X, estimate = 100 * estimate, conf_low = 100 * conf_low,
              conf_high = 100 * conf_high)
}
SPLINE_CELL_MODELS <- c("splines in climate and income" = "spline climate and income",
                        "linear in climate and income" = "linear")
spline_cell_curves <- bind_rows(lapply(seq_len(nrow(income_cells)), function(i) {
  cell <- income_cells[i, ]
  bind_rows(lapply(names(SPLINE_CELL_MODELS), function(label) {
    income_spline_curve(SPLINE_CELL_MODELS[[label]], cell$variable, cell$climate, cell$inc) %>%
      mutate(model = label)
  })) %>%
    mutate(variable = cell$variable, climate_third = cell$climate_third, third = cell$third)
})) %>%
  mutate(model = factor(model, levels = names(SPLINE_CELL_MODELS)))
SPLINE_CELL_COLOURS <- grid_colours(names(SPLINE_CELL_MODELS))
for (v in c("TM", "RR")) {
  cells <- filter(income_cells, variable == v) %>%
    mutate(label = sprintf("%d units, %s", units,
                           if (v == "TM") sprintf("%.1f °C", climate) else sprintf("%.2f m", climate)))
  p <- ggplot(filter(spline_cell_curves, variable == v),
              aes(x, estimate, colour = model, fill = model)) +
    geom_hline(yintercept = 0, colour = GRID_MUTED, linewidth = 0.3) +
    geom_vline(xintercept = 0, colour = "grey85", linewidth = 0.3) +
    geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = conf_low, ymax = conf_high), alpha = 0.15, colour = NA) +
    geom_line(aes(linetype = model), linewidth = 0.8) +
    geom_text(data = cells, aes(x = -3, y = Inf, label = label), inherit.aes = FALSE,
              hjust = 0, vjust = 1.5, size = 3, colour = GRID_MUTED) +
    facet_grid(climate_third ~ third) +
    scale_colour_manual(values = SPLINE_CELL_COLOURS, name = NULL) +
    scale_fill_manual(values = SPLINE_CELL_COLOURS, name = NULL) +
    scale_linetype_manual(values = c("solid", "longdash"), name = NULL) +
    scale_x_continuous(breaks = -3:3) +
    labs(x = paste(if (v == "TM") "Temperature" else "Precipitation",
                   "deviation (horizon SD, demeaned)"),
         y = "Effect on growth of GDP per capita (pp)",
         title = paste(if (v == "TM") "Temperature" else "Precipitation",
                       "response by long-run climate and income, spline interactions"),
         subtitle = paste0(main$label, ", ", INCOME_FORM, ", ", INCOME_DEFINITION,
                           " deviations; rows: third of long-run climate, columns: third of ",
                           "long-run income;\neach panel at its units' mean climate and income; ",
                           "bands: 95% CI, clustered by country")) +
    theme_results() +
    theme(legend.position = "top", strip.text = element_text(face = "bold"))
  print(p)
}
```

## Sectors: interactions with climate and income, and splines

The sections above ask whether the climate gradient is one of income on GDP
per capita. The same question by sector: agriculture, industry and services
can respond to the climate and to income differently, and a gradient that is
one of income in one sector may be one of climate in another. The outcomes
are those of "Sector growth (World Bank)": the growth of GDP per capita and of
each sector's value added per head, on the rows of each World Bank panel with
the growth of all three sectors (identical rows for every outcome), with the
horizon deviations. Long-run income is the log mean GDP per capita of the
World Bank panel over its horizon, centred on these rows. Each outcome has
five models (summed over the arms a, with the controls and fixed effects):

```text
without income              dev_a x (c_a + b_a clim)
linear                      dev_a x (c_a + b_a clim + h_a inc)
spline climate              dev_a x (c_a + f_a(clim) + h_a inc)
spline income               dev_a x (c_a + b_a clim + g_a(inc))
spline climate and income   dev_a x (c_a + f_a(clim) + g_a(inc))
```

`f_a` and `g_a` are restricted cubic splines as in "Splines in climate and
income", with knots at the `r paste(100 * SPLINE_KNOT_PROBS, collapse = ", ")`th
percentiles of the units of each panel's sector rows.

1. World Bank x ERA5: the fit of each model, the verdict of the linear model
   against the one without income and of the splines against the linear
   model, the Wald tests of the non-linear terms of each variable in the
   climate and in income, and the joint tests of all the income terms and of
   all the climate terms;
2. the three climate datasets: income against no income, splines in both
   against linear, and the income and climate tests in each;
3. World Bank x ERA5, splines in both: the effects of a +/-3 SD year in each
   cell of units by third of long-run climate and third of long-run income
   (at the cell's mean), for every outcome;
4. figures: the effect of a +/-3 SD year on each outcome across the long-run
   climate at the average income, and across income at the average climate,
   linear and with splines in both (95% CI; ticks: the units).

```{r sector-income-splines, fig.width = 13, fig.height = 13}
SECTOR_SPLINE_SOURCES <- c("ERA5", "CRU TS", "UDelaware")
SECTOR_SPLINE_OUTCOMES <- SECTOR_SETS$growth
# Each World Bank panel: the rows of "Sector growth" (every sector's growth),
# the horizon deviations, long-run income, the knots of the climates and of
# income (quantiles of the units of these rows) and their non-linear terms; for
# each outcome, the model without income and the four versions of
# INCOME_SPLINE_MODELS.
sector_spline_runs <- lapply(SECTOR_SPLINE_SOURCES, function(source) {
  wb <- national_panels[[match(paste("WB x", source), panel_labels)]]
  d <- add_deviation_terms(wb$clean, DEFINITIONS[[INCOME_DEFINITION]]) %>%
    inner_join(select(wdi_growth, GID_0, year, all_of(SECTOR_COLUMNS)), by = c("GID_0", "year")) %>%
    filter(if_all(all_of(SECTOR_COLUMNS), is.finite))
  d <- add_income(wb, d)
  units <- distinct(d, GID_1, inc, inc_level, clim_TM, clim_RR)
  knots <- lapply(c(TM = "clim_TM", RR = "clim_RR", inc = "inc"), function(z) {
    stats::quantile(units[[z]], SPLINE_KNOT_PROBS, names = FALSE)
  })
  d <- add_spline_terms(d, knots[c("TM", "RR")])
  inc_nonlinear <- rcs_nonlinear(d$inc, knots$inc)
  for (j in seq_len(ncol(inc_nonlinear))) d[[paste0("inc_nl", j)]] <- inc_nonlinear[, j]
  fits <- lapply(SECTOR_SPLINE_OUTCOMES, function(y) {
    c(list("without income" = fit_model(form_terms(FORMS[[INCOME_FORM]]), d, outcome = y)),
      lapply(INCOME_SPLINE_MODELS, function(s) {
        fit_model(income_spline_terms(s[["climate"]], s[["income"]]), d, outcome = y)
      }))
  })
  stopifnot(length(unique(unlist(lapply(fits, function(f) vapply(f, stats::nobs, 0))))) == 1)
  list(source = source, data = d, units = units, knots = knots, fits = fits)
})
names(sector_spline_runs) <- SECTOR_SPLINE_SOURCES
sector_era5 <- sector_spline_runs$ERA5

# 1. Fit and tests, World Bank x ERA5.
sector_spline_tests <- function(run, outcome, k) {
  f <- run$fits[[outcome]]
  m <- f[[k]]
  base <- if (k == "linear") f[["without income"]] else f$linear
  added_p <- if (k != "without income") added_terms_p(m, base)
  tibble::tibble(
    climate = run$source, outcome = outcome, model = k,
    aic_vs_linear = round(stats::AIC(m) - stats::AIC(f$linear), 1),
    bic_vs_linear = round(stats::BIC(m) - stats::BIC(f$linear), 1),
    within_adj_r2_pct = round(100 * fixest::fitstat(m, "war2")[[1]], 3),
    verdict = if (is.null(added_p)) "" else fit_verdicts(m, base, nested_p = added_p),
    T_climate_nl_p = arm_terms_p(m, "TM", "clim_TM_nl[0-9]+"),
    P_climate_nl_p = arm_terms_p(m, "RR", "clim_RR_nl[0-9]+"),
    T_income_nl_p = arm_terms_p(m, "TM", "inc_nl[0-9]+"),
    P_income_nl_p = arm_terms_p(m, "RR", "inc_nl[0-9]+"),
    income_all_p = if (k == "without income") NA_real_ else wald_p(m, "inc"),
    climate_all_p = wald_p(m, "clim_")
  )
}
bind_rows(lapply(names(SECTOR_SPLINE_OUTCOMES), function(y) {
  bind_rows(lapply(names(sector_era5$fits[[y]]), function(k) sector_spline_tests(sector_era5, y, k)))
})) %>%
  select(-climate) %>%
  mutate(across(ends_with("_p"), ~ signif(.x, 2))) %>%
  knitr::kable(caption = paste0(
    "WB x ERA5, ", INCOME_FORM, ", ", INCOME_DEFINITION, " deviations, sector rows (",
    nrow(sector_era5$data), "): each outcome without income, with linear interactions in the ",
    "climate and income, and with restricted cubic splines in the climate and/or income; AIC and ",
    "BIC against the linear model, within adjusted R2 (%), the ", VERDICT_NOTE, " (linear: ",
    "against the model without income, nested: the income terms; splines: against the linear ",
    "model, nested: the non-linear terms); Wald tests (p) of the non-linear terms of each ",
    "variable in the climate and in income, and of all the income and all the climate terms"))

# 2. The three climate datasets: income, and splines in both.
bind_rows(lapply(sector_spline_runs, function(run) {
  bind_rows(lapply(names(SECTOR_SPLINE_OUTCOMES), function(y) {
    linear <- sector_spline_tests(run, y, "linear")
    splines <- sector_spline_tests(run, y, "spline climate and income")
    tibble::tibble(climate = run$source, outcome = y,
                   income_vs_without = linear$verdict,
                   linear_income_p = linear$income_all_p, linear_climate_p = linear$climate_all_p,
                   splines_vs_linear = splines$verdict,
                   splines_income_p = splines$income_all_p,
                   splines_climate_p = splines$climate_all_p)
  }))
})) %>%
  mutate(across(ends_with("_p"), ~ signif(.x, 2))) %>%
  knitr::kable(caption = paste0(
    "World Bank panels, sector rows: linear interactions in the climate and income against the ",
    "model without income, and splines in both against the linear interactions (", VERDICT_NOTE,
    "); joint Wald tests (p) of all the income and all the climate terms in each"))

# 3. The cells of climate and income, World Bank x ERA5, splines in both.
sector_cells <- bind_rows(lapply(c("TM", "RR"), function(v) {
  clim <- paste0("clim_", v)
  sector_era5$units %>%
    mutate(climate_third = factor(CLIMATE_THIRDS[[v]][dplyr::ntile(.data[[clim]], 3)],
                                  levels = CLIMATE_THIRDS[[v]]),
           third = factor(c("poorest third", "middle third", "richest third")[dplyr::ntile(inc, 3)],
                          levels = c("poorest third", "middle third", "richest third"))) %>%
    group_by(climate_third, third) %>%
    summarise(units = n(), climate = mean(.data[[clim]]), inc = mean(inc), .groups = "drop") %>%
    mutate(variable = v)
}))
bind_rows(lapply(seq_len(nrow(sector_cells)), function(i) {
  cell <- sector_cells[i, ]
  at <- tibble::tibble(clim = cell$climate, inc = cell$inc)
  cells <- unlist(lapply(names(SECTOR_SPLINE_OUTCOMES), function(y) {
    vapply(EFFECT_AT, function(x) {
      e <- income_spline_effects("spline climate and income", cell$variable, x, at,
                                 sector_era5$fits[[y]], sector_era5$knots)
      sprintf("%+.2f%s", 100 * e$estimate, stars(2 * stats::pnorm(-abs(e$estimate / e$std_error))))
    }, "")
  }))
  names(cells) <- as.vector(outer(sprintf("%+d SD", EFFECT_AT), names(SECTOR_SPLINE_OUTCOMES),
                                  function(x, y) paste(y, x)))
  tibble::tibble(variable = ifelse(cell$variable == "TM", "T", "P"),
                 climate = as.character(cell$climate_third), income = as.character(cell$third),
                 units = cell$units, !!!as.list(cells))
})) %>%
  knitr::kable(caption = paste(
    "WB x ERA5, splines in the climate and income: effect (pp of the outcome's growth) of a",
    "year at +/-3 SD in each cell of units (third of long-run climate x third of long-run income,",
    "at the cell's mean); *** p < 0.01, ** p < 0.05, * p < 0.1"))

# 4. Curves across the climate (at the average income) and across income (at
# the average climate of the rows), World Bank x ERA5.
sector_mean_inc_level <- mean(sector_era5$data$inc_level)
sector_spline_curves <- bind_rows(lapply(seq_len(nrow(INCOME_SPLINE_EVENTS)), function(i) {
  e <- INCOME_SPLINE_EVENTS[i, ]
  unit_climate <- sector_era5$units[[paste0("clim_", e$variable)]]
  along <- list(
    climate = tibble::tibble(clim = seq(min(unit_climate), max(unit_climate), length.out = 80),
                             inc = 0),
    income = tibble::tibble(clim = mean(sector_era5$data[[paste0("clim_", e$variable)]]),
                            inc = seq(min(sector_era5$units$inc), max(sector_era5$units$inc),
                                      length.out = 80))
  )
  bind_rows(lapply(names(along), function(a) {
    bind_rows(lapply(names(SECTOR_SPLINE_OUTCOMES), function(y) {
      bind_rows(lapply(INCOME_SPLINE_COMPARED, function(k) {
        income_spline_effects(k, e$variable, e$deviation, along[[a]], sector_era5$fits[[y]],
                              sector_era5$knots) %>%
          mutate(interaction = ifelse(k == "linear", "linear", "splines"),
                 position = if (a == "climate") along[[a]]$clim else along[[a]]$inc + sector_mean_inc_level)
      })) %>%
        mutate(outcome = y)
    })) %>%
      mutate(event = e$event, along = a)
  }))
})) %>%
  mutate(outcome = factor(outcome, levels = names(SECTOR_SPLINE_OUTCOMES)),
         event = factor(event, levels = INCOME_SPLINE_EVENTS$event))
sector_spline_rug <- bind_rows(lapply(seq_len(nrow(INCOME_SPLINE_EVENTS)), function(i) {
  e <- INCOME_SPLINE_EVENTS[i, ]
  bind_rows(
    tibble::tibble(along = "climate", position = sector_era5$units[[paste0("clim_", e$variable)]]),
    tibble::tibble(along = "income", position = sector_era5$units$inc + sector_mean_inc_level)
  ) %>%
    mutate(event = e$event)
})) %>%
  mutate(event = factor(event, levels = INCOME_SPLINE_EVENTS$event))
for (a in c("climate", "income")) {
  p <- ggplot(filter(sector_spline_curves, along == a),
              aes(position, 100 * estimate, colour = interaction, fill = interaction)) +
    geom_hline(yintercept = 0, colour = GRID_MUTED, linewidth = 0.3) +
    geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = 100 * conf_low, ymax = 100 * conf_high), alpha = 0.12, colour = NA) +
    geom_line(linewidth = 0.8) +
    geom_rug(data = tidyr::crossing(filter(sector_spline_rug, along == a),
                                    outcome = factor(names(SECTOR_SPLINE_OUTCOMES),
                                                     levels = names(SECTOR_SPLINE_OUTCOMES))),
             aes(x = position), inherit.aes = FALSE, sides = "b", alpha = 0.4, colour = GRID_MUTED) +
    facet_wrap(~ event + outcome, ncol = 4, scales = "free",
               labeller = labeller(.multi_line = FALSE)) +
    scale_colour_manual(values = grid_colours(c("linear", "splines")), name = "Interactions") +
    scale_fill_manual(values = grid_colours(c("linear", "splines")), guide = "none") +
    labs(x = if (a == "climate") "Long-run climate (C, or m a year)" else
           "Log long-run GDP per capita (horizon mean)",
         y = "Effect on the outcome's growth that year (pp)",
         title = paste0("Effect of a +/-3 SD year on each sector across ",
                        if (a == "climate") "the long-run climate" else "long-run income",
                        ": linear or spline interactions"),
         subtitle = wrap_text(paste0(
           "WB x ERA5, ", INCOME_FORM, ", ", INCOME_DEFINITION, " deviations, with income, ",
           "identical rows (every sector's growth); columns: growth of GDP per capita and of each ",
           "sector's value added per head; ",
           if (a == "climate") "at the average income" else "at the average climate of the rows",
           "; splines in both the climate and income; bands: 95% CI clustered by country; ",
           "ticks: the units."), 150)) +
    theme_results()
  print(p)
}
```

## Income or the agricultural share

Agriculture is the sector that responds to dry years at every income, and
poor countries have large agricultural shares, so long-run income in the
interactions may stand for the share of agriculture in the economy. Here the
deviation terms are also interacted with the agricultural share:

```text
growth = sum over arms a of  dev_a x (c_a + b_a clim + h_a inc + k_a agr)  + controls + FE
agr    = agricultural share: the World Bank's agriculture value added over that of
         the three sectors (constant 2015 US$), centred on the rows
```

The share comes in two versions:

- the long-run share (the main one): each country's mean of the lagged share
  over the horizon years with data, like long-run income. It drops only the
  countries with no sector data, but for about half of the countries the
  data start after 1990, so their long-run share is that of a later period
  (agricultural shares fall over time);
- the lagged share of the year (the share of the year before), on the rows
  that have it: no mismatch of periods, but about 28% of the rows are lost,
  mostly early years.

On the rows of each national panel (its GDP outcome, exclusions, controls and
fixed effects) with the share, six models, linear or with splines (as in
"Splines in climate and income", knots at the
`r paste(100 * SPLINE_KNOT_PROBS, collapse = ", ")`th percentiles of the units;
of the rows for the lagged share):

```text
income                          climate + income                 (linear)
share                           climate + share                  (linear)
income and share                climate + income + share         (linear)
splines: income                 splines in climate and income
splines: income, share linear   splines in climate and income, share linear
splines: income and share       splines in climate, income and share
```

1. the rows and countries kept with each version of the share;
2. the share and income across the units: they are closely correlated, so the
   two are hard to separate;
3. PWT x ERA5 and WB x ERA5, both versions of the share: the fit of each model,
   its verdict (share against income: non-nested; the others: the joint test of
   the added terms), and the joint tests of the income terms and of the share
   terms, all and by variable;
4. every national panel, long-run share: the model with both against income
   only, and the tests of income and of the share by variable;
5. PWT x ERA5: each event in the poorest and in the richest third of the units
   of its climate third, with income only and with both; with both, also with
   the income of one third and the share of the other. These swapped
   combinations lie outside the data (no rich country has the share of a poor
   one): they show which of the two terms carries the gradient, not the response
   of a country;
6. figure, PWT x ERA5, splines: each event across income with the share at its
   mean (and in the model without the share), and across the share with
   income at its mean.

**Investment and lagged income.** On the PWT panels, the same models are also
estimated with four more controls: investment, the growth of the capital
stock per head (log difference of PWT's `rnna` over population) in t and t - 1,
and log GDP per capita in t - 1 and t - 2 (matched on calendar year; the rows
without them are dropped). The capital stock is PWT's, so the World Bank panels
are left out. Investment in t can respond to the weather of the year: with it
held fixed, the weather effects are those net of the investment channel. To
separate the controls from the change of rows, the models without the
controls are also estimated on the same rows:

7. the rows and countries kept with the controls;
8. the coefficients of the controls (model with income and the share, linear);
9. on the controls' rows, without and with the controls: the joint tests of the
   terms of T and of P, of the income and the share terms of each variable, and
   of the climate terms;
10. the poor against rich table of 5 on the controls' rows, without and with the
    controls.

```{r agricultural-share, fig.width = 10, fig.height = 11}
# The models: the interactions of every arm with the long-run climate (linear
# or spline), income and the agricultural share (none, linear or spline), and
# the model each is compared with (nested, except share against income).
AGR_MODELS <- tibble::tribble(
  ~model,                            ~clim,    ~inc,     ~agr,     ~against,
  "income",                          "linear", "linear", "none",   NA,
  "share",                           "linear", "none",   "linear", "income",
  "income and share",                "linear", "linear", "linear", "income",
  "splines: income",                 "spline", "spline", "none",   "income",
  "splines: income, share linear",   "spline", "spline", "linear", "splines: income",
  "splines: income and share",       "spline", "spline", "spline", "splines: income"
)
AGR_SHARES <- c("long-run", "lagged")
# Investment and lagged income (PWT panels only: the capital stock is PWT's):
# the growth of the capital stock per head (log difference of rnna / pop, PWT
# 11.0) in t and t - 1, and log GDP per capita in t - 1 and t - 2; matched on
# calendar year (a gap gives NA).
AGR_GROWTH_CONTROLS <- c("dlk", "dlk_lag1", "lgdp_lag1", "lgdp_lag2")
pwt_growth_controls <- load_econ_panel("PWT110") %>%
  group_by(GID_1) %>%
  arrange(year, .by_group = TRUE) %>%
  mutate(lk = log(k_pc_usd),
         dlk = lk - lag_by_year(lk, year),
         dlk_lag1 = lag_by_year(dlk, year),
         lgdp_lag1 = lag_by_year(lgrp_pc_usd, year),
         lgdp_lag2 = lag_by_year(lgrp_pc_usd, year, 2)) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  select(GID_1, year, all_of(AGR_GROWTH_CONTROLS))
# Rows of panel `p` with the horizon deviations, long-run income and the
# agricultural share: the long-run share (mean of the lagged share over the
# horizon years with data; the countries with none are dropped) or the lagged
# share of the year (the rows without it are dropped); with `control_rows`,
# only the rows with every AGR_GROWTH_CONTROLS; income and the share centred on
# these rows; the knots (quantiles of the units, of the rows for the lagged
# share) and the non-linear terms clim_<v>_nl<j>, inc_nl<j>, agr_nl<j>.
agr_panel_data <- function(p, share, control_rows = FALSE) {
  d <- add_deviation_terms(p$clean, DEFINITIONS[[INCOME_DEFINITION]])
  if (control_rows) {
    d <- inner_join(d, pwt_growth_controls, by = c("GID_1", "year")) %>%
      filter(if_all(all_of(AGR_GROWTH_CONTROLS), is.finite))
  }
  if (share == "long-run") {
    s <- wdi_growth %>%
      filter(year >= p$start_year, year <= p$end_year, is.finite(s_agr)) %>%
      group_by(GID_0) %>%
      summarise(agr_level = mean(s_agr), .groups = "drop")
    d <- inner_join(d, s, by = "GID_0")
  } else {
    d <- inner_join(d, select(filter(wdi_growth, is.finite(s_agr)), GID_0, year, agr_level = s_agr),
                    by = c("GID_0", "year"))
  }
  d <- add_income(p, d)
  d$agr <- d$agr_level - mean(d$agr_level)
  units <- d %>%
    group_by(GID_1) %>%
    summarise(across(c(clim_TM, clim_RR, inc, inc_level), first), agr = mean(agr), .groups = "drop")
  quantiles <- function(x) stats::quantile(x, SPLINE_KNOT_PROBS, names = FALSE)
  knots <- c(lapply(c(TM = "clim_TM", RR = "clim_RR", inc = "inc"), function(z) quantiles(units[[z]])),
             list(agr = quantiles(if (share == "long-run") units$agr else d$agr)))
  d <- add_spline_terms(d, knots[c("TM", "RR")])
  for (z in c("inc", "agr")) {
    nl <- rcs_nonlinear(d[[z]], knots[[z]])
    for (j in seq_len(ncol(nl))) d[[paste0(z, "_nl", j)]] <- nl[, j]
  }
  list(data = d, units = units, knots = knots)
}
# The terms of model `spec` (a row of AGR_MODELS).
agr_terms <- function(spec) {
  nl <- seq_len(SPLINE_NONLINEAR)
  extra <- unlist(lapply(c("TM", "RR"), function(v) {
    arms <- paste0("dev", v, FORMS[[INCOME_FORM]][[v]])
    c(if (spec$clim == "spline") as.vector(outer(arms, paste0(":clim_", v, "_nl", nl), paste0)),
      unlist(lapply(c("inc", "agr"), function(z) {
        c(if (spec[[z]] != "none") paste0(arms, ":", z),
          if (spec[[z]] == "spline") as.vector(outer(arms, paste0(":", z, "_nl", nl), paste0)))
      })))
  }))
  c(form_terms(FORMS[[INCOME_FORM]]), extra)
}
# Weights of a deviation x of variable v in model m (spec) at long-run climate
# `clim`, centred income `inc` and centred share `agr`.
agr_weights <- function(m, spec, v, x, clim, inc, agr, knots) {
  mods <- stats::setNames(list(clim), paste0("clim_", v))
  spline_mods <- function(value, k, prefix) {
    nl <- rcs_nonlinear(value, k)
    stats::setNames(as.list(nl[1, ]), paste0(prefix, "_nl", seq_len(ncol(nl))))
  }
  if (spec$clim == "spline") mods <- c(mods, spline_mods(clim, knots[[v]], paste0("clim_", v)))
  values <- list(inc = inc, agr = agr)
  for (z in c("inc", "agr")) {
    if (spec[[z]] != "none") mods[[z]] <- values[[z]]
    if (spec[[z]] == "spline") mods <- c(mods, spline_mods(values[[z]], knots[[z]], z))
  }
  deviation_weights(names(stats::coef(m)), FORMS[[INCOME_FORM]][[v]], v, x, mods)
}
# Effects (linear_combination) of x of variable v in model k of run r at each
# row of `at` (columns clim, inc, agr).
agr_effects <- function(r, k, v, x, at) {
  m <- r$fits[[k]]
  spec <- AGR_MODELS[AGR_MODELS$model == k, ]
  G <- t(vapply(seq_len(nrow(at)), function(i) {
    agr_weights(m, spec, v, x, at$clim[i], at$inc[i], at$agr[i], r$knots)
  }, numeric(length(stats::coef(m)))))
  colnames(G) <- names(stats::coef(m))
  linear_combination(m, G)
}
# The runs: every national panel with the long-run share, PWT x ERA5 and WB x
# ERA5 with the lagged share; and the PWT panels on the rows with investment
# and lagged income, with them as controls ("+ controls") and without them
# ("controls' rows").
AGR_PWT <- c("PWT x ERA5", "PWT x CRU TS", "PWT x UDelaware")
agr_run <- function(label, share, control_rows = FALSE, controls = FALSE) {
  list(panel = national_panels[[match(label, panel_labels)]], share = share,
       control_rows = control_rows, controls = controls)
}
agr_runs <- c(
  lapply(stats::setNames(panel_labels, panel_labels), agr_run, share = "long-run"),
  lapply(stats::setNames(c("PWT x ERA5", "WB x ERA5"), paste(c("PWT x ERA5", "WB x ERA5"), "lagged share")),
         agr_run, share = "lagged"),
  lapply(stats::setNames(AGR_PWT, paste(AGR_PWT, "+ controls")), agr_run, share = "long-run",
         control_rows = TRUE, controls = TRUE),
  lapply(stats::setNames(AGR_PWT, paste(AGR_PWT, "controls' rows")), agr_run, share = "long-run",
         control_rows = TRUE),
  list("PWT x ERA5 lagged share + controls" = agr_run("PWT x ERA5", "lagged", TRUE, TRUE),
       "PWT x ERA5 lagged share controls' rows" = agr_run("PWT x ERA5", "lagged", TRUE))
)
agr_runs <- lapply(agr_runs, function(r) {
  s <- agr_panel_data(r$panel, r$share, r$control_rows)
  fits <- lapply(stats::setNames(seq_len(nrow(AGR_MODELS)), AGR_MODELS$model), function(i) {
    fit_model(c(agr_terms(AGR_MODELS[i, ]), if (r$controls) AGR_GROWTH_CONTROLS), s$data)
  })
  stopifnot(length(unique(vapply(fits, stats::nobs, 0))) == 1)
  c(r, s, list(fits = fits))
})

# 1. Rows kept.
bind_rows(lapply(national_panels, function(p) {
  long_run <- agr_runs[[p$label]]$data
  lagged <- inner_join(p$clean, filter(wdi_growth, is.finite(s_agr)), by = c("GID_0", "year"))
  tibble::tibble(panel = p$label, rows = nrow(p$clean), countries = n_distinct(p$clean$GID_0),
                 long_run_rows = nrow(long_run), long_run_countries = n_distinct(long_run$GID_0),
                 lagged_rows = nrow(lagged), lagged_countries = n_distinct(lagged$GID_0),
                 lagged_first_year_after_1990 = sum(tapply(lagged$year, lagged$GID_0, min) > 1990),

})) %>%
  knitr::kable(caption = paste(
    "National panels: rows and countries in the panel (after the exclusions), with the long-run",
    "agricultural share (a share in any horizon year) and with the lagged share of the year; the",

# 2. The share, income and climate across the units (long-run share).
main_agr <- agr_runs[["PWT x ERA5"]]
main_agr$units %>%
  mutate(third = factor(c("poorest third", "middle third", "richest third")[dplyr::ntile(inc_level, 3)],
                        levels = c("poorest third", "middle third", "richest third")),
         agr_level = agr + mean(main_agr$data$agr_level)) %>%
  group_by(third) %>%
  summarise(units = n(), gdp_pc = round(exp(mean(inc_level))),
            mean_share_pct = round(100 * mean(agr_level), 1),
            share_range_pct = sprintf("%.1f-%.1f", 100 * min(agr_level), 100 * max(agr_level)),
            .groups = "drop") %>%
  knitr::kable(caption = sprintf(paste(
    "PWT x ERA5, units by third of long-run income: GDP per capita (geometric mean) and long-run",
    "agricultural share (%% of the value added of the three sectors); across the units,",
    "correlation of the share with log income %.2f, with mean T %.2f, with mean P %.2f"),
    stats::cor(main_agr$units$agr, main_agr$units$inc),
    stats::cor(main_agr$units$agr, main_agr$units$clim_TM),
    stats::cor(main_agr$units$agr, main_agr$units$clim_RR)))

# 3. Fit and tests.
agr_tests <- function(r, k) {
  m <- r$fits[[k]]
  spec <- AGR_MODELS[AGR_MODELS$model == k, ]
  base <- if (!is.na(spec$against)) r$fits[[spec$against]]
  nested_p <- if (!is.na(spec$against) && k != "share") added_terms_p(m, base)
  tibble::tibble(
    model = k,
    aic_vs_income = round(stats::AIC(m) - stats::AIC(r$fits$income), 1),
    bic_vs_income = round(stats::BIC(m) - stats::BIC(r$fits$income), 1),
    within_adj_r2_pct = round(100 * fixest::fitstat(m, "war2")[[1]], 3),
    against = ifelse(is.na(spec$against), "", spec$against),
    verdict = if (is.null(base)) "" else fit_verdicts(m, base, nested_p = nested_p),
    income_all_p = if (spec$inc == "none") NA_real_ else wald_p(m, "inc"),
    income_T_p = arm_terms_p(m, "TM", "inc"), income_P_p = arm_terms_p(m, "RR", "inc"),
    share_all_p = if (spec$agr == "none") NA_real_ else wald_p(m, "agr"),
    share_T_p = arm_terms_p(m, "TM", "agr"), share_P_p = arm_terms_p(m, "RR", "agr"),
    climate_all_p = wald_p(m, "clim_")
  )
}
AGR_DETAIL <- c("PWT x ERA5", "PWT x ERA5 lagged share", "WB x ERA5", "WB x ERA5 lagged share")
for (k in AGR_DETAIL) {
  r <- agr_runs[[k]]
  print(bind_rows(lapply(AGR_MODELS$model, function(m) agr_tests(r, m))) %>%

    knitr::kable(caption = paste0(
      k, " (", if (r$share == "long-run") "long-run" else "lagged", " agricultural share; ",
      nrow(r$data), " rows), ", INCOME_FORM, ", ", INCOME_DEFINITION, " deviations: AIC and BIC ",
      "against the model with income, within adjusted R2 (%), the ", VERDICT_NOTE, " against ",
      "the model in `against` (nested: the joint test of the added terms; share against income: ",
      "non-nested), and the joint Wald tests (p) of the income terms and of the share terms (all, ",
      "of T, of P) and of all the climate terms")))
}

                   share_vs_without = t$verdict, income_T_p = t$income_T_p,
                   income_P_p = t$income_P_p, share_T_p = t$share_T_p, share_P_p = t$share_P_p,
                   climate_p = t$climate_all_p)
  }))
})) %>%

    "National panels, long-run agricultural share: the model with income and the share against ",

# 5. Poor against rich: each event at the mean climate of its climate third,
# at the mean income and share of the poorest and of the richest third of
# those units, and with the income of one and the share of the other.
AGR_EVENT_THIRDS <- c("T +3 SD" = 3, "T -3 SD" = 1, "P -3 SD" = 1, "P +3 SD" = 3)
agr_swap_table <- function(r) {
  bind_rows(lapply(seq_len(nrow(INCOME_SPLINE_EVENTS)), function(i) {
    e <- INCOME_SPLINE_EVENTS[i, ]
    clim <- paste0("clim_", e$variable)
    u <- r$units %>%
      filter(dplyr::ntile(.data[[clim]], 3) == AGR_EVENT_THIRDS[[e$event]]) %>%
      mutate(third = dplyr::ntile(inc, 3))
    poor <- filter(u, third == 1)
    rich <- filter(u, third == 3)
    at <- tibble::tibble(
      cell = c("poor", "rich", "poor income, rich share", "rich income, poor share"),
      clim = mean(u[[clim]]), inc = c(mean(poor$inc), mean(rich$inc), mean(poor$inc), mean(rich$inc)),
      agr = c(mean(poor$agr), mean(rich$agr), mean(rich$agr), mean(poor$agr))
    )
    cell <- function(k, rows) {
      ef <- agr_effects(r, k, e$variable, e$deviation, at[rows, ])
      sprintf("%+.2f%s", 100 * ef$estimate, stars(2 * stats::pnorm(-abs(ef$estimate / ef$std_error))))
    }
    bind_rows(lapply(c(linear = "linear", splines = "splines"), function(s) {
      without <- if (s == "linear") "income" else "splines: income"
      with <- if (s == "linear") "income and share" else "splines: income and share"
      w <- cell(with, 1:4)
      tibble::tibble(event = e$event, interactions = s,
                     climate = sprintf(if (e$variable == "TM") "%.1f C" else "%.2f m", mean(u[[clim]])),
                     share_poor_rich_pct = sprintf("%.0f / %.0f",
                                                   100 * (mean(poor$agr) + mean(r$data$agr_level)),
                                                   100 * (mean(rich$agr) + mean(r$data$agr_level))),
                     "income only: poor" = cell(without, 1), "income only: rich" = cell(without, 2),
                     "with share: poor" = w[1], "with share: rich" = w[2],
                     "with share: poor income, rich share" = w[3],
                     "with share: rich income, poor share" = w[4])
    }))
  }))
}
agr_swap_table(main_agr) %>%
  knitr::kable(caption = paste(

    "where the income of one third is also combined with the share of the other; *** p < 0.01,",

agr_curves <- bind_rows(lapply(seq_len(nrow(INCOME_SPLINE_EVENTS)), function(i) {

  share_grid <- tibble::tibble(clim = clim, inc = 0, agr = grid(main_agr$units$agr))

    agr_effects(main_agr, "splines: income", e$variable, e$deviation, income_grid) %>%
      mutate(model = "income only", along = "across income",

      mutate(model = "income and share", along = "across income",
             position = income_grid$inc + mean(main_agr$data$inc_level)),
    agr_effects(main_agr, "splines: income and share", e$variable, e$deviation, share_grid) %>%
      mutate(model = "income and share", along = "across the agricultural share",
             position = 100 * (share_grid$agr + mean(main_agr$data$agr_level)))
  ) %>%
    mutate(event = e$event)
})) %>%
  mutate(event = factor(event, levels = INCOME_SPLINE_EVENTS$event),
         model = factor(model, levels = c("income only", "income and share")))
agr_rug <- tidyr::crossing(
  event = factor(INCOME_SPLINE_EVENTS$event, levels = INCOME_SPLINE_EVENTS$event),
  bind_rows(tibble::tibble(along = "across income",
                           position = main_agr$units$inc + mean(main_agr$data$inc_level)),
            tibble::tibble(along = "across the agricultural share",
                           position = 100 * (main_agr$units$agr + mean(main_agr$data$agr_level))))
)
ggplot(agr_curves, aes(position, 100 * estimate, colour = model, fill = model)) +

       subtitle = wrap_text(paste0(
```

# Extrapolating across climates: country responses around the climate gradient

The confidence intervals of the effects above are the uncertainty of the
climate gradient `c_a + b_a clim`, the mean response of the countries at a
climate. They assume that every country at that climate responds as the
gradient says. A country moved to another climate (India at the climate of
Italy) has a response of its own as well, which the gradient does not carry
over; and where few countries have a climate, the gradient rests on those few.

To measure that, the response of each country is estimated on its own, and the
country responses are regressed on climate allowing for a spread around the
gradient (a random-effects meta-regression):

```text
step 1: growth = sum over arms a of  dev_a x beta_a(i)  + controls + FE
        (one coefficient per country and arm, horizon deviations, the arms of
        the preferred form; heteroskedasticity-robust variances v_a(i), since a
        coefficient of a single country cannot be clustered by country)
step 2: beta_a(i) = c_a + b_a clim(i) + u_a(i),   u_a(i) ~ N(0, tau_a^2),
        estimated by REML with sampling variances v_a(i) (metafor::rma)
```

`tau_a` is the spread of the true country responses around the gradient that
the long-run climate does not explain (I2: the share of the variance of the
country estimates that it accounts for; the rest is sampling noise). A
confidence interval of the gradient uses only the uncertainty of `c_a + b_a
clim`; a prediction interval adds `tau_a^2`, and is the interval for the
response of a country at that climate. Each country-arm enters the
meta-regression if the arm is non-zero in at least `MIN_ARM_YEARS` of its
years (a coefficient from a handful of years has an unreliable robust
variance). On `r main$label`:

1. each arm: the gradient of the pooled model (the preferred form, clustered
   errors) and of the meta-regression, `tau`, I2 and the test that the
   country responses have no spread beyond sampling noise;
2. the effects of a +/-3 SD year at each long-run climate: the pooled model's
   CI, the meta-regression's CI and its prediction interval, and how much
   wider the prediction interval is than the pooled CI;
3. figure: the country estimates, the gradient, its CI and the prediction
   interval, over the range of the countries' climates;
4. India at the climate of Italy: India's and Italy's own responses (the
   gradient at their climate plus their own deviation from it, shrunk), the
   gradient at Italy's climate, and India at Italy's climate (the gradient
   there plus India's own deviation), for the temperature arms.

```{r country-responses}
MIN_ARM_YEARS <- 10
EVENT_SD <- max(EFFECT_AT)
# The arms of `form`: term, variable, the deviation of the +/-EVENT_SD event and
# its label.
form_arms <- function(form) {
  bind_rows(lapply(c("TM", "RR"), function(v) {
    tibble::tibble(variable = v, suffix = form[[v]], term = paste0("dev", v, form[[v]]),
                   positive = grepl("_pos", form[[v]]))
  })) %>%
    mutate(x = ifelse(positive, EVENT_SD, -EVENT_SD),
           value = mapply(term_value, suffix, x),
           label = paste0(ifelse(variable == "TM", "T, ", "P, "),
                          ifelse(variable == "TM", ifelse(positive, "hot", "cold"),
                                 ifelse(positive, "wet", "dry")),
                          sprintf(" year (%+d SD)", x)))
}
response_arms <- form_arms(FORMS[[PREFERRED_FORM]])
response_data <- add_deviation_terms(main$clean, DEFINITIONS[["Horizon"]])
pooled_model <- fit_model(form_terms(FORMS[[PREFERRED_FORM]]), response_data)

# Step 1: one coefficient per country and arm.
country_model <- fit_model(c(sprintf("i(GID_0, %s)", response_arms$term), CONTROLS), response_data)
country_V <- stats::vcov(country_model, vcov = "hetero")
arm_years <- response_data %>%
  group_by(GID_0) %>%
  summarise(across(all_of(response_arms$term), ~ sum(.x != 0)), .groups = "drop") %>%
  tidyr::pivot_longer(-GID_0, names_to = "term", values_to = "arm_years")
country_climate <- distinct(response_data, GID_0, clim_TM, clim_RR)
stopifnot(!anyDuplicated(country_climate$GID_0))
country_slopes <- tibble::tibble(name = grep("^GID_0::", names(stats::coef(country_model)), value = TRUE)) %>%
  mutate(GID_0 = sub("^GID_0::([^:]+):.*$", "\\1", name),
         term = sub("^GID_0::[^:]+:", "", name),
         estimate = stats::coef(country_model)[name],
         variance = diag(country_V)[name]) %>%
  left_join(arm_years, by = c("GID_0", "term")) %>%
  left_join(country_climate, by = "GID_0") %>%
  left_join(select(response_arms, term, variable), by = "term") %>%
  mutate(climate = ifelse(variable == "TM", clim_TM, clim_RR)) %>%
  filter(arm_years >= MIN_ARM_YEARS, is.finite(variance), variance > 0)

# Step 2: the meta-regression of each arm.
meta_fits <- lapply(stats::setNames(response_arms$term, response_arms$term), function(a) {
  s <- filter(country_slopes, term == a)
  metafor::rma(yi = estimate, vi = variance, mods = ~climate, data = s, slab = GID_0,
               method = "REML")
})

# 1. The gradients.
coef_cell <- function(e, se) sprintf("%.3g (%.2g)", e, se)
pooled_ct <- fixest::coeftable(pooled_model)
bind_rows(lapply(seq_len(nrow(response_arms)), function(i) {
  a <- response_arms$term[i]
  r <- meta_fits[[a]]
  inter <- interaction_name(a, paste0("clim_", response_arms$variable[i]), rownames(pooled_ct))
  tibble::tibble(
    arm = response_arms$label[i], countries = r$k,
    pooled_c = coef_cell(pooled_ct[a, 1], pooled_ct[a, 2]),
    pooled_b = coef_cell(pooled_ct[inter, 1], pooled_ct[inter, 2]),
    meta_c = coef_cell(r$beta[1], r$se[1]), meta_b = coef_cell(r$beta[2], r$se[2]),
    tau = signif(sqrt(r$tau2), 2), I2_pct = round(r$I2, 1), no_spread_p = signif(r$QEp, 2)
  )
})) %>%
  knitr::kable(caption = paste(
    paste0(main$label, ", ", PREFERRED_FORM, ","), "horizon deviations: each arm's gradient c + b clim",
    "(coefficient per SD, or SD^2 for a quadratic arm; clim in C or m), pooled (clustered SE) and",
    "from the meta-regression of the country coefficients (SE); tau, the SD of the country",
    "responses around the gradient; I2 (%); no_spread_p: the test that tau = 0"))

# 2. Effects at each climate: pooled CI, meta CI and prediction interval (pp).
pp_interval <- function(e, lo, hi) sprintf("%+.2f [%+.2f, %+.2f]", 100 * e, 100 * lo, 100 * hi)
bind_rows(lapply(seq_len(nrow(response_arms)), function(i) {
  ai <- response_arms[i, ]
  terms <- names(stats::coef(pooled_model))
  clim <- EVAL_CLIMATE[[ai$variable]]
  G <- t(vapply(clim, function(m) {
    w <- stats::setNames(numeric(length(terms)), terms)
    w[[ai$term]] <- ai$value
    w[[interaction_name(ai$term, paste0("clim_", ai$variable), terms)]] <- ai$value * m
    w
  }, numeric(length(terms))))
  colnames(G) <- terms
  pooled <- linear_combination(pooled_model, G)
  p <- stats::predict(meta_fits[[ai$term]], newmods = clim)
  tibble::tibble(
    arm = ai$label, climate = EVAL_LABELS[[ai$variable]],
    pooled_ci = pp_interval(pooled$estimate, pooled$conf_low, pooled$conf_high),
    meta_ci = pp_interval(ai$value * p$pred, ai$value * p$ci.lb, ai$value * p$ci.ub),
    meta_prediction = pp_interval(ai$value * p$pred, ai$value * p$pi.lb, ai$value * p$pi.ub),
    prediction_vs_pooled = round(ai$value * (p$pi.ub - p$pi.lb) /
                                   (pooled$conf_high - pooled$conf_low), 1)
  )
})) %>%
  knitr::kable(caption = paste(
    paste0(main$label, ":"), "effect (pp) of a year at +/-3 SD at each long-run climate: the pooled model",
    "(95% CI), the meta-regression (95% CI) and its 95% prediction interval for a country at that",
    "climate; prediction_vs_pooled: the width of the prediction interval over that of the pooled CI"))
```

```{r country-responses-figure, fig.width = 10, fig.height = 7}
# 3. The country estimates (pp of the event; larger points: more precise),
# the gradient, its 95% CI and the 95% prediction interval.
response_curves <- bind_rows(lapply(seq_len(nrow(response_arms)), function(i) {
  ai <- response_arms[i, ]
  s <- filter(country_slopes, term == ai$term)
  grid <- seq(min(s$climate), max(s$climate), length.out = 100)
  p <- stats::predict(meta_fits[[ai$term]], newmods = grid)
  tibble::tibble(arm = ai$label, climate = grid, estimate = 100 * ai$value * p$pred,
                 ci_low = 100 * ai$value * p$ci.lb, ci_high = 100 * ai$value * p$ci.ub,
                 pi_low = 100 * ai$value * p$pi.lb, pi_high = 100 * ai$value * p$pi.ub)
}))
response_points <- country_slopes %>%
  left_join(select(response_arms, term, label, value), by = "term") %>%
  transmute(arm = label, climate, estimate = 100 * value * estimate,
            precision = 1 / sqrt(variance * value^2))
# The vertical range: the prediction interval, with some room; the points
# beyond it are not shown.
response_limits <- response_curves %>%
  group_by(arm) %>%
  summarise(low = min(pi_low, pi_high), high = max(pi_low, pi_high), .groups = "drop") %>%
  mutate(pad = 0.25 * (high - low), low = low - pad, high = high + pad)
response_points <- response_points %>%
  left_join(response_limits, by = "arm") %>%
  mutate(shown = estimate >= low & estimate <= high)
arm_order <- function(d) mutate(d, arm = factor(arm, levels = response_arms$label))
response_curves <- arm_order(response_curves)
response_points <- arm_order(response_points)
response_limits <- arm_order(response_limits)
ggplot(response_curves, aes(climate)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, colour = "grey55", linewidth = 0.4) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = pmin(pi_low, pi_high), ymax = pmax(pi_low, pi_high)),
              fill = "#2a78d6", alpha = 0.12) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = pmin(ci_low, ci_high), ymax = pmax(ci_low, ci_high)),
              fill = "#2a78d6", alpha = 0.3) +
  geom_point(data = filter(response_points, shown), aes(y = estimate, size = precision),
             colour = "grey35", alpha = 0.45, stroke = 0) +
  geom_line(aes(y = estimate), colour = "#2a78d6", linewidth = 0.8) +
  geom_blank(data = response_limits, aes(x = NULL, y = low), inherit.aes = FALSE) +
  geom_blank(data = response_limits, aes(x = NULL, y = high), inherit.aes = FALSE) +
  facet_wrap(~arm, scales = "free") +
  scale_size_area(max_size = 3, guide = "none") +
  labs(x = "Long-run climate of the country (horizon mean; C, or m a year)",
       y = "Effect on growth (pp)",
       title = "Country responses around the climate gradient",
       subtitle = paste0(main$label, ", ", PREFERRED_FORM, ", horizon deviations.\nLine: ",
                         "gradient; dark band: its 95% CI; light band: 95% prediction interval ",
                         "for a country at that climate.\nPoints: country estimates (larger: more ",
                         "precise); beyond the vertical range, not shown: ",
                         sum(!response_points$shown), " of ", nrow(response_points), ".")) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 11) +
  theme(panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
        strip.text = element_text(face = "bold", hjust = 0))
```
