```{r country-responses-move}
# 4. India at the climate of Italy. A country's own response: the gradient at
# its climate plus its estimated deviation u (the BLUP); moved, the gradient at
# the other climate plus the same u (SE: the two variances, their covariance
# left out).
MOVES <- tibble::tibble(from = "IND", to = "ITA")
# A metafor list of predictions as a data frame with the countries as row names.
by_country <- function(x, r) {
  d <- as.data.frame(unclass(x)[c("pred", "se", "pi.lb", "pi.ub")])
  rownames(d) <- as.character(r$slab[r$not.na])
  d
}
bind_rows(lapply(seq_len(nrow(MOVES)), function(j) {
  from <- MOVES$from[j]
  to <- MOVES$to[j]
  bind_rows(lapply(which(response_arms$variable == "TM"), function(i) {
    ai <- response_arms[i, ]
    r <- meta_fits[[ai$term]]
    u <- by_country(metafor::ranef(r), r)
    own <- by_country(metafor::blup(r), r)
    stopifnot(all(c(from, to) %in% rownames(u)))
    clim_to <- country_climate$clim_TM[country_climate$GID_0 == to]
    at_to <- stats::predict(r, newmods = clim_to)
    moved <- at_to$pred + u[from, "pred"]
    moved_se <- sqrt(at_to$se^2 + u[from, "se"]^2)
    k <- ai$value  # pp_interval() converts to pp
    tibble::tibble(
      arm = ai$label,
      !!paste(from, "own") := pp_interval(k * own[from, "pred"], k * own[from, "pi.lb"], k * own[from, "pi.ub"]),
      !!paste(to, "own") := pp_interval(k * own[to, "pred"], k * own[to, "pi.lb"], k * own[to, "pi.ub"]),
      !!paste("gradient at", to) := pp_interval(k * at_to$pred, k * at_to$ci.lb, k * at_to$ci.ub),
      !!paste("any country at", to) := pp_interval(k * at_to$pred, k * at_to$pi.lb, k * at_to$pi.ub),
      !!paste(from, "at", to) := pp_interval(k * moved, k * (moved - 1.96 * moved_se),
                                             k * (moved + 1.96 * moved_se))
    )
  }))
})) %>%
  knitr::kable(caption = sprintf(paste(
    "Effect (pp, 95%% interval) of a +/-3 SD temperature year: each country's own (gradient at",
    "its climate plus its deviation), the gradient at the climate of %s (CI), a country drawn at",
    "that climate (prediction interval), and %s moved to it; long-run T: %s %.1f C, %s %.1f C"),
    MOVES$to[1], MOVES$from[1], MOVES$from[1],
    country_climate$clim_TM[country_climate$GID_0 == MOVES$from[1]], MOVES$to[1],
    country_climate$clim_TM[country_climate$GID_0 == MOVES$to[1]]))
```

## Country responses with long-run income

Hot countries are also poorer, so the climate gradient of the country responses
may be one across incomes (as in "Long-run income in the interaction" for the
pooled model). Here step 2 has the country's long-run income as a second
moderator, next to its long-run climate:

```text
step 2:  beta_a(i) = c_a + b_a clim(i) + h_a inc(i) + u_a(i),   u_a(i) ~ N(0, tau_a^2)
inc(i) = log of the mean GDP per capita of country i over the horizon, minus its
         mean over the sample rows (as in "Long-run income in the interaction")
```

and three estimates of each country's own response are compared, all with both
the climate and the income terms:

- country OLS: the country's step-1 coefficients (the country alone, robust
  variance);
- mixed: its BLUP in the meta-regression with climate and income, the
  gradient at its climate and income plus its estimated deviation u;
- pooled: the preferred model with every arm also interacted with income
  (the "with income" model of "Long-run income in the interaction"), at the
  country's climate and income (clustered SE).

On `r main$label`:

1. each arm: the climate gradient without and with income, the income
   gradient, the spread of the country responses (tau) and the share of
   tau^2 that income explains, and the meta-regression with income against
   the one without (ML fits: AIC, BIC and the likelihood-ratio test);
2. the effect of a +/-3 SD year in each estimate, for India, Brazil, the
   United States and China (table and figure).

```{r country-responses-income}
RESPONSE_COUNTRIES <- c(IND = "India", BRA = "Brazil", USA = "United States", CHN = "China")

# Step 2 with long-run income as a second moderator.
response_income <- add_income(main, response_data)
country_income <- distinct(response_income, GID_0, inc, inc_level)
stopifnot(!anyDuplicated(country_income$GID_0))
income_slopes <- left_join(country_slopes, country_income, by = "GID_0")
stopifnot(!anyNA(income_slopes$inc))
moderated_fits <- lapply(stats::setNames(response_arms$term, response_arms$term), function(a) {
  s <- filter(income_slopes, term == a)
  fit <- function(mods, method) {
    metafor::rma(yi = estimate, vi = variance, mods = mods, data = s, slab = GID_0, method = method)
  }
  list(climate = meta_fits[[a]], income = fit(~climate + inc, "REML"),
       climate_ml = fit(~climate, "ML"), income_ml = fit(~climate + inc, "ML"))
})

# 1. The gradients with and without income (in pp of the +/-3 SD event, per C
# or m of long-run climate and per log point of income).
bind_rows(lapply(seq_len(nrow(response_arms)), function(i) {
  ai <- response_arms[i, ]
  f <- moderated_fits[[ai$term]]
  k <- 100 * ai$value
  lr <- stats::anova(f$climate_ml, f$income_ml)
  tibble::tibble(
    arm = ai$label, countries = f$income$k,
    b_climate_only = coef_cell(k * f$climate$beta[2], k * f$climate$se[2]),
    b_with_income = coef_cell(k * f$income$beta[2], k * f$income$se[2]),
    h_income = coef_cell(k * f$income$beta[3], k * f$income$se[3]),
    income_p = signif(f$income$pval[3], 2),
    tau_climate_only = signif(k * sqrt(f$climate$tau2), 2), tau_with_income = signif(k * sqrt(f$income$tau2), 2),
    tau2_explained_pct = round(100 * (1 - f$income$tau2 / f$climate$tau2), 1),
    delta_aic = round(lr$fit.stats.f[["AIC"]] - lr$fit.stats.r[["AIC"]], 1),
    delta_bic = round(lr$fit.stats.f[["BIC"]] - lr$fit.stats.r[["BIC"]], 1),
    lr_p = signif(lr$pval, 2)
  )
})) %>%
  knitr::kable(caption = sprintf(paste(
    "%s, %s, horizon deviations: each arm's meta-regression on long-run climate, and on climate and",
    "income; b (per C or m) and h (per log point of income) in pp of the +/-3 SD event (SE); tau",
    "(pp), the SD of the country responses around the gradient; delta AIC and BIC (ML fits, with",
    "income minus without) and the likelihood-ratio test of income; across the countries,",
    "correlation of income with mean T %.2f, with mean P %.2f"),
    main$label, PREFERRED_FORM,
    with(distinct(income_slopes, GID_0, clim_TM, inc), stats::cor(inc, clim_TM)),
    with(distinct(income_slopes, GID_0, clim_RR, inc), stats::cor(inc, clim_RR))))

# The slope of arm `ai` in model `m` at the moderators `mods` (named list:
# clim_<v>, inc), with its delta-method SE.
moderated_slope <- function(m, ai, mods) {
  b <- stats::coef(m)
  V <- stats::vcov(m)
  idx <- c(ai$term, vapply(names(mods), function(z) interaction_name(ai$term, z, names(b)), ""))
  w <- c(1, unlist(mods))
  c(estimate = sum(w * b[idx]), se = sqrt(drop(t(w) %*% V[idx, idx] %*% w)))
}

# The pooled model with every arm also interacted with income.
pooled_income_model <- fit_model(c(form_terms(FORMS[[PREFERRED_FORM]]),
                                   paste0(response_arms$term, ":inc")), response_income)

# 2. The three estimates of each country's own response to a +/-3 SD year.
RESPONSE_ESTIMATES <- c("Country OLS", "Mixed", "Pooled")
own_responses <- bind_rows(lapply(seq_len(nrow(response_arms)), function(i) {
  ai <- response_arms[i, ]
  clim_name <- paste0("clim_", ai$variable)
  blups <- by_country(metafor::blup(moderated_fits[[ai$term]]$income), moderated_fits[[ai$term]]$income)
  bind_rows(lapply(names(RESPONSE_COUNTRIES), function(g) {
    clim <- country_climate[[clim_name]][country_climate$GID_0 == g]
    inc <- country_income$inc[country_income$GID_0 == g]
    own <- filter(country_slopes, term == ai$term, GID_0 == g)
    stopifnot(nrow(own) == 1, g %in% rownames(blups))
    pooled <- moderated_slope(pooled_income_model, ai,
                              stats::setNames(list(clim, inc), c(clim_name, "inc")))
    tibble::tibble(GID_0 = g, country = RESPONSE_COUNTRIES[[g]], arm = ai$label, value = ai$value,
                   estimate_type = RESPONSE_ESTIMATES,
                   slope = c(own$estimate, blups[g, "pred"], pooled[["estimate"]]),
                   se = c(sqrt(own$variance), blups[g, "se"], pooled[["se"]]))
  }))
})) %>%
  mutate(effect = 100 * value * slope, half = 1.96 * 100 * value * se,
         low = effect - half, high = effect + half)
own_responses %>%
  transmute(country, arm, estimate_type,
            cell = sprintf("%+.2f [%+.2f, %+.2f]", effect, low, high)) %>%
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = estimate_type, values_from = cell) %>%
  knitr::kable(caption = paste(
    "Effect (pp, 95% interval) of a +/-3 SD year on the country's growth: its own coefficients",
    "(country OLS), its BLUP in the meta-regression on climate and income (mixed), and the pooled",
    "model with climate and income interactions at its climate and income (pooled)"))
```

```{r country-responses-income-figure, fig.width = 12, fig.height = 8}
ggplot(own_responses %>%
         mutate(country = factor(country, levels = RESPONSE_COUNTRIES),
                arm = factor(arm, levels = response_arms$label),
                estimate_type = factor(estimate_type, levels = rev(RESPONSE_ESTIMATES))),
       aes(effect, estimate_type, colour = estimate_type)) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, colour = GRID_MUTED, linewidth = 0.4) +
  geom_errorbar(aes(xmin = low, xmax = high), width = 0, linewidth = 0.7, orientation = "y") +
  geom_point(size = 2.4) +
  facet_grid(country ~ arm, scales = "free_x") +
  scale_colour_manual(values = grid_colours(RESPONSE_ESTIMATES), breaks = RESPONSE_ESTIMATES,
                      name = NULL) +
  labs(x = "Effect on growth of a +/-3 SD year (pp, 95% interval)", y = NULL,
       title = "Own response of four countries, with climate and income interactions",
       subtitle = paste0(main$label, ", ", PREFERRED_FORM,
                         ", horizon deviations. Country OLS: the country's own coefficients; mixed: ",
                         "its BLUP\n(meta-regression on climate and income); pooled: the preferred ",
                         "model with income interactions at its climate and income.")) +
  theme_results() +
  theme(legend.position = "top", panel.grid.major.y = element_blank(), axis.text.y = element_blank(),
        plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 8.5))
```

## Country responses from regional data

A country's own coefficients rest on one series: about fifty years of one
growth rate. The regions of a large country add observations, and their
weather is not the same in a year. The comparison holds the data and the
units fixed, so that what differs is only the variation used:

```text
national, PWT       step 1 (the country's own coefficients), on the years the
                    country has in DOSE
national, DOSE      the same, with the country's growth from DOSE: the growth of
                    the summed GDP of its regions over their summed population
                    (the regions with a growth rate in the sample in that year
                    and the one before; a year enters if they hold at least 90%
                    of the country's GDP)
regions             all the DOSE regions in one panel, with the strategy of step 1:
                    each country its own coefficients, year effects common to
                    every region of every country, region effects and quadratic
                    trends, the controls;
                      g(r,t) = sum over arms a of  dev_a(r,t) x beta_a(country of r) + ...
                    weighted by the region's share of the country's GDP in the year
                    before (the weights of a country add up to one in each year,
                    as one country-year of the national panel), so that the
                    coefficient is that of the country's GDP, not of its average
                    region
regions, split      the same, with each region's deviation split into the part its
                    country shares in that year and the region's own:
                      x(r,t) = n(c,t) + [x(r,t) - n(c,t)],  n(c,t) = sum over the
                      country's regions of weight x deviation
                    the arms of n (nationwide shock) and the arms of x minus those of n
                    (regional shock), each with its own coefficients
```

The deviations are in the country's national SD (that of the national panel):
each region's demeaned deviation in degrees or metres (times the region's own
SD) divided by the national SD, so that a coefficient means the same in the
national and in the regional estimates (a region's weather varies more than its
country's average, so a regional SD is larger). The regional deviation in the
split is identified from the regions' differences within a year, which the
national estimates cannot see; the nationwide part from the country's
year-to-year variation, as the national estimates. Equal coefficients of the
two parts say that a local shock and a nationwide one act alike (no spillovers
between regions, national prices or transfers); then the regional estimate
measures the national response with more power. Regional GDP is in constant
local prices at one conversion factor (`r params$dose_variable`): no
movements of the exchange rate. The weights and the national DOSE growth need
each region's population; the regions DOSE gives none for are left out (in
Brazil four states, among them Rio de Janeiro and Rio Grande do Sul).

Standard errors are Driscoll-Kraay (correlation across all units in a year and
over years), the national ones as well, so the precision of the two is
compared on the same footing; clustering by region, shown for comparison,
would leave out the correlation between neighbouring regions. On India, Brazil,
the United States and China:

1. the data: years, regions, the GDP of the regions in the national DOSE
   growth, the correlation of the national DOSE growth with PWT, and the SD of
   the regions' deviations in national SDs;
2. the effect of a +/-3 SD year (national SD) in each estimate, and the test
   that the nationwide and regional parts are equal;
3. the standard errors of the national DOSE and the regional estimates;
4. figure.

```{r regional-responses}
# Regional GDP without exchange-rate movements: constant local prices at one
# conversion factor per country (see DOSE_GDP_VARIABLES).
stopifnot(params$dose_variable %in% c("lcu2015_usd", "lcu_2015", "lcu2015_ppp"))

# Each region's GDP and population, and those of the year before (econ_panel.R).
dose_levels <- load_econ_panel(resolve_econ_source("DOSE"), params$dose_variable) %>%
  filter(gadm_level == dose$level) %>%
  group_by(GID_1) %>%
  arrange(year, .by_group = TRUE) %>%
  mutate(gdp = grp_pc_usd * pop, lag_gdp = lag_by_year(gdp, year), lag_pop = lag_by_year(pop, year)) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  select(GID_0, GID_1, year, gdp, pop, lag_gdp, lag_pop)

# The deviations of the national panel, and each country's national SDs.
national_sd <- distinct(response_data, GID_0, national_sd_TM = sd_TM_all, national_sd_RR = sd_RR_all)
stopifnot(!anyDuplicated(national_sd$GID_0))

# The regional rows: the DOSE sample with the GDP weights, for the countries of
# the national panel.
regional_data <- dose$clean %>%
  left_join(select(dose_levels, -GID_0), by = c("GID_1", "year")) %>%
  inner_join(national_sd, by = "GID_0") %>%
  mutate(has_levels = is.finite(lag_gdp) & lag_gdp > 0 & is.finite(lag_pop) & lag_pop > 0 &
           is.finite(gdp) & is.finite(pop))
# Regions of the sample that DOSE gives no population (or total GDP) for, in
# the countries of the comparison: left out, nothing is filled.
regions_without_levels <- regional_data %>%
  group_by(GID_0, GID_1) %>%
  summarise(without = !any(has_levels), .groups = "drop") %>%
  filter(without)
regional_dropped <- sum(!regional_data$has_levels)
regional_data <- regional_data %>%
  filter(has_levels) %>%
  group_by(GID_0, year) %>%
  mutate(weight = lag_gdp / sum(lag_gdp)) %>%
  ungroup()
# The deviations in national SDs, and their arms.
for (v in c("TM", "RR")) {
  dm <- paste0("dm_", v, "_all")
  regional_data[[dm]] <- regional_data[[dm]] * regional_data[[paste0("sd_", v, "_all")]] /
    regional_data[[paste0("national_sd_", v)]]
}
regional_data <- add_deviation_terms(regional_data, DEFINITIONS[["Horizon"]])
# The nationwide part n (GDP-weighted mean of the country's regions in the
# year) and the regional part, in the arms of the preferred form.
regional_data <- regional_data %>%
  group_by(GID_0, year) %>%
  mutate(n_TM = sum(weight * devTM), n_RR = sum(weight * devRR)) %>%
  ungroup()
for (i in seq_len(nrow(response_arms))) {
  ai <- response_arms[i, ]
  common <- term_value(ai$suffix, regional_data[[paste0("n_", ai$variable)]])
  regional_data[[paste0(ai$term, "_common")]] <- common
  regional_data[[paste0(ai$term, "_within")]] <- regional_data[[ai$term]] - common
}

# The national DOSE growth: the summed GDP of the regions over their summed
# population, on the regions of the sample in the year (and their levels of
# the year before), and the share of the country's GDP they hold; a year
# enters only if they hold NATIONAL_MIN_SHARE of it (a break year can leave a
# single region with a growth rate).
NATIONAL_MIN_SHARE <- 0.9
national_dose <- regional_data %>%
  group_by(GID_0, year) %>%
  summarise(dose_growth = log(sum(gdp) / sum(pop)) - log(sum(lag_gdp) / sum(lag_pop)),
            regions = n(), lag_gdp_sample = sum(lag_gdp), .groups = "drop") %>%
  left_join(dose_levels %>%
              filter(is.finite(lag_gdp)) %>%
              group_by(GID_0, year) %>%
              summarise(lag_gdp_all = sum(lag_gdp), .groups = "drop"),
            by = c("GID_0", "year")) %>%
  mutate(gdp_share = lag_gdp_sample / lag_gdp_all,
         dose_growth = ifelse(gdp_share >= NATIONAL_MIN_SHARE, dose_growth, NA_real_))

# Step 1 on the national panel, with the countries of the comparison on their
# DOSE years: their growth from PWT, or from DOSE.
regional_names <- names(RESPONSE_COUNTRIES)
on_dose_years <- response_data %>%
  left_join(select(national_dose, GID_0, year, dose_growth), by = c("GID_0", "year")) %>%
  filter(!GID_0 %in% regional_names | is.finite(dose_growth)) %>%
  mutate(growth_dose = ifelse(GID_0 %in% regional_names, dose_growth, .data[[OUTCOME]]))
own_terms <- c(sprintf("i(GID_0, %s)", response_arms$term), CONTROLS)
# All the DOSE regions in one panel, each country its own coefficients.
regional_model <- function(terms) {
  fixest::feols(make_panel_formula(paste(c(terms, CONTROLS), collapse = " + "), OUTCOME, FIXED_EFFECTS),
                data = regional_data, weights = ~weight, panel.id = c("GID_1", "year"), vcov = "DK")
}
own_models <- list(
  national_pwt = fit_model(own_terms, on_dose_years),
  national_dose = fit_model(own_terms, on_dose_years, outcome = "growth_dose"),
  regions = regional_model(sprintf("i(GID_0, %s)", response_arms$term)),
  split = regional_model(c(sprintf("i(GID_0, %s_common)", response_arms$term),
                           sprintf("i(GID_0, %s_within)", response_arms$term)))
)

# Coefficient of country g on `term` in own_models[[model]] and its SE (vcov:
# a fixest vcov type); each covariance matrix is computed once.
vcov_cache <- new.env()
country_coef <- function(model, g, term, vcov) {
  m <- own_models[[model]]
  name <- paste0("GID_0::", g, ":", term)
  if (!name %in% names(stats::coef(m))) return(c(estimate = NA_real_, se = NA_real_))
  key <- paste(model, paste(deparse(vcov), collapse = ""))
  if (is.null(vcov_cache[[key]])) vcov_cache[[key]] <- stats::vcov(m, vcov = vcov)
  c(estimate = unname(stats::coef(m)[name]), se = sqrt(vcov_cache[[key]][name, name]))
}

# 1. The data.
bind_rows(lapply(regional_names, function(g) {
  r <- filter(regional_data, GID_0 == g)
  n <- filter(national_dose, GID_0 == g) %>%
    left_join(select(response_data, GID_0, year, pwt = all_of(OUTCOME)), by = c("GID_0", "year"))
  units <- distinct(r, GID_1, sd_TM_all, sd_RR_all, national_sd_TM, national_sd_RR)
  tibble::tibble(country = RESPONSE_COUNTRIES[[g]], years = paste(min(r$year), max(r$year), sep = "-"),
                 regions = n_distinct(r$GID_1),
                 regions_without_population = paste(c(sum(regions_without_levels$GID_0 == g),
                                                      regions_without_levels$GID_1[regions_without_levels$GID_0 == g]),
                                                    collapse = " "),
                 region_years = nrow(r),
                 national_years = sum(is.finite(n$pwt) & is.finite(n$dose_growth)),
                 years_below_share = sum(n$gdp_share < NATIONAL_MIN_SHARE, na.rm = TRUE),
                 cor_dose_pwt = round(stats::cor(n$dose_growth, n$pwt, use = "complete.obs"), 2),
                 sd_dev_T = round(stats::median(units$sd_TM_all / units$national_sd_TM), 2),
                 sd_dev_P = round(stats::median(units$sd_RR_all / units$national_sd_RR), 2))
})) %>%
  knitr::kable(caption = sprintf(paste(
    "DOSE x ERA5: years and regions of each country (with a population); regions_without_population:",
    "the regions of the sample DOSE gives no population or total GDP for (left out); national_years:",
    "the years of the national comparison (with both growth rates); years_below_share: years left out",
    "of it because the regions with a growth rate hold less than %.0f%% of the country's GDP;",
    "cor_dose_pwt: correlation of the national DOSE growth with PWT; sd_dev_T, sd_dev_P: median over",
    "the regions of the SD of their deviations in national SDs. Region-years left out for a missing",
    "population or GDP, all countries: %d"),
    100 * NATIONAL_MIN_SHARE, regional_dropped))

# 2. The effects of a +/-3 SD year (national SD), Driscoll-Kraay.
REGIONAL_ESTIMATES <- c("National, PWT", "National, DOSE", "Regions", "Regions: nationwide part",
                        "Regions: regional part")
regional_responses <- bind_rows(lapply(seq_len(nrow(response_arms)), function(i) {
  ai <- response_arms[i, ]
  bind_rows(lapply(regional_names, function(g) {
    est <- list(country_coef("national_pwt", g, ai$term, "DK"),
                country_coef("national_dose", g, ai$term, "DK"),
                country_coef("regions", g, ai$term, "DK"),
                country_coef("split", g, paste0(ai$term, "_common"), "DK"),
                country_coef("split", g, paste0(ai$term, "_within"), "DK"))
    tibble::tibble(GID_0 = g, country = RESPONSE_COUNTRIES[[g]], arm = ai$label, value = ai$value,
                   estimate_type = REGIONAL_ESTIMATES,
                   slope = vapply(est, `[[`, 0, "estimate"), se = vapply(est, `[[`, 0, "se"))
  }))
})) %>%
  mutate(effect = 100 * value * slope, half = 1.96 * 100 * value * se,
         low = effect - half, high = effect + half)
# The test that the nationwide and regional parts are equal (Driscoll-Kraay).
split_V <- stats::vcov(own_models$split, vcov = "DK")
equal_parts_p <- function(g, terms) {
  b <- stats::coef(own_models$split)
  common <- paste0("GID_0::", g, ":", terms, "_common")
  within <- paste0("GID_0::", g, ":", terms, "_within")
  if (!all(c(common, within) %in% names(b))) return(NA_real_)
  R <- matrix(0, length(terms), length(b), dimnames = list(NULL, names(b)))
  for (k in seq_along(terms)) R[k, c(common[k], within[k])] <- c(1, -1)
  d <- R %*% b
  stats::pchisq(drop(t(d) %*% solve(R %*% split_V %*% t(R), d)), length(terms), lower.tail = FALSE)
}
regional_responses %>%
  transmute(country, arm, estimate_type, cell = sprintf("%+.2f [%+.2f, %+.2f]", effect, low, high)) %>%
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = estimate_type, values_from = cell) %>%
  left_join(bind_rows(lapply(seq_len(nrow(response_arms)), function(i) {
    tibble::tibble(country = unname(RESPONSE_COUNTRIES), arm = response_arms$label[i],
                   equal_parts_p = vapply(regional_names, equal_parts_p, 0, response_arms$term[i]))
  })), by = c("country", "arm")) %>%
  mutate(equal_parts_p = signif(equal_parts_p, 2)) %>%
  knitr::kable(caption = paste(
    "Effect (pp, 95% interval, Driscoll-Kraay) of a +/-3 SD year (national SD) on the country's",
    "growth: step 1 on the national panel with PWT or DOSE growth on the country's DOSE years; the",
    "DOSE regions in one panel (GDP weights); and the same with the nationwide and the regional part",
    "of the regions' deviations; equal_parts_p: the test that the two parts have the same coefficient"))
tibble::tibble(country = unname(RESPONSE_COUNTRIES),
               all_arms_equal_p = signif(vapply(regional_names, equal_parts_p, 0, response_arms$term), 2)) %>%
  knitr::kable(caption = "Joint test that the nationwide and regional parts are equal in every arm (Driscoll-Kraay)")

# 3. The standard errors (pp of the event): national DOSE against regions.
bind_rows(lapply(seq_len(nrow(response_arms)), function(i) {
  ai <- response_arms[i, ]
  bind_rows(lapply(regional_names, function(g) {
    k <- 100 * ai$value
    se <- c(national_hetero = country_coef("national_dose", g, ai$term, "hetero")[["se"]],
            national_dk = country_coef("national_dose", g, ai$term, "DK")[["se"]],
            regions_dk = country_coef("regions", g, ai$term, "DK")[["se"]],
            regions_region_cluster = country_coef("regions", g, ai$term, ~GID_1)[["se"]])
    tibble::tibble(country = RESPONSE_COUNTRIES[[g]], arm = ai$label, !!!as.list(round(k * se, 2)),
                   regions_over_national_dk = round(se[["regions_dk"]] / se[["national_dk"]], 2))
  }))
})) %>%
  knitr::kable(caption = paste(
    "Standard errors (pp of the +/-3 SD event) of the national DOSE estimate (heteroskedasticity-",
    "robust and Driscoll-Kraay) and of the regional one (Driscoll-Kraay and clustered by region),",
    "and the ratio of the Driscoll-Kraay ones (below 1: the regions are more precise)"))
```

```{r regional-responses-figure, fig.width = 12, fig.height = 8}
ggplot(regional_responses %>%
         filter(is.finite(effect)) %>%
         mutate(country = factor(country, levels = RESPONSE_COUNTRIES),
                arm = factor(arm, levels = response_arms$label),
                estimate_type = factor(estimate_type, levels = rev(REGIONAL_ESTIMATES))),
       aes(effect, estimate_type, colour = estimate_type)) +

                         "years. National: step 1 with PWT or DOSE growth; regions: the DOSE regions in ",
```

# Within and between countries: the 20-year climate gradient

With the horizon mean, the long-run climate is a constant of each unit, and
its interaction is identified only across units: the response of hot countries
stands for that of a country after warming. With the 20-year matched
interaction (`clim_TM = mean_TM_lag_20`, the mean of the 20 years before),
the long-run climate also moves within each unit. Split into the unit's
average and its movement around it,

```text
clim(i,t) = clim_between(i) + clim_within(i,t)
clim_between(i)  = mean of clim(i,t) over the unit's sample rows
growth = sum over arms a of  dev_a x (c_a + b_a clim_between + w_a clim_within)  + controls + FE
```

`b_a` is the gradient across units and `w_a` the gradient each unit has lived
through as its own 20-year climate changed. If the cross-section can stand for
a change of climate, they are the same; the model with one interaction
(`clim`, the 20-year matched model) is this one with `b_a = w_a`. The movement
within units is small (see the first table), so `w_a` is imprecise: how
imprecise says how little a unit's own history tells about a climate it has
not had. On `r main$label`, `r PREFERRED_FORM`, the 20-year matched deviations:

1. how much the long-run climate moves within units and across them;
2. each arm's gradient between and within (per SD, or SD^2, of the deviation,
   per C or m of long-run climate), and in pp: the change of the effect of a
   +/-3 SD year when the long-run climate is 1 C (0.1 m) higher; the test that
   the two are equal;
3. the joint tests of equality for each variable and all the arms, and the
   verdict of the split model against the one-interaction model.

```{r within-between}
split_data <- add_deviation_terms(main$clean, DEFINITIONS[["20-year, matched interaction"]]) %>%
  group_by(GID_1) %>%
  mutate(clim_b_TM = mean(clim_TM), clim_b_RR = mean(clim_RR)) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  mutate(clim_w_TM = clim_TM - clim_b_TM, clim_w_RR = clim_RR - clim_b_RR)
split_arms <- form_arms(FORMS[[PREFERRED_FORM]])
split_terms <- c(unlist(lapply(seq_len(nrow(split_arms)), function(i) {
  a <- split_arms$term[i]
  v <- split_arms$variable[i]
  c(a, paste0(a, ":clim_b_", v), paste0(a, ":clim_w_", v))
})), CONTROLS)
split_models <- list(
  "one interaction" = fit_model(form_terms(FORMS[[PREFERRED_FORM]]), split_data),
  "between and within" = fit_model(split_terms, split_data)
)
split_model <- split_models[["between and within"]]
split_terms_fit <- names(stats::coef(split_model))

# 1. How much the long-run climate moves.
CLIMATE_STEP <- c(TM = 1, RR = 0.1)  # the change of long-run climate in table 2
bind_rows(lapply(c("TM", "RR"), function(v) {
  w <- split_data[[paste0("clim_w_", v)]]
  b <- distinct(split_data, GID_1, .data[[paste0("clim_b_", v)]])[[2]]
  movement <- split_data %>%
    group_by(GID_1) %>%
    summarise(range = diff(range(.data[[paste0("clim_w_", v)]])), .groups = "drop")
  tibble::tibble(variable = ifelse(v == "TM", "T (C)", "P (m)"),
                 sd_within = signif(stats::sd(w), 2),
                 within_p5_p95 = sprintf("%.2f to %.2f", stats::quantile(w, 0.05), stats::quantile(w, 0.95)),
                 median_range_within_unit = signif(stats::median(movement$range), 2),
                 sd_between = signif(stats::sd(b), 2),
                 between_p5_p95 = sprintf("%.2f to %.2f", stats::quantile(b, 0.05), stats::quantile(b, 0.95)))
})) %>%
  knitr::kable(caption = paste(
    paste0(main$label, ":"), "the 20-year long-run climate within units (around the unit's average, over",
    "the rows; and the median range a unit covers) and between units (the units' averages)"))

# 2. The gradients between and within, and the test that they are equal.
restriction <- function(term, v) {
  H <- matrix(0, 1, length(split_terms_fit), dimnames = list(NULL, split_terms_fit))
  H[1, interaction_name(term, paste0("clim_w_", v), split_terms_fit)] <- 1
  H[1, interaction_name(term, paste0("clim_b_", v), split_terms_fit)] <- -1
  H
}
split_ct <- fixest::coeftable(split_model)
bind_rows(lapply(seq_len(nrow(split_arms)), function(i) {
  ai <- split_arms[i, ]
  v <- ai$variable
  rows <- vapply(c("clim_b_", "clim_w_"), function(z) {
    interaction_name(ai$term, paste0(z, v), split_terms_fit)
  }, "")
  step <- CLIMATE_STEP[[v]]
  pp <- 100 * ai$value * step * split_ct[rows, 1]
  pp_se <- 100 * abs(ai$value) * step * split_ct[rows, 2]
  tibble::tibble(
    arm = ai$label,
    between = coef_cell(split_ct[rows[1], 1], split_ct[rows[1], 2]),
    within = coef_cell(split_ct[rows[2], 1], split_ct[rows[2], 2]),
    between_pp = pp_interval(pp[1] / 100, (pp[1] - 1.96 * pp_se[1]) / 100, (pp[1] + 1.96 * pp_se[1]) / 100),
    within_pp = pp_interval(pp[2] / 100, (pp[2] - 1.96 * pp_se[2]) / 100, (pp[2] + 1.96 * pp_se[2]) / 100),
    equal_p = signif(wald_linear_p(split_model, restriction(ai$term, v)), 2)
  )
})) %>%
  knitr::kable(caption = paste(
    paste0(main$label, ", ", PREFERRED_FORM, ","), "20-year matched deviations: each arm's gradient across",
    "units (between) and within units (coefficient, SE); in pp, the change (95% CI) of the effect",
    "of the arm's +/-3 SD year when the long-run climate is 1 C (T) or 0.1 m (P) higher;",
    "equal_p: the Wald test that the two gradients are equal"))

# 3. Joint tests of equality, and the split model against one interaction.
equality_H <- function(v) {
  i <- which(split_arms$variable %in% v)
  do.call(rbind, lapply(i, function(k) restriction(split_arms$term[k], split_arms$variable[k])))
}
equality_p <- wald_linear_p(split_model, equality_H(c("TM", "RR")))
tibble::tibble(
  test = c("between = within, T arms", "between = within, P arms", "between = within, all arms",
           "between and within against one interaction (AIC / BIC / R2)"),
  result = c(signif(wald_linear_p(split_model, equality_H("TM")), 2),
             signif(wald_linear_p(split_model, equality_H("RR")), 2), signif(equality_p, 2),
             fit_verdicts(split_model, split_models[["one interaction"]], nested_p = equality_p))
) %>%
  knitr::kable(caption = paste0(main$label, ": joint Wald tests (p) of equal gradients, and the ",
                                VERDICT_NOTE))
```
